title: Noisy Air Purifier Requires Expensive Replacement Filters
text:
In my bedroom, this MOLEKULE MINI AIR PURIFIER (with PECO Purification Technology, White) doesn’t seem to be as effective as my [[ASIN:B01LCX9QWG GermGuardian Air Purifier]] at clearing particulate matter from the air. The Molekule is supposed to destroy (not simply kill) germs, which is why I purchased it (from the manufacturer’s web site). However, there is no way to verify this germ-destroying claim.

My [[ASIN:B07JF53NRK Temtop indoor air quality monitor]] shows about the same readings for particulate matter, volatile organic compounds, and air quality, regardless of which air purifier (Molekule Mini or GermGuardian) that I use. The GermGuardian does come with a UV light for killing germs, and the light does seem to make a difference in how clean the air feels. (Again, there’s no way to verify the manufacturer’s germ-killing claim). The GG UV light requires replacement from time to time, but not as frequently as the manufacturer suggests.

The Molekule Mini is more expensive than the GermGuardian, and much noisier. I find that the Level 3 fan setting (out of 5) is the highest “always on” fan setting that is reasonable, and even this setting makes it hard for a nearby Amazon Echo device to hear the wake word.

The Molekule Mini requires expensive replacement filters every 6 months. The GermGuardian also requires replacement filters, but they’re less expensive, and the GG is pretty forgiving if you don’t replace the filters right away.

The Molekule Mini is kind of heavy, and has a surprisingly large footprint on my bedside table. Unlike the GermGuardian, the Mini lacks a display that shows the particulate matter count, and it doesn’t have an Auto setting that makes the fan speed up automatically if extra pollutants are present in the air. (There is a new, more expensive model of the Molekule Mini that does have some kind of particulate matter display.)

Overall, I was extremely disappointed with the Molekule Mini. After using it for 6 months, I decided to take it out of service. It doesn’t improve the air quality in my bedroom (over what I get with the GermGuardian); it’s too noisy; and the filters are too expensive.

I already knew where I would try these out and that I would KNOW for sure if they worked or not based on the very specific odor I would be hoping to eliminate. Guess where?

The litter box area.

We have a litter box set up in a small spare room (10'x10') on our second floor, and we have a litter box set up at base of the stair case. And elsewhere, but those were my target areas. I plugged one of these in both of those locations.

Its been hot, muggy, and extra stinky. This little air purifier is a trooper. I don't know exactly how it works, but it does. I am already a fan of the large corded air purifiers where I have to turn it on and off, so while I could put one in the litter room, I wouldn't want it running 24/7 or having to remember to turn it on and off.

This wee little thing just gets plugged in and that's it! No on and off. No big energy consumption.

Just fresh air. So weird to me. I imagine it works elsewhere for other air purifying/ odor eliminating/reducing needs.. but testing it in our liter box area made me realize how much it works. SUPER Happy to report that I love this set of BLANDSTRS Air Purifiers.

By the way, it just plugs in. While it is small, it has made it hard for me to plug anything else it. I think I could plug a lamp in, but I had to pop out the night light.

title: Pollen, dust and dander, you will not win
text:
There was only one thing that was not clear in the manual provided for the Oreck WK16002, so I will clarify it for you should you have the same mental block I did when I tried to figure out where the odor filter goes. It is a thin black filter that attaches directly to the white pleated HEPA filter. Inside the box, inside the air purifier, are both filters which have been attached to each other as needed. Remove the plastic, replace the filters and you are ready to use this. Attached to the machine is a second odor filter which can be used when the time comes to replace the one that was inside the purifier.

Operating this is as straightforward as is the look of the machine. It's more attractive than pictured, having a front which simply is pulled forward to gain access to the filter area. The controls are lit and visible at the top of the machine, the most simple I've seen. You have a power on/off button which remains visible at all times, an Auto selection, a Speed selection, and a Timer. The Light area enables you to turn off all lights except the power icon, a feature that is perfect for those of us who don't want our appliances to glow. When the lights are on, however, you can see a colored rim of light which alerts you as to the condition of the filters. When used on the Auto setting, this is very quiet, so quiet that I wondered if it was operating. Even when operated on High, it's not as loud as other purifiers I've used, but it circulates the air very quickly so I've found that I have not needed to operate it on High for very long. The circulated air is noticeably fresh, as I've found myself going over to the purifier and breathing in the air from the top. I expect that I'll stop doing this after the novelty of the new appliance wears off. This comes with a 2 year warranty.

The build quality is great. It's easy to change the filters. They last up to 18 months. They're made from layered plastic, so they probably can be cleaned to last even longer.

title: The lack of buttons is annoying, has no air sensors, but would be great for a massage therapist
text:
This would be great if you had a spa, massage studio, or other setting where you are stuck in a small room with one person and would like to filter and sanitize the air. If you expect to leave it on all day and need the technology to remove viruses and bacteria from the air, then this is a solid unit.

That said, as a home unit, I like it a lot less than my other air purifiers from Coway, and also the big Molecule that costs quite a bit more but also has air sensors, and some serious power to help filter much larger rooms. The problem with this one, is that it is indeed very small, and doesn't seem to do much in a standard sized room.

The other issue is that there is one hidden button that does everything. You do a short press to change the airspeed from powers 1 to 5, and a long press to turn the thing off. However, that long press often doesn't work, and there's not a lot of indication as to what is going on. So when I go to turn this thing off, I fumble with it, it takes a lot longer than I think it should, and I often end up turning it way up before successfully turning it off. Maybe I'm impatient, but I don't really want to stand there for five seconds while my air filter realizes that I'm trying to turn it off.

That said, I love the cute little felt strap, the ease of moving this around, and for the right spot, it has the potential to be very helpful. When I had somebody working here recently, I set it up in the restroom so that small, enclosed room would feel safer from viral spread.

So I packed up all 6 … And returned them ... free shipping. And then re-bought only 2 at the discounted price also free shipping.

I think they have a good product… But even with a good product .... great customer service is Important. Won’t support them again by purchasing any more of their products.

text: I have had the worst allergies and asthma this year than I have ever had. I bought my Aren air purifier in 2016 and used it a lot for a while but got out of the habit of turning it on. Recently my asthma was so bad I could barely breathe and I moved it over close to my chair and turned it on. In an hour I felt better. I've been using it day and night for the last two weeks and the improvement is amazing. I run it on auto which means that sometimes it  runs low and other times it's very high and the fan is noisy at that point. Fortunately most of the time it stays in the blue zone now that it has cleaned things up. The fan is very quiet at the lowest speed.

title: Quiet
text: This is a good size filter. It is so quiet. I started dusting and it kicked on, barely any noise. Portable.

title: Really wanted to like it
text:
Really liked the way the product functioned. Quiet on sleep mode. Went to sleep mode automatically. Only had to cover the tiny green sleep mode light at night. Nice to look at. Would have been able to hang on wall. Functions were nice to live with.
But...it made the room stink.
At first I had thought it was my imagination.
The last day of ownership, I came home after 8 hrs of it being on turbo (which should be a good thing). When I walked into the house it smelled awful, my nose stuffed up and I started coughing pretty much immediately.
I turned it off, but kept coughing and being irritated for several hours. So then I knew it wasn’t my imagination.
Next morning I took the filters apart to check it out. I had ordered the pet filter on purchase. I put each filter up to my now back to normal nose for a sniff test. All were fine except the carbon filter. That was the smell that had filled the room.
Done. This thing had been running steadily for two weeks. Any off gassing should have been over with in my opinion. If it takes more time than that, I can’t wait. All filters were sealed new upon arrival. Wrappings then removed before usage. Back it goes.
I have a small Pure Enrichment machine in my bedroom with a carbon filter that makes the room smell great. UV-C light not being used.

title: Excellent fan/air purifier
text: The bladeless fan is perfect for a house with small children - no blades spinning to hurt little fingers or other body parts.  This fan puts out a decent amount of air as well and the oscillation is fine, though I wish it had a wider oscillation range than 90 degrees - like 180 instead, but that's just me.  As for the air purification, it is subtle, not as noticeable as a room-sized, strictly air purifier would be, but I have no doubt that it is purifying the air.  This is also a good size - can be set on the floor, but is not so big that it can't be placed on a coffee table or nightstand.  Oh, and it is very quiet and lightweight enough that it isn't a problem moving it from room to room.  The remote is fine, though I am trying to replace many things in my house with smart items so I can control them through Alexa or a phone app.  Remotes get lost...I haven't lost my phone, ever!  So, just a wish list to those producing this unit - incorporate smart tech into it and you've got the next big thing!

title: I have a smaller one in my bedroom
text: As I age, I seem to have more allergies coming to the surface and having an air filter helps me from sniffling, sneezing, coughing and having burning, itchy eyes.  Anyway, I have a smaller air filter in my bedroom due to the size of the room, but this one is great for my living room/kitchen area.  This is where my two bitty dogs spend most of their time during the day and while I'm not allergic to my dogs, any of their dander that might float in the air gets snatched up and cleaned out of the room.  I am please with how quiet this air filter is and it seems to adjust itself to the air in the room, meaning if my air is cleaner, like later in the evening when the dogs are sleeping and I'm sitting still, it doesn't come on as often.  That will help with the cost of running it as well and in how often I will need to change the filters.  I just got a "permanent" filter for my furnace that is very easy to clean and the put back in/on.  I realize the HEPA filter will need to be replaced, but hope that it won't be too often as the filters can get to be a cost on their own.  Granted, to be able to breath well and not suffer any allergic reactions is worth it.  This would be good for a baby's room or folks that have a den or a large bedroom.

title: Worth it.
text:
A remarkable product, it changed our lives. I'm not trying to be hyperbolic.
Our downstairs neighbors smoke and the smell was coming up through the floorboards. We were getting desperate because in the middle of the night it was like someone was lighting up in the room with us. We tried fans, we tried opening the windows, nothing was working.
We went through a bunch of articles and websites about air purifiers and filters. Everything we read pointed us towards a purifier with a HEPA. They seemed a bit pricy but we decided it was worth it for our comfort and health. We really lucked out. The night we got the O2+ we figured we would leave it on at medium speed and see how well it worked. The change was immediate. The smell was gone, we had no discomfort and even though the fan was running all night the sound wasn't too bad, it was about as loud as leaving a box fan on in the room. (It does get really loud on full throttle if you are concerned about that, but the amazing thing is the Eco mode.) Night two we figured we could see how the automatic settings would do, and again, no smell no discomfort, not only that the fan was almost silent. Since then we have tried turning it off and the smell comes back immediately. We have been leaving it on automatic and if it gets too loud just switching to Eco and letting it do its thing.
Its easy to clean, we just run a vaccume over the front filter and apparently the others will last a year.
In my opinion the O2+ is worth every penny.

title: Mediocre Product
text:
Seems to work fairly okay-ish.
It hasn't reduced any of my allergy symptoms, but it does collect a fair amount of dust and fur.
The device, for some reason, is almost always on yellow or red, indicating poor air quality, even in a closed room where it has been running for hours.
If it's on yellow, and I set it to Auto, it will almost immediately turn red, every time, so I think the auto mode doesn't work that well.

Update: adjusting to two stars for poor customer service.
Mine started malfunctioning very quickly after I received it. It is always on "red" and so the automatic feature doesn't work.
I contacted support, and they did nothing to assist me.
Be aware, if something goes wrong with the product, you may be stuck with it.
On yellow it's pretty loud, and on red it is extremely loud, so I tend to just end up setting it manually to the second-lowest setting. The other reason being, it goes nuts if I spray cologne or air freshener.
All-in-all, an okay product. Nothing special, and pretty overpriced.

title: Nothing short of amazing
text:

Afterwards I moved it to the bathroom for an hour or so, and the room smelled as if it was sterilized, just a clean natural smell.
I feel like a fool for all the money I've spent over the years on stupid scented plugins and gel deodorizers, really.

title: Beautifully made, practical, and effective
text:
This is impressive.
Looking at the manual, I expected there to be a screen on the top, but could not see one, I looked at it from many angles - no, nothing there. I plugged it in, and the buttons and screens appear - very cool indeed.
It has a light around the edge that has three colors representing good, okay and bad air. That's a great start - and reassuring that my house got the good air rating. When you switch it on, it has three settings, 1 is light, near silent. 2 is slightly louder, and a little bit stronger. 3 is a lot louder, and forces torrents of air across the room!
you can set it to come on for 2, 4, or 6 hours, or just to stay on. If you want it running overnight, you can press the light button, and the top goes dark, except for the light button itself, which glows gently so you can relight and see what the settings are and change them ans needed.

This is the 1st Oreck item I have owned, and I can see why they have such a good reputation. The manual is easy to follow, everything is clearly labelled, its very well built, beautifully designed. I am very happy with this device.
After running all night in a bedroom, the room just smelled fresher the next day (in previous days we had spring-cleaned this room, dusting everything, steam cleaning the carpet, so we thought it was clean!) the ir had that "new house" smell to it.

title: I like this Oreck purifier that I will consider getting one for my son's room.
text:
I have 2 hunter air purifiers that have washable filters so I am never required to buy new filters. They are supposed to save money over the years but I realized that it could be a hassle to clean the filters. You could rinse the filters with water which I usually do in the tub but then I would have to clean the tub afterwards. I would have to wear a face mask and gloves so I do not get the dust all over me which I am allergic to dust so I would have to take a shower to rinse off afterwards. I have considered if it is better to save money and do the clean up or is it worth replacing and buying new filters. The Oreck estimates that the hepa filter last up to a year and the odor filter about 6 months. There is a odor filtered already installed and there is a 2nd odor filter to be swapped out later. On the Oreck site, I checked that a replacement filter kit which includes 1 hepa filter and 2 odor filters is $34.99 for use up to 12 months. I think $34.99/yr is worth paying to replace the filters.

I have 2 bunnies so the filters get filled with rabbit hair alot and their litter pan could stink. So far I had the Oreck running for over a month now and I do noticed that it has help with the litter pan odors. It does not fully eliminate the odors all together if the litter pan needs cleaning of course but it helps reduce the smell. I have slight Asthma and I do seem there has been reduction in weezing but not yet fully eliminated so I hope it will help more when I get more Purifiers in the other rooms.

There are 3 speed settings. #1 being the lowest and #3 being the highest. On #1 you can not hear a thing but there is still some air that comes out from the vents holes on top. On #2 you could hear the noise but it is still considered low and tolerable where you could still watch TV and the air is still not too strong. But when it is on #3 it jumps greatly in noise and wind compared to #2. I think it is still a reasonable noise level when I put it at the corner of the room and for the amount of air coming out, the noise is not as bad as I would expect. A tip is to turn the filter on #3 when you are not home then switch it to the lower setting when you come back if the noise is too loud. The Air Quality indicator bar is suppose to have 3 colors: blue, purple,and red but so far the bar has stayed blue the whole time for me. It either means that the air particles in my apartment is not bad or the light is not working properly. I just hope that it is working and my air really is clean.

The look is sexy as described by my husband on first sight. It has a modern sleek design. I like that the Oreck is designed to be safe for my 2 year old son's fingers. The holes on the top where the air comes out is small and there is nothing on the sides that i need to worry about either. My old Hunter purifiers and another brand I use to have (I forget which brand) all had fans on top with these large openings that I had objects fall in and I had to try to turn it upside down to shake it out. The opening for my older purifiers were so large that my son would be able to fit his whole hand in between the slits (of course he never tried). Fur would build up inside the fan area but the slits where not big enough for me to clean deep inside. With the Oreck I do not think I will have the issue of things falling inside and fur will be minimized since the holes are small. With the Oreck, the fan is located inside behind the 2 filters so it is hidden away from my son. Another design I like is that there are actually 2 handles on each side to carry and move the Oreck but they designed it where it blends in so you do not know it is there and there are no handles that stick out and get in the way. The handles makes it easy to move the Oreck Around. With my Hunter purifiers there was 1 handle which was built into the front cover so each time I used the handle to move it, the cover would come off along with the odor filter which frustrated me so much. It would happen every time so that is why I love the handles on the Oreck. The overall size of the Oreck is a decent size. I was expecting it to be bigger because it is the Large size and it is supposed to be able to cover up to 310 sq feet so I am happy with that it is more compact than expected. I might consider getting the small size for my son's room. All the buttons are located on top. They are touch buttons. When the power is off the only thing you see is the power button, when you press the power button on, then the buttons light up (look at photo). If you press the light button off then it just shows the power button and the light button. There is the Power button, Auto setting button to have it automatically sense and change speeds. The 3 speed button, Timer for 2, 4, 8 hrs. light button for the display and there is a filter button that is suppose to show up when the filter needs changing.

I like this Oreck purifier that I will consider getting one for my son's room.

title: Works incredibly well!
text:
I picked one of these up on a whim since we had a continuous bad smell underneath our basement stairwell. It just smelled like a musty basement under there, where as the rest of the basement smelled fine.

The day I received this thing, we had a catastrophic rainfall which unfortunately caused the sewer to backup into our basement flooding it with 12" of sewer water and the worst smells imaginable.

After the water got pumped out of the basement we had to wait for a the tear out crew to arrive, so I decided I would plug this thing in downstairs on full blast overnight to see what it could do. Much to my amazement, in the worst conditions imaginable this thing actually created an area around itself with clean smelling air, pretty impressive actually.

So in extreme conditions like that it works amazingly well, but that's where it comes to a few drawbacks. If you are only trying to fight mild odors you will have to put this thing on the absolute lowest setting, otherwise it creates a smell of its own that my sensitive nose can detect. It doesn't smell bad, but it has almost a medicine smell to it.

Also, I didn't notice this right away but this thing does make a noise when its on, It's likely the noise coming from a small fan running inside. Our house is very quiet and I can hear this thing running in the entranceway which is a good 25+ feet away and around a corner.

I am very impressed with the product, and I think I will continue to use it, but on the lowest setting possible, and only as needed since the sound and smell would bother me if it was on all the time.

title: Decent, simple air filter
text:
I used to have a couple air filter things, but they gave off ozone which I later found out was not very good. Woops.

Since then, I've been looking for another, and I grabbed this one for "free" (I have to pay a lot of taxes on this "free" stuff, I am finding out now that it's tax season... and not all the free stuff I've gotten has been decent, which is kind of the point of reviews.)

Anyway, it is simple as can be. You take it out, remove the plastic from the filters inside (don't forget this step), plug it in.

It has an "auto" feature which sets the fan speed based on how much junk you have to filter from your air. I don't know if this is working or not, but if you're buying it for this reason, maybe consider not. It has a light bar to indicate air quality. It has just stayed on blue for me and only ever uses fan speed 1. I just use it on manual instead and use the speed I want to use.

Fan speeds: 1 is quiet as can be. 2 makes some noise (which I actually like to sleep with). 3 is loud as a bus and really moves a lot of air.

Anyway, this is all I want, basically, a very simple air purifier. I wonder if I could have gotten a cheaper one without the (kind of useless) bells and whistles.

One thing I worry about is how often the filters will need replacing, and I am a bit confused about how to reset the filter indicator things. They don't light up until you need to replace things, I guess. I wonder if they light up early and if the filters cost much. I always just washed the filters in my old one and stuck them back in. :) Might not get away with that with this one.

So there you go. Sorry, not much of a review, just my experience with it. I do like it a lot, and I can't think of anything I'd change. The price seems all right. Again, if I were looking for something that I had to buy with my money instead of just my taxes (I probably pay for 30% of the thing tho), I'd look for something without the light bars and sensors and stuff that I don't need and that I'm not sure even works or not.

title: Expensive but...
text:
I've had this for almost two years now.

The good:
It's quiet.
If you're cooking something it actually did make a noticeable difference with odor. Sometimes I actually lamented this (good odors) but not when the wife cooked fish. It's been about two years (24/7) and it's abilities seem diminished now (hence looking for replacement).
The filter collected quite a bit of dust at my old apartment and required frequent cleaning. I would normally assume this meant it was working.
It has a clean look and looking at other models it's definitely something that won't be completely hideous to look at.
The blue light can make a great night light (that's what I used it for)
It's been two years and it's still going.

The Bad:
It's EXPENSIVE.
That pretty blue bar is BRIGHT as are the other lights. My wife being sensitive we've duct-taped all lights that can't be turned off (keep in mind we don't have clocks either... so this likely won't bother most)
I had pretty bad allergies at my old apartment. This had zero effect on my allergies. I shower when I get home because they can be pretty bad. I vacuum to help reduce my issue... and I still didn't notice a huge difference between inside or outside.

Overall... bang for the buck, this isn't a filter I highly recommend. When I last reviewed this product there were a lot more negative reviews (the product has been removed and reposted since but it's the same model it just lost the old reviews. You can go through my past reviews to find the product as well as others commentary.).

If you like the look and have the money to take a chance that my situation is unique or the product has improved since early 2009, then go for it. It definitely did a great job removing odors for me, which left me dumbfounding as to why it didn't do a great job on the pollen. In fairness it may have been my older place was too contaminated and the vents were the biggest issue... although I would have expected a good air filter to reduce the irritation and despite showering and vacuuming (canister with hepa filter not bag) it never felt like this did.

Keep in mind replacements are $75 (at this moment when I'm looking at replacing 7/12/11) as well.

***UPDATE 2013.04.24***

I ended up losing my filter during a move to a new house. In that time and while searching for a replacement I became VERY educated on air filters. I came to discover that you want a hepa filter AND that it's incredibly important for the filter to filter 4-6 times an hour the square footage that you need filtered. Failure to be able to do that will result in no allergy relief. This may be the real issue i had with the filter, it simply didn't cycle through the air enough to provide me allergy relief as it only does 350sqft twice in an hour on turbo (per note below) which actually means it would only work for me in a space approx 175 sqft although the measurement assumes 8' ceilings so it's even less with taller ceilings.

Anyway, happy hunting in your air filter searching.

title: USA Made Air Cleaner Purifier 1000 Sq. Ft. Room, UV & HEPA & VOC Filtration-Whisper Quiet Multispeed
text:
I'm troubled with allergies year around and don't get full relief from OTC meds. This is the ideal, Top Quality USA Made solution for both cleaning the air in my room as well as sanitizing it. Picture 1 shows it as received after unboxing it with the back slide open panel off. The manual and bulbs are carefully secured inside. This large unit has 2 main filters. A really big HEPA filter (P.5&6) removes everything that gets past the first stage filter which filters pollen, dust and even mold spores, viruses and bacteria from the air. Overall both filtration systems have a 99.9% efficiency. HEPA means high-efficiency particulate absorbing filter and high-​efficiency particulate arrestance filter. I loved the estimated 2 Year lifespan for this big HEPA filter! Replacements are available from the American Manufacturer EnviroKlenz at their Amazon Store.

The 1st filter (P.7) removes Volatile Organic Compounds and nasty things like formaldehyde from the air as well as bacteria, mold and viruses. When you have new carpeting or paneling or even some flooring it can off gas formaldehyde which is quite unhealthy. This solves that! This filter has a somewhat shorter lifespan at an estimated 6 months. It is "military grade" for ability to remove harmful chemicals from the air I breathe.

This unit has 2 specialized UV 9W Bulbs which sanitize the air and kill harmful bacteria. The 2 bulbs shine onto the big HEPA filter and sanitize the inside of the unit. It is important when plugging in the bulbs not to touch the glass with bare hands. I recommend using a pair of powder free nitrile gloves to install them. Open the bulb boxes at the end without the dot (P. 2,3 &4), remove from the tray and carefully plug them in. I loved that they can be turned on or off at the main control panel and that an indicator light shows if the bulbs are on - if on and not lighted then it needs replacement. These bulbs are special because they produce no ozone due to a tuned UV C wavelength output. Ozone is NOT beneficial to one's health.

The unit sits on casters so is easy to move around though it is heavy at around 40 lbs. Note the easy to slide off back panel has a safety switch at the bottom to turn the unit off (P.9) when opened. That's excellent!

This unit is indeed whisper quiet! There are multiple air speeds I can select: 85,150, 200 and 250 CFM. (P.8).That's real useful especially at nite. This is absolutely well designed and solidly made. I really appreciate this company's quality product. The cost of replaceable filters and UV bulbs may be around $250 a year over time and dependent on use. For the peace of mind, health benefits and top notch quality I get this unit is well worth it.

I Highly Recommend this EnviroKlenz Air Purifier Plus Up to 1000 Sq. Ft. Area - White. American Made with tip top dependable quality, 5 year limited warranty on non-replaceable items.

title: Super easy to use, thought out controls, does not put out hot or cold air, quiet
text:
****edit***
I thought I would not use the child lock function unless my grandchildren were visiting....though with the pandemic, they'll likely be old enough to know better by the time it's safe to visit. I was wrong. I have a young dog from a shelter who will look me straight in the eyes and do these long 'ice cream cone' licks on things that you wouldn't expect, usually when she wants food when it's nowhere near dinner time. She licks walls. Cabinets. This air cleaner. After putting the settings back to where I wanted twice in 30 minutes, I felt she was doing it on purpose...not changing the fan speed maybe, but because it made it beep when it went from auto to manual. It's more than a child lock. It's "nuisance proof"! ***end edit***

This came in a shipping box almost as big as me, so I was afraid it would be much larger than I expected. The actual product box is not large, and the product itself is quite light. It is about as tall as the seat of a dining room chair. and slightly wider than a 20 oz soda on it's side. (for people who need to picture a size!) There is a carry handle indent near the top back, and it's light enough you can move it around one handed, or set it on a counter or table. In the product box are a registration reminder, instructions and a small FAQ insert, as well as the actual product. It has foam packaging materials, a plastic bag over the whole unit, a plastic bag over the filter inside the back panel, and a twisty tie on the cord. Remove the packaging, plug it in and it's ready to use. The back panel opens without tools, and the included filter can be vacuumed several times before you have to replace it entirely. (they recommend vacuuming twice a week and replacing at least every 6 months)

Previous air cleaners I've had have blown out enough heated (or cooled) air to change the temperature of the room an uncomfortable amount. This does not.

Operation of the unit is equally easy. There are six buttons on the front, arranged around the middle LED display like a clock. Clockwise from the top are:
a child lock: hold three seconds while unit is on for both lock and unlock
manual fan speed setting: cycles through 1, 2, 3, and sleep mode
Auto fan speed setting: unit adjusts based on air quality
Power/Standby button
Timer: Looks like you can set it to come on, or set it to turn off in 1-12 hours, in increments of one hour. No way to set a specific time.
Filter Reset: will glow red after the unit has run 2,500 hours. Long press to reset after changing the filter

Additionally, if you hold the manual fan and auto buttons together, you can turn off all lights but the power button, which stays at half brightness. Press them again to turn back on. Good function if you have this in a bedroom.

To test this out, I set it in the middle of our main floor, at the junction between kitchen, dining and living rooms. I'm told I can't keep it there though :/ The display numbers in the middle show the fan speed for a few seconds when you change it, then it shows the air quality. While in auto mode, the numbers are constantly changing. Mine changes from 1 to 7 or anything in between after the first hour, only going higher for a minute or so when a nearby door to outside is opened.

When I first turned it on, the ring around the controls glowed a kind of yellowish greenish color that I wasn't sure was either color. After a minute or so, it switched to a very green green, like Christmas LED green. If you aren't sure if it's yellow or green, it's yellow. It switched to different speeds on auto for the first hour, then has stayed on low ever since. From a distance (and on low), it's slightly louder than my new refrigerator that has a quiet pack, so it's pretty quiet. With the TV or even the fireplace on, I can't hear it at all. It sucks air in through the back and blows it out the top, but it does not cool or heat the room any, so I will be able to use this year round. They do recommend enough space for air circulation when you place it. (50 cm on either side, not near a window or furniture) I look forward to this keeping my house air nicer in our low air quality summers. It's small and light enough to move from room to room as needed.

All in all, I really like this so far. The controls are well thought out and it doesn't have a bunch of unnecessary things to cover for poor function and make it gadgety. I like the auto function, and if I had smaller children around more, I might use the timer function, though this would be excellent in a baby's room if you use quiet white noise. There are no fans a child or pet can poke fingers into, and no small bits they can eat. The child lock and other secondary button functions are easy enough to remember how to use, but difficult enough that a toddler won't be able to figure it out. It's easy to clean and change the filter. If any of this changes, I will update. If it remains this good, I will likely buy more.

title: works well, but a bit flimsy in places and offgasses
text:
Overall this is a decent air filter for a small room, but strikes me as overpriced. For $50 I'd say it's a great filter, but it's disappointing for $180.

PROS:
* Filters air well
* Customizable - settings for air filter speed and time (2/4/8 hours)

CONS:
* The offgassing is strong- one month in, it still makes any room I put it in smell like plastic
* Loud-ish. Honestly you're going to expect most filters to generate some white noise, but this one generates more than my whole-house filter. I don't mind it, but people who are sensitive to noises might
* A bit flimsy in places - the sides are easy to remove for changing filters, but they also tend to pop off even when I'm just picking up the filter to move it from one room to another. For now I can pop them back on and they'll stay put, but it feels like the kind of thing where they'll start falling off of their own accord after a few more months
* Price - if this filter cost $50 I'd give it 4 stars, but for $180 (as of today), I'd expect a lot more for my money

NEUTRAL
* The "auto" feature doesn't work for my conditions (kids' room smells musty or has a strange chemical odor) - it thinks the air is already clean - so I think this setting works for particulate air issues only

title: I am finally not being devoured by dust mites!!!
text:
This works instantly. My parents are super sensitive to dust, dander, pollen, everything. They get asthma and have inhalers ready nearby. I bought one of these, and they INSTANTLY noticed the difference. Every family member now has one in his/her room.

We bought the newer Model 540 sold at Costco (WAY cheaper there ~$79). It is super quiet on the lowest setting, and loud on the highest (there are 3 levels). What I LOVE is that I can leave it on 24-7 and not need to buy new filters. When the red-light comes on, it's time to clean the existing filters. With a tube vacuum, the filter is cleaned in under a minute. To reset, I press the Time and Power buttons down together, and it's good to go.

I recently became more dependent on this than ever when I began to react badly to dust mites. I am suddenly so sensitive to dust mites and other common household allergens that my limbs break out in unbearable hives within seconds, no matter whose just-cleaned house, mansion, or office I go to. It was driving me insane, but friends and family wouldn't have to worry about being bit, because if I was in the room, it would choose me. I took a comprehensive approach this, and I have finally won the battle against dust mites! Note: I live in a breezy place so dust is a daily battle, I have cats and little dogs, and have hard wood floors--no carpeting.

If you're battling allergic reactions to dust mites, here's what I did. I have this air-purifier on 24-7 (Costco); use a half-cap of Allersearch liquid allergen wash (Amazon), which is a MUST-HAVE for all bedding, curtains, and clothes; the TRU Lite Bedding mattress cover (Amazon); the newest Roomba sold at Costco, Model 805 (another must-buy if you have pets); any body wash that contains peppermint or tea tree; and tea tree oil.

After scrubbing my body with peppermint soap (Dr Bronner's is the cheapest where I am), I rub tea tree oil on my skin while it's wet for dilution then pat dry. I am so happy to say that I have not been bitten since no matter where I go, that my scars can finally heal, and that I no longer wake up swollen and congested!

title: Hard to tell if I'm getting my money's worth, not very hot, but it's quiet
text:
I like that this unit is quiet (on lowest fan mode, where I keep it). It's nice to have an all in one machine. That said, the rest of this review is in the spirit of constructive criticism. I'd say it's fine overall, but given what the thing offers, I do think the price largely reflects the Dyson brand name.

I keep a clean house and don't have allergies so I'm personally not a great detector of air quality. But I was hoping a $400 air purifier would tell me if I have VOCs or other undetectable pollutants inside my house. Basically, I can't tell if I need to be running a purifier and whether it's working.

The heating function is only on or off and isn't terribly hot. You can set the temperature, but that only functions to turn off the heat when the ambient temperature reaches that target. You can turn the fan up, but it doesn't increase the intensity of the heat. So I pretty much sit next to the unit while it's on focused mode.

Most of the controls are in the little remote. The only button on the unit itself is the power button, which you can use to cycle through the target temperatures, but not adjust any of the other functions. So don't lose that remote.

Lastly, you're supposed to move the unit around by grasping the base, but I find that incredibly unwieldy.

title: The Sexiest Little Air Purifier That Could
text:
[[VIDEOID:9fde47d3114bb57d2bed07f002218ab4]] I am so allergic to dust that if the power goes out in my home, I need to go sit outside until it comes back on and all the air purifiers in my home come back online. Over the years, I have collected quite a collection of air purifiers as we’ve moved from smaller to bigger homes and my allergies have turned into full-blown allergic asthma requiring weekly then monthly shots and daily medication consisting of both pills and inhalers. I buy exclusively from two brands, IQAir and Alen having given up on Blueair altogether in favor of Alen.

I own (2) IQAir HealthPro air purifiers and (1) IQAir HealthPro Compact, which I use in our two bedrooms and our living room. Our home has an open layout with a lot of room to cover and so we use a Alen BreatheSmart in our kitchen (with the handy HEPA-OdorCell filter), another in our main room of our back house. I also own (2) Alen T500s, which we use in our back house bedroom and for travel, one of which I received from Alen to test and keep. Vistors are often shocked by the amazing air quality in our home. It's fresher inside than the great outdoors of Los Angeles.

I haven’t tried the Fit50, the now middle child of the BreatheSmart line so I’ll be comparing the Flex primarily with the original flagship BreatheSmart model. The first thing I noticed was how SEXY the Flex is and how much more compact it is than the original BreatheSmart while still feeling quite and if at all possible, more sturdy. It comes in a giant box that’s easy enough to open and is reminiscent Amazon’s frustration-free packaging.

The front panel of the Flex is weightier than the BreatheSmart's and lined with gray plastic and I believe all over magnetics so it need the annoying hinges that the BreatheSmart does. Overall, the materials used look similar but look and feel much improved. The brushed metal surfaces feel quite nice against your skin if you’re planning on cuddling with it. (Kidding.) The darker silver finish and white front are truly aesthetically pleasing. The display is also fantastic with it’s a flat sleek surface with a touch display that is a vast improvement on the clunky push-down buttons of the original BreatheSmart. You can shut off the display lights or keep them on. Also, unlike the BreatheSmart, it offers the same Lock function as the Fit50 which is really useful if you have a little toddler who loves to those push buttons on the original air purifier. Like the other models, the Alen will tell you when your filter is still good (green), when you should order a new one (yellow) and when you’re filter needs replacing (red).

At the lowest setting, the Flex is pretty much silent while the third is barely a whisper with the fourth Turbo mode setting is loud but softer than expected but this last setting is really the one you’ll only use when you need to get a room de-dusted quickly, like say in your hotel room, new home office or while staying in the dust mite haven that is your mother-in-law’s really, really dusty back house.

The Flex is 15 pounds so it’s almost twice as heavy as the portable travel-friendly Alen T500 tower, which is 9 pounds, but smaller than the 21-pound BreatheSmart and only a pound lighter than the Fit50. The Flex is also stripped down as far as some features that both the BreatheSmart and Fit50 have: the ionizer is gone on the new Flex, as is the SmartSensor, Air quality feedback light and Automatic mode. I'm not sure I personally could not live with the automatic mode which decides on its own what setting is necessary or the SmartSensor that tells me in different colors that the air quality in a specific room is great or really poor. It is also not energy certified and the CADR results are still pending and uses 36 watts on the highest setting whereas the BreatheSmart uses 105 and the Fit50 uses 60.

The Alen promises the same filtration rate as all the BreatheSmart models: 99% of particles great than 0.3 microns eviscerated keeping you safe from those dust mites. The filter life is paired down to 6-9 months, a sharp decline from the Fit50’s 10-12 months (awesome!) but only slight change from the BreatheSmart’s 8-9 months. The powers supply comes in at 115V instead of the 120V of the other models. The Flex is recommended for average size rooms up to 700 sq. feet so it falls between the Alen T500 (up to 500 sq. ft) and the Fit50 (at 900 sq. ft) with the BreatheSmart offering the most coverage of up to 1100 sq. ft for large and open spaces. Like all the Alen air purifiers, it comes with the standard HEPA-Pure filter which is the base filter available with the same three options getting slightly more expensive: the HEPA-Silver, HEPA-FreshPlus and HEPA-OdorCell. The HEPA-OdorCell is truly brilliant in the kitchen, where smoke or garbage might cause some terrible smells, and a baby’s room where a diaper pail might do the same.

Unlike the vastly more expensive 10-year warranty on the IQAir, which Alen rightly deems “overkill” for most people and their homes, the Alen has a lifetime warranty and they truly stand by it. I had problems with the T300, which the T500 replaced, and received a whole new air purifier each time as a replacement. After being offered the Alen T500 to test by Alen when it first came out, I sold my T500s and bought a second T500 and a third for a friend.

If I didn’t already have the top of the line BreatheSmart with the less awesome display, I would really consider this little Flex in my bedrooms. Alen is the air purifier I recommend to anyone with basic allergies or allergic asthma like myself who cannot afford the louder, bulkier, energy-sucking and more complicated and expensive filter requiring energy-sucking IQAir. The IQAir is $200 more than the BreatheSmart’s $599 price tag and the Flex comes in at $399 about a $100 less than the listed price for the Fit50.

And last but not least, the Alen Flex offers 14 designer panels to “complement” your décor just like the BreatheSmart and one more than the Fit50. We plan to take advantage of this feature for the first time with the Flex as we will be using this model in the small office where my husband works. The Flex has also made me more curious about the Flex and left me wondering if Alen has plans to upgrade the display on the original flagship model. I highly recommend the Flex and ALL the aforementioned Alen air purifiers.

title: Was skeptical, but months later (bought before covid), I'm still happily surprised
text:
It's a beautiful thing, for one. And an advantage I didn't expect: the sound it emits is very relaxing. I keep mine on high speed usually since my space is so large but I smoke, and wanted to smoke indoors this past (cold) winter, and that plus cat hair was to be its primary function. (And since the covid thing, I've been smoking more). The last purifier we had didn't have this nice, low/steady "hum", but more like an irritating noise. But I don't notice this one, except that I think the sound has helped keep me relaxed! (Come to think of it, a paranoid type might find it hypnotic). But if I want absolute quiet (rarely), it goes off.

Another effect I should have expected with the whole concept: it cools the room. We already have central air, but in my "smoking section" of the house (my sitting room with a sofa and 2 desks), the air is noticeably cooler. I've turned the speed down or even off to warm up at times.

The light doesn't go orange with a cigarette lit! Maybe it's far enough away, or cleans it as the smoke goes through? But I know something works well, because if I spritz hairspray or cleaning fluids: insta-RED! And note: don't expect miraculous "clean smelling air": smoke and other aromas can still have left a residue on clothing and furniture, so those things will keep the area smelling like smoke (or wet animals, etc) until you wipe down or clean surfaces. But overall, this thing helps the air smell a LOT. —Even a possible "negative": I love scented candles, but cannot smell them beyond the air purifier! I still buy them, but you've basically got to turn Hatha all the way down just to enjoy the candles or baked goods!

I'm going to pick up more (name-brand) filters, so that means this is a "pretty good 5 star" for me. However, the whole setup could be FAR more impressive with (1) better instructions - I'm still not sure what "sleep" does exactly (it's not just "dimming lights", so I think it's like a laptop's sleep mode but loses the settings?); and Timer is useless for me (does the thing go off, or just to Auto, when time's out?). The worst, though: (2) the AWFUL remote layout, and possibly the purifier's panel layout (which I never use). On the remote, I've learned to ignore all but the sleep and speed buttons. I'm going to put little knobs on the random "middle" Speed and Sleep buttons, because hitting the wrong button is frustrating (especially if you're sleepy, or in a rush to get out). But fix those simple things, I'd call this a "solid" 5 star versus a "good enough" 5 star; worth the (hefty, imo) pricetag.

title: Good Filter, High Radio Frequency (RF), WiFi Runs 24/7 Even While Not In Use
text:
First off, the filter part of this product is good, I think, although it's hard to say unless you do some type of more scientific testing.

This product uses a trickle of electricity all the time, even when turned off. So if you are really counting pennies and care about every last dollar, then unplug it when not in use. Where I live, this would cost you about $35 a year just to plug it in, even if you never use it.

If you care about Radio Frequency and WiFi, be warned that this product emits a very strong radio frequency constantly. 24/7, even when TURNED OFF. On average, this product emits 12 to 80 times the recommended maximum radio frequency in a family household. I know most of you could care less, but for those that have actually done the research, this is a big deal.

There are only two ways to stop this from emitting a constant very high radio frequency. The first way is to unplug, because even when turned off but plugged in, there is a constant radio frequency coming out of this product. This still emits the radio frequency while you are using the filter, but stops it when you unplug from the wall.

If you want to use this but disable the radio frequency, the other way to disable the RF is to remove the front cover, remove the 4 screws to the top panel located at the top of the unit, and disconnect the small cable labeled WiFi. Then you will instantly have zero radio frequency.

I can't believe this thing broadcasts WiFI radio frequency 24 hours a day, even when turned off.

title: It’s Nice!
text: This purifier is an excellent value! I am a fan of Winix, having been well-served for the past few years by my 5300-2 air purifier, which continues to function just as well as the day I bought it. What I love about Winix air purifiers, and what I feel separates them from their competitors, are their washable pre-filters. The pre-filters really make all the difference in terms of extending the life of the HEPA filters. All you have to do is vacuum them every couple of months to maintain optimal airflow. Another great feature about the C545 and the 5300-2 (as well as a few other models) are the carbon filters. You get four carbon filters for every HEPA filter, and since the carbon filters are placed before the HEPA filter, they also serve as an extra layer of protection to keep your HEPA filter clean and extend its life. These companies make most of their profit off of filters, so it’s a credit to Winix for designing units that aren’t designed just to force consumers to buy replacement filters every four months by directing all the particles into the HEPA filters (I could name a few companies that do just that, based on all the research I’ve done over the years on air purifiers). This is a 250 CFM unit, which for the price is next to impossible to find. In terms of aesthetics, the C545 is nice-looking, certainly more attractive than my 5300-2, and interestingly, it’s smaller and more lightweight than my other Winix, though they function exactly the same. The C545 has a rated power of 65 watts, while the 5300-2 maxes out at 70 watts. I measured the decibels on my phone and both the C545 and my old 5300-2 came in exactly the same: 53.6 DBs. Connecting the C545 to WiFi was a breeze. I just followed then instructions and in less than 2-minutes was able to turn the air cleaner on and off, view the air quality in real time, and adjust the fan speed on my phone. I don’t keep the WiFi connected because doing so is an unnecessary (albeit minuscule) power drain and turning the WiFi on and off is as easy as pressing one button on the purifier.

title: C545 uses irregular sized filter!
text:
I've got a number of Winix air cleaners around the house. I have a 5300 in the kitchen, 6300 in the living room and a 535 up in my bedroom. All three of these air cleaners use the exact same "size A" Winix HEPA filter and carbon pre-filter, which is extremely helpful and makes keeping the filters replaced pretty braindead simple (the only thing to factor in is which seller and brand to pick from, some vary in terms of quality of filter media and fitment, but all the ones I've purchased from Veva, Insilive and LifeSupply seem to have been just fine. These filters are about 12 1/2 x 16 1/4 inches.

So I stumble upon this c545 (refurbished, looks good as new other than the box it came in) on Woot for about 1/3 the typical price and figure, why not? Before pulling the trigger, I do some googling for "winix c545 filter replacement" and get results for the 115115 filter that I'm oh so fond of. Wonderful, I think, this will work nicely with my family of air cleaners! Hit the button and wait, and here it is. Before I even had it out of the box I could tell I'd be disappointed; they either really crammed that filter into a very small unit, or it uses a different, smaller filter. Turns out this uses a "Size S" filter which is just about impossible to find online anywhere (for what I consider an acceptable price). This unit uses a filter that's 11 x 13 1/4 inches, more or less. That's about 145 square inches vs the just over 203 square inches on the other units. Hmm. I just dug through my trash for the manual and this unit takes "Winix Item: 1712-0096-00" as a replacement filter. You guessed it, this much less popular and ubiquitous filter, that's smaller, costs more to replace. Crappy. Also I'm not seeing my preferred retailers carrying a compatible, lower priced filter. BEWARE!

This does use, like the C535, the little pre-filter screen in front of the carbon filter which helps keep it from getting impregnated prematurely with buildup. I typically vacuum off the carbon filter every other week and replace it every other month to keep the very limited odor reducing capabilities maintained.

All in all the unit itself is pretty nice. It's refined in operation and layout compared to the older 53/6300 models. I have no intention of ever using the gimmicky, unnecessary wifi capabilities. Just leave it at speed two or three and forget about it.

This is NOT a good buy! The long term cost of ownership is higher than other similarly sized/square foot rated air cleaners even from Winix. There is no sense whatsoever (in my opinion) to pay a premium for a useless feature like wifi connectivity. So yes in summary my main complaint is that this uses a smaller, pricier filter that has not (yet) been made available by third parties. Who knows whether the filter I know and love will stay at the price I'm used to forever, even... maybe this will be the new standard size filter (28% smaller). As of this time, this is the only model device to use this special size filter. AVOID. Try to find a c535, 5300 or a 6300 used/refurb'd instead. The x300 series aren't as pretty and modern looking, but they work very well at removing crud from the air.

title: Versatile addition to the nightstand
text:
The Safety 1st Fresh Clean Air Purifier meets several needs. It is a small yet versatile addition to the bedside nightstand and I am pleased by its versatility.

Arriving well packaged, the air purifier has a honeycomb style white plastic base and solid white plastic top section. Included in the box are the top and base sections of the unit, plastic-wrapped HEPA filter, instructions, and AC power adapter, which plugs into the rear bottom of the top section. Once assembled, it measures 6" wide at the base and stands 9" tall. All the controls and night light are located at the top of the unit, including the air exhaust. You only need to unscrew the bottom section to replace the small HEPA filter, which nests inside. With the fan operating, room air is pulled in from the honeycomb base, passes through the HEPA filter, and exits from openings at the top of the unit.

The air purifier has a three-speed fan, which is relatively quiet, as well as a three-level white ring night light. There is also a white noise generator, with five loudness levels. The night light is more than adequate at the lowest setting. The highest setting can light up a room. The white noise generator likewise is adequate for me at the lowest setting. The instructions are simple and straightforward, and include warranty information (one year) and how to purchase replacement HEPA filters.

There is no information provided on the listing or instructions on the HEPA filtration efficiency. Normally, you expect to see the number of air exchanges per hour and room size designed to clean the air. Also, most HEPA filters are designed for one year of continuous use. The Safety 1st HEPA filter is supposed to be changed after 1,000 hours of use, equal to about four months at eight hours a night. It is only sold by the manufacturer on their website.

I wish the manufacturer provided the efficiency of their air purifier to help consumers. I also wish it were available in colors other than just white. Combining a handy nightlight, white noise generator, and HEPA filtration, the Safety 1st Fresh Clean Air Purifier is a useful addition to a nightstand and warrants a solid 4 stars.

If you replace the filters once a year (like I intend to) your cost is $6.25/month. If that's too expensive for creating a virtually dust and allergy free environment, then you can't afford the machine to begin with! Compare that cost to some of the items that we replace annually in our automobiles, for example, to keep them running at an optimum. Catch my drift? I think the filter replacement cost is inexpensive, relative to what the end result yields.

My final verdict? Buy this product, and crank it up to start enjoying fresher, cleaner air today!

title: Helps in reducing allergies but less than optimal for removing second-hand smoke!
text:
3-18-19 UPDATE COMMENT: I purchased the Rabbit Air Purifier directly from Rabbit Air two years ago and I attest it is a quality purifier compared to less expensive brands. The problem lies with replacement filters -- thus, if you reside around smokers, vapers, yearly wildfires, heavy street traffic you will need to replace the filters more often than the yearly recommendation. Several recent replacement filters I received have been inconsistent in their quality. My most recent order arrived with a leaky activated carbon filter (black dust in packaging and residue on my hands when touching the filter) and foul chemical odor in the HEPA and Odor filter that their customer service attributes to "off gassing". They sent me replacement filters but wanted photos of the filters I was returning. And to think, I was going to purchase a second air purifier from them. See the email from their customer service rep. Stay away from Rabbit Air and read the three star reviews as those reviews are right on!

Hi Christine,

Thank you for your email and I apologize that the exchange process became a hassle.

In trying to be thorough, it looks like it became more inconvenience than necessary. Per your request. we will cancel the shipment of the odor filter, but in the future, if it's ever needed, you are welcome to contact us again.

For the charcoal dust that you were concerned about, according to our researchers, we assume that there will be no health risks from the carbon dust. Due to the particle size, carbon dust is heavy, therefore, it would not become airborne easily. In addition, carbon dust could be very difficult to get into the body through the respiratory system even if it were to become airborne.

If you have any questions or if there is anything else that we can assist you with, please let us know.

Regards,

Tamina Park
Rabbit Air

Christine Carlino

7-19-2017 UPDATE COMMENT: After four months using the Rabbit Air Purifier in my 560 sq ft condo, I notice dust and small particle accumulation around the sides and bottom of the interior frame that holds the filters. For reference, I remove and clean the first filter that is washable and vacuum the four filters every other week. Unfortunately, this air purifier is no match for second hand cigarette smoke and marijuana odor from neighboring apartments. I purchased this filter because it does not off gas as many air filters do. I would not repurchase because of price. I'd recommend it for single family homes in controlling dust and light household odors, and those who are diligent in vacuuming and cleaning in general. Not optimal for attached condos or apartments in harsh environments.

ORIGINAL COMMENT: My allergist recommended this purifier to reduce allergens and help with second-hand smoke odors. I consider this to be a quality 5-filter purification system. For optimal results when I first received it, I ran the unit on Turbo or High for 72 hours in the bedroom and small living space to clear the air. I did not wake up with a stuffy noise and the air was fresher. Here is my analysis after a month:

Pros:
• Quality, solid craftsmanship. Stylish.
• Easy to read instructions and assemble right out of box.
• Air quality sensor light. Manually adjustable speed selection and auto mode.
• Removes airborne dust and particles in room size around 300 sq. ft or less.
• Good return policy and excellent customer service.
• Negligible ozone production.
• Manually adjustable speed selection and auto mode.

Cons:
• Pricey.
• The unit goes to 'sleep' in dark room, thus I run the system on manual low or medium at night to ensure the air is being filtered.
• Not good for older apartments or condos with leaky windows and doors.
• Detects and seems to eliminate kitchen / cooking smoke and odor but is less than optimal with reducing second-hand marijuana and tobacco odor (or smoke) from neighbors. The special “Odor” filter does not contain enough activated carbon to contain these odors.

NOTE: There is currently no air filter on the market that will “REMOVE” tobacco and weed smoke including the IQ Air Gas purifier. The IQAir has had issues with its V-5 Cell filter emitting foul odors.

title: As Described and Sturdy Build
text:
I decided on the Air Pura R600 due to its robust construction and simple controls. The idea of 18 lbs of activated charcoal was appealing since the grand kids mentioned that the house had a smell at times and I noticed kitchen odors occasionally myself. So far so good with the odor removal. It takes a while, but the R600 eventually clears the air. I'm hoping that my allergies are improved as well as they were particularly bad so far this year. Due to the open kitchen, nook and relatively large two story family room a purifier with the capacity of the R600 is required to adequately handle the load. I really like the completely variable fan speed so I can choose exactly the speed and noise I want to put up with. The family room always had a dust issue more than other rooms so I am hoping for improvements there but it's still too early to assess the results. The impression I have is that the Hepa and charcoal filter life "should" be decent but I'm a bit concerned about the prefilter. The description of the R600 indicates that it can simply be vacuumed from outside occasionally and replaced annually but, to me, that looks like a pain. I'm not sure how effective vacuuming over all those tiny intake holes is going to be. Based on the included "manual" - a very unfriendly and primitive pamphlet - you need to remove all three filters in order to change out the prefilter. That seems a little non-user friendly to me.
One of the reasons I liked the large amount of activated charcoal in the first place was that I had read you could buy replacement media and refill it for much less than the $199 replacement filter price. Unfortunately, I haven't yet been able to find any place that sells activated charcoal or anthracite media cheap enough to make refilling worthwhile so I may be stuck with the $199 charcoal filter replacement every couple years. We will see if I regret not having filter life indication or other bells and whistles, but so far, the R600 does meet my purchase criteria.
Shipping seemed to be a little too slow and it took over a week to get the notice of shipment so, if in a hurry, you might want to go with a different vendor. I used Allergy Buyers Club via the Amazon site.

text: PLEASE READ Manufacturer's calculations.  They say, "350 sq. ft."  Square Feet are used for laying tile, there is NO HEIGHT.  A room is a cube, Length, Width, Height.  A room MUST be measured in Cubic Feet, Length x Width x Height.  Manufacturer claims 350 Square Feet.  This is non-information, because it tells you to think in Length and Width.  This is a SCAM!  They are trying to CONFUSE YOU, because most people don't think about the difference between SQUARE FEET and CUBIC FEET. They just pull out a tape and measure the floor in 2 directions (L x W). They FORGET about the HEIGHT of their ceiling. This information is USELESS and they are dishonest to their customers.

title: For those with pet allergies...
text:
I have suffered a really, really long time with extreme dog allergies (I'm allergic to cats too, but my allergy to dogs is REALLY severe). Since the National Health Institute has found that 100% of households in America (even those without pets) have pet dander in their home, and I live in an apartment complex with two dogs next door and six dogs underneath me, I decided that I was just going to keep getting sicker and sicker. I was sneezing up to 50 times a day when I was at home and I would wake up every morning with swollen, runny eyes and had asthma attacks all of the time.

That's all gone, thanks to Rabbit Air. I actually initially bought the [[ASIN:B000LDWJ6O Rabbit Air BioGS (model 421A - covers 600 sq. ft.) High Quality Ultra-Quiet Air Purifier - Low Maintenance - Washable Filters!]]. I didn't really see a reason to go for the MinusA2, except it looks nicer and has an extra customized filter and some other things. Everything you have ever read about Rabbit Air's awesome customer service is 100% true. They treat their customers like royalty and they honor their warranties and will go above and beyond to help you.

Well, sadly (sort of), my BioGS was defective. The auto mode stopped working completely. I called Rabbit Air and they were so apologetic that they sent someone to come pick it up for me and four days later this arrived as my upgrade, free of charge because of the hassle I went through. I was so impressed with how professional and helpful they were!

I liked the BioGS, with what little time it worked. When it was working, it was extremely sensitive to pollutants and I stopped sneezing within a day. I went without sneezing until it left me. The four days that I waited for this to come in? All of my allergies came back. I was sneezing non-stop and having asthma attacks all of the time. I set up the MinusA2, and within 24 hours I was feeling great again.

This thing is SO sensitive to odors and pollutants. You can literally have bad breath or open the door or walk by it smelling oddly (self-tanner!) and it picks it up. On auto mode it goes from blue (clean air) to red (dirty air). Even when the furnace comes on, it goes to red. I also opted for the pet allergy filter for the customized one, just to be safe.

I am a person that sometimes suffers from buyer's remorse, and I have NONE for this. This has absolutely changed my home life. I can now feel like a normal healthy person at home! Now, since I did have the BioGS and MinusA2 in my possession, you may want to know....

SHOULD I GET THE BIOGS OR THE MINUSA2??

If you aren't really on a budget, by all means go for the MinusA2. You get the customized filter, it's quieter on all levels, you can mount it on the wall, and it covers more square footage. I also feel like it is more sensitive than the BioGS. But I'm not sure that my BioGS was ever quite working correctly, so I can't be 100% sure on that one. But the BioGS never started going on high when the furnace came on like the Minus does. In my opinion, the MinusA2 also looks nicer. They are both sleek and elegant and in my opinion the best looking air purifiers on the market, but the BioGS is a little too futuristic looking for me or something. I definitely prefer how the MinusA2 looks.

If you're on a budget, don't feel bad getting the BioGS at all. That's what I initially did, and I loved it before it broke. It still cured my allergies and I was in love with it! There is nothing wrong with either....they are both superb products with excellent customer service. Seriously. Customer service is really important when it comes to something like this. You don't want to pay $300-$600 on a product and then have the representatives treat you like garbage. Rabbit Air has the best customer service I have EVER dealt with in my life. You'll know what I mean when you buy one from them.

With the combination of this machine and the nifty [[ASIN:B001ADL1SG Crane 2.3 Gallon COOL Mist humidifier, White and Blue]], I feel healthier, happier, and more at ease at home and have a much higher quality of life.

Thank you, Rabbit Air!

I think it's easy to operate, looks great, and is made well.  Downside: finding a replacement filter shouldn't be as difficult as it is.  I've posted some photos and a video and hope that they, along with my experience, helps you out a bit with your choice.  Thank you!

title: Thin plastic housing,  Subpar filtration
text:
[[VIDEOID:fd92c27b560b604d95307db2b96ee32f]] Although there are features I find positive about this Elechomes Air Purifer,  some of the components are less than desirable.  I'll start with the plusses.  First, it's an attractive unit that has a small footprint.  It's housing is all plastic so it's lightweight and easily moved from to room to room if needed.  The center touch control panel is easy to operate by just simply pressing the soft touch icons. (PLEASE SEE: operating video posted with noise recording) This purifier can be set on automatic where it will cycle for you and set the fan speed according to your rooms air quality.  You can also manually select fan speed, set an operating timer function, along with securing it with a child proof lock.  A filter reset button is also displayed. On it's lowest speed, the unit is quiet,  but when set to a higher setting, very noisy. 
Now I must, in all good conscience, point out what I find concerning.  The plastic housing, notably the back panel is a very thin plastic.  Care must be given to removing this panel as well as the thin plastic base. I'm concerned about the longevity of the thin plastic tabs that hold the panel in place.  Now on to the most important feature in any air purifer,  the filter itself. The mesh liner is one you'll have to keep checking and cleaning. To some, the idea of being able to vacuum this filter may be desirable,  but I much prefer installing a filter and waiting for an indicator light to inform me of replacement. Having to keep tabs on this extra maintenance step of inspecting this removable mesh often, pulling out my hand vac in order to have this purifer running at optimal performance, is just a bother for me and one that needs to be kept in mind. If you, like me,  prefer to "set it and forget it" then you may want to consider another purifer.  And last, but certainly not least, is the built in carbon layer this filter has. It's subpar to say the least, in fact I don't know why they even bothered with it as the carbon is scarce in content. I posted a side by side comparison of another brand's purifer carbon filter and Elechomes carbon filtration side by side so you can see the difference for yourself.  I'm obviously disappointed with overall quality at this price point; I expected better. A purifer is only as good as the filter it houses that purifies the air. I've posted a video and photos and hope that they,  along with my experience, help you to make the best choice for your home. Thank you.

text:
bought pre-owned unit (780a) and just received it. WOW this thing is so much more efficient than my germ guardian (38-Low,43-Med,48-High watts max) . Although this unit does cost about 6 times as much, you can run the 780a at half the wattage (medium setting vs medium setting) at the same cleaning power.

power/noise/cleaning efficiency:
Turbo speed is 58 watts max (-3w error). Turbo is pretty loud, probably slightly louder than the germ guardian on high. the amount of air blown out is much more powerful than the Germ guardian. I'd say as powerful as my box fan on low.

high speed is 27 watts. noise level probably matches germ guardian on med/high. currently have this propped up at an angle on the ground with the air output pointed at me keeping me cool.

medium speed is 17 watts. This speed is probably quiet enough to keep on at night without earplugs. white-noise level.

low speed is 8 watts. computer desktop fan quiet. not sure how efficient this mode would be but I guess if you had to keep the fan on constantly, this would save you a lot of money in the long run.

silent speed is about 6 watts. slient PC fan quiet.

Auto mode works great. cleaned the sensor as recommended. I've been testing it with my dylos air quality monitor and the air sensor seems to be in line with the dylos. It will go into medium mode when the air quality is in the "fair" range and then into low mode when in the "good" range. My dylos air monitor cost $230, so I guess you can factor in that value into the higher cost of this unit.

Tried to test the light sensor to see how that works. covering the light sensor didn't do anything so the entire unit probably needs to be in the dark.

Air filter: mine came with a $70 non-OEM filter installed. They work, but I did check non-OEM filters to save money for future purchases. There is a difference in the Activated Carbon Charcoal Filter. The non-OEM will have about 50-70% filled sacs vs 80-90% filled sacs on the OEM. The difference is 30 dollars every 1-1.5 years. I would think this will affect some more than others.

I just realized the pre-owned unit is almost 10 years old according to the manufacturing date...it is functioning like new, so hopefully it lasts another 10 haha
