title: Worth the Investment
text:
The Hathaspace Smart True Air Purifier was worth the purchase. After careful comparison and consideration, I decided to spend a little more. I kept coming back to the fact that this model promised to clean such a large space every hour than all the others I viewed. The delivery was quick and the packaging excellent. A few pieces of tape and removal of the film covering key areas, and I was done.

The model is slick and modern, something that looked great! The large electronic readout is easy to read, with a dynamic analysis of the air was enchanting. I found myself referencing the color bar in the manual because of the visual color displaying in the front. The design is clean. The model is substantial without overpowering any space, and many times better than those square, odd-looking alternatives (I'm sure people who bought them try to hide). The noise levels are so low that I had to dash upstairs to the loft a few times, just to confirm it was running.

But beyond the look and feel was the reason why I purchased this air purifier. Within the first few minutes of turning on my unit, the readout displayed the air quality around 14, a number that is actually good. But within that first hour, it dropped down to 9 (lower numbers are best). It may not seem that significant but there was an immediate and noticeable difference. This was especially true the next morning.

Anyone with allergies will know what it feels like to breathe normally through the night or wake up without sneezing during the fall. The Medical Grade HEPA (H13) filter that comes with the Hathaspace is just another reason to purchase.

Use your favorite search engine. You find all the other competition use H9-H12 HEPA filters, meaning that those other units you are thinking of buying (and hope to save a little bit of money) allow more contaminates to escape back into your environment. And if you're going to buy an air filter, why not get one that cleans the best.

I'm careful about what or who I recommend, but this was easy. If you purchase something else after reading my review, then I suggest the following... Save the box. You'll be returning it soon.

title: So glad I went with this model!
text:
I will start by saying this air purifier made such a difference in my asthma/ allergies that I purchased a second unit 2 days after I bought the first.

VOLUME
My husband HATES white noise, so I was concerned about this being too loud. I check the decibel ratings on all new appliances because it makes such a difference to him. This does not bother him on auto during the daytime, and works for him in our bedroom at night if he set the unit to level 2 so it does not keep changing speeds.

EFFECTIVE
My kids have even commented on how the air "smells cleaner". We aren't fighting odors, so I did purchased the base level HEPA filter model. However, we have a lot of dust and dander from our 2 big dogs and 3 cats. I actually never realized just how much until we started running this. I like how the unit clearly shows on top when there are more particulates in the air, and adjusts itself accordingly.

We have a VERY open floorplan in the living room, kitchen, and great room, then our 2600 sq ft house is shaped like a U leading to the bedrooms and laundry. One 1100 sq ft unit was obviously not enough to do the entire house with all of our pets. Two units are making a substantial difference, though hardly ever on "blue" that shows fully clean, by having one on each side of the house.

When I say substantial, I mean I am no longer having to take my allergy medicine every day and am not waking up having to blow my nose every morning. My allergies are to poor air quality, not specifically any one thing, and this has done the trick!

QUALITY
Wow! I have to say that from just opening the packaging, you can tell this unit was made with quality in mind. I HATE assembling new products, and I am the person that reads ALL of the directions, much to my husband and son's amusement. This was so well packages, the directions were so simple and well-written, and it was the easiest to assemble product I have ever purchased. So much so, that I actually looked forward to putting together the second one when it arrived.

SIZE/ APPEARANCE
This unit is much larger than I expected. I thought I would be able to put it in an unobtrusive spot by our fireplace, but it is much too large for that. That being said, the white has a sleek appearance and the effectiveness of the unit is worth the space it takes up.

WEIGHT
The design is nice and simple and the unit was light enough (about 15 pounds) that I could easily carry it to and from my bedroom each morning and night. The bulky size made it awkward, but not undoable had one unit been enough to keep up with my house full of pets.

CONS
Price, price, price.... We invested over $1000 just pruchasing the 2 units and the filters are expensive to replace. In my household full of furry critters, filters will probably need to be replaced much more often than the manufacturer states. They are however, like everything else about this unit, of very high quality and quite thick. Pricing for the replacement filters appears to be $80-$110, but I haven't shopped around for them yet.

RECOMMENDED?
YES!!!! I actually will probably end up buying a third one because I am so happy with this purchase and would recommend it to anyone with sensitivity to air quality.

title: they really do work, but use enough per room to do the job correctly!
text: Ok, I read all the reviews and decided to give these a try. I got the 3 pack. I have 3 dogs, and we hike daily, often getting wet from sudden showers or because I let them go for a dunk in streams, deep puddles, lakes, etc. And then my house smells of wet dog for days! One of my dogs also has skin problems, not bad but enough that she often has a musky odor to her, which permeates the entire house. So when they arrived, I placed one in the livingroom, one in my bedroom, and one in the family room, which is always the worst smelling room because all of their beds are in that room. After 3 days, to my dismay, every morning I'd wake up, walk into the family room and the funky smell would hit me smack in the nose. And I thought, these things don't work worth a darn! I unplugged the one in my bedroom, to pack up to return... and thought "wait a minute... that family room is big, 13X11 feet big! So, I placed the one I had just removed on the opposite side of the family room from the one that was already working in there. BINGO! Within hours the family room smelled NORMAL! WITHOUT washing dog beds for the umpteenth time, without shampooing carpets again, and without bathing the dogs! That was a week ago. I have not had a single dog odor in the entire house since then. Seems the smells were all coming from that family room! So yes, these things do work, and they work well. But if you're using them in a large room, you'll need more than one in there to do the job! I read reviews where people were returning them because the directions say to not leave them on if you're leaving the house for long periods. I honestly don't think they mean overnight, or longs days at work! They're talking about going away for a few weeks or months. The exposed tiny filaments that actually do the ion charging can build up with dust, which in turn can cause a flash which can cause a fire. So of COURSE you're remove them if you leaving for a long period, you DO have to clean them off monthly, or as often as you see a dust build up on them. Mine have been in use for about  2 weeks now, maybe a little longer, and there is still no build up on the little "fingers", so unless you have a very dusty home, I don't think it will become a problem. Just do regular checks on them to make sure everything is clean. And enjoy your clean smelling home!

My family is getting used to that smell, since it is better than what the cat had offered.

My concern is over how it works, which is not stated in the description above. It calls itself an "Ionic" air purifier. After reading about air ionizers on Wikipedia, I learned that there are two methods of air purification: ionization and ozone. This product uses the word ionic, but doesn't actually say that it ionizes the air. It does have a vague reference to adjustable "ozone concentration". Ozone is toxic, and is restricted by the US FDA. So this worries me. Next time, I will buy a purifier which openly states its method of operation.

title: I did a lot of research first. I'm very happy with this.
text:
I waited a long time to review this because I didn't want it to be like most 'new wave' products and dupe you into a good review only to break the second you hit the submit button.

This unit is very quiet even on high. I have it in an 800sq ft 1 bedroom apartment. It's in the living room and I leave it on high with the UV and anions on all the time.

The UV light is rather ingeniously designed to shine on the paper filter which keeps bacteria from growing on it. If you've ever had an air purifier with one of those automotive style filters, you know that germs take up residence in them when they get old and the unit smells like your grandfather's window air conditioner.

This unit is free of that problem because of proper placement of the UV light.

I'm on my second set of filters now and I'm still very happy with the machine. The blower is very strong and as the filter clogs it is strong enough to pull unfiltered air around the edges which will make the inside of the unit dirty. Look at your filter every once in a while and change it when it gets dirty. I don't think tapping this filter out is a good idea so I just replace it. If you know more than I do and know how to make it last longer, more power to you.

The anions charge the dust in your air and make it stick to walls which may sound gross but it's nice because it's out of the air before it gets inside computers. I also vacuum my walls from time to time so it's not a problem for me.

This is a giant fan so it does show up on the power bill. Be prepared for that.

This device is unobtrusive and it keeps your house clean. It is of good quality and the filters last most of a year in my very dusty apartment. When this unit is off, I dust every day. When it is on, I don't have to dust anything for weeks.

title: Cleans Quietly and Not an Eyesore
text:
Most air purifiers are ugly and look like they belong in the basement. They are also noisy as hell (like being in a wind tunnel), and that was true for my Honeywell Envirocare, which took up a huge amount of space in my small apartment.

Which is why I practically fell over when I found the Rabbit. It's cool-looking, has a small footprint, and it's quiet.

But it's also uber-expensive -- close to $600. I hesitated, then finally took the gamble and bought it.

Was it worth it? Yes. I have several birds, all of whom shed dander, crunch food, throw food, and poop every thirty minutes. Even if you make cleaning up a full-time job, you end up with a "birdy" smell. Once I turned on the Rabbit, it was gone. You would never know that I had even one bird. To me that alone is worth it. (Rabbit Air actually has a Web page devoted to birds and their air purifiers, although I found that after I purchased the unit.)

The fact that I could have a clean smelling apartment, listen to tv without having to turn up the volume full blast, and had an air purifier that looked decidedly upscale and didn't look like an air purifier justified the purchase. The customer service is first rate. The only reason the Rabbit gets 4 stars instead of 5 is because not all the lights turn off in the dark. If you want it for your bedroom, that's an issue. But overall, a very good investment.

title: STAY CLEAR...DON'T BUY THIS PRODUCT!
text:
I've had a string of bad luck with Dyson products this past year. I've purchase a few and both were lemons right out of the box brand new. Luckily the manufacturer warrant covered issues. There's not necessarily any blatantly misleading information with how this is advertised but you need to consider a few things before purchasing it.

First, I'll defend Dyson with some negative reviews as it relates to the heating. Clearly this is NOT a space heater. This should NOT be purchased if that's primarily what you're looking for. Common sense should tell you that this in no way would generate the heat needed for any space other than a very very small room. The heat works just fine if its close to you (approx. +/- 10 ft). It's pretty good at that distance.

Next, read the previous paragraph for the cooling feature. Basically a similar type of idea. This is not an air conditioner. Obviously.

Lastly, my issue comes with the controls for this system. Besides the base unit having a power button, there's not much else. If you lose the remote or if the remote only occasionally works properly (like in my situation), you're basically screwed with an oversized paperweight or air purifier that you can't control the flow to or make oscillate. The app controlled Dysons made the HP01 worthless. Buy the other model, not this. However, the other model(s) that offer this feature are significantly more expensive. I seriously question Dyson's QC lately and will no longer purchase anything they make. You have to ask yourself, how much is a fancy looking air purifier worth? To me, there are better options that are easier to operate and do a equal to or better job than Dyson air purifiers. On a side note, all quality HEPA replacement filters are very expensive so that alone shouldn't be a deterrent. Anyways, look elsewhere for a device that you want primarily for air purification. They don't have many quality options that just do that and don't suffer from issues. They seem to try to cram other features in unnecessarily to justify their inflated prices. They're not worth their typical $400-650+ price tag.

title: Generates dust instead of capturing it
text:
My husband Oscar and I have used an Austin Air Healthmate 400 for at least 15 years, since 2005 if not earlier. In December of 2018 the fan became disruptively noisy and not because we were running the machine on high. The only way to repair it was to ship the entire unit to Austin Air, at substantial expense (to save on some of the expense, we shipped without the heavy filter, per Austin Air advice that the filter was not needed for the repair). Austin Air wrote to me that the problem was a "bad motor" and that they had put in "a new motor, switch, and prefilter." Upon receiving the repaired unit, we began using it continuously again. The only difference was that we ran it on its low setting, whereas before we had run it on medium; the reason for the change is that we could no longer tolerate the substantial level of noise produced at the medium setting (at the high setting, the noise is completely intolerable).

Months ago the machine began emitting a kind of whining sound at its low setting; we used a high quality white noise machine to try to cover up the whining sound, but the result was not entirely satisfactory. I reported the problem to Austin Air and they invited me to ship the machine to them for repair, but I pointed out that I'd had it repaired just three years ago. I declined to ship it, for the two reasons I gave them: 1. the trouble and expense involved and 2. the fact that I'd rather apply the money to purchasing a second Rabbit Air A3 machine: we recently purchased one of these and it is much quieter and nicer than the Healthmate 400. So Oscar took apart the Healthmate 400, salvaging for recycling the parts that can be recycled and garbaging the rest.

I can now turn to the main problem with the Healthmate 400. Once we stopped using it, which was about two weeks ago, a mysterious dust problem that we had been having in our apartment for many years immediately stopped being a problem! All these years that we had been using this Healthmate, and even after every thorough vacuuming of our apartment, a layer of bluish-grey dust would quickly return and coat our floors and furniture again. We suspected that the Healthmate might be responsible for this scourge of dust but we could not be sure. Now we can be. The fact that the disappearance of this dust coincides with the discontinuance of our use of the Healthmate is too remarkable to ascribe to happenstance. By the way, since our receipt of our Rabbit Air A3 about three weeks ago we have been running it continuously and it is not generating any dust; on the contrary, it is doing what it is supposed to do: capture dust, not be a major cause of it!

title: I LOVE THIS THING!
text: I am over-the-moon to live near an Amazon liquidation center so that I get to try lots of items for pennies on the dollar. I bought one of these little purifiers without having much faith that it would do much of anything. I have bought several different wick-type deodorizers--I want to make an interior bathroom not smell funky. All those items failed--one leaked so badly, I was afraid it would short out when the cord got wet. This appeared not to have been used--it only came with one filter, not the set of three included in the higher-priced set. It's nice looking and has more settings than the air scrubbers we run on our porch. I am amazed at the job this does in a very short amount of time. I read some of the other reviews--one mentioned that a piece of toilet paper would not stick to the sides--so the review surmised the purifier isn't drawing air. What the buyer failed to notice is that the air is drawn through the top of the Zhengxoo unit, not the sides. Another said that the filter remained clean while cat hair and dust piled up on surfaces in the same room. Since we run air scrubbers in a room that a smoker uses, I am very educated on air purification and the machines that provide it. A purifier draws in ambient air, runs it through a filter and exhausts that air out again. It does not stir up particulates that have settled out of the air. We've had ionizers out on the porch--they make particulates sticky, making cleanup tough. This has three settings; all three can be run on high or low. It is a simple machine--no claims are made about it stirring up the dust or impurities around a room and catching them in its filter. If a room--especially a bathroom--smells funky, it's kind of embarrassing if you appear to be making no effort to change that. I don't like aerosols and don't like making my guests responsible for dispersing any odors they may have created. I didn't pay what you did but even if I did, I would say it's worth every penny. If you're going to plug it into an outlet (rather than a USB), you'll need a converter. Really works!

title: Excellent air purifier with some software quirks
text:
Right off the bat: I love this air purifier. I have a cat and live in Oregon, so aside from COVID concerns, I have both pet dander and wildfire smoke in my home. I bought two of these purifiers for my two-bedroom apartment a year ago, with a subscription through their website for Overreactor filters every six months.

The Mila purifier does a great job! Between my purifiers and regular cleaning, I haven't run into any concerns with pet dander in my home. Guests comment on how clean my apartment seems, despite the cat. I can also *definitely* tell the difference between my apartment and outside during wildfire season; so long as I keep the windows shut and these purifiers running, I can barely tell it's wildfire season at all. I recently got linen sheets, and although I vacuum constantly, my Mila in the main bedroom helps minimize lint in the air, as well. It is extremely quick and easy to switch the filters, too--just pop the magnetic front off, slide out the filter, wipe down the inside, slide a new filter in, and replace the magnetic front.

This is the best-looking air purifier I found in my search. I have midcentury modern furniture in my apartment, and the little wooden legs on the Mila are adorable. Most air purifiers look overly utilitarian or futuristic; this one looks like a tiny piece of furniture.

I love that you can easily see the indoor AQI by glancing at the screen or by opening the mobile app, and the mobile app is very well-designed. I also love that there are all kinds of air quality statistics in the app; earlier this year, the heater in my apartment stopped working, and I was able to use the graphs from the temperature sensor to negotiate a rent decrease for the month. Sleep mode is great, which lets you run the purifier at a high level before bed, so it doesn't have to make as much noise overnight. Sometimes I wonder whether my purifiers are doing anything at all because the screens always read as "0 AQI"--but then I'll cook, and they'll automatically increase effort to minimize smoke in the air. The graphs in the app give me greater confidence that the air filters are actually doing something, unlike with a lot of "dumb" air purifiers that require purchasing air quality sensors separately and require manual adjustment.

My only complaint is that the on-device interface isn't very intutive. Aside from just increasing or decreasing the purification level, I have no idea how to do anything at all without the app. Guests who stay with me sometimes want to change settings on the Mila in my office/guest bedroom (e.g. to minimize noise), and they end up just unplugging it, instead. I recently moved apartments, and the purifiers somehow lost connection to the Wi-Fi network. It took me a full hour to sort through their customer service portal and the devices to get them to connect to my phone and Wi-Fi again. That said: if you're okay with just using the mobile app for everything, you should be good--and you will rarely need to reconfigure the purifiers once they're set up.

All said, if I were buying air purifiers in 2022, would I buy these again? *Almost definitely.* I am debating buying a third to keep in my living room right now.

title: Good performance in a small package
text:
I live in a coastal climate where there always seem to be mold issues and musty indoor air, so I've been through several air purification systems trying to find one I can live with - and the Molekule Mini seems to be one of the better units all-around.

Out of the box, it seems as good as any of the other units I've tried in terms of quality. It's a bit larger than I expected, but I'd still call it a compact unit that should fit just about anywhere. It's just a few minutes to setup...simply unwrap, install the filter, and plug it in. Unlike some other reviewers, I didn't find there to be any unusual odors initially - just clear air pretty much immediately.

In my case, I put it in a 250 square foot bedroom that's often had stale and musty air. My habit is to run it at mid/high speed during the day, then drop down to the lowest setting at night. After doing this for a few weeks, an AirMentor 2 air quality metering system reports that the air quality in this room is improved substantially, and I give the credit to the Molekule. VOCs and fine particulate matter are both down about 30%.

My biggest complaint is that the motor seems to emit somewhat higher frequency noise than most of the other units I've tried. I don't think the Molekule is any louder in an absolute sense, but the higher-frequency noise is easier to hear in a quiet room. After a few days, I became used to it - so I'm not sure this is a huge problem, but it is a difference between the Molekule and other units I've tried.

After about a month, I can definitely see particles building up on the filter. I have a HEPA filtration system in our HVAC system, so this tells me the Molekule is picking up particles that my HVAC system doesn't - that also seems like a good thing.

The operating costs for this filter are fairly low. The unit itself draws very little power, and doing a little math for where I live, the daily electric cost is only about $0.10. The only other cost are the filters, and those for the Molekule are fairly expensive at $75 each every six months. This puts the overall annual cost at about $110, which in my opinion is pretty typical for most products in this space.

Overall, the Molekule is one of the more effective units I've tried - if you have issues with indoor air quality, it (or it's larger cousin) are worth a look.

title: All-around Purifier
text:
I've got roommates that smoke and have allergies, and generally realized that I have poor air quality, so I decided to look into air purifiers.

A heavy dose of research later, and I decided on this unit. Why? This unit meets the criteria I developed from research, which were essentially effectiveness, operating cost, noise, and appearance.

EFFECTIVENESS
Obviously effectiveness is going to be the most important aspect since it is why you purchase an air purifier. This model's design shines to me because it has the bases covered - HEPA filtration (removes solid particles), chemical and carbon filtration (gases and super small solid particles like smoke), and ionization (adds electrons to air, makes filters more effective on next pass and much more).

The pre, medium, and HEPA filter combo is efficient for filter life and effectiveness over that life. Particles that would otherwise get caught in the HEPA are caught earlier and extend its life. This part of the purifier does its job well and the dust level is way down.

Carbon filtration and the toxin absorber (my choice) remove impurities because their molecular structure causes gases and tiny particles to stick as they pass by. The carbon filter is relatively thin and so it requires more than one pass and depending on the severity of the odor/smoke you have, you will need to underrate the purifier a bit if you want full effectiveness, which I cover further down.

Ionization's value goes beyond improving the effectiveness of the purifier. It is worth a bit of research if you are interested. All I will say is that I definitely keep it turned on.. The ozone level at the output is nothing to worry about.

OPERATING COST
In a get-it-now society, operating cost may not get as much thought since it is a long-term consideration. The truth is that it will cost less to operate a MinusA2 than many cheap models because of its low power draw. Where I live power is cheap and the annual stats for power use are twice the filter cost. It really is worth the up-front investment because it will cost less over time.

It turns out that this unit is progressively more efficient in terms of CFM as you run it at lower speeds, so if you want to be economical, running two units (at two notches lower) will be half as loud and use less than half the power on average to clean the air by the same amount. You'll have some headroom available too if you need more power. The second one will pay for itself over a few years (covering the same area).

NOISE
The MinusA2 is quiet enough for me on the medium and lower settings from a couple feet away for pretty much any task except for some audio work I do, in which case I turn to silent. However, I've been running it on turbo most of the time anyway because I have loud roommates and I can't even hear it over their noise. In fact, the noise is actually a pleasant "smooth" sound that is less of a hum. This is because the motor itself is very quiet and the noise is predominantly turbulence at the exhaust. Visual inspection tells me that the turbulence could be lowered (and the noise) at high CFM with some moderate re-design of the exhaust, although I will admit I am not an expert in fluid dynamics. There is some shaping, but I think more thought could be put into it.

APPEARANCE
Out of all air purifiers I've seen so far, the MinusA2 is hands-down the most pleasing to my eye. I like the layout of the controls and the look of the mood light. If they could improve it at all, I'd say it would be with an extra button to allow multiple brightness levels.

TIPS
A few quick tips to wrap up my review follow:

Air Changes: Based on my experience with my unit, I recommend getting enough CFM to change the air over four times in an hour while chugging along quietly and then have the ability to ramp up to 15+ when needed. This is only appropriate for rooms that would require 4 or less units (up to 500 square feet) to achieve this because beyond that point airflow affects the results more. At that point I would place 4 units near the heaviest source of pollution and work to achieve airflow to those units. Of course, in industrial applications there are large-scale machines. This is a residential recommendation. 1 per 120 sqft up to 4 units.

Airflow: Even in smaller rooms a purifier will work best when you ensure that the airflow of the room works with the purifier and not against it. Perhaps a cheap fan (low-noise) will be necessary in some cases.

LAST WORDS
Quiet, effective, economical, elegant. If you're looking for an all-around purifier, this is the one. If you plan to run auto mode all the time, go 700A. If you plan to run turbo like I do, go 780A. May your clean air needs be met.

title: Does the job—but that price!
text:
The Oreck WK16002 Air Response HEPA Air Purifier with Odor Control & Auto Mode for Large Rooms—wow, that's a mouthful of a name for a device that does one thing: suck air through a filter. Honestly, that functional specificitymakes a detailed review difficult, since it either does that one job well or doesn't. Not a lot of nuance there.

UNIT FACTS
MODEL: Oreck WK16002 Air Response HEPA Air Purifier
DIMENSIONS: Approx. 17" W x 9" D x 20" H
WEIGHT: 13.8 lbs.
MADE IN: China
UL LISTED: Not shown on labels
POWER: 120VAC, 60Hz, 95W
WARRANTY: 2 years
MANUAL: 30 pages, English, Spanish & French
REPLACEMENT FILTER KIT: #AK46002—two odor filters, plus one HEPA filter
CADR RATING: 200, rated for rooms up to 310 square feet

PROS
+ Does the job—rapidly cleaned the air and removed odors
+ Operates whisper-quietly in all modes
+ Features stylish, minimalist, buttonless, and intuitive touch-based control display
+ Features self-adjusting auto-cleaning modes, plus three manual cleaning modes
+ Features filter change indicators that light only when activated
+ Features timer, which can shut off unit after 2, 4, or 8 hours
+ Minimalist air-quality light bar indicates unit operation, provides air cleanliness level, and keeps unit visible in a dark room (though lighting can be disabled)
+ Replacement filter kit is reasonably priced (Oreck's site lists $34.95 MSRP)
+ HEPA filter lasts a full year, while the two pre-stage odor filters last six months each
+ Lacks a plastic cover grill to fill with sucked-in dust—smooth surfaces and design

CONS
- MSRP as of this writing is $269.99—yikes
- Offgassing from plastic components persists for a couple weeks
- Personal experiences with China-made home appliances has been terrible, YMMV

MIXED
* Looks like a paper shredder
* Oddly, Amazon does not have the replacement filters available on its site (as of the date of this review)

THOUGHTS
I set up the WK16002 in my living room. During the cold months, we have a large fig tree in a half-barrel planter that we keep in the room. Unfortunately, toward the end of the cold season, it puts off allergens that not only create a smell in the room but can cause watery eyes. Within a couple hours of running the Oreck, both the smell and the allergens were gone, proof enough that the unit works. And it does it so quietly, you wonder if it's running.

While the unit itself is not the snazziest looker, the control panel is nicely designed and counters the boringness of the rest of the unit's looks. Everything about the unit is intuitive. Nicely done, Oreck engineers.

SUMMARY
Overall, it's hard to find many detraction points with the Oreck WK16002. That said, I would price this unit as a $130 device, not a $270 one. Yes, the replacement filter pack is not as outrageously priced as some other HEPA air filters on the market, but still. I received the unit as part of a Vine review, and I'm certain I would not otherwise shell out that MSRP. For that reason, I can't give this a five-star review, mostly for pricing issues alone. Oreck makes a model above this in another line that includes a humidifier, and that might be the better value, but even it seems overpriced. I mean, really, at its heart, this unit is merely a fan and a paper filter. How costly should it be, especially when it's made in China?

text:
The Austin Air arrived today. Boy, is it heavy. In anticipation of its arrival, I read the unpacking instructions and knew exactly how to wrangle the purifier without stressing my body.

Here's the thing: the Austin Air IS louder than the Winix on Turbo . . . BY TWO DECIBELS (lol). IOW, without a sound meter to distinguish the difference, they sound EXACTLY THE SAME.

The Austin Air on high is NOT louder than other air filters on high. IMHO, anyone complaining about the noise is WAY too sensitive. It's the first day, so I'll be running this machine for the next 24 hours on high. And I will sleep just fine. After that I will turn it on low and keep it running 24/7.

This is a REAL air purifier and after being on for a couple of hours, the dangerous levels of formaldehyde in my bedroom have already fallen to a safe level. For once I can look forward to sleeping peacefully in a non-toxic environment!

I bought this product new from a competitor at a much better price. So the "Verified Amazon Purchase" doesn't apply. Nevertheless, once I heard the Austin Air for myself, I felt compelled to write this review. The reports of loudness are GREATLY exaggerated.

title: Very good machine!
text:
We live on a VERY dusty gravel road. We couldn't figure out where all the dust came from inside our house for awhile after we moved here. We also noticed we woke up with uncomfortable stuffy noses almost every day. Once we realized the white, powdery dust on every surface was from the road, we knew we needed better air quality fast!
We ordered this machine and it was delivered promptly. The set up was SUPER simple and soon it was busy cleaning our air. Before turning it on for the 1st time, I dusted all our furniture and glass surfaces ... One week into usage, and I still have not needed to dust again (it was a daily or every-other-day necessity before the purifier was added)! Not to say there is ZERO dust on the furniture; but it is a small amount and nothing like it was without the machine.
We have also noticed cooking smells are eliminated in just a few of minutes. We keep our unit on "Auto" so it senses the cooking odors, runs on medium or high until they are removed from the air, then returns to it's normal "low" operation. Our dogs sometimes run into the house smelling like sweaty dogs, and this purifier takes care of that in seconds!
An added bonus is this filtering system seems to have removed allergens inside our home to the level where my husband's very sensitive allergies are not triggered! That's amazing to us! He uses much less allergy medicine now, and basically has to go outside to trigger an allergic reaction!
As far as "noise" - we don't notice the very quiet, soothing hum of the unit unless it is filtering out sudden, dirty air - like when I cook hamburgers inside. You will notice the fan whirs moderately loudly while it cycles the offending air, then it returns to whisper-soft operation. (We keep the unit set on "Auto", so we don't have to manually control the fans/purification. It senses the air isn't clean and "power cleans" until the levels are back in the cleanest level.
We are amazed by this machine and the almost immediate difference it has made in our home. Our air smells fresh and clean and feels "softer" - that's the only way to explain it. This machine is a substantial investment, so we hope knowing our experience helps you decide if it is what you need. We were so impressed, we bought the smaller unit for our bedroom and have had the same experience with it - but never even hear that fan at all, even when in "high filtering" mode (to be fair, it is about 1/3 the size of the large unit). Also, the "sleep" mode keeps it quiet while you sleep and there is a light control button to turn off the lights on the display when you sleep. We don't even notice it is in our bedroom and we wake up with MUCH less sinus congestion! Recommend highly and would not hesitate to buy again.

title: Decent filtration with convenient automatic speed control
text:
This air purifier offers a solid combination of features and performance. Its modern styling fits into most decors and is a nice change from the boxy look of many other purifiers. The touch-sensitive controls work well, and the child lock is a useful bonus that many competing units lack. However, this purifier doesn't remember its settings if it loses power, so you'll need to turn it back on manually after a power outage, and it can't be controlled by an AC outlet timer or smart plug.

From a filtration standpoint, the H13 HEPA filter does a great job with reducing airborne particles, but this isn't the most effective purifier I've used in terms of odor reduction. This one has small charcoal pellets in its filter panel, but I've generally experienced better odor control from purifiers that pass air through a sponge-like charcoal layer.

One of the best features of this purifier is its air quality sensor and automatic fan speed control. I keep this unit near the kitchen, and it's great to have the purifier ramp itself up when needed. It's not perfect, however, as the sensor doesn't include any hysteresis, so the fan speeds up and slows down repeatedly when air quality hovers around one of the thresholds. The up/down speed changes are more distracting than if the fan just stayed at a higher speed for a longer period of time.

Overall, I’m pleased with this air purifier. It runs quietly at the lowest of its three fan speeds, and the air quality sensor generally does a good job of increasing air flow as needed. For a medium to large sized room, this purifier gets the air clean of particles, but others can do a better job of making it smell fresh. Four stars.

title: A good air filter with some good esthetics at a premium price
text:
As a comparison, we have used air filters in this size/capacity from Coway, Winix, and Honeywell.

Pros:
1. Nice design. This tower definitely looks better than the Honewell-utilitarian aesthetic. I would say that it is on par with the Winix machine, which has a brushed metal look.
2. Filter design. The fit of the HEPA filter is quite snug, which gives one confidence that unfiltered air is not finding a channel around the filter as on some other units.
3. Air flow. This unit moves a ton of air on its high setting.
4. Pressing the power button once turns the LED indicators off so that they do not light up a dark room. A great feature to help it blend into the home.

Cons:
1. Size. This unit is quite large compared to, say, the Coway, which is arguably my favorite of the ones we have tried. We're talking nearly twice the size, though it does occupy less depth if that dimension is important in your location.
2. Noise. As with all of these units, on its high and highest settings, the Alen makes a lot of noise and will need to be adjusted for certain applications (watching television, having conversations, et cetera).
3. No automatic mode. Both the Coway and the Winix have automatic modes that allow them to adjust their own speed depending upon what it determines the air quality is.
4. The front plate (which is interchangeable) is made of a plastic that is a magnet for pet hair, which is particularly unfortunate because the unit will literally draw pet hair towards itself. I have to frequently vacuum the front plate to eliminate this problem.
5. Expensive. This unit has some great features, but you pay quite a premium for those features.

title: Bought 3. My thoughts - bright LEDs - Cleaner Air
text:
***UPDATE*** - So I returned one of these and may return another but keep one. I'm not super happy that the device goes blue right away which signifies good air quality. My nose is clogged from waking up and my pup still sneezes. We washed blankets and sheets to get rid of any dust mite remains but well...maybe we need more time with the device. I can say that working out in my gym room this time of year is tough and while I had this on full blast and still wanted to quit, I made it thru my hour. I've quit workouts 30mins in like "Nope, can't breathe, I'm done". Here I could breathe, struggling, but could breathe. So it was a crappy workout that I pushed myself thru but before this device - I couldn't and would just stop halfway in. For that reason, I'd keep one constantly on full blast in that room just cause I really don't believe the sensor but then again I got to do a full workout.

It's far from perfect for sleeping at night, but just may do the trick for stuffy home gyms and cardio workouts :)

I made the plunge of buying 3 and after reviewing different products I took the plunge on this one because it was under $1K to get three products.

Opening the box. Packed really well. They use styrofoam which is difficult to recycle. The unpacking was easy. I opened the product to take the plastic off the filters. All HEPA filters were not sealed. The company must run the units through tests. I think they should provide sealed filters but ok. Not that big of a deal. I turned the unit on following the directions and set the product up to clean.

I was very surprised to see the unit go from red to blue within an hour. Maybe I need to clean the sensor. This happened on all 3 units. I have one unit in the bedroom, one in my gym room and one in the living area.

Pros
Price - one of the least cost for 1,000sqff
Weight - very light. Can move easily
Style - I like it. Very modern and color blends well too
Performance - I can tell the difference in air quality. Let's see if it holds up well

Cons
Customer Service - No offer to replace filters. Send these new - it's an expensive product. We can have everything new

LED lights - pretty bright. I'll have to see if there is a way to dim those down

Sensor - I don't like that the sensor went from red to blue in an hour. The bedroom is great but my true test was in my gym room doing cardio. I could tell the difference but there was still air pollutants that blocked my breathing. Will continue to review over the next week. That unit may go back, we'll see. I want my gym room clear so that I can get my maximum cardio workout.

Dumb - Alexa won't talk to dumb devices. If they can add smart capabilities to this it would be a cool add on as other companies are doing this.

No Remote - ok so not smart is one thing but to control you need to be at the machine. I think the remote capability is fairly inexpensive and should be looked into

Overall - so I can't speak for other products but my guess is this should compete well and does the job effectively. I'm only 24 hours into this and will report sleep patterns and if cardio workouts improve. If I don't see an improvement in cardio I may swap one of the devices out with a competitor to compare effectiveness

title: Can't recommend
text:
I had gotten this to place in my small office. I have a much larger unit in the main living area but as my office is pretty separate I felt a unit there would be useful. Overall this unit is small and unobtrusive. The fan on high is pretty loud but on low, it is not too noticeable. As to why I can't recommend it, read on.

First, the manufacturer provides little information about the capability of this purifier. There is nothing noting what size room it is suitable for. Nor is there any information about how many CFM the unit puts out. The only helpful information is buried in the small manual under the specifications. There it is noted that this unit has a CADR (Clean Air Delivery Rate) of 95-120m. This is a pretty wide range for a CADR, it is usually a single number listed for each particle type (smoke, pollen, dust). The CADR rating for this unit does suggest that it is suitable for a small room. It should work in a room up to 10*15, perhaps a bit larger.

The bigger issue is regarding the filter. The unit uses a round filter cartridge but the manufacturer gives no information on replacement filters. The manual states that to clean the filter you should brush it and then place it in the sun (ok). Then the manual states the filter needs to be periodically replaced. It does not give any indication of when this should happen. Supposedly the unit has a reminder light that comes on when it needs changing. The problem is, nowhere does it say what the replacement filter is or where to get one. The only notation about the filter is that it is an h13 HEPA filter. H13 is the type of HEPA filter but tells nothing about the filter size. The only way I can think of to find a replacement would be to measure the height and diameter of the filter and then review all available round filters to try and find a match. Even on the manufacturer's Amazon page, there is no information about replacement filters (nor is there any mention of this particular unit). Filters typically last 3-6 months. After that, this unit becomes a paperweight.

In terms of using it for any aromatherapy, there is no pad or sponge to put your oil on. There is only a small indentation in the plastic top case that, I guess, is to hold the essential oil.

If the manufacturer added information about replacement filters I could see this unit being a decent choice for a small room. Without that information, there are better choices that will give you the information you need for long-term use.

The Back Story: We live on a farm with 3 dogs, horses, goats etc and have had major fires in 2014 & 2015 and are living in the burn scare of the 2 largest fires to hit the state. The ash is everywhere, the wind will kick it up and the air is filled with a haze of blowing ash, it gets into everything, it is a very very fine ash. We have extreme dust/ash conditions!!! Before we bought the BreathSmart we were dusting and wiping down counter tops every morning and evening during windy conditions, every day during non-windy conditions. Now we do it every 8 to 10 days depending on how windy it is, and I don't have to wipe the TV every time I want to watch it. House is 3500 sq ft, the unit is located in the living room, (main floor) we do have to dust the bathroom and bedroom more often than the living room, dining room, and kitchen, but not every day or every-other-day as we were doing before. I have had no problem with the unit, contact with customer service was outstanding (info on what would be the best filter for our condition). title: It works exactly as described
text:
I saw a few reviews from people who seemed confused, who insisted these do nothing. I thought I'd buy them and see what was up.

Firstly, I'm in the medical field. I knew of ion generation as a antiseptic technique. It has been used to take out tuberculosis, salmonella, and others.

Here are the highlights in FAQ:

1. Do they produce ozone?
a. Technically, yes. When you create negative ions, you also create a electrostatic field. When this field discharges, it creates ozone. Have you ever lifted a wool blanket and watched the static shocks? Do you remember the smell? That is ozone. These produce less ozone than your wool blanket.

2. Do they disinfect?
a. A little. Negative ions are wrestlers. They can pin down particles and vapors that might carry airborne disease. They don't KILL the germs, at least, not as well as ozone. But the certainly can keep them out of the air.

3. Do they work? How do you know?
a. I know they are producing ions because they have an electrical potential across the carbon fiber brushes. My voltmeter read 8.5v on DC, and 16 on AC. Of the four brushes, two are anodes and two are cathodes. You can short out the device with a conductor across one anode and one cathode.

Each one can provide coverage for 300 ft^2. Keep that in mind.

They have a soft green light the pulses slowly. It doesn't work well as a nightlight. I purchased 6 units and noticed a difference in air quality within 4 hour or so with 1400 ft^2.

title: Unsafe Product
text:
I was operating this product in a small bathroom at it's lowest setting. My eyes were burning and watering. I Googled "ozone toxicity", found this Environmental Protection Agency report: [...]

EPA Report Conclusions:
Whether in its pure form or mixed with other chemicals, ozone can be harmful to health.
When inhaled, ozone can damage the lungs. Relatively low amounts of ozone can cause chest pain, coughing, shortness of breath and, throat irritation. It may also worsen chronic respiratory diseases such as asthma as well as compromise the ability of the body to fight respiratory infections.
Some studies show that ozone concentrations produced by ozone generators can exceed health standards even when one follows manufacturer’s instructions.
Many factors affect ozone concentrations including the amount of ozone produced by the machine(s), the size of the indoor space, the amount of material in the room with which ozone reacts, the outdoor ozone concentration, and the amount of ventilation. These factors make it difficult to control the ozone concentration in all circumstances.
Available scientific evidence shows that, at concentrations that do not exceed public health standards, ozone is generally ineffective in controlling indoor air pollution.
The concentration of ozone would have to greatly exceed health standards to be effective in removing most indoor air contaminants. In the process of reacting with chemicals indoors, ozone can produce other chemicals that themselves can be irritating and corrosive.
Top of page
Recommendation
The public is advised to use proven methods of controlling indoor air pollution. These methods include eliminating or controlling pollutant sources, increasing outdoor air ventilation, and using proven methods of air cleaning.

title: Even Helps Multiple Chemical Sensitivity Sufferers
text:
I love this air purifier! It’s the best thing that I’ve purchased in a long time. It only takes up the space of a travel mug; therefore it fits into the cup holder of my car. It’s small enough to fit in my purse next to my stainless steel water bottle. I take it everywhere! I try to look cool when I hold it, as if I’m sporting a chic travel mug (Especially since I don’t drink coffee.)

How I use my Wynd. Whenever I go anywhere in public, I pull it out of my purse and turn it on. Depending on the surrounding noise, I turn it up as loud as it can go without being annoying. I’d say it ranges from a soft purr to as loud as a hair dryer. But the soft purr—the lowest setting—is strong enough when aimed directly at my face, about a foot away, to give me the fresh air I need. I use the Wynd to direct fresh air at my face or to aim bad smells away from me.

I have multiple chemical sensitivities. While some scent particles are too small to be filtered by the Wynd (therefore they do go right through the filter), I can use the Wynd to blow them away from me. I have noticed that when I come across smells that make me sick (flulike symptoms and all), having fresh air blown into my face helps immensely. Sometimes I will discreetly aim my Wynd at the offending person to blow the scent away from me and back at them.

One of my lesser symptoms includes a horrifically itchy nose. This usually occurs from people wearing clothes soaked in fabric softener or by being around people who are pet owners. As soon as my nose starts up, I hold Wynd right under my nose, and in a little as a few seconds, my nose stops itching. (Wynd works great for pollen and dander.)

I’ve even taken Wynd to the theater. And thank heavens I did. The poor soul next to me was coughing the whole time (the horror!). I balanced my Wynd on my lap, using my coat and scarf to support it and aimed fresh air right at my face the whole movie. I didn’t end up sick.

I’ve had an occasion to run my Wynd after burning something in my oven. Smoke stunk up the house. The burnt smell was awful. I ran Wynd in my personal space while I worked, and it did a great job at filtering the smell.

Other than being an air purifier, it has other redeeming qualities. It’s a great portable fan for hot days. Perfect for menopausal women who get hot flashes. Sweaty pits? No problem. Aim Wynd Essential where the moisture is gathering, and you’ll be dry in no time. The ring of light at the top, which can be turned off, makes an impromptu flashlight or a light to hold under your chin when telling scary stories. And often I use my Wynd as a pretend microphone, to sing obnoxiously and embarrass my children.

Several of my friends have asked about my Wynd, wondering if it is an Alexa. That’s how cool it looks with its glowing ring at the top and sleek cordless design. So I named mine Lexa. My kids groan every time I ask them to bring me Lexa.

Cons. The stand to tilt my Wynd broke in about a month. It’s a cheap plastic bit. I don’t miss it. The on/off button sometimes gets hit by accident. (It’s in a place where I tend to hold my Wynd.)

Otherwise—The Wynd is easy to use! Love it!

title: It doesn't filter the air at all
text:
The pictures I attached show the following: my screen capture of the actual unhealthy air. As you can see, it is at 140, so in the unhealthy. This is outdoors, so I decided to test the HATHASPACE Smart True HEPA Air Purifier for Home to see if it will capture this dirty air. Inside the house, it shows always green, and so it's impossible to tell if it detects anything.

Upon taking the unit out, a waited several minutes to see if it will change to anything other than what it showed indoors, after all, it is now in a very unhealthy air. I expected it to turn color and start to filter strongly but nothing happened.

I also have a particle counter air quality checker at home and so on the next picture I took that also out into the bad air to see if it would capture the air quality. It sure did! Immediately! On my balcony it captured air quality at 122, which is hazardous. Note that the HATHASPACE Smart True HEPA Air Purifier for Home didn't change and remained green all along.

I left both outdoors for a few more minutes, giving the benefit of the doubt to the HATHASPACE Smart True HEPA Air Purifier for Home but nope, it never changed! It clearly doesn't work at all.

Too bad because it is lovely for looks and the ease of placing the filters in and it is also quiet and not bright, so easy going at night. However, it doesn't work so this baby is going to travel back to the warehouse where it came from.

title: Price isn't justifiable
text:
I realize that there are benefits to this fan that cannot be found in other fans. Bladelessness means less dust getting thrown at my face; filter means less dust being thrown at my face. But a fan still kicks up dust, so it's not like my allergies are magically relieved.

And for $400? I just don't understand. A separate fan and air purifier wouldn't cost that much. And while there aren't many bladeless fans available, the ones that are undercut the price by 200$.

If this were a quiet fan, maybe I'd be more impressed. But it's not any quieter than my regular tower fan. And since I have A/C, I tend to use this fan with the windows open. Which means the filter is working harder, (though that's only an issue until the summer temperatures hit us.)

And let's talk about the design for a second: you are not supposed to move the fan by lifting it from the top. You have to pick it up from the base. But the natural inclination is to grab the top. I can train myself out of this.
In the end, I'm stuck on the price. I get it. It's a new kind of fan with a purifier. It's not going to be priced for the masses.

text: I'm a clean freak. Wrong! Sure they collect dust on their metal plates but those small surfaces don't compare to the dust that still collects on my dresser, tables, floors and everywhere else. You would need 1 Ionic Breeze per Square foot in your house to ever see a measurable reduction in surface dust. title: Produces ozone, bad for lungs. Clean, dry 6 to 24 hours every few weeks. Filtration much worse than "true HEPA" air purifiers.
text:
Oreck XL Professional is not recommended, not rated by Consumer Reports magazine.

The removable assembly of metal plates and wires is called "Truman Cell". The cell has wires to ionize the air particles which are then captured by electrically charged metal plates.

Problems with the Truman Cell :

(1) Cell produces ozone, which is converted to oxygen by the non-removable zeolite panel after it. This panel gets clogged with dust after 6 months and stops converting. Vacuuming does little good.
Ozone increases in concentration inside your house, damages your lungs and can cause lung cancer. Ozone is an air pollutant and health hazard reported daily by the weather service.

Search on the internet about ozone generators. The instructions will tell you to "close off and vacate" the area to be treated. "Make sure the unit has been turned off for about an hour" before reoccupying the space. That is, people or pets should not be in areas with much ozone.

(2) Cell "must" be washed with cleaner and water every 2 to 3 weeks or whenever the red light comes on or when "annoying" sparking occurs. A dirty cell lets the dirty air pass through it with little filtration.

(3) Cell must be "completely dried" after cleaning, for 6 to 24 hours, depending on humidity, otherwise the air purifier will not start.

(4) Cell captures a higher percentage of particles at lowest fan speed than at high speed.

(5) Percentage of particles captured by Cell varies from 0% to 80% depending on how clean the Truman cell is. A "true" HEPA filter captures 99.97% of particles 0.3 micron or bigger, even when dirty.

Get you a "true" HEPA air purifier made by IQair, Whirlpool, Honeywell etc. No cleaning every few weeks. No drying for 6 to 24-hours. No downtime. No lung-damaging ozone.

Please click "Yes" if this review is helpful to you. It takes time to research these information.

title: Comparison of Hathaspace with Wagner WA888 - winner: Hathaspace
text:
Bought two air purifiers from two companies for comparison: Wagner WA888 and Hathaspace. The winner was Hathaspace, which is explained below.

Wagner WA888 features that makes it distinguished:
- touch screen operation
- 2 remotes instead of one
- air particulate matter count values on panel
- temperature display
- filter change reminder in display board
- comes with medical grade hepa 0.1 micron
- stronger fan, but is also noisier even at lowest setting

Cons:
- plug comes out of the right side and not the back of the unit, not the best place to put it
- fan at lowest mode is louder than my refrigerator
- plastic case is thin and feels fragile
- plastic clips to hold the front panel to protect filter will wear out quickly because they are not magnets or something better
- where the power line comes out it is in the seam of two plastic cases. When filter is replaced, when putting the front case back the rubber gasket of the line will get in the way of creating a closed case.

Wagner comes with:
Warranty: 3 years
Filter cost: $37
Unit cost: $180

Hathaspace features that makes it distinguished:
- quality magnets are used to latch the front case filter protection panel
- quieter filter fan operation
- sleep mode turns all panel lights completely off, good for keeping bedroom dark
- thicker plastic and stronger case, feels premium and looks good
- 5 year warranty if one joins Hathaspace filter club which delivers a new filter to home every 4 months (currently $31.49 per filter free shipping). 4 years warranty if one registers unit on the website. 2 years with no registration.
- standard hepa filters are less expensive
- website sells medical grade filters but at a slightly higher price, $38.69

Cons:
- medical grade filters are available in Hathaspace website at a higher price, $38.69
- fan is smaller and is only for a space of 350 sqft or less
- no filter change reminder in the unit

Hathaspace comes with:
Warranty: 2 to 5 years
Filter cost: certified standard hepa filters $35 or $31.49 if one joins filter club
Unit cost: $165

My pick: Hathaspace air purifier. I am able to sleep with it in my bedroom, almost no noise. The Wagner is still too noisy during sleep mode, louder than my LG refrigerator. Hathaspace is the winner.

In my neck of the woods we are covered in thick blanket of brown haze of smoke and to make matters worse a field is on fire down the street from us.
If you zoom in on the picture one can kinda see the haze but it's better noticed by naked eye.
We live in an open two story home with 35' ceilings in an open loft type lay out. I set the unit up in the middle of the room.
Upon plugging it in the air quality sensor turned red and within SEVEN minutes it went to yellow then green. It obviously smells of smoke inside my house and I don't understand how it can so quickly call it good in such short time.
I decided to put it upstairs in our bedroom and same results. Seven minutes and it's good.
Scratching my head.
Is this on a timer to fool you or is it just not detecting the smoke in the home. I have small expectations so I'll leave this on in our bedroom for several hours on medium to see if it helps with the air quality in there.
I'll be back with a further update in couple days after I hear back from the mfg on why it's calling the air good so quickly.

title: Quieter & cheaper than the Honeywell of similar size.
text:
No motor noise, whining, whirring, or vibration at all. Just the sound of rushing air. On high, it's a lot of air rushing though (white noise). On the mid & low speed it's almost silent. The filter it ships with it slightly smaller & less robust than the one shipped with the similar sized Honeywell model. But other types of filters also fit this unit. Works better than expected for a unit this size & price. If you're handy, you can cut the front off the plastic housing that holds the replaceable filter (on either unit) so you can buy, cut, & install heating, & AC filters or other cheaper filters in the units.

To extend the use of the filter, just tape a piece of toilet paper over the disposable filter. It will act as an additional fine particle pre-filter. Just tape it on each corner & a small piece in the middle at the edge. No need to tape around the whole thing. The suction of the unit will hold the rest in place just fine. Use the cheap or generic single ply thin toilet paper. The heavier stuff & paper towels will block too much air flow. You can test the paper by putting a piece over your mouth & see if some air can be sucked or blown through it. The will be some restriction, that's how fine particle filters work, but not too much air restriction.

When air flow gets weaker over time or the paper turns brown, it's time to replace the toilet paper. In my house, about 2-4 weeks. You don't want the paper to get too clogged. It will reduce too much air flow, & it may suck a hole through the paper due to too much suction on the paper when it gets clogged.

I bought both the Honeywell & this unit because I needed 2, so if one wasn't good enough, the other might be. If I had it to do over, I would have just bought 2 of these. The Honeywell is way too noisy, & also vibrates a lot at all 3 speeds, but doesn't seem to blow any more air. It's not air flow noise either... the more air a unit handles, the more air noise you'll get. But the Honeywell has a whirring whine noise. Turning down the unit only lowers the pitch or the whine & frequency of the vibration, but doesn't reduce the noise at all. The whine is extremely annoying at any spped, & can be easily heard even from another room of 2 away.

title: A mediocre product, at best.
text:
DISCLOSURE: This product was bought under another account, of which I live with that account holder. This review beholds my opinion, and none of which should be taken as scientific evidence (from a research firm).

Abstract: We bought this in the beginning of 2021, in hopes that it would greatly reduce the following in the living/dining room:

- The chances of transmitting the SARS-CoV-2 virus, known to cause COVID-19
- To reduce the prevalence of pet dander, dead skin cells and other dust particulates, therefore reducing the need to vacuum a fully carpeted area
- To control other VOCs (Volatile Organic Compounds) and odours
- Explore different brand names that are not native to our country (United States)
- Overall satisfaction and durability of the product

The price as of the time was roughly $130 - $160, with included discounts on Amazon.

Results: While we haven’t been able to verify *if* this was able to slow or stop the transmission of any viruses in particular, we also aren’t confidently certain *if* it made any significant improvement over the following *several months* since we bought this product. However, observing the filter appears that it has been doing its job, but we haven’t noticed any observable difference in controlling odours—if there were any, at all. However, this product shows quite a plethora of issues that were not only mere oversights, but they were also egregiously condoned to be the norm as per the company’s (azeus’ or Azeus’) standards.

Details: First and foremost, we contacted their customer support after attempting to establish a warranty with them, which the product came with a pamphlet that claimed you can either get a free replacement filter (valued at $30 at least), or get a meagre $10 Amazon gift card. After uploading the screenshots as per their request, we opted for the free replacement filter. They, much to *our* surprise, *did not have any available on their end*. After some back-and-forth, we were left with no other option other than to allow them to give us a tiny return investment of $10 towards our Amazon gift card balance. We gave them the benefit of the doubt, since the supply chain during that time was severely affected, making availability on a *number* of products very scarce. How *that* came to pass was *also* just as peculiar: while I don’t know any intricacies involved, they ended up generating a gift card key/code at first, but the first one they gave turned out to be invalid or had already been used. So then they gave us another moments later, which that seemed to work. I don’t know if it took two or three attempts total to give us a working Amazon gift card code, but the way they went about it raised red flags to be quite honest: I thought all of this was purely shady business practises going on here. (I also want to note that I think they had an issue with us purchasing from an “unauthorised reseller” on Amazon, even though they were the *only choice on Amazon when we bought this air purifier*, which I think they used that as a reason to not honour either the warranty itself, or apply the warranty. Do not quote me on this one.)

Taking a look at their main website, it is an exceptionally sterile, web-only business website with no known physical location able to be found from the naked eye. Not a whole lot is given in the way of showing any modicum of legitimacy towards the average consumer. Perhaps it is a *new* way of starting up a business? But to not give *any* address besides an e-mail address, whatsoever, makes things feels either completely unfamiliar, or utterly suspicious. Every business we’ve dealt with so far already *has* an established address available for the public. And given the way the customer support speaks, they appear to be somewhere overseas. Not only that, but these icons they use to represent themselves appear more or less as if they used a stock photo that you could normally find on Google Images. That, or it coincidentally is also a professional shot for a business. It’s honestly unnerving, considering almost every business I came in contact with for a web chat practically had *nothing* like that.

Now back to the product, itself.

When we bought this, it was (at the time of purchase) rated to purify up to 560 sq. ft. to my recollection; we have a 500 sq. ft. combined living and dining room. But about 2 – 5 months later, the manufacturer seemingly updated their product page, *now claiming* to purify up to 1,080 sq. ft. rooms. This is seemingly more than *double* in comparison to the initial rating. Yet, we have no idea *how* they managed to make a relatively tiny device pull off that much. I think that’s *really suspicious*, to be frank. Also, it's worth mentioning that the original product page that we bought this air purifier from is no longer available, which is why I am reviewing it on this product's page.

When I examine the instruction manual, the fluency of English is at an acceptable state, noting some minor misspellings that most English-speakers would easily pick up, while there are some other unfamiliar phrasings used that is not widely accepted in the English language; again, this denotes that Azeus is *clearly* an overseas company that many can assume they are either from China, or somewhere within the “Middle East” (e.g. India). However, not *all* companies that use semi-fluent English originate *just* from these countries, either; other central European companies, such as “be quiet!” tends to not have the correct translation or phrasing of words translated from German to English at a similar rate. Though, the main issue tends to rear its ugly face, such as the feature of using the “ioniser”, which there is no real indication whether it is actually being used, and the UV bulb included in the product, which there is no indicator that it is—in fact—on, when you press the “UV” button. Interestingly enough, there is *no* button on the device for the UV bulb, either; it’s only unique to the remote. This is quite the massive oversight, indeed.

However, every time we turn it on without changing the fan speed, it operated in a rather foreign fashion where I had not expected an air purifier of *any* calibre to do what was known later a preset cycle that *always* occurs every time it is turned on. I’m not particularly impressed with the inanely loud noise the turbine fan produces when it is at its highest; I find this embarrassingly unbearable and it makes conversations more likely to be hard to follow, and it can be difficult for people to focus in mere silence. Therefore, as time went on, the fan speed is *always* set to medium. The featured, yet overly simplified air quality indicator is semi-consistent, where you may not always be certain if it is truly accurate. We have no idea how they managed to make it “sometimes” detect bacteria and viruses, yet consistently detect odours and fine particulates/dust, and frankly it would be very resourceful if consumers had access to that level of information.

When we used it for several months in total, we had not seen based on the instruction manual a “replace filter indicator” go off. In fact, the only thing that started to literally go off is the ioniser light, followed by the light for the selected fan speed on the device. This gives me even *far less confidence in this product* than they tried to let on, making me feel that, as my hunch dictated earlier, this was made to only be tossed out in the landfill after it met its very short-term use.

I also want to make one thing very clear: having a convectional air purifier, on paper, is a great concept. However, the intake on both sides of the product (on the smaller edges of this oval-shaped air purifier) *clearly* shows just how restrictive the overall air flow is. It is a neat concept that allows it to stay comfortably snug in very compact environments; it does *not*, however, make a very effective air purifier by not fully utilising the full surface area of the composite filter when it comes to pulling the “dirty air” in thru its intake vents. Ideally, it’s a great idea to have air go thru as little resistance as possible in order to make *any* fan-driven device extremely effective at its intended purpose. The fact that this is making air go through the equivalent to two 90° angles, followed by a multi-layered (yet also very expensive: at least or more than $30 per piece as of this writing) filter makes people like me syncope from such a ridiculous design.

Another note: I do think that the sleep mode functions as designed, noting that all lights go off after a brief period of time and reduces the fan speed at the lowest possible, making it virtually imperceptible while in operation. That’s a good plus. But! I don’t like how the lights, themselves, are unbearably bright: a light dimmer function would have been nice to have.

Overall impressions: They are generally **low**. I’m very uncertain on purchasing a new filter for this product, and I’m concerned that they are intentionally ripping their customers a new one. I have a higher probability of trying to find options provided by manufacturers such as Honeywell (brand owned by Kaz USA, Inc.) and GermGuardian (their entity, Guardian Technologies, is now acquired by Lasko, LLC as of January 2021: *also* an American manufacturer long known for their budget-oriented fans with high marks), which are well-known, well-established brands in the United States.

– End of review. Written on 30 November 2021, 1732 local time. –

title: Worked wonders for me; it may for you
text:
A cold laid me low; I was sneezing, wheezing, miserable. My son bought this from COSTCO, plugged it in, switched on the UV option and almost instant relief. This handles a 20 x 15 ft bedroom well, and has been cooling as well as clearing the air. It is easily moved by a convenient on-the-top handle. Three options for the fan strength (high, middle, low); UV on or off; lights out option for night. About 2 1/2 ft tall, 8 inches diameter column, not obtrusive at all.

With regard to noise, my house is carpeted, and this is positioned about 3 ft from my bed. It is quieter than my overhead fan on low and medium levels; about the same at high levels. Since the hum is steady, for me it is soothing. As an unexpected bonus, this cleans the air so thoroughly that this room is now totally dust-free. I expected pathogens would pack their bags and leave---I am sure happy about the absence of dust. Effectiveness might vary depending on atmospheric dustiness and allergens as well as individual needs. For me, it has been handling volcanic vog which is pretty wicked stuff to breathe.

Any alerts? Buyers should be aware this unit needs to be about 2 to 3 feet from walls for good intake airflow. Also, it probably would be better to put it on wood or tile than on carpet, although the carpet may help keep the fan hum so quiet. The color is black with a silver top, which fits my bedroom, Some buyers may want white or a more colorful case but I don't know if this is available. Cleaning has been easy by following the clear directions step by step. No special skills needed, as far as I can tell.

Overall: I am totally pleased and happy to report since it arrived about six months ago, no sneezes at all! An excellent value and worth every penny of the price, for me.

title: Perfect for travel
text:
Overall this is a great air purifier. I travel for work and spend a lot of time in hotel rooms. You never know who has been in that hotel room before you and even though it may look nice, that hotel may be an older hotel. I always end up with a stuffy nose and scratchy throat after spending a week in hotel rooms. Wynd has solved that problem.

Wynd is quiet at the low setting, yet creates the perfect white noise at higher settings. I love that there’s not just 2 or 3 settings. You turn the top of the purifier to get at least 15 different settings. There is a night light, but you can turn it off, unlike almost all the other purifiers in this category.

Most importantly, it works. I have used it for 2 weeks now in different hotel rooms and I always wake up refreshed and feeling great. The filter is easy to change and they are not very expensive. Once you download the Wynd app, you can connect to your purifier via Bluetooth and you can control your purifier and check filter life.

Yes it is on the expensive side, but there’s no other purifier in this category that comes close to the size, features and how well Wynd works. Last thing to be tested is durability as I have only had this 3 weeks. It seems to be made really well so I’m looking forward to using it for a long time.

text:
[[VIDEOID:71405ffa1a5183ac2ecd26e5f8787f51]] While planning my trip to India, I learned that the air pollution is off the charts, with the AQI in the Hazardous range quite frequently.
I frantically did some research to find how I could protect myself. In addition to buying some fabric masks to wear while walking around outside, I was also looking for something that would not take up too much precious room in my luggage that could filter the air in the room I was staying in. The Wynd Air purifier seemed to be the best bet without having to pack a large air purifier separately in it's own luggage case. When arriving at the international airport in New Delhi, I instantly knew that I would need to use any air protection I could get my hands on after taking my first breath of air. Average AQI readings (as read on the app) were hovering around 250 - 300, which is in the "very unhealthy" range, and it occasionally went up to the "hazardous" range a few times - yipes!
When I first got to the hostel, I set up the air filter on the night stand and plugged it in via the adapter. The air inside continuously smelled of the sooty air pollution inside, but I believe that the Wynd air purifier helped a bit, and at that time, I would take any quick steps to clean the air. Not surprisingly, after 3 days, I removed the air filter inside of the purifier and found that the filter was pretty dirty - after only 3 days! (see my video) I kept the air filter next to my bed, so at least that area near me could be filtered somewhat. I'm not sure of the science behind that, but I believe it helped.
My next trips were to Dehradun, and Rishikesh India, and although the pollution is down a level from Delhi, it's still up there in the 100 - 150 range on the air quality index, so I continually used the air purifier in those areas also.
Would I use this solely at home to purify my bedroom air? Nah, I would invest in a larger air purifier that a larger air filtration capacity in addition to containing a heap filter, and, a UV treatment element to the air.
