text:
I received the Flex air purifier a little under two weeks ago, and am very pleased with how it has made such a noticeable difference in the quality of the air in my master bedroom. I have since purchased and received the 75i model and am just as pleased with it.

I don't have a lot of experience with air purifiers, but here's what I can tell you. The Flex model is louder than the 75i model, which I can barely (have to try) hear. It is a more basic model without all the bells and whistles of the 75i model. It looks the same, only a little smaller. Both have a sleek, clean, and aerodynamic look about them. They fit against the wall and take up very little floor space as a canister model would take up. I noticed a difference in the air quality in my bedroom within 2 hours of running the Flex air purifier on high setting. I run it 24/7 on the highest fan speed. I am getting used to the loudness of the fan on the Flex. It's not any louder than the HVAC fan when it's running, but it is louder than the 75i model, and it is noticeable for a bedroom. I'm not sure I'd notice it in the kitchen, bathroom, or hallway. It's not keeping me awake, but I wish it was as quiet as the 75i.

It doesn't have the bells and whistles the 75i model has - no auto clean mode, no colored lights to tell you the quality of the air, and no ionizer, but is also under half the price of the 75i model and well worth every penny.

After nearly 2 weeks of constant 24/7 operation, the Flex model is well worth the investment, and I'm very pleased with it.

title: Surpassed my initial expectations by a lot, but concerns over warranty stipulations
text:
Edit: I posted my concern regarding the warranty, and the seller (Hathaspace) responded that the extended warranty went into effect with my purchase. Relieved and pleased about that, though I feel the seller could have made that more clear on their web site. Still very pleased with this product’s performance.

To be completely honest, this unit was my second choice. My wife and I have been experiencing some respiratory issues, and we suspected the large amount of dust we've noticed in our home had something to do with it. After seeing how effective a much higher-priced brand worked at my daughter's home (they have two cats and an toddler, so "litterboxes" for felines and humans are present), we decided that we also needed an air purifier in our home. I wasn't willing to pay THAT much, though, so 'settled' for this Hathaspace 2.0 unit. I guess 'settled' is a bit tongue-in-cheek now, though, because I've been THOROUGHLY impressed by this device.

Unboxing and preparing the unit for use was beyond easy. The control panel is big, bright, and VERY easy to understand and use. Even at it's highest speed, the device is VERY quiet.

On first use, the device took about a minute to gauge the air quality around it. During this time, the LED strip on the front was blue. Because I'd set the device on the 'auto' mode, it set itself at the HIGH setting and ran at that speed for approximately an hour. After that, though, we noticed the light strip changed to green, and the fan speed began to reduce itself.

It's quite sensitive to changes in the air quality; we initially set it up about 15 feet from our front door, and we noted that each time the door was opened the AQI meter would go down and the unit began revving up, only reducing the fan speed once the AQI meter had gone up sufficiently.

It's fantastic at removing odors as well; my wife is Filipina, and cooks some amazing food, but also uses some ingredients that - while very delicious - emit some atrocious odors not found in a typical American kitchen. Fish sauce, for example, is made from fermented salted anchovies. It's a delicious, flavorful condiment, but it smells to high heaven. Under normal circumstances, the lingering odor of cooking with this condiment is evident for several days afterwards, but with this air purifier in place, the lingering odor was barely noticeable after a couple of hours, and simply not present the next day. While I never complained about the lingering odor, that fact that this device could remove it so effectively was pretty huge (but PLEASE don't tell my wife!!).

My only concern is with the warranty. The documentation that came with it showed a QR code that (it claimed) would direct me to a site where I could register my device and receive an extended 5-year warranty. Yet, when I arrived on that URL, I wasn't given an opportunity to register my purchase. Instead, I saw a notice that the manufactured would ONLY warrant the device if it was purchased from THEIR web site, and there was no way for me to register it. I was concerned that purchasing it on Amazon would disqualify me from any kind of warranty, even though the listed seller was Hathaspace. So, as of this writing, I have to assume that my air purifier is not registered, and unwarranted. This is literally the first appliance purchase I've made from Amazon where the manufacture has prevented me from registering my purchase for even the minimal warranty. This is a pretty big concern for me; I spent close to $300 USD for this device, and I'm not very happy I'm unable to register for warranty service. Hell, I can register my toaster; why can't I register my air purifier? That alone prevented me from rating this device at 5 stars. Its not a good customer experience when the manufactures tells you they won't guarantee their product unless you purchased it directly from their web site.

title: This purifier has made a huge difference in our house!
text:
**We've had this purifier for a year and half and it is still doing great! I don't change the filters as often as I should, although I do clean them every few months. I still highly recommend this machine!**

I have a 3000 sq ft house where the living room is open to the second floor. In the afternoons, I would see large and small dust particles and pet hair floating around in the beams of sunlight. With three pets and a big house that doesn't get dusted like it should, it was a lot! Within a few days, the dust was visibly reduced to just the smallest particles showing in the sunbeams, and the reduced collection of dust on surfaces proves it works. It really does detect smells and kick on. The review talking about her kids "testing" it? Yup. Some reviewers complained about it running on high for 15 mins when it first turns on and then saying the air was clean. Yes, it does that, but it's supposed to. I think it's looking for any big issues and testing the air. If the quality is passable it will then switch to low. It doesn't mean your air is completely clean. It just means there is no massive bad smells to clean at that moment. Trust me, if someone uses our guest bath (next to where the unit sits) or when I'm cooking something stinky, it kicks on until the smell is gone. title: Basic but effective
text:
*Updated on 4/13/2017
Oreck WK16000 Air Response Hepa Purifier is a basic, no frills filter that essentially does its job as advertised. Upon a thorough inspection of its exterior components, I could not find any sensors that would control its operation due to the amount of dust particles, aka DustSense. However, when set to AUTO, it does indeed "magically" notice the change in air quality and speeds up the blades for an increased air flow. I discovered this by accident, while treating my carpets the other day.

The operation controls of this air purifier offer an automatic sensor switch, 3 air flow/speed settings, a shut off timer, and also allow you to turn off the exterior LED lights. The latter feature is important if you plan to use this air purifier in your bedroom, since the bright blue LED lights can interfere with your sleep. The air purifier is generally quiet, and I expect any air purifier to emit a certain amount of hum due to the airflow. However, this Oreck, due to its design, also emits a notable whine which can be unbearable to some people. In fact, my wife has ended up removing it from our bedroom. You see, most air purifiers have a front (or back) grill through which the air travels. This Oreck is designed to intake air from side openings (see product photos). This is why, I suspect, it creates a bit of a whine. The whine is especially noticeable on speed 2 and speed 3 setting.

A few more brief observations:
1. The filters are easy remove.
2. The front panel is securely attached
3. The functionality, effectiveness, and the looks of this air filter are certainly above average.

I think that this Oreck is a very good, effective air purifier, although I think it has been priced out of the "basic" air purifier range, probably due to its household/staple brand name. A slight whine is something to be aware of as well. Otherwise, this is a very solid product worth considering.

** 1/28/2018 Update **
I have not called the manufacturer yet, but the unit just stopped working. The power sensor button is lit, but none of the controls are. I cannot reset the purifier in any way. Power-cycling the unit did not help. Replacing / cleaning the filters did not help either. I am puzzled.

title: Nice for a bedroom
text:
I am using this in a bedroom. I sleep on one side of a king-size bed (the dogs get the other side). The My Happi is on the nightstand by the other side of the bed. So it is about three to four feet away. I am running it on auto. I can't hear a thing. I do not use the night mode, I find no need. It is very very quiet. If I stand next to it and get real quiet I can faintly hear it.
The UV light is faint - you can see a very faint glow coming from inside - nothing that would disturb my sleep. The gauge on the front is well lit but it is not facing me. If I had it position so that I was staring right at it in bed, I may have to go into sleep mode to turn down the gauge.
So for a bedroom air purifier, it is great.

Now when I first plugged it in, the reading was on the edge of blue (good air quality) and white (great air quality) After a couple of days the reading showed it getting better and better. I have noticed if I open the window the air quality goes down. Makes sense, I am getting dust and pollen from outside. After the windows are closed for a bit, the air quality improves. I also have a cleaning lady and the quality went down after she cleaned. Again it makes sense, dusting and vacuuming kick up dust and dirt. Again in a very short period of time, the quality improved.

I do have some minor allergies and this seems to help. I do sleep better with it in my room. I was impressed with how well made it is and it was easy to set up and get running.

The only minor negative was trying to get info on replacement filters. I had to hunt a bit. They don't appear to sell them via Amazon. Their website was listed in the manual and I found that they do sell replacements there. I don't expect that I will need to replace them often. The manual says to every complete of months to remove the filter and wipe it down to remove the build-up and put it back in. They don't list a specific interval for replacing the filter as it will depend on usage.

Overall very pleased.

title: Superb air purifying performance with great design and quality
text: After an exhausting search for a high quality air purifier, I ended up purchasing the Brondell - and I am oh so glad I did. The purifier arrived in perfect condition and after unpacking, you first notice the high quality materials, including solid and smooth glossy plastics and aluminium on top where the controls are. This is superb design and craftsmanship! Remove plastic from filters, reinstall and off you go. I leave it on automatic and delight in watching the unit measure air quality and cycle through varying fan speeds (the unit is very quiet in its lowest setting, the highest setting is rather noticeable, but it is a pleasant "swwwoooosh" kind of sound; besides, the highest fan speed is only active for a few minutes in automatic mode. If air quality is great, the unit turns itself off). I absolutely love the visual color indication of air quality in the "cross" - you always know what the air quality is like in your room (and it can be turned off for bedroom use). The unit will exchange an entire room's air quickly on highest setting and remove dust and odor reliably. I immediately noticed a difference in air quality and now my living and bedroom smell fresh and clean all the time. I highly recommend this product - I am glad I purchased it, will buy another one for my business, and can't believe I have lived without one for so long!

text:
My house is full of air purifiers. We had 4 different air purifiers until recently. Now we've got 3 with this Molekule Mini being one of them. We also own a PHILIPS Air Purifier Series 2000, which is good for large rooms and costs around the same as this Molekule Mini. I don't know how much more effective Molekule's filters are over traditional HEPA filters but if the marketing is to be believed, it not only traps the pollutants, it destroys them. Overall I am very happy with this device. It's quiet, easy to move around the house, and has a very simple interface (one button). Although it has 5 fan speed settings, I never use anything other than the lowest setting. Anything else is too loud. That being said, my only real gripe is the price.

Pros:
- The fan on the lowest setting is quiet enough that it sounds like faint white noise. You can definitely go to sleep at this setting. Anything higher and you will definitely notice it.
- Very easy to use. Great carrying handle to move the filter around.
- Comes with an easy to use app that you can use to connect your filter to wifi. Helps you manage your device and see its status.

Cons:
- It's expensive. Very expensive.
- The other fan speeds are too loud to ever be used.
- My Phillips air filter has a sensor that can detect the quality of the air and uses this information to automatically adjust the fan speed. I wish this filter had something like that, especially since it's so expensive.
-Consumer Reports tested the bigger version of this filter and gave it its lowest score. It basically said it’s not great at actually filtering anything. I’m not an expert but do some research.

title: One suggestion for a better product...
text:
I literally just received this handy dandy compact air purifier. Brand spanking new out of the box, the low setting is very quiet and suitable for use on a desktop without causing major headaches. The high speed, which obviously would process more air, is much like sitting with your ear next to a box fan. I purchased this unit, along with a couple of others, for a smoker in the household hoping to not only eradicate my house of the smoke smell, but also to try and capture the smoke itself. I looked at the various "smoke eating" ashtrays, but besides looking like they would be a pain to clean, they are not exactly useful whenever the cigarette is removed from the ashtray itself and actually smoked.

My issue with this Holmes Arm & Hammer Odor Grabber Air Purifier is that the front of the unit is attractive enough and looks rather innocuous, the rear of the unit, where the real work takes place, is not quite as attractive. All you see back there is the back side of the exposed filter. To me, this is a definite design flaw. Unless you are able to set the unit smack dab in the middle of your room, its intake is going to be greatly limited if set, say on a bookshelf or on a table near a wall. When placed on a desk, the fan, even when set on low, creates quite a breeze which is a bit chilly in these winter months. With the unit turned around, however, it is much better and I could see smoke from an ashtray placed nearby being sucked right into the unit and clean air coming out via the fan. Facing forward, all the unit did was blow the smoke further into the room and while I assume it would eventually get circulated through the unit if the room were kept closed off from the rest of the house, placing the unit with the backside towards the source of the odor and allergens seems like it would be a much more efficient use of the unit and its purification abilities. I plan on purchasing a small piece of black wire mesh/screen that I can cut, bend and fold to fit over the filter and give it a little more polished look.

title: Stylish, Functional, Modern
text:
UPDATE: FEBRUARY 22, 2014

I think it's time for an update after four years of continuous use. The machine itself has been running solid with no problems. My simple maintenance is an occasional vacuum of the filter to de-clog the dust that has accumulated in front of the screen. I also take the time to vacuum the outside and inside the machine including the vents and where the filter parts fit. I put the filter back and start it up again.

Yearly maintenance is, of course, the set of filters. When I first wrote about this the cost of the filter is $75.00. Now these same filters cost $85.00. Disappointed that with it's popularity they have increased their cost as well rather than decrease. Like any manufacturer that sells consumable parts, they try to make more money on this aspect to grow their business.

Which is a bit disappointing considering they feel their customers will stick with them regardless of price. What they don't realize is consumers will easily jump to the next big thing if they know the cost becomes unreasonable over time.

I will maintain it's overall 4 star rating for now, but I would take caution in the fact that they need to find a way to lower the cost of their filters should they want to maintain their existing customers for the long term.

But Rabbit Air needs to watch out for when Dyson comes out with an air purifier with a killer design that doesn't require replacement filters and still become Asthma certified. People like myself can easily jump ship.

----------

ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW:

Air purifiers have come a long way in terms of design and technology. I've gone thru the simple HEPA filters, charcoal filter, UV bulbs, electrostatic ionizers, washable collector cells, and controversial ozone emitting products.

Now I'm down to two in my home one of which is the RabbitAir MinusA2 air purifier. I love it's stylish design that doesn't look boring, kitschy, or even gimmicky. I can place it in any part of my home and it doesn't look like an eyesore.

PROS:

1. Design - slim and modern

2. Controls - chrome-like buttons all laid out on one side

3. Remote - a small plastic remote emulating all the chrome buttons on the unit that is especially useful if you decide to hang the unit on a wall

4. Mood Light / Night Light - a horizontal strip of light in the front of the unit which contributes to the ambiance in the home.

5. Technology -

a. Silver Ion Pre-Filter - washable filter similar to A/C units with a fine mesh weave that capture large dust
particles. RabbitAir goes one step further by coating it with silver ions which have been proven to retard or even eliminate bacteria growth.

b. Anti-Bacterial Medium Filter - which appears to be a blue cotton filter and captures finer dust particles, pollen, mold and bacteria.

c. BioGS HEPA filter - (technology found on the previous BioGS models) and captures even more of the above plus fungus, dust mites, odours, smoke and greenhouse gases.

d. Customized Filter - another stage in filtration to specifically tailor to your choice of "Germ Defense", "Pet Allergy" and "Toxin Absorber".

e. Charcoal Based Activated Carbon Filter - the final stage in filtration in an old reliable charcoal filtration method that helps absorb more odours and toxins.

All of the above filters are housed in a relatively sturdy filter case which helps organize and arrange these for easy removal and replacement.

f. Negative Ion Generator - which further helps purify the air by clinging to suspended particles that haven't passed thru the filter and essentially making them fall to the floor rather than float around.

g. Brushless Motor - essentially produces a longer motor life and a quiet operation due to a friction-less design.

6. Filter Life / Cost - Less time consuming and relatively less expensive replacement method by being able to operate for a year in between changes. Of course, regular monthly maintenance is recommended by vacuuming and/or washing the pre-filter as well as cleaning the vents and odour analyzer.

7. Function -

a. Odour Sensor - a vent on the right side that detects changes in air quality and adjusts fan speed accordingly for faster air purification. Of course, effective placement of the air purifier matters for a more effective operation.

b. Light Sensor - detects available light and shuts down the mood light (if used) and air quality indicator.

c. Air Quality Indicator - gives a visual indication of present air quality by changing from blue (good) to purple, pink and then red (bad).

d. Easy front panel removal - no clumsy clips here. Elegant magnet on the bottom and a simple latch on top to facilitate easy pre-filter cleaning and filter replacement.

CONS:

My gripe is the filter replacement cost. As of this writing the marketing of the filter can last "up to two years". If you further read the manual and manufacturer FAQ, this of course means operating the unit non-continuously at only 12 hours a day. But RabbitAir has stated this on their website FAQ:

----------

Q: Why should I run my air purifier continuously?

A:To be truly effective, ALL air purifiers should be run continuously. Scientific researches confirm that indoor air pollution rapidly returns to pretreatment levels when an air purifier is turned off.

----------

To truly benefit from the air purifier, then it is a no-brainer to operate it for 24 hours a day (unless it's on a vacation home that sees traffic a few times a year). Which means under "normal use" then filter life is really good for a year. Replacement cost then amounts to $75 a year plus shipping and taxes, where applicable. I would have preferred the manufacturers offer discounted filter service and free shipping KNOWING that loyal customers will be replacing their filters anyway at this predictable time frame.

Throw us a bone and make it more convenient so we won't go looking for other air purifiers down the road.

OVERALL:

I would recommend this product with it's higher quality manufacturing and design that sets it apart from other air purifiers. Are the air filters with it's multi-stage redundant layers gimmicky? I don't know. Independent reviews and studies (not provided by the manufacturer) will prove in time. And it does beat simple one-layer filters of other machines, well, at a higher price to pay.

Of course, air purifier manufacturers will tell you that "there is no price to pay for your health". Well there certainly is a price to pay for buying these purifiers and if RabbitAir can improve their product filter replacement cost down the road and independent studies can prove the performance of their filters, then we definitely have a winner in the MinusA2 model.

As for which model to buy - SPA-780A or SPA-700A. I can only say that they are exactly the same on the outside as well as filter replacement parts. The only difference is a more powerful motor to help cover a wider space and essentially guarantee up to 815 sq feet of area as well as a choice of glossy black or glossy white. Choose well.

text: The Dyson Pure Cool is fantastic, but it's definitely for a niche audience. Yes, there are cheaper air purifiers. There are also definitely cheaper fans. It barely qualifies as white noise until you get to half of the 10 speeds available to you, which says a lot -- level 5 is as powerful as most air purifiers I've dealt with. I didn't have to change the filter, but I did take it apart to check the process. It's a 90 second swap. My favorite little touch is the remote. You can control it wherever you are, and since having another remote sitting on a table isn't stylish, you can attach it to the top of the fan where a magnet will hold it in place. The Pure Cool is well-made, fully featured, and well made. I love it. If it's in your price range you can do no wrong by adding it to your cart.

title: Quiet Powerhouse
text:
The positive reviews for Hathaspace's other (smaller) air purifiers led us to believe they may be doing something right in the industry. We had intended to order one of the smaller units, but when we learned they had recently released this larger HSP002 model, we knew we had to try it. We wanted the extra capacity to purify the whole house, rather than just our bedroom. We could NOT be happier with the decision we made. The amount of air this thing can move is nothing short of impressive. And the quieter night mode is so silent you can barely tell it's running with your head right next to it. The way this thing detects impurities in the air is also very impressive. If you even set a dirty laundry basket next to it, the sensors will detect impurities and ramp up the fans in "auto" mode. We have also experimented with putting this in our cat's litter box room to see if it rids smells with positive results. The very large filter is thick and heavy, suggesting quite a bit of technology and quality are packed inside. And the washable pre-filter is a great piece to help lengthen the life of the somewhat pricey replaceable filter that Hathaspace recommends you service every 3 months.

The only thing I would make as a suggestion to the manufacturer is to do with the lights on the machine itself. I was thrilled when I saw that one of the control buttons on the top panel was for the light. Thinking this would enable me to turn of all the lights on the machine's display for dark nights when it is running in our bedroom. Sadly that button only turns off the air quality light on the front of the machine that changes from green to blue to red - indicating the air quality around the machine. That's basically useless at night, because the display panel on top of the machine is the brightest / most annoying light source on the machine. It lights up our entire bedroom and is impossible to ignore. We have taken to placing a folded hand towel on top of the machine when we go to bed to block out the light, which works just fine because the top panel is perfectly flat so the towel doesn't slide off. If the light button would allow you to cycle the control panel illumination on/off as well as the air quality indicator, this would be an 11/10 product for me. But I still don't feel this justifies knocking a star off this review. The machine itself is working wonders in our home.

If you're looking for a reasonably priced, high-volume, & high quality air purifier for your home; I would definitely recommend looking into the Hathaspace HSP002

**Update** 05/15/2020

In my review, I showcased an issue with the whining sound when you pressed the 2nd setting. I reached out to customer support who then found my review and gave me a few suggestions to fix the whining sound. I was told to turn the unit upside down and press the power button which didn’t work. They then told me I should take out the filter packaging which I told them was already done. I didn’t get any responses back about getting a replacement unit and haven’t been contacted back for over a week now. I’m incredibly surprised by the lack of good customer service from this company and have reflected my review as such to 3 stars. If you have any issues with this companies products you’re going to have a tough time with replacements. My unit still works well... but I’m unimpressed by the customer service over their flagship product.

This AGH550 Glory Days Hepa Air Purifier is the flagship purifier from Airthereal and is a well built machine for cleaning the air in your home. Feel free to check out my video unboxing review!

Pros:

-Packaging looks premium for a flagship air purifier. It was packed very well for protection.
-AHAM Verified. This is important. Having a machine independently reviewed for quality assured buyers are paying for a great machine to have their clean.
-ARB Certified for federal ozone emissions limit
-Energy efficient
-Air purifier is well made and looks sleek and will fit right in to any home decor you may have.
-The LED screen on top of the purifier is nice and bright even in well lit rooms. The buttons function very well and has a nice colored indication (green, yellow, and red) to reveal the air quality level.
-The laser sensor works great for indicating the air purity level. I tested in various rooms and gave me different readings and cleaned the air fast!
-The lowest mode (1) is extremely quiet. I can barely hear it a few feet away. The higher modes show off the motor inside the purifier and it get can get loud! But definitely shows off the power this machine has.
-This purifier has a sleep mode and child safe lock which are handy for parents or if you don’t want to LED lights to be on while you sleep. Very handy.

Cons:

During my unboxing I noticed a whining sound coming from the 2nd air level. I don’t know if that sound goes away over time or is a small defect in my machine. I will contact support to see if there is a fix as it can be bothersome if next to the machine.
-The machine can be prone to fingerprint and smudges. Not a big deal, but you might have to wipe it down if you have children touching it often.
-This is a small gripe, but I thought on the top of the device where is shows the colored air predication level, I would have hoped it would glimmer across the screen as the videos for the product made it seem to have. Again, very small gripe that isn’t a huge deal.
-Machine on the higher settings can get really loud past the level 3 setting. It does make for some great white noise while sleeping though!

Feel free to ask me any questions you may have about this air purifier. I check on here often so feel free to ask if there is something I didn’t cover that you’re curious about. I will be updating as I have this device longer!

title: Chlorine Dioxide air cleaner.
text:
This works well, and it’s especially great for the cars of smokers and vapers. The little black packet marked “do not remove seal” is supposed to be opened, according to the details on the replacement filter page here. Also according to info from other users based on replies from the seller. So you’re supposed to ignore that sticker and open it. Strange. Is the sticker for liability issues possibly? This is your CIO2 (Chlorine Dioxide) releasing packet, and replacements are sold on this page. The round filter is your charcoal filter.

CIO2 is a disinfectant similar to bleach and kills odors, viruses and fungi, among other things, so it might be great for purifying the air, however, it is also a severe lung and eye irritant if inhaled in large amounts. It is unclear just how much is being released by this thing, but I doubt it’s enough to worry about. So far I haven’t noticed any problems after using it in a car with the windows up. But if you have issues like asthma, be wary of any coughing, breathing issues or irritated eyes. Also, best to keep away from children and to be careful when opening and handing the CIO2 packet. You can also just not open it of course.

But as I said, so far, so good. The great thing about this is that it’s easy to see the fan level by the bright colored light at the top, and it has a big button so it’s very easy to use while driving as it doesn’t take your attention away much from the road. Replacement filters are also readily available right here on this page, which is a huge plus. It does filter the air well, and you can even vape with the windows up while on the freeway or while it’s raining and it will help keep your whole car from fogging up. Also probably great for smokers, to help with air quality and odor. It fits well into a cup holder, although a bit tall. Will update with any issues, but so far, the best car air purifier I’ve used yet.

text:

We’ve had the flex running 24/7 on setting 3 or turbo since 2/18. Within about 3 days we noticed a dramatic decrease in the amount of eye discharge from the toddler, less sneezing and coughing from everyone else in the house and less crap in the vacuum cleaner.

We keep it in the living during the day/evening and move to the master bedroom at night. Fan noise on stages 1-3 are barely noticeable. Turbo is a little louder but it’s nice white noise while sleeping. I like the design and the control panel is easy to use. Definitely appreciate the lock so the kid doesn’t mess with it.

I did not notice any smell with the pre-filter when we first started using it. Also - I used a small handheld vacuum after about 4 days to clean off the prefilter. That will likely be a weekly task to maintain the filter life.

title: Great but expensive operation
text:
We agree with most of the positive comments in other evaluations: the unit is very nice, elegant, solid built, absolutely quiet in all speeds except slight hum in the top speed. In cleans the air well and fast. It has nice features: light indicators, timer, odor sensor.

The only issue – for which I removed 1 star – is the filter capacity. New filter costs over $33+ and (according to the description) should be replaced every 3-6 months when used daily. We used the air purifier every night and sometimes for short periods during day for almost 1 month to our full satisfaction. Then the air developed a strong smell and the purifier became unusable. The odor originated from the (strongly smelling) filter; once the filter was removed from the unit the odor disappeared. On this subject the Amazon sale site says: “Air Choice air purifier for home is supported by a 2-year full with 24/7 dedicated customer support & FREE FILTERS “ (capitals in the original text). When we contacted the seller, Amazon passed our complaint to the manufacturer and manufacturer declined our complaint, claiming our faults (“the ambient air quality” and “… you have to remove the plastic bag when replace the filter ...”). Both are nonsense: the purifier functioned perfectly for almost a month (obviously, with the bag removed; what they think, that we are morons ?) and we had always closed all windows in the house (hot summer). Our request for the “FREE FILTERS“ for 2 years was ignored. (too good to be true ?)

The original package with the unit contained also a card requesting our comment on Amazon site with promised reward of a “FREE FILTER”. I am afraid that this may end up similarly as the promised “2-year full with 24/7 dedicated customer support & FREE FILTERS”. And my advice: if you do not mind to purchase a new filter every month, go ahead a buy this unit. The filter is very easy to install and the lights blink in 4 different colors. :-)
P.S. Changed experience: relied too much on "Amazon's Choice" ?

title: Worth every cent, allergy relief almost immediately
text: We recently got a mini schnauzer puppy a couple of months ago. I am highly allergic to most dogs and all cats. Even though the schnauzer is considered hypoallergenic, I know that no dog is truly hypoallergenic. We have a small 880 foot condo and keep her crate in the living room. Starting on the first evening we had her, my allergies started to flare up, as well as my wife's. This was not acceptable. I originally had a levoit large room purifier but knew it was time to step it up. After perusing Amazon reviews, I decided on the Alen Breathe smart i45. A major plus to this unit was the air sensor which automatically adjusts speed and intensity based upon air quality. When I first got it, I immediately plugged it in and it got to work. The air quality light showed red and it continued running at high intensity for several hours and I saw the air quality improving. After a day or two, my allergy symptoms were completely gone. I was ecstatic! This purifier is meant to run 24/7, so that is what I do. It is a LIFESAVER! Now we can co exist with our four legged friend in peace. Make sure to register on their site for the lifetime warranty activation. I also signed up for the filter subscription as it makes things easier than having to manually order. I would recommend this purifier to anyone who has allergies and/or wants better air quality! Can't give this thing enough praise. Note: Few comments here recommend the gosund app for wifi monitoring. While I tried doing so and it did work, I quickly cancelled the connection and deleted the gosund app. I think it's a security risk to give some unknown app your WiFi network password, and also when I contacted Alen, they said there is no app right now for monitoring purposes. The wifi capability is for remote troubleshooting if issues arise. So I recommend not using any third party app with the purifier.

title: Good unit, bad Amazon experience
text:
Wildfire smoke was making life miserable in the Pacific NorthWest and we have small birds in the house who need clean air, so, after some research I bought this unit from Amazon. There are several things I'd like to say. Firstly I was flat-out enraged that Amazon dropped the price by $90 the day after I ordered this. I know Amazon has a really aggressive "what the market can bear" pricing policy and I may have occasionally lucked out in the past, but this time I got badly burned. It hurts -- not enough to dump my Prime membership, but a lot.
Then there is the fact that the output air clearly smelled of cigarette smoke for several days. Obviously it was a demo or otherwise used unit that had been cleaning up the air at a Bed Bath and Beyond location (it's origin, according to the shipping information).
I am giving the product four stars, which may not be fair to Alen. I get the feeling that the unit will turn out to have been a good, if too expensive, purchase. It is quiet and effective. Really, 5 stars for Alen, 1 star for Amazon.

Update: July 2019. The unit STILL smells of cigarette smoke -- even when turned off. Again, no fault of Alen. This is on Bed Bath and Beyond and Amazon for selling a used unit as new.

title: REALLY AWESOME PERFORMANCE
text:

Of course you can't open windows in the winter or even summer in Az., so I thought maybe I needed an air purifier, which I am SO glad I bought. I was working on my nails tonight, and I can see that the dirty air monitor came on as expected, and is working beautifully. Not even a whiff of monomer downstairs, which is usually very heavy. there and everywhere.

This is the best investment I have made ever.. You will not be disappointed with this one. and I love the ease of operation, and the fresh air, which is so appreciated! I am so glad I made this purchase. I also had made prime rib yesterday and the fat rendering off in the oven smoked up the whole house. text:

Here's where it loses a lot of stars - while it is quiet at silent, IT'S NOT A CONSISTENT QUIET, the fan speed ramps up/ramps down when NOT in automatic mode, the fan does not keep a consistent noise profile so its like random. This is by far the most annoying feature of this air purifier, easily makes me hate it. This is not a comforting white noise, this is one of those things you notice and hate (if odd sounds bother you, or inconsistent sounds). Also, it sometimes makes a high pitch rattle/wobble which I did contact customer service about and they said it WAS NORMAL. So, if you're sensitive to sound, this supposedly quieter air purifier might not be for you.

I kind of wish I went for Blue Air instead.

Also, let's not get it confused, the odor remover barely works, there's simple not enough activated charcoal to make a difference (whereas Blue Air has SmokeStop which makes a huge difference for odor removal).

That's not to say Rabbit Air has failed me, I run it 100% of the time and it has made a difference in the bedroom, it's just really annoying since it's right next to my bed and since it makes random unpredictable sounds it's more distracting than comforting.

Date: 1/21/2018

I've decided to update this review. It took me a really long time to get used to the sound this thing makes in my bedroom (which is also my office). The noise is much more consistent if you run it on say medium rather than silent (that is so weird to say), because at silent the internal mechanism (blower) kind of moves back in forth and makes an inconsistent rattle whereas at a much faster speed it doesn't move around and make that annoying rattle that bugged me so much before.

title: A Tale of Woe...
text:
This is titled A Tale of Woe", not because there's anything wrong with the unit, rather I'm upset because I have been unable to register the product hence there will be no recall notifications, and I am not verified as the owner of record so my unit is not subject to factory warranty service if required.

I bought this unit from Amazon and as a Prime member, received it in two days (unimportant but very nice), set it up and plugged it in. It began to function, I assume as advertised. While there was a owner registration card enclosed, I opted to use the Internet. First problem: the form I attempted to complete was for ORECKCANADA. Well, we in the USA, we don't have Provinces or seven digit zip codes. I called there and got the ORECKUSA phone number. I called there only to discover that while Amazon once was a Oreck dealer, they were no longer so I would have to work through the actual seller on Amazon. A company, believe it or not named "always bargain". I got this name, phone number and website from Amazon. I called their customer service number in early afternoon only to find my call went to a voice mail service provided by that carrier whose web based service one can buy at the local drugstore for under $20.00 per year.

Growing frustrated, I visited "always bargin's" website. Guess what I found? This company sells parts for professional electric pet groomer clippers, etc., and nowhere could I find any sort of Oreck product or supplies, so while they sell this unit through Amazon they don't really sell it or anything Oreck at all. I later checked Oreck's catalog and to my further surprise couldn't find this particular unit offered for sale any longer.

Next I called Amazon Customer Service who keep their service representatives hidden away somewhere in the Philippines but at least they require that their off shore staff speak very good English. Language aside, attempting to explain my rapidly growing problem was pointless. I was put on hold while the representative called back to Amazon in the USA for further instructions, which apparently weren't forthcoming.(I recently bought an excellent speaker phone for just this purpose.) I finally insisted on speaking to someone further up the Amazon food chain who was hopefully still based in America.

Surprise, there are still Americans working at Amazon! The lady I spoke with was at a complete loss to explain policies or procedures regarding third party sellers especially one like this who sells pet grooming supplies AND incidentally this Oreck Air Purifier, I must assume at Amazon's behest. The lady extended some sort of warranty that is normally sold with small appliances and then to calm me down, credited my account with the premium cost.

At the end of this saga, my air purifier remains unregistered and unwarranted while I remain a less than happy Amazon customer.

title: Effective and easy to use
text:
Air Purifier

I wanted to wait a few months before writing a review for this air purifier. I’ve had it for around 7 months now and I am so glad I purchased it.

The design is reminiscent of a product designed by a fruit company in Cupertino. By that I mean it is a very modern and attractive design. With clean lines and lots of small thoughtful elements that make for a overall great presentation. The large high-contrast, backlight display is located on the top of the unit. The touch sensitive buttons are large and easy to see. The filter compartment is accessed by a door held on by magnets. This is a very well considered design choice. The sounds this unit makes when powering on and pressing buttons is very pleasing to my ear. Even the alert sound to change the filter wasn’t harsh or jarring like other purifiers I’ve owned. PSA: To reset the filter replacement reminder just hold down the buttons that are pulsing for a few seconds. The generally flat surfaces make it very easy to clean. I have a significant visual impairment and I was easily able to unpack and set this up with no issues.

I noticed a difference in the quality of the air in my bedroom within 30 minutes of starting the unit. I mainly just leave it on high and put it in turbo mode before bed and after I get up. This mode puts the fan to an extra high setting (about 66db according to my Apple Watch) for one hour then returns the purifier to your previous setting. When I walk out of my bedroom in the morning. I can tell a significant difference between the smell of the air there and the smell in the rest of the house. It makes me want to put these in every room. However that’s not an option due to budget limitations. Speaking of budget limitations. The filter cost is substantial. When taking into account the every 90 day replacement recommendation.

I did have two issues with my unit. The first was a bad laser sensor that measures the air quality. Customer service was quick to replace the sensor. The second was an intermittent high pitched noice coming from the fan. That I didn’t share with customer service. Customer service was excellent. They were easy to understand and quick to offer solutions to my issue. I had a third issue that was totally user created and they resolved it quickly. I will not go into detail here because I know every case is different.

In summary this is an item I hope to be using for a long time to come. It’s much like an Apple product. It just makes you feel good when you are interacting with it. But like Apple products there is a high cost of ownership. In this case I think you get what you pay for. Is it for you? Can you find something more economical that will fit your needs? These are questions I can not answer for you. What I can say is this. It’s been several months since my purchase and I don’t regret it one bit.

Thanks for taking the time to read my review. Pleas feel free to post any questions you have and I will do my best to answer them.

title: Long Review - Worth the Investment
text:
Feb. 15th 2019 Purchase
May 15th 2019 Review

Ok so I’ve been waiting a while to review this product as I wanted to really test it out and see if it was not only worth the hype, but the money. Below are my lengthy comments.

1. Living in Austin, TX
Allergies are bad, like #26 worst city in the entire nation bad. Needless to say, we all suffer in this house. Between the dogs and just the location, we are on a first name basis with our ENT and have severe allergies that turn into sinus infections at least 6x a year. It’s that bad. Seriously. The ENT told me to move after my allergy test.

2. The Unit Itself
This thing is big, like very big. Roughly 3ft y’all and 2 feet wide and just a box body white (you can change the face cover) contraption. Is it pretty, no, does that matter if it works? To us, no, but just be aware that this is a little air purification unit you can just put in the corner and nobody will notice.

3. Amount Needed
Make sure you really buy the units based on your sq. footage. We ended up buying 4 units to place in the downstairs of our home alone so it does matter. I can’t speak on it we only had one if it would work, but the 4 are what we have strategically placed. Don’t forget to not butt them against the wall either. They need room to breathe and collect air.

4. Simplicity of Use
These units are VERY easy to put together; all the lights are simple to understand and the instructions are straightforward. We have our 4 units running on high 24/7/365 and have not had one issue at all. The main light on the top indicates air quality; red =bad, yellow =OK, blue = good. It’s a great way to keep track of how the air quality is throughout the day.

5. Noise
I wouldn’t say this is at all invasive when it comes to noise. Now, when we turn them off it seems very quiet in the house but when they are on and running there is not a noise you notice or that is bothersome. All in all they are incredibly quiet.

6. Uses
I want to preface that we bought our units for allergies, not air scent purification. We do have 5 dogs but I can’t say whether or not they helped with the “dog smell” - I would like to say our home doesn’t have a dog smell at all as they are all short coated dogs and we have a 3x a week housekeeper. I only say this as we bought these units to help with allergies and allergies only, not for smoking, bad smells etc so although our home always seems fresh and airy, I can’t speak to that here about the units.

7. Do They Work?
Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes. Wow - this is where I get excited. Since February until now, May when we all usually are at the ENT getting more meds and nose sprays we haven’t been once time this year. Now, does that mean we didn’t suffer from allergies? No, we still did, it has just been reduced measurably. We can breathe again, year round and living in Austin is truly much less miserable allergy wise. They aren’t cheap, and they may not be pretty to look at, but these units work, really well and we are so grateful for that because it sure beats the alternative of the doctor all the time. If you’re on the fence about them, pull the trigger. It’s worth it.

title: Quiet and good at first, loud and unstable sensor after only a few months
text: When I first got this in Nov 2019 it was incredibly quiet. I had it in my bedroom and was able toeave it on auto and sleep well. After about a month and a half (about early Feb) the noise increased, even if I manually set it on the lowest fan setting to a point it was too loud to leave in my bedroom. I moved it to the living room and put it back on auto. It was definitely louder but tolerable in the bigger room, and it would rotate from green air quality to yellow when I would cook in the nearby kitchen and increased the fan to clear any kitchen odors or particles then went back to low and green. Seemed to still be doing its job. After another month (early March) it decided that no matter the time of day or what is going on that the air quality is red and it must run on high, which now sounds like a small rc plane running in my living room. I wondered, did my air quality change that drastically when I have done nothing different? I changed my furnace filter and no change in the Alen so I have a different brand air purifier in my bedroom that I moved to the living room to see if it thought the same. It did not. Other brand runs on low and says the air quality is good except when cooking. It makes me think there is something with the sensor or filter on the Alen so I changed the filter (even though the filter says it is still fine) and used canned air to clear any dust. Same high noise and always will run on high when in auto. I have had to just manually set the fan speed to low and resign myself to having a medium level hum in that corner of the room. It annoys me enough that I have opted for a different brand air purifier for the second bedroom instead of another Alen, which is a shame as this one was so much quieter in the beginning and I like the design and single filter system much better. I couldn't justify the higher cost of the Alen if it was going to get so much louder after a couple months and then have something go wonky with the sensor after a couple more. Yes, I am still using it, but I can't honestly recommend it based on these issues.

title: Great product. Read for comparison against 582A
text:
I wanted to post this review mainly because there is no real comparison between [[ASIN:B000R52Z2O Rabbit Air MinusA2 (covers 700 sq. ft.) Ultra-Quiet Air Purifier - 6 Stage Filtration! - built in Mood Light]] and the [[ASIN:B000KMRZNI Rabbit Air BioGP (model 582A - covers 780 sq. ft.) Ultra-Quiet Air Purifier w/ Germicidal Protection- Low Maintenance - Washable Filters!, Pearl White]] out there. This is to give you an idea if you're making a choice between the two. [...]

I first purchased the 582A but returned it after a few months of usage due to some minor defect for an exchange with MinusA2 (RabbitAir support was extremely helpful). As a result I have experience with both of these units. The main reason I purchased an Air Purifier was dust elimination and for that particular purpose in mind both these products exceeded my expectations.

In the order of importance for me, these are the differences:
- As I am posting this review MinusA2 is $[...] more expensive than 582A. So why should you even consider MinusA2? Read on...

- Filtering:
(a) MinusA2 has 2 more levels of filtering. The Medium Filter (which filters medium sized particles and increases the efficiency/lifespan of the main HEPA filter) and a Customized Filter of your choice.
(b) On the other hand although RabbitAir boasts about the benefits of BioGP HEPA filters over the regular HEPA filters on their website, it's not clear if the MinusA2 HEPA filter is also BioGP (yet it's made by 3M and looks high quality). The price of the 582A's HEPA filter is more expensive. I am not sure if this is due to the surface area or because 582A's filter is really more effective.

- Noise level: This is where MinusA2 shines due to its more efficient new engine.
(a) I was pleasantly surprised to find out MinusA2 improves quite a bit over already very silent 582A. To compare at different speeds the noise and Clean Air Flow, check the Features tab in RabbitAir's own website for each product.
(b) I am not sure how RabbitAir calculates the sq ft. coverage but I run these units at the highest speed for which noise is acceptable (~ about 30dB in my opinion). Consequently I can run MinusA2 at Medium speed producing 97 Cubic Feet/min of clean air as opposed to 582A's Low speed producing 85 Cubic Feet/min.

- Area of coverage: Although 582A is rated at 780 sq ft. versus 700 sq ft. of MinusA2, if you check the Features tab for each product on RabbitAir's website you'll find out that MinusA2's clean air output is generally higher at the same speed setting as well as its CADR (clean air delivery rate) rating. I imagine RabbitAir's sq ft. calculation is based on the maximum setting in which 582A outputs 208 Cubic Feet/min vs 187 Cubic Feet/min of MinusA2. However I think this is unrealistic and I doubt many of you will choose to use it at the highest setting due to high energy consumption and noise.

- Design and build quality: MinusA2 wins this comparison by far.
(a) I must say though that there's room for improvement for both of these products. For both of them the plastic construction looks a bit cheap although this is more apparent with 582A. I wish their build were metallic.
(b) However MinusA2 is quite handsome overall with its square lines.
(c) It could also be wall mounted.
(d) One more thing I'd like to mention is I really liked the tiny remote of 582A. I think MinusA2's remote is not only less functional but is bulkier for no reason. I also miss 582A's the tiny remote control pocket behind the unit which reduced remote control clutter in the house.
(e) By the way although the mood light of MinusA2 adds to its cool looks, I believe RabbitAir's own claim of the Mood Light "helping normalize blood pressure, pulse, and facilitate deep breathing blah blah" is total nonsense. I think this sounds totally unscientific and if anything has negative influence on my view of RabbitAir as a honest company with high quality products. Also you will find out that you can't change the color of this light as you wish (based on your mood) but the unit sets that itself (based on its own mood).

- Energy consumption: MinusA2 consumes between 8 to 47 Watts whereas 582A consumes between 7 to 67 Watts. I believe the lower consumption of MinusA2 is due to the newer generation Mitsubishi engine employed. Therefore you can expect lower energy usage if you plan to run the unit at anything beyond the Silent setting.

- Sensors:
(a) Note that MinusA2 does not have an odor sensor although 582A has. I think this is quite useful with 582A and I don't understand why RabbitAir chose to drop this from MinusA2.
(b) On the other hand MinusA2 has a light sensor. Certainly it does not help to do a better air purification, but if you're using the Auto mode then the unit goes to the Silent setting automatically a few mins after the lights are dimmed. I think this should've been optional even in the Auto mode but it's a useful feature nevertheless.
(c) The particle sensor of MinusA2 looks more elaborate and I imagine it does a better job.
(d) Furthermore MinusA2 has adjustable sensor sensitivity. This is extremely useful, and the reason I returned 582A was because the sensors of the unit I received was simply too sensitive and was changing from "clean" to "very dirty" for no apparent reason in a split second (during late nights etc when there was no virtual change in room conditions).

Overall I think MinusA2 is a great unit and improves on the already impressive 582A. I thought it's worth the price difference. I already ordered a new one after RabbitAir customer support said they could give me a discount for an additional unit.

title: Be careful when reading the reviews - there are two models being sold from this one page, and they appear to be quite different.
text:
The awful fires burning in Napa and Sonoma and Santa Rosa began blowing a tremendous quantity of smoke into San Francisco on Sunday night. I shut my windows and went to bed before midnight. By Monday morning my eyes and nose were raw and I knew I'd have to do something before the end of the day.

That evening I stopped by Target on the way home and picked up the last air purifier they had in stock, the large version of this filter. I checked the reviews here on Amazon and they all said it was quiet and effective, although at that point I'd have settled for just effective. I'd been thinking about getting an air filter anyhow for the past decade - I have terrible sinus problems - and the fire pushed me into doing it.

Well, it was money well-spent, even if it was a lot of money, and in spite of a couple of problems. The first problem is, most of the reviews here are clearly for the small unit, not its bigger brother. Naturally, I hadn't filtered the reviews to only look at those for the large version - buyer beware! Truly, these products should each be on their own separate page - I think it's very misleading for them to share a single page and their reviews. That kind of toggle should be reserved for products that only vary by color or some other minor, non-functional attribute.

Anyhow, this unit could only be characterized as "quiet" on the low-speed setting, and even then it's hardly silent. While the smaller unit may or may not be quiet, this larger unit is incredibly noisy on the high speed setting and loud even on medium. It does however move a lot of air on both the medium and especially on the high settings, so much that my apartment has remained almost entirely smoke free during this horrible disaster. My allergies have been no worse than normal and today - having stayed home with the filter running on high all day - are actually better than average.

The unit does seem to be a bit bulkier than it needs to be - I wish it were an inch or two shallower, so it could more easily tuck between furniture and the wall. It also takes a whopping three small HEPA filters and 3 small carbon filters, which I'm sure are going to be expensive to replace when the time comes. While they appear to be fairly common filters, the unit would probably be more effective and cheaper to run with one large filter, and might be quieter too.

On the plus side it's plain looking and not overdesigned or unattractive. I love the fact it vents from the top - I've placed it in a spot near the window, and during periods when the smoke has cleared outside and I've opened the door to get some ventilation, the purifier has done a wonderful job helping to circulate the cooling breeze around the room. And while it's loud when operating on high - it sounds like I'm sitting in the cabin of a jet plane - it's a constant, low-pitched formless whooshing noise, so it's fairly easy to ignore and at night acts as white noise. I've slept fine with it running full out all night long. I may actually get rid of my desk fan - which I seldom use except during a heatwave - and just rely on this purifier going forward, because on the high setting it circulates air all around the room and keeps it comfortable a good five degrees past where it would otherwise become stifling. And it does it all without stirring up a bunch of dust and driving my allergies insane.

So if you've thought about buying an air purifier I'd highly recommend giving one a try. I'm not positive I'd buy this model again if I had more time to make a choice - I'd definitely want to try out a few and do more research before taking the plunge - but for a product I bought in a panic at the end of a long unpleasant day I'm extremely happy it's working as well as it does. Very glad I made that snap decision the other night.

title: Still the BEST purchase for my health, a year and a half later
text:
Honestly this was the BEST purchase I could have made for my health. I have a medium-haired cat, and I'm sensitive to her, not to mention the dust that she carries around and digs up. Plus, I live in the garden-level of a house, and my room is particularly dusty anyway - I have no idea where it all comes from!! Also, my cat was getting recurring ear infections and allergy attacks.

Anyway, before this filter I could vacuum weekly and have TONS of dust bunnies. When I'd leave town and come back, even if I shut the room out from my cat and no one went in, it would be covered with dust - even if the vents were closed. If I came home with a cold, I would take weeks to get better, or not at all until I stayed in the living room for a few days. I would sometimes randomly have asthma attacks - it was unbearable and I hardly had another living situation available any time soon.

I purchased the Rabbit Air MinusA2 black 780 version. My room is hardly bigger than 150 square feet - if that - I purchased it mainly because it was the only version available that was black (fits best in the coloring of my room), and the fact that I purchased this for the future when I have my own place.

Anyway, this has been a LIFE-SAVER. I've cut down the number of incidents I have respiratory issues significantly - and the turnaround for recovery is also greatly increased. My need for vacuuming is incredibly decreased - hardly ever have dust bunnies. My cat's wheezing has stopped too, which is awesome. You walk into my room and the air just screams "clean".

The maintenance for this is also incredible - just once a month I vacuum the pre-filter. The filters are also not too expensive - especially since you only have to replace them perhaps once a year for 24 hour use - but given my dustiness I might do it sooner.

I purchased this several months ago, and am considering purchasing it for relatives that I like to visit that I have extreme allergies to their dog to see if this helps!

Update 4/25/18 - it has been more than a year and a half, still amazing! I don’t regret this, and saw that the new model has maintenance reminders with an app, which is awesome!

Update 10/31/019: still great!

title: It's Loud!
text:
I wanted to write this review after I had used the air purifier for at least 18 months through all seasons! I have asthma and seasonal allergies, and I've used some of the small air purifiers before in my 200sq ft room.

The heat and cooling features work quite well, and have reduced our overall need for central AC!

The air purifier seems to have improved the air quality, but there is no definitive way of knowing by how much. My allergy symptoms have gone down by half (but I've made other lifestyle changes too)!

The purifier is powerful enough that it can improve the air quality in a large room. But, you have to keep the doors and windows closed and keep it running all the time. This is where it can get really annoying. It's obnoxiously loud! And the longer it goes, the louder the sound gets in your head. I have often had to take a break from using the purifier for an entire day just because the noise is obnoxious. It's like a 24/7 frat party on a Boeing 737.

And if I stop using a purifier because of the noise level, then the point is lost! (Note: The heater is less noisy than the cooler, and the higher settings are noisier than the lower settings)

If you have a room over 200 sq ft, and severe allergies, and are able to tune out loud noises, and have mild to moderate heat/cold needs, you may want to consider this air purifier. If not, the smaller, quieter air purifiers will give you the same allergy relief in most standard-size rooms!

title: Hathaspace vs Germ Guardian
text:
I have owned a Germ Guardian for 5 yrs and liked it so much I bought 2 others. One I gave as a gift and the other for our basement. After 5 yrs of continued use my first Germ Guardian stopped working so I decided to replace it with this Hathaspace unit on it looks and reviews.

Comparing it strictly on looks the Hathaspace hands down is nicer looking but that is where my "like" ends. There Germ Guardian is basic in that there is no sensor controlling the speed like the Hathaspace does. In comparing the units just on eliminating cooking odors the Hathaspace ran all day (the automatic sensor turned the speed down) and 5 hrs later I still needed to turn off and put my Germ Guardian for 30 mins and the smells were gone. The sensor deal is annoying because you are not in control of the running speed at all. Supposedly when the sensor senses the air is clean it shifts to a slower speed but and it shifts in a matter of minutes - how can it tell that quickly the air is good when say - a cooking odor is still very much there after 5 hours? The Germ Guardian will remain on high until you change the level and I like that feature - especially when you do want your home to be odor free for company. I guess my theory is if a smell remains for that long why wouldn't everything else remain there?

The Germ Guardian does a better job of cleaning the air all the way around. The Germ Guardian filters show more dust, dirt and pollen than the Hathaspace does.

Personally, I would say - if you want a nice looking unit get the Hathaspace. If you truly want it for pollen, pet, dust and smells get a Germ Guardian.

With my air purifier that replaced this one, I tried to hide the unit because it was ugly. This unit is looks good and I do not try to hide it at all. Further, the materials seem to be a better quality then the similar Honeywell models (I am going solely on look and feel).

When looking for an air purifier, I wanted a unit where I didn't have to replace any filters. The unit features two large permanent HEPA filters that every three months you clean by vacuuming the filters. There is a reminder light when it is time to do so. There is three speed settings. The lowest setting is very quiet. The highest setting is quite loud. I can sleep to both the low and medium settings. Not so with the high setting.

There is also a timer so after 2, 4, or 6 hours the unit will shut itself off. Another feature is an automatic setting which is supposed to monitor the quality of air and adjust the settings. I am not sure if the unit really does try to sense anything or just goes through a preset routine. I guess it is the preset routine. FInally, there is an ionizer. Some people say this is bad for the air, some say it is good for the air. I really have no idea what is true. I do know that after a while ionizer air seems dryer, which I do not like. This machine allows you to shut the ionizer off or on to suit whatever your take on the issue might be.

Overall, I am quite pleased with the purchase. There might be better units, but they will likely be 1) uglier (subjective I know), and 2) cost more. For disclosure, I have had the product for only two weeks, but I have ran it constantly taking it through the paces.

title: An amazingly quiet, mid-power air purifier.
text:
I wanted an air purifier for my living room where I have some electronics that need protection from smoke and dust. I also needed a unit that could realistically and reliably clean the air sufficiently in this 250 square foot area and help remove the odor and particulate matter from occasional cigarette smoke that may drift into the room. It's a large volume area because of the high cathedral ceiling and open design. While that may not sound too difficult to accomplish with many mid to large air purifiers, I also wanted a unit that was as silent as possible, and that's not so easy to find.

I spent several weeks researching air purifiers and came away with the conclusion that IQ Air, Austin Air and Blueair are probably the best that the industry has to offer as far as big and powerful air purifiers go these days (IQ Air has a carbon filter with 5 pounds of charcoal and Austin Air has 15 pounds of charcoal ... 15 pounds!). So why didn't I choose one of those? Price, noise level, size and looks were the determining factors (although Blueair has good noise ratings and they look attractive, but are a bit on the pricey side). Excluding any of those models wasn't easy. Nor was it easy to cross off less expensive mid-power sized units from Sharp and Winix. I also had a difficult time choosing between several models of Rabbit Air. Decisions ... decisions....

In order to educate myself in the murky waters of outrageous air purifier claims, I turned to the internet, but at first I found no real help (not many websites review air purifiers). I had recently purchased a small, one-room air purifier from Alen and didn't do enough research. Turned out that I wasn't exactly thrilled with that purchase (although it's really not a bad unit per se ... I rated it 3 stars). Fortunately, I eventually found a website that took reviewing and testing of these products very seriously, which gave me more confidence when I decided to go for a more powerful (and expensive) unit in the living room. I highly recommend Air-Purifier-Power as the one and ONLY source (at present) to help shed some light on this less than stellar industry. Personally, I wouldn't rely on Consumer Reports as far as air purifiers go. I found them to be of little help and their testing methods for air purifiers have been under fire for years, and I can see why. What they rated highly gave me a good chuckle.

So now that I have the Rabbit Air 700A, what do I think? As the title indicates, this is a very quiet air purifier, perhaps one of the top two or three in the industry (of the ones that have fans ... I won't go into what I think about those that don't have fans). This unit has five different fan speeds (silent, low, medium, high and turbo). To me, noise level was as critical as cleaning ability. What good is an air purifier if it interferes with your daily living? I didn't want to have to turn up the TV to drown out a fan. Of course at the two top speeds (high and turbo), one can easily hear the 700A throughout the house. Still, its high speed is quieter than many products at mid speeds. So do yourself a favor and check out fan output (CFM) and the associated noise level (dBA) on any model you may want to purchase. The Rabbit Air 700A is about 46 dBA on turbo speed (@ 187 CFM) and under 21 dBA on silent speed (@47 CFM)! BTW, some products are even quieter than this, but check the CFM to see if they are putting out as much air at that noise level.

I chose the 700A over the 780A for a couple of reasons, even though I would have preferred black over white (not too impressed with the looks of this white model). The two reasons were value and noise level. These two models are virtually identical except the fan is revved up a bit on the 780A, making it a tad louder, but has the ability to suck in and blow more air and cover a little larger area. The first three speeds on the 700A (silent, low, medium) are indeed quiet, and the silent speed is aptly named. I have to get within 4 or 5 feet to begin hearing it. The CADR (clean air delivery rate) rating on the 700A and 780A is the same (except the 780A has a slightly better Pollen rating). As far as square footage is concerned, divide any number that these manufacturers spew out by two (normal ceilings) or three (high ceilings) and you will get a closer idea of what is realistic. If you assume the manufacturer's claims are legit, you may be in for disappointment (I'm pretty sure they calculate all these numbers based upon normal ceiling height and maximum fan speed, which is unrealistic in the normal home environment). I'd like to see a CADR rating at each fan speed and the use of volume in addition to square footage as far as coverage specification, but fat chance that these will ever be implemented.

What separated the Rabbit Air products from each other (the 700A and 780A vs their other models), as well as other manufacturers models, is the ability to choose a custom filter (they have four to choose from at present: germ, toxin, pet allergy and odor). This is a great idea, and one can order a specific filter type depending upon one's needs. I find this makes perfect sense. And installing and changing filters is simple and painless (pealing off the cellophane wrapper on these filters is a bigger pain than installing them). It also has a permanent pre-filter one can vacuum and/or wash, which I find a very important feature. Pre-filters pick up the biggest particulate matter, and I will no longer buy an air purifier without a cleanable pre-filter. Live and learn.

The ad states that it is a six stage purification system: anti-microbial pre-filter (read silver), anti-bacterial medium filter (additional dust catcher, which is unusual in the industry and helps not to overtax the HEPA filter), BioGS HEPA filter (I guess it gets that name because they added some anti-viral agents ... yeah, whatever), custom filter (not many companies I know, if any, have this option) and carbon filter (although I doubt there is much more than a pound of charcoal in it, but I haven't measured the weight). I guess the mysterious sixth stage is a negative ion generator (the good kind, but who knows these days?). I like the fact that their filter kits, which include the four changeable filters, are reasonably priced and are one of the better values I have found.

This model comes with a decent set of electronics and lights for giving you information, plus it performs automatic cycling (changes fan speed depending upon the air quality that the particle sensor reads), but it doesn't come with an odor sensor. This probably isn't too big of a deal since these sensors are hardly reference quality to begin with. However, even knowing the limitations of these sensors, I like the idea of having them included and thought for the price I paid for the 700A an odor sensor should have come with this unit. At least the particle sensor gives me some feedback (accuracy not withstanding) and a baseline to go from.

Rating air purifiers may not be too accurate unless one has used their particular model for a full filter cycle (anywhere from 6 months to a year depending upon the environment it is in). I've only owned this product for a little over 2 months now, and during that time I found the quality and performance has been very good. If things change during the year, I'll report back. So, between 1 and 10, I rate the Rabbit Air MinusA2 SPA-700A (that's a mouthful) an 8, or a solid 4-star rating, but this is assuming it will give me years of untroubled service (it does come with a 5 year warrantee, which is a big plus). Other than thinking it should have included an odor sensor (one of their cheaper models include this), I wish it had a more hefty carbon filter, say 3 pounds of charcoal at minimum, but it is what it is. This marginal carbon filter is the reason I selected the custom odor filter option (although I may opt for a different custom filter later on and swap them whenever I choose). I also felt that they should have provided a wall mounting bracket since they advertise it being wall mountable. Now if this bracket was an expensive to make add-on, I'd understand. But it's a bracket they make for a buck and sell for 10, so I consider this wringing out every cent they can from the consumer. I also had to laugh at their ridiculous claim concerning their "mood" light. Still, I'm pretty happy with this unit, but for the life of me I don't know where I can put it so it will be unobtrusive (but that would be the case for any of these devices).

Update 03/10/13: Well, it's been three years since I bought this machine and it is still going strong and is just as silent. I put in my third set of filters last month. I suspect that ripping out carpet, cutting several rooms of drywall as well as sawing wood flooring reduced the life of the second filter set by quite a bit. While it is obviously pulling out dust particles from my home, one has to wonder how much it really makes a difference in the long run.

Update 04/20/14: Another year (the 4th) and all is well. The price of the filter kit went up 10 bucks, however.

text:

For that purpose it works great, not that I have the expertise to actually measure air quality, but I run it continually in auto mode and once in a while it kicks into high when I'm cooking or when I'm removing the ash from my wood stove. I've seen it switch automatically between all three modes, although it doesn't seem to spend much time on medium. Anyway, that sensor is not a gimmick, it really does work. On the low (blue) speed, it makes almost no sound.

UPDATE: I've had it for about a year now and it's working well. One curious thing: If my wood stove overheats the house anywhere above 68 degrees, the Oreck always seems to shift into medium speed and stay there. This seems to be a function purely of temperature, not particulates in the air. The Oreck is about 6 feet from my stove.

UPDATE: Lately I've started to do a small amount of concrete work in my space --casting custom concrete blocks. If you've ever worked with concrete you know the dust gets everywhere. I think the problem with my use is that the sensor has become contaminated with the dust and continually signals for high speed. It endured about a week of concrete work --switching from low to medium to high and back down as needed, but after that it has pegged to high and stays there. I tried cracking the case (7 screws) and dusting off the sensor and around it really well with Q-tips but it still prefers high speed. Of course the manual speed settings still work, but I'll miss the sensor control.
