title: Excellent oder remover and really like the 'smart' part
text:
This does an excellent job of clearing out cooking oders from an open area that includes the kitchen, breakfast nook, and family room. It is really quiet, and even the fan speed's highest setting is not too noisy under most circumstances. And the fan and motor combination has a really high quality sound (not annoying and simply hums away efficiently doing its job). I really like the shape factor, which allows it to be tucked against walls in compact spaces. I prefer the simple black facade that I purchased, since that attracts the least attention and allows the unit to more easily blend in with existing decor.

I especially like the 'smart' features of using my Android phone to control this model with wifi. This is actually very practical, since the physical controls on the unit are extremely difficult to see when it is sitting on the floor. However, the app is a real pain to initially get connected with the unit, and there needs to be a set of tips / hints and FAQ to facilitate this. Also, several features, like the timer and scheduler, are only available with this wifi model.

I definitely like the Alexa skill, which allows me by voice to turn it on / off, set the fan speed, and set the mode to Pollen or Auto. However despite Rabbit Air's website mentioning setting timers with Alexa, I couldn't figure out how to do that (Alexa kept setting up a regular timer with the name that I used for my air purifier). I called Rabbit Air for a complete list of all Alexa commands, and per the call with a very nice rep, she responded via email to get back to me. However, after consulting with a colleague, she said that this skill is still being tested, so a full list of commands isn't available. Hmm, already released as a skill on Alexa for several months, and still being tested? Wonder if that means that the current users of this skill are defacto beta users? By the way, just like the Android app, this Alexa skill was a real pain to add with an Android phone. Had to use a laptop that had Alexa installed, and then the laptop's browser to complete the process. This also needs a set of tips / hints and FAQ.

Here are the Alexa commands that seem to work so far. Start with "set rabbit air to", then follow with any of the following words to set the fan speed: "silent", "low", "medium", "high", "turbo". Instead saying words for the fan speeds, can instead say the following for the fan's mode: "auto" or "pollen". I haven't been able to set a timer yet, even though that Alexa capability is advertised by Rabbit Air. If anyone else has more verified commands, it would be great if someone could list them in a review!

In addition to Alexa, this really needs integration with Google Assistant and IFTTT! This is already available from some of Rabbit Air's competitors, and at least the IFTTT integration would really increase its smart Home Automation capabilities (in addition to allowing it too be added to Google Assistant via a 'back door').

Overall, very happy with its air cleaning capabilities and Smartphone app functions. However, it would really help new users with the set of tips / hints and FAQs I mentioned above.

title: Extremely quiet and efficient

title: Great Product But Silent Customer Service Assistance
text:
Bought one of the SP001 units in September to possibly help with the wildfire smoke seeping into our home. The SP001 unit is fairly light and easy to handle to place it wherever you need it. The sound is somewhat elevated when on "high," but it automatically cycles down after a while and becomes whisper quiet. Also, the ability to shut off the devices light display makes it great for sleeping. The instructions for the unit and remote are simple and easy to follow; and, the remote's features are very good for our homeowner needs.

Overall, great pricing, nice features, and easy to install (and reasonably priced) filter elements. For now, we have "upgraded" our filters to "medical grade quality" and are confident that our units are helping keep our home safer. We liked this unit enough to purchase a second one in early November to help increase the specific coverage areas in our home without having to move a single unit around every day

My only issue has been with the complete lack of response to my emails to "team hathaspace". Following their printed information - Hathaspace.com/pages/warranty - merely provides text information. Any attempt to seek and provide user registration information simply routes back to the initial page - just goes around in a circle. No way to register my purchases, and no other options or windows that help. Have sent three emails (two in late September and one in mid-November seeking help), but no response to date.

The units we have seem to be working just fine, and we are very happy with them, but so far, "team hathaspace" has not responded to any of our written requests for assistance. Yes, I could call (and wait in line for however long these days) to try to eventually reach a live person, but with all their enclosed and specific printed information and the onscreen pages, that should not be required. On this detail, I am not impressed.

text:
I bought this Ozone Machine to hopefully clear out the smell of smoke brought on by a house fire. After several days of constant use in different rooms, the smoke smell slowly went away. If you turn this thing up too high, your house will start smelling like chlorine. Personally, I found it to be pleasant, but you need to turn it down if that is the case.

SIDE NOTE: (WARNING)

This thing is not an air purifier, do not use it as one. I left it running in my room for about 2 months on medium settings. I usually kept the door closed as well as the windows. One night I had a lot of trouble breathing and I ended up going to the ER. While I was there for the day I started feeling better but as soon as I got home and into my room the trouble started up again. This Ozone Machine had put dangerous levels of O3 in my room and was essentially destroying my lungs slowly over time without me even knowing.

BOTTOM LINE:

This thing works great and does what it is supposed to do without error, but if you are going to make the purchase you need to read the warnings and safety information. Keep your rooms ventilated and only use it as needed. It will get rid of the smell of just about anything. Food, smoke, pet urine, you name it. Solid choice!

-EDIT: OK, I found the problem. I ordered it with the option for the filters to already be installed. So, since I already own 2 other units like this, I wondered if Amazon had properly installed the filters. When I checked it out, I saw that all 5 filters were still wrapped in plastic. WTF! What's the point of offering the filter install option if I have to take out all the filters, unwrap, and put it back together! Normally, I would just have to unwrap and install. But, the option to have it already installed is no advantage. In fact, it adds an extra step. And, without realizing that the wrap was still on the filters, it adds confusion and aggravation. At least let me know that they're still wrapped, but noooo.

So, the unit is fine (and has 5-star performance). But, I don't whether to blame Amazon or RabbitAir for the waste of my time with the filters. So, one star removed for this bonehead option. Buy the unit, but DON'T BUY IT WITH THE FILTERS INSTALLED OPTION!

title: We sleep better and breathe easier with our Rabbit Air - with some minor exceptions.
text:
I waited a few months to review this air purifier. The air quality in our terrible town is often at unhealthful levels. My wife and I began to develop allergies from the many pollutants in the air. despite changing our central air filters every two months, this didn't solve any issues for us. Along came the Rabbit Air I ordered from Amazon. Pooling some gift cards together made this unti more affordable for us here than direct from the manufacturer.

In the first two weeks running the purifier at night, we immediately recognized the transformation in our sleep habits. We both were able to breath a little easier. The bonus of the white-noise effect helped to drown out some of the local nightlife and street racing nearby.

The first night we realized the lights were simply too bright on this machine. I took the liberty to purchase some adhesive light-dimming dots to place over the operational LED lights. If you sleep in total darkness, this unit will be as bright as the noon day sun without it.

The wonderful pollutant sensing feature of this device is great for day-time use, but when the unit ramps up and down in the middle of the night it can disturb the sleep. We generally now leave it on medium for a constant clean and continual noise level that we both easily sleep with. Just don't forget to turn it on before one of you falls asleep, there is a triple tone for turn on and turn off that is quite loud in a silent room.

Cleanup is easy, when we vacuum the house weekly, we simply open the front and take out the front screen of the filter.

Pros:
- Cleans great
- Looks great
- Easy to operate
- You can feel/breathe the difference.
- Replaceable filter seems inexpensive when compared to the initial cost of unit.

Cons:
- Cost
- Super Bright LEDS
- Musical startup and shutdown can disturb someone if they are sleeping.
- Automatic adjustment feature is difficult to sleep with due to the velocity of the fan changing constantly.

title: I rounded up
text: This is between a 4 and 5 star product for me.  This is the sixth Alen I have bought since October.  I gave my mother this one for Christmas.  Amazon had a deal on an open box with a smoke filter and it was too good to pass up.  The Flex uses the same filters as the 45i including the heavy smoke filter with over 2 lbs of active carbon.  My air is already almost always clear of PM 2.5 with as many filters as I have in my house.  What was a little high was HCHO and TVOC.  Most people would want these filters for wildfire smoke, for me cooking odors and chemical reduction is a priority.  Most people shopping for this purifier are comparing it to the 45i.  Their is about a $100 difference between them.  For that the 45i gets wifi, auto mode, an ionizer, and a little more CADR.  Ionizers are a hotly debated topic on here and I only use mine before I vacuum to collect a little more dust.  I do love the Flex and my mother does not need to have her purifier on the internet.  So my best advice to you is to buy either one if it comes on sale in your color.  The 75i is a true workhorse, but even on sale is much more expensive.

title: I have become air obsessed
text:
What started as browsing for an inexpensive air purifier became a $2000 investment in health. Years ago I took efforts to make sure my water was double filtered coming from our well. To this day our water is the best I have ever tasted. Even my wife noticed the quality difference and she is usually oblivious to such things. Everything started a little over six weeks ago. When I finally decided an air purifier was in our best interest I researched every make and model possible, as I’m sure many of you do. Alen had a few bad reviews, but their specs and design grabbed my attention. Their filters are exceptional and longer lasting. The machines are very energy efficient. My 75i never goes over 20watts. Haven’t tested the 45i yet, but assume it is close. No point in running a machine 24/7 if you are worried about your electric bill the whole time. Alen can be controlled remotely using the GoSund app and it gives you the pm2.5 count as well. Up to this point other reviews have all mentioned what I have said so far.
I studied cadr rates and air change intervals ad nauseam. The thing I learned is that the square footage claims by all manufacturers are exaggerated if you truly want allergy free air or close to it. A cadr of 247 might effectively filter up to 375sq ft not 800 ft. That is figuring closer to 5 air changes vs 2 per hour. Again all manufacturers do this. I’m running two 75i’s and one 45i in an area of 1400ft with high ceilings. Is my air cleaner than it ever has been? You bet. One would of helped for sure, but the three working together purify the air a little quicker and much more often. It still takes an hour or two to get air quality at good levels after cooking. No exhaust fan present in our house. I got Covid a month ago today and I honestly believe the quality of my air made an incredible difference. The H13 hepa filters most likely reduced the amount of the virus in the air along with a hepa vacuum. I know most people can not afford more than one of these. For bigger spaces a 75i is where you need to be looking. If sleeping problems are more of an issue than the 45i is perfect for bedrooms. It is where I have mine.
Alen reminds me of Apple. I resisted Apple for years. Telling myself they were overpriced and overhyped. I’m writing this review on an iPad so what does that tell you? Once you are on their ecosystem everything else looks inferior. Same thing with Alen. When I was shopping for my third purifier on Black Friday I was only looking at Alen. They make you feel good about their products, service, warranty, and overall quality. We all need to feel good a little this year and not like you can go on vacation. Alen is an American company, so at least some of the benefit stays here. Look if you have read this far you most likely have an interest in this product. Try one. A 75i if you can swing it financially or a 45i if you have a smaller space or Christmas spending has got out of hand already. You will never know what you did without one. Oh and if you buy a second or third I’m betting it is an Alen.

If you try to troubleshoot it with this company you'll get gems like this:

Rep: "Well, after 1 year, use or no use, the wires inside the purifiers die and need replacing"
Me: "So, every year or so I must spend another $100 to get these working again?!!!"
Rep: "Yes, Sir. That's correct."

Reminds me of the time the mechanics at an auto dealership told my Dad that they couldn't fix his driver side window (it jerked going up and down) because it was old. ?!? lol. I said What?! Did the window grow up or something? Dad was like yeah, what the heck!?

For contrast, I bought the twin pack of the full size Ionic Breeze with GP ($500 at the time) back in 2001. 10 years ago. I have one right here beside me, still going strong with the original blades, purifying the air. I haven't had it in service non-stop for the whole 10 years but at least 5 years of continuous service for sure.

Save your money. Pay a little more for quality. It almost always lasts longer and it almost always does the job right.

title: Not worth the money
text:
I got this item 'free' when I bought two of the Ionic Breeze GP a long time ago.

Sounds perfect for the bathroom and the nice little night light was actually a good feature. But, did I notice a difference in air quality in the bathroom? Nope. The unit was for sure removing dust and 'stuff' from the air, the dirty collection blades attest to that but the blade surface area is so small and the amount of air being cleaned so tiny that it really didn't make any difference in my opinion.

These units, especially the earlier models, are designed in a way that makes it difficult to keep the whole unit clean. The collector blades can be cleaned easily enough when there is enough space to actually get a microfiber cloth between the blades. Beware the units that don't allow good access to the interior for cleaning. Lots of gunk will build up inside that is unreachable.

So, if you have a lot of problems with allergies or something along those lines then this is a worthwhile purchase - it does clean the air, the blades get dirty. Otherwise pass on it.

title: Your car’s cabin could be a hypochondriac’s nightmare.
text:
I drive part-time for a rideshare service. I drive full-time taking my kids here and there. So, I was very interested in getting a purifier for my car. Pollen count can get quite high when the weather gets warmer here in DC. Meanwhile, someone (including myself) will be invariably sneezing or coughing in my car during the colder months. Your car’s cabin could be a hypochondriac’s nightmare.

It's hard for me to say, though, whether this product works as advertised or not. Like the streetlamps in my neighborhood, I’m glad that they are there but I don’t think too much about them. They run in the background and I know that my life is safer/better for it.

I will just share some factoids:
1. I uploaded to my phone an app that measure decibels. With the fan at half-power (half the lights show up on the ring), the app reads 38 dB. With the fan at full power (all lights show up on the ring), it registers at 58 dB.

2. Apparently, there are some bugs that Wynd knows about and is working to fix. Specifically, the Wynd device may not let you know you’ve paired your phone with it even though you already have. Below is an email exchange to help you get the full picture of this issue.

-======================================
[Me] It appears that my Android phone and Wynd Essential won’t pair. I follow the steps but I do not get a “confirmation” that the two have paired successfully.
[Wynd] I apologize, it seems that a small number of people are being affected by a bug in the Android version of the app that’s causing the app to not recognize when a device is being paired and thus will continue to state that it is waiting to pair with a device. I’ve listed your specific case to the development team, and they are working on a fix for that.

If you can toggle Night Mode on/off or change the fan speed from your phone, it means that you are paired.

[Me] “I DO NOT see a button that allows me to turn on/off Auto Mode though.”
[Wynd] You are correct, I ran a test on my Essential and I am also missing the “Auto Mode” button in my app. The development team has explained to me this is a bug and should be fixed soon. You should be able to turn on/off Auto Mode when your phone and Wynd Essential are paired.

[Me] Does Wynd Essential default to the auto-mode when it is turned on?
[Wynd] The Essential will not default to Auto Mode. It should always default back to the last known fan speed. For now (until this bug is addressed), you will have to manually press the “A” button to enable auto-mode.

[Me] “Oh … can you turn the Wynd unit itself on/off via Bluetooth? Or is that always done manually?”
[Wynd] At the moment, you can only turn the unit on/off manually.

That said, I would still recommend the device. It should be able to “clean up” the air within your 8x10 office without issue. It certainly can cover the space of your car’s interior. It probably would work fine enough if you took it with you the next time you stayed in a typical middle tier hotel room (with square footage clocking in at 325 sqft).

I do like how you can access a few functions via the Wynd app. I like its design (although I wished they offered other colors). I’ve been satisfied with their level of customer service. Once the “bugginess” has been addressed, I’m sure I’ll breathe easier (see what I did there?).

title: Get Winix instead.
text:
You can’t tell from the pictures, but once you open it you realize that it’s another cheap chinese product copying other brands.

The plastic is cheap, there is no washable pre filter, and the display LEDs are also a generic cheap panel that is way too bright.

When I say the plastic is cheap, I mean this thing is built like the children’s toys you’d find in the toy section at a pharmacy. Fat screws visible everywhere.

It also doesn’t move that much air at its highest setting.
The power cable is also very short and looks very cheap as well.
The design doesn’t even make sense either. It has holes on the side that let air in while the front grille has minimal space for air flow. This isn’t going to do a good job of stopping large particles before they get to the filter at all. This reduces life of the filters.

This isn’t exactly a bad unit, but it really shouldn’t be worth $160+.

I also own a Winix air purifier and it is MUCH better at this price point. I was shopping for other purifiers because I was wondering if there’s something better out there than the Winix brand. That’s not the case with this purifier at least.

This filter definitely cleans air which is why it has high ratings. But every filter cleans air. There’s no way this unit should sell for more than $99.

This very expensive item seemed to have the highest reviews so I threw caution to the wind and paid the price for this air purifier. When we walked into the closed room in the morning the room smelled fresh and clean with NO hint of any cigar smoke whatsoever. I can honestly say it was worth the price tag. Of course I realize I will have to purchase new filters every so often but that's par for the course.

I noticed that it works harder when the heat is on. (Purchased in late Feb.) **Changing out the furnace filter more often helps the quality of air, and stops me from coughing, IMO.

Yes, the filter isn’t cheap, but it’s good for a year, pending the level of filth it has to clean throughout the year. I’m checking it monthly because I’m retentive like that, but I’d rather be able to breathe and not blow my wad on something I don’t need than something I actually do.

text: I purchased this air purifier with the hope it would help eliminate the mold problem I have in my house in two ways, first, that mold and mold spores might be cleared from the air and, second, that the endotoxins the mold produces would be eliminated.  I had added the toxin filter to the stages.  I placed the unit in my basement of 1000 sq ft.  I used smoke to test the range of filtration since it is advertised to clean a 700 sq ft area.  At best, the filter could pick up the smoke in a 15 by 15 space or 225 sq ft. After one year of use, it made absolutely no difference in the basement, even after confining it to 500 sq ft.  I replaced the filters with new ones and tried it in my living room, which is 260 sq ft.  It seemed to help a little, but I still cannot enter that room, like the basement, without wearing a respirator.  I have learned that mold spores can measure 0.003 microns, so all the hype about HEPA filters clearing 0.3 micro particles is not so helpful.  I replaced the filters again this year (brand new ones) and tried placing in a new travel trailer - only 120 sq ft.  I had hoped it would clear the fumes gassing off the new trailer - VOC's volatile organic compounds, especially since it had charcoal and the toxin filters.  After 72 hours the machine says I need to replace the filters - brand new filters lasted on 3 days and those filters run $95 a pop.  Way over priced, doesn't work.  Nice try

title: Allergy sufferers here...don't know how we lived without these before now
text:
What can I say? The Rabbit Air MinusA2 has been a godsend for us.

We live in a really heavy juniper area...to which both my spouse and I are quite allergic, and the allergy season for that lasts about 3 months each year. Spouse gets it worse than me, but it's pretty miserable for both of us. Me, I then get the double-whammy of ragweed, chamisa and other late-blooming pollens which are really bad. Both seasons, when my sinuses are screwed up, I'm far more prone to migraine headaches.

We decided to take the plunge and, after a lot of online research, buy two units -- one for each of the rooms in which we spend most of our time each day. (We may yet purchase a third if finances hold up, to cover the middle of our open-plan house.) The air purifiers arrived in original manufacturer boxes, with the 'odor control' filter as the extra optional customized fourth stage filter. Suits us just fine. Boxes were sturdy, with styrofoam inserts to hold the purifiers. There were three separate sets of instructions on how to set up the purifier -- a Quick Start single-pager, a longer user guide, and also a large illustrative sticker on the inside of the front cover. The only real hassle was removing all the plastic on each of the filter stages save the pre-filter. (Note: You GOTTA remove the plastic filter wrappers or the purifier won't work at all!) Took care to note which way was marked 'Front' on each filter component on re-assembly, put the front cover on and set it to running.

We both noticed the purifiers on Auto mode ran at pretty high speed and indicated poor air quality for about the first 10-15 minutes before quieting down. Then, after that, they went to higher speed maybe every 20 minutes or so for perhaps 20-30 seconds tops. Now, after owning them for a while now, we've noticed neither of them is running at higher speed nearly as often. (Although they nearly always react when we walk near them, probably because we're raising dust from the pile carpeting they're on.)

Over the last week, the difference for us has been dramatic. Oh, we still suffer the allergies, but we can easily tell the difference between when we're outside versus inside, in terms of being snuffly and having itchy eyes. Another common effect during heavy pollen season is we accumulate a lot of house-dust, most visible on polished surfaces like my desk. The day after I fired up the Rabbit Air, I dusted my entire home office...and days later, it's basically still mostly dust free.

Pros:
- Really purifies the air, to a degree cheaper air purifiers and filters just can't match in my experience
- Have noticed general household odor reduction overall, especially after the purifier's been doing its thing after we've been cooking
- Attractive unit design, and I like the idea it can be mounted on a wall; still haven't quite decided whether to do that here though
- Definitely dead silent on the lowest fan speed, just audible on low. Can definitely hear it on medium or high (and of course Turbo), but it's not an unpleasant noise by our standard; certainly no more noisy than when the heat pump central air comes on.
- Rather energy efficient for an air purifier

Cons:
- Other people have mentioned this: It would be nice to have an automatic / pollen mode that ignores the light levels entirely and just stays active, including with the mood light and air quality sensor light. However, at least in Pollen mode, the unit will change speed based on impurity levels detected, even if the lights won't stay on. (Given pollen is heaviest at dawn and dusk, that's the setting we use on both units.)
- Yeah, it's very pricey for an air purifier. But after the research I did, "You get what you pay for" seemed to be one of the truisms. Only if one jumps to the way, way more expensive (more than a thousand bucks) models were the results and performance noted to be better than the Rabbit Air models. When when I looked at the models priced in the 150-300 range, results and reviews were mixed, but I was concerned at how many were of Chinese manufacture and accompanied by reviews that dinged them for noise, durability, manufacturing quality, and effectiveness. (Also did NOT want to buy any purifier that had filters reported to out-gas on initial use. That would not be acceptable at all.) There's almost no point in buying a sub-hundred dollar purifier...as we've already learned with some of the other cheap ones we've bought over the years and found they didn't really help at all.

Just Is:
- I know some folks have said replacement filters are expensive, and they have a point, but at the same time it's still competitive in pricing versus replacement filters for other makes and models of air purifiers at roughly this purifier-quality level, and these ones are supposed to last about a year. I for one plan to disassemble and clean what I can -- washing the pre-filter and vacuuming the others -- about every 3 months; pre-filter monthly, as recommended, of course. Word is Rabbit Air has promotions every now and then which can reduce the replacement filter prices somewhat. But seriously, when I divided 'time between replacement' by the price of those replacement filters, the Rabbit Air is cheaper than most -- particularly since a lot of those have you replacing every 3 months.
- For example, the Rabbit Air is often compared to Blue Air models. Well, the latter cost more, use way more energy, are much louder, and their filters are significantly more expensive.

Would we buy these again, if given a chance to reconsider? Yes, no question. The only unknown at this moment is just how reliable and durable these air purifiers will be over the long haul. I would definitely revisit this review if something goes wrong and we're not able to resolve it. For now though, we're both enjoy much better sleep, and as I said the allergies aren't gone, seeing as how our house isn't and can't be hermetically sealed -- but the allergies are quite manageable now. Also looking forward to having to do a tad less dusting around here...

title: Well made, extremely quiet
text:
I did a lot of research and looked at tons of different products from Allen, BlueAir, and others. I'm very happy with the RabbitAir, you get a lot of features such as air sensors, ion generator, carbon filter, etc. that you don't see in the competitors until much more expensive products.

The biggest consideration for me given that I am sleeping next to it is how quiet it is. It has a "silent" mode that is truly silent, I have to hold my hand over the output to even tell that it is doing anything. Even the low and medium modes are still perfectly reasonable to work with it a few feet away. Compared to the competition, the rabbit air gets as quiet as 20.8 dBA, where something like the blue air classic 205 starts at 32 dBA, a huge difference.

My only complaint it the night mode. If you have it in auto mode (which works well) and the lights go off or it gets dark in the room, the filter automatically scales down to silent mode and turns off the lights. I prefer to have it on low as I am sleeping, so I have to push the button a few times to change it to manual mode and then change it back in the morning. If I leave the room with the lights off during the day, it will stay in silent even if it should be filtering faster. Every other feature on the machine has some way to turn it on or off, but the night mode does not. I'm considering rigging up a small LED and taping it to the front over the sensor location so that it doesn't trigger, but I shouldn't have to jury rig something in the first place.

title: You really can't put a price on clean air!
text:
I hemmed and hawed over this purchase for a couple weeks, because 600 bucks is steep enough that I won't commit to a purchase lightly. But I took the plunge. Winter's coming on, the windows are all sealed up, and I'm starting to get a mold problem. Mostly noticeable in my indoor plants after watering or on windowsills if condensation builds up and drips, I'll get a white fuzz buildup. Well, I did a deep clean of everything, and ran this Alen air purifier on the highest settings for three straight days, periodically moving it from room to room (I live in a 1000 sq ft apartment), before the air quality indicator finally switched from red to yellow. Now I have it on auto and it stays blue for the most part, really only switching back to yellow or red if I do something to stir up dust, like vacuum or run the clothes dryer or something. Now going back to the white fuzz buildup, I surgically fried the dirt with a little butane pencil torch to kill the mold without harming the plants or poisoning the soil. Then watered them. After week 1, the mold had grown back to about 50% of what it usually does. I blowtorched and rewatered, and then the mold was just a fraction of what it used to be. Barely noticeable at all. So that's a pretty clear indicator that the spore count in the air has decreased by I'd estimate 90% in two weeks. And that's just with one unit running.

Noise level is comparable to a normal box fan, and tends to blend into the background as white noise. You really only notice it if you have it set to Auto and it switches speeds when you're in the room. Visually, while I'm no interior decorator, I would think this would blend in with any sort of decor. Neutral colors and rounded edges give it an almost organic feel.

Should you buy this? Well like the headline says, you can't put a price on clean air. 600 bucks is steep, no doubt about it, and you will have to replace the filter about once a year so keep that in mind as well. Unless you buy one for every room it's not going to be a magic overnight solution. With just one if you run this thing for long enough, and move it around, it WILL clean your air. So if you're done screwing around and want your air cleaned, then yes, you should buy this. If you're not done screwing around yet, this will still be waiting for you when you're ready.

text:

In desperation we set it up in the middle of the condo, hoping for a slight improvement at best given that it's rated for a maximum of 800 square feet and we were challenging it to deal with about 1000 square feet on two levels. Much to our surprise within a few hours the smoke smell was gone! I happen to own an air quality detector, and while the air outside was at 45 ppm of smoke particles, inside the air measured 4. This unit is pricey compared to others, but the extensive automated controls, ease of use, effectiveness and lifetime warranty make it well worth the investment.

title: Just plain works
text:
After one year of using the Rabbit Air Minusa2...I consider the purchase "money well spent" on a product that works as advertised.

Just replaced the filters after one year of use and boy could I tell the filtration system does its job. I consider our house to be "clean" by most standards so I was surprised at the level of contaminants obvious on the first two filters...(first filter and medium filter). I have no doubt the remaining 3 filters did their job as well. I did clean the first filter twice during the year...about every 4 months or so and this review encompasses what I noticed those two times as well. This is on top of the normal HVAC filtration system which has never been overly dirty anyway. For perspective, I run a MERV 12 filter on the HVAC.

The Minusa2 with the WiFi is extremely easy to use and I appreciate the ability to view the Minusa2 settings and monitor as needed...which is not very often. I tend to use the ionizer several times a month and the app make this a breeze.

The unit is installed about 6 foot off the ground, 30 feet from the kitchen. Never ceases to amaze me when the Rabbit Air comes to life while I am cooking on the stove...meals you wouldn't think put off enough particulates to set it off does. I also notice it comes to life if any of the doors leading outside are left open for any length of time especially spring, summer or fall. For reference, I keep the Minusa2 setting for sensitivity on the normal or middle setting.

The unit is very quiet day in and day out. Only time it is noticeable is when the fan is on max setting but even then it is not egregious to me.

Rabbit Air Minusa2 w/WiFi has worked extremely well in my situation.

title: Highly recommend; effective and quiet
text:
Wow! I've been afraid to write a review because I keep thinking I'm missing something.

Let me start by saying I bought 2 Oreck air purifiers about 20 yrs ago and they literally transformed our smaller home. I was having major sinus problems, nose bleeds, swelling of my sinuses and eyes, etc, and doctoring with 3 different doctors . Getting the purifiers was part of what I did to try to deal with my extreme issues.

We heated with a wood burner so I put one of the purifiers in that room. The other, I placed in our bedroom and kept the door closed when I could, unless I had to open it for the heat. When you walked into the bedroom, the air quality was noticibly different. The room with the woodstove, was noticibly less dusty. I could always tell when the filters needed changed because of the amount of dust on the furniture. As a side note, all my sinus issues also greatly improved.

We replaced the bearings on those machines several times over the years. Because of my husband's line of work, he had access to them.

We moved 3 yrs ago but I've been without those machines for 5-6 years total. Our new home is all cedar, has a big "great room" with a loft. (About 2000-2500 sf in that space alone) I purchased the large unit a week ago after we noticed a LOT of dust particles in the air. It was very bad and my furniture always had a lot of dust pileup, daily. (We also changed the filter on the AC.) Since doing both of those things, we have very little floating particles visible in the sunlight now and after 5 days, I have no dust on my furniture. And, the air just feels so much cleaner to breathe.

After seeing the difference with just the one, I have now ordered a second large unit that I will place in the loft, and a medium one that I will place in our bedroom. Going into allergy season for me, I'm trying to do what I can to be ready.

It is a huge investment, financially, to purchase 3 of these, but it will most likely keep us healthier and probably prevent sinus infections and other sicknesses. I have thought long and hard before spending this money, because it does not come easy. But my air filter/vacuum quit working 2 weeks ago and this investment was a whole lot cheaper than having to replace that vacuum.

We also have 2 Lab dogs in the house all the time, and a 3rd one (over 100#) 3-4 days /week. They are confined to the great room, where I have 2 dog beds next to the air purifier. I'm fanatic about preventing dog odors and this will help with that also.

I do highly recommend this product. On the "Auto" setting and Speed 1, it is so quiet you can't hear it. Speed 2 is also quiet but you can hear it a bit. Speed 3 is like a quieter fan.

I'm very pleased with this purchase and felt confident in making it because of my 20 years of experience with Oreck air purifiers.

*No one has contacted me about writing a positive review. No one has offered me any free gifts in exchange for a review.

title: Know what this is and what it isn't
text:
I originally purchased this for a room where I have a couple of aquariums that have a low-intensity/faint earthy smell. I liked the idea of having something small and quiet to help take the smell from "barely perceptible" to "not perceptible". For the price, it seemed worth a shot. Upon arrival I plugged it in and read the enclosed materials describing the technology behind it. It sounded impressive, but I wanted to leave it in for a few days to see if it actually worked. Unfortunately - it had little to no affect on the faint odor from the aquariums. So I decided to do some additional research on this technology (ionizer / ion generator) to see if there was any merit to the claims. I found that there are some, but they are limited and should not be classified as "Air Purification":

For example: "While ion generators may remove small particles (e.g., those in tobacco smoke) from the indoor air, they do not remove gases or odors, and may be relatively ineffective in removing large particles such as pollen and house dust allergens."

There is no "filter" in this product, so please be aware of what you are getting. I would recommend doing your research first before ordering to determine if this product will achieve what you are hoping for. For me it did not.

title: Money Well Spent!
text:
I rarely write reviews of products, and only do when I'm a believer. I purchased this unit directly from Amazon Dyson Store on sale. I should add I've been debating for several years to get one of these and am very happy with the purchase. I have mild allergies and my spouse has cancer, so I needed an air purifier and she needed a heater as she is always cold due to chemo treatments. We needed to replace our old large space heater, which was seeming more and more like a fire hazard each day. So we decided to buy the Dyson which combine machines and now have one less thing to plug in and take up space.

It has helped immensely with dust--we have three English springer spaniels and they are actively putting off dust and odor 24/7. We can tell that the air feels & smells cleaner and my dust allergies have been subdued.

The fan/cool mode works nicely as a fan should. Air flow can be widely distributed or directly, and has a range of speeds--which is a nice feature. I'm not sure why some people gave it low reviews due to the fact that the air is not cold--no where in the description does it say it's an air conditioner. The sound isn't too loud or abrasive and is actually very pleasing on any setting.

We think that the heater is great as well. It does in fact heat the entire dining room and living room (open concept) but standing directly in front of it, one would not know. I really like the wide range in the temperature settings and most importantly, it is not hot to touch. Dyson does advise to use caution when moving it, but I've not felt it ever get too hot. Finally, does not make my skin feel desiccated like other space heaters. It's a soft comfortable heat.

I regret not purchasing one of these earlier and hope to purchase the WiFi w/ heater and humidifier next year and retiring this one to my kitchen. In my opinion, it will be worth the price because if I were to buy a separate high quality air filter, safe space heater, and a quality humidifier--all with a Wifi feature-- I'm practically paying the same price for one device such as the Dyson. We can't wait to get it!

title: REVISED AGAIN AFTER MONTHS OF USE
text:
Revision, April 3, 2019
After a few months of use of the replacement we received I am happy to report that the Hathaspace Air Purifier is working well and doing a great job of cleaning the air in my home office. Any and all previous complaints on my part are null and void and I can say with confidence that this is the best air purifier available, as I have tried quite a few others. I am now giving it the 5 stars it deserves.

Revision, June 27, 2018
We received a replacement as soon as the Hathaspace purifier was back in stock. I have upped the review to 3 stars due to their stellar customer service. They were constantly in touch with me keeping informed about the replacement and they paid for the return of the broken one. Sometimes a product is defective through no fault of the seller, but the seller has the responsibility to make it right and in this case Hathaspace did just that. I will add that of four different air purifiers we have owned, priced from $99 to $200, the Hathaspace is by far the best of all. Hopefully the replacement will last a long, long time. I will revise this review again later once we know how the replacement is going to hold up and work as it is supposed to.

Revision, June 10, 2018
I want to comment on the Hathaspace customer service. After writing the above review they immediately reached out to me and offered a refund or product replacement. Since the Hathaspace was the best of (now) three other air purifiers that we have tried we really were disappointed that it failed so soon after purchasing. When it was working properly it was doing an excellent job of cleaning the air and making it smell and feel fresher. However, as I mentioned above it did have a plasticky smell initially that seemed to decrease as time went by and when it failed that plasticky odor came back many times more noticeable. It's unfortunate that these products aren't made of BPA free plastics.

Due to their excellent customer service I am upping the review to two stars, only because I feel that reviews should be more about product than customer service, although customer service is certainly an important aspect. But, the best customer service cannot make up for a faulty product. If and when Hathaspace sends us a replacement I will report back on the progress of the new product and give it a fair and honest second review. I sincerely hope that the original one we bought is a just a rare manufacturing defect because overall it is a great product when it is working properly.

title: Great Performance, VERY Long-lasting Media, with Minor Caveat
text:
Initial thoughts: silent on low speed, very subtle white noise on medium, and moderate (but again unobtrusive white noise) volume on high. As an *extremely* severe allergy sufferer, the PM2.5 meter I keep in my room via my weather station shows the unit is very effective, keeping indoor levels well below outside ambient! The auto-sensing feature works great too - it kicks speed to medium or high for an hour or so after vacuuming.

After 6mos use 24/7 in our master where our two elderly yellow labs sleep 12-18 hrs a day (eek!), I just took mine apart (the filter, NOT the labs, to be clear!) to see how things were looking, and though pretty caked up, the felt/odor pre-filter looks like it's catching 95% of everything... and it was VERY easily washed by hand in the sink - five minutes tops. Plus, they give you a backup odor/pre-filter. I'd estimate the HEPA filter will easily last a year or three under heavy use in a fairly high-dust environment.

The only caveat: after said 6mos of 24/7 use, a very slight bearing squeak started, but my g/f couldn't even hear it, and it only happens on medium speed. A tiny dot of oil on the motor bearing (very middle of fan/motor assembly) instantly took care of it. I'm sure Oreck would have replaced under warranty as well, but fixing myself was far easier!

Side note, I'm a HVAC/energy engineer (PE) and in my consulting days designed hospitals and clean rooms. That said, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this product. I've not read about any other units exhibiting the super minor bearing squeaks mine once had, so will consider that a one-off experience.

title: No more sneezing!
text:
I've only had this for a few days, but so far so good. I was sick of waking up everyday sneezing and constantly blowing my nose, so I decided to get myself a good air purifier to clear the dust and mold from my apartment. I wanted one with both a HEPA filter and an ionizer. This has both of those, plus a couple of other filters to boot. Even better, the HEPA filter is washable. The icing on the cake for me was the remote control, so I can set the purifier up high, where it is most effective. And it's rather attractive for an air purifier. With a three-year warranty, I figured this was the best one on the market for me (and I found it new for significantly less on eBay).

The day after it arrived, I did not wake up sneezing. What a relief!

I have yet to use the ozone function (which requires the space to be unoccupied), but I'm going to blast my bathroom when I go out today. I anticipate this is a function I will only use on occasion to deal with mold, but it's good to have the option.

Another nice feature of this model is the sleep mode, which turns off the ionizer, the UV light, and the LCD display, so that there's no light pollution, which I'm very sensitive to. The sleep mode comes in two speeds, as opposed to the five fan speeds for normal daytime use. The first night I found the lowest speed too loud, but I slept all night with it on the second night.

Did I mention it has a timer too? You can't set it to turn on while you're out (that would be an amazing feature), but you can set it to switch itself off after a half hour or more (in half hour increments). This is especially useful if you want to blast the ozone for a while and have it be done before you reenter the space.

title: Doesn't Seem So Smart
text:
I received this for my birthday. I've had it plugged in for less than 3 hours and I already know I'm going to return it. The "smart" air quality detection not only does not seem to work properly, it seems that it's programmed to say that it's doing a great job at what it's supposed to. When I first turned it on, it detected bad air quality. Makes sense since I have 3 pets and my home is very dusty. Within just a few minutes, I had noticed that the air quality went from bad to good. That seemed odd to me. It was too fast for the size of the room, the rate at which it claims to work, and the air quality I suspected I had to start. So I ran a little test. I brought it to the smallest room in my home, a tiny bathroom that has a currently smelly cat litter box in it. It took exactly 3 minutes to go from bad air quality to moderate, and exactly 1 minute to go from moderate to good. The bathroom didn't smell any better from what I could tell. I then tried it in a larger room and then a larger room after that and then another larger room after that. Each time, it started at bad air quality, exactly 3 minutes later it dropped to moderate, and exactly 1 minute after that it dropped to good. Larger rooms should take longer to purify than smaller rooms, but every single room had the same result. I then returned it to the original room I had it in, about 20 minutes after I moved it to test it. It had been running in that first room for about 2 hours before I started testing in other locations. One would expect that after only 20 minutes, the air quality wouldn't be so bad. However, I ran it and got the same result: bad air quality at the start, exactly 3 minutes to moderate, exactly 1 minute to good. And then I ran one more test. I have an always-dusty welcome mat in my entryway. No matter how much I vacuum it, it's always dusty. I brought it over to the purifier as it was running and indicating good air quality. I beat the mat right next to it. There was much dust in the air and I beat it for a while. There was no change to the "smart" reading: it still claimed the air quality was good, even as I could see the dust in the air around it, right next to the air inflow area.

I will say this is a very quiet air purifier. The filters seem very robust and it was easy to set up. Maybe it purifies really well and I'm missing out what it can do. But I won't have it long enough to find out. The smart air quality detection being programmed as such feels deceitful and I can't justify keeping something at this price point that does not truly have all the features advertised.

I am aware they produce some ozone and that this is not good for you. The cats go into their room only to use the litter box. We have 5 boxes. None of the cats sleep in this room. title: Auto-Adjust Fan Speed Issues
text:
Purchased this unit based on the seemingly favorable reviews, and the 'upscale' pricing, figuring it was a get-what-you-pay-for kind of a deal.

The unit is indeed very quiet on all but the highest setting, and has a very large filter, and has a nice display panel for the controls.

The issue I had was when the display lights were turned off (say for sleeping at night in bedroom, etc.) the unit would stay 'stuck' on whatever fan speed the unit deemed necessary at the time. It was like the sensor wouldn't differentiate between clean/dirty air unless the display lights were on. As soon as you would turn on the display lights again, the fan speed would slow down (provided the air was cleaner).
Not an end of the world issue, but still not operating exactly like it should.

If you look at the 1 and 2 level reviews, you'll find that most of them are from people that have actually owned the unit for more than a short while, and have had the unit long enough for issues to surface.

Seems a bit over-priced compared to a number of other brands, not sure if it's worth the money or not...ended up returning mine and haven't decided on a replacement.

title: Cleans the air well but caution using the ozone generator
text:
This small unit packs a lot of punch. To safely use it requires some understanding though. The hepa filter and additional carbon and ion filters will clean the air in a surprisingly large area. I use it in my garage where I smoke a cigar in the evenings - but I also supplement it with my shop filter system. Prior to using it, the shop system would clean the air but not eliminate the smoke odor. With this little cleaner running, the odor is gone by the next morning. The downside is the fan is too weak for the level of filtration and it does not pull the rising smoke through the filter immediately. I took one star for that.
Now for the detail any purchaser needs to be aware of. The ozone generator is really effective in removing odors - but it should not be used when people are in the area. Ozone can irritate the respiratory system. It isn't like you will be poisoned if you enter the room, but it is unwise to run the generator when you are spending time in the affected area. There is a note on the unit not to run it when people are in the area.
Having said that, it is the most reasonably priced ozone generator I have found and would be worth it just for that function. Ozone generators are very useful for removing seemingly permanent odors - but should only be used while the space is unoccupied.
All in all it is a small but effective unit at a very reasonable price. I don't think I would use it by itself to remove smoke - it simply takes too long - but it would be a nice unit for normal day to day room air cleaning.

title: Okay products. Have 2 A2s and one BioGS
text: I have 3 Rabbit Air units: 1 BioGS and 2 MinusA2 units.  On the upside, I think that the Rabbit Airs do a fair but not great job of clearing cigarette smoke smell that enters my home from neighbors, even if I run it on Turbo mode. I think that the units do help as one component of allergy management and were helpful when the more thick smoke from not-so-near forest fires drifted into town. As to longevity, my vintage BioGS unit is still going strong -- it was never meant to be super quiet, and thus lives in the livingroom. The BioGS has the advantage of a turbo mode that shuts off automatically after a certain amount of Rabbit Air defined time. The A2s are for quieter areas of the home. The A2s developed minor, but irritating high-pitched bearing noise at most speeds after a few years. For those with sensitive ears (I use them for a living), I would recommend minding the warranty expiry date, during which repairs are free-of-charge. I would also recommend taking a measure of noise if you have the tools, as when Rabbit Air listened to my unit, they did so in a conference room, which likely had noise that masked some of the Rabbit Air noise. Thankfully, a senior customer service person went above and beyond to help resolve the noise issue promptly, and for this I am truly grateful.

title: Love the air sensor, not sure Purifier worth $$
text:
I really appreciate the mission behind this company. If you travel a lot and stay in hotels/motels/wherever, you will likely be very surprised by the lack of air quality you are surrounded by. I was recently on vacation in Florida and stayed in a studio apartment with wall A/C unit near the beach. I brought the entire unit but only used the sensor due to unit having no battery power. It was really empowering to be able to see when the air quality was diminishing in our room and knowing I could improve our air by seeing that the air quality outside was 5x better. Instead of suffering through a night of poor air quality, I opened some windows (even through it was hot outside) and within 30 minutes the air quality was dramatically better in our room. I left the ac running on low so it was kind of a balancing act of comfort and air quality.

My main gripe is that I dont beleive the air purifier itself is extremely helpful in actually improving thr air quality on a large enough scale. For a 300 sq ft room, I cant see it really making a bug big enough impact unless you run it for hours and the battery isnt really made to leave it on for part of a day.

Its also pretty noisy if you want to run it on high, which is what you'll need to impact the air quality around you in any meaningful way unless you having it blowing 3-4 ft from your face.

I can see it being useful to position aimed at your face on a nightstand, while plugged in, if you sleep with earplugs like I do at night.

Overall, the air purifier has merit but needs improvements and I'm not sure it warrants the price yet.

The sensor is amazing but needs its own charger, which isnt included with thre air purifier so you have to travel with the entire unit to charge the sensor.

Love thr sensor and would recommend buying it alone.

title: Great product! I received it
text:
EDITED for important update 11/11/15- I highly recommend this product for people suffering from allergies. My daughter has always had asthma, she grew out of it a bit as she got older (shes 25 now) but she suffers a lot when she visits from my dog and cat. I even entertained the terrible thought of going pet-less for her to feel comfortable at my place, since she has been over more. So last night I had my first test of how well this device works. I had the ionizer/air cleaner on the whole day with occasional bursts of ozone on the low range (about 3 on the dial). I had a window cracked as i usually do. My daughter came over and was here for 5 hours and did not sneeze, cough, feel itchy, break out or use one tissue. In her prior visit just a few days earlier she went through 3 packs of tissues and was a mess :(. Although i do not suffer from allergies myself, the air is noticeably fresher and cleaner with no scents. I also feel given how small my place is the ozone might have zapped some of these mold spores floating around this time of year (warm fall here in the northeast). I have to say, if you have really suffered from allergies, especially to mold spores and airborne stuff this is a great product for you. Please remember to read instructions and the Q&A section on this item. It works and works well. A few other notes, the fan is really quiet, there was no humming or buzzing sound. The original review is below..

Great product! I received it, read the instructions carefully (please do this as well). In a small apartment (approx 700 sq ft) the low settings (about 3 on the dial ) worked wonders in about an hour. No odor from pets (dog/cat) etc. I have the machine elevated on a small table but after reading other questions/comments will try it on the floor. It has a very soft fan sound, no buzzing or humming. It is important to read up on the use of the OZONE part of the machine (left dial). You only want to use this on low while home for a brief period of time and not leave it on or on high settings unless you and pets and plants are out of the home. I always keep a window and the slider cracked in my place for ventilation even before I bought this so I feel very comfortable using it on low settings. If your place is more airtight I would consider using that feature sparingly for brief periods of time. The worry over too much ozone is pretty much alleviated once you read up on it, but you should as it is very important. The air in here smells amazingly clean. It is doing its job zapping ions and UV killing things *has a soft blue glow inside* from the UV light. My device came with the plates already inside it and just needed to plug it in. You can confirm this yourself by loosening the top two screws in back (before you plug it in of course) and pulling the hepa filter out from the top. I mention this because the instructions say to insert the ceramic plates but they were already inserted. I was looking for a good solution and think I found it in this device. I will follow up on this review when my daughter who is highly allergic to pets and other things comes by to see if it makes a big difference.

title: Passed a big test on its first day
text: We had just set it up for the first time (very easy) and it was humming along at automatic low speed showing a PM 2.5 reading of between 1 and 3 (very good).  We have it covering about a 750 sq ft area that includes a family room, open concept kitchen, breakfast room, hallway, and a hall bath.  We forgot about some rolls in the oven and began to smell something burning.  When we opened the stove, smoke poured out.  The rolls were black.  The PM 2.5 reading in the adjacent family room shot up to 77 (very bad) and the rooms reaked of smoke.  The PM 2.5 reading of 77 would probably be equivalent to about 400+ on the Air Quality Index Scale (AQI), so the air was terrible.  The unit immediately showed a red color banner and it kicked itself up to high fan.  Within 5 minutes or so, the air was clean, PM 2.5 was below 6, and the banner was green.  It returned to low speed automatically.  I don't know how it will perform long term, but it certainly was a star in its first few hours in our home.

title: Turning it UP reduced the odor it produces!
text:
I have three cats who share two large cat boxes in one small space (which happens to be located in my bedroom and next to my bathroom). I use a high quality litter and I scoop regularly, but three cats can produce a fairly pronounced stench very quickly in between box cleanings.

When this product arrived, I turned it on the very lowest setting possible, because I had read warnings about the very detectable odor it produces, even as it does a good job of eliminating (not masking, eliminating) the odor of the cat box.

Set up was easy. Unpack, plug it in, turn it on. Done.

My teenager told me a few days later, "ugh. You've replaced one gross smell for another gross smell." Sigh. He was right. I wasn't detecting an odor of feces, urine or canned Natural Balance cat food anymore. But the ozone scent was rather harsh.

After about a week, I experimented by turning it up, rather than leaving it on its lowest setting. Within minutes, the ozone scent was gone and has stayed gone.

It does produce a sound, but but it is a steady white noise sound, so it is not disturbing. As much as such an appliance can be considered attractive, this is a lovely little gadget. At least, it is not ugly. It's glow is nice - like a tiny night light.

And my cats actually enjoy it - they like to hop up on the counter it is near and "play" with the stream of ionic air pouring it.

I place air fresheners in all of our bathrooms, but those are generally used -- IF they are used -- by the human who created the offensive odor, after the fact. I am considering getting one for each of our bathrooms, so I don't have to politely remind the humans to use the air fresheners OR run in there, hold my nose, spray and run back out again.

text:

Perfectly easy to set up. Pull it out of the very well packaged box, remove plastics, remove a few bits of tape and plug it in. Easy peasy.

Efficiency, you bet and it has a Lifetime Warranty. You just in-Velcro the pre-filter to clean it when you wish. And replacing the filter is as easy as pulling the old one out and pressing the new one into place. Oh! And, the cover is magnetized. So you don’t have to worry about braking off plastic grip-things that normally hold covers in place.

It is really easy to carry with the built in hand grip. Really. Easy. Not bulky. And, the cord can be wrapped around the bottom section of the unit, do you aren’t fighting with a dangling cord if you decide to move it.

It is also light weight. They have really thought of everything.

I bought two.

And I bought two towers. The smaller towers are wonderful as well. They aren’t quite as quiet as the larger unit though.

Love them all!

text:

The unit is very quiet on the first 3 levels. 4 and 5 are a bit noisy in a quiet room. There is a noticeable smell for the first hour or so after running it for the first time with a new filter. Another great feature is that it uses a hardware check to make sure you’re not using a knockoff filter.

It’s very easy to move from room to room. Not too heavy and the strap is convenient. The app setup and registration of a new molekule is very simple and straightforward. I’ve read a lot of complaints about the iOS app and was concerned. Fortunately I didn’t have any issues and really like being able to control it remotely.

As mentioned, the one con is that it can be a bit loud on the highest setting.

title: Difficult to Review
text:
This is difficult to review, as air filters are notorious for being subjective with results. However, I have noticed a few things. First, it does very little to help with dust. We have this on the floor in our living room, and there is dust all around it within a day of vacuuming all over again. So this fails miserably in that department. (We have the pet filter pack). However...

My husband was pretty mad when I bought this, telling me how naive I was for falling for the empty promises air filter companies dish out. He was the one who pointed out the dust after we had it running for a couple weeks. But I bought it because we have a new baby in our house and tons of pets and allergies inside. I thought it was worth a try. I was disappointed when I noticed the dust and thought it was a complete waste. The turning point came when I started to cook. My husband hates me to touch onions and leaves the house for a few hours when I even so much as quarter one in our kitchen. One day I was cooking up a month of meals and had to mince up 2 hot onions, then cook them for 20 minutes on the stove. Normally this would have made our eyes water for days afterwards as hubby and I are very sensitive to onions. At the end of the cook time, my husband walked in the room behind me and asked what I was doing and realized I was cooking onions. I asked him, "didn't you notice 45 minutes ago when I started to cut them?" He got thoughtful and went back in the living room to look at the rabbit and realized the air quality light was red. After he realized that the purifier had successfully purified our house from stinging onion as I was cooking (my eyes didn't even water a whole room away as I was cooking them) he was convinced! There have been other instances that have continued to convince me since then- the sensor turns purple when my cat walks past. My newborn son puked near it and the sensor came on and the smell went away very quickly. Some food caught on fire and it took the smoke and smell out within minutes... I really like having this in our house! It has no weird chemical smell, has a nice white noise fan sound on high setting, and can be as quiet as a mouse if necessary! If you don't lose it the first day, the remote is very handy as well:) It doesn't take up much space, and the aesthetics aren't too bad either

title: Not happy
text:
Bought 2 direct from the manufacturer & received a week ago. My house isn’t big (less than 1,000 sq ft) & I keep all rooms closed off to the animals but the living room & kitchen, so I really only needed to clean the air in less than half the area than 1 unit is supposed to be able to clean. I have 3 cats & a small dog &, although I keep my home clean, an odor has developed in the last 6 months. As directed by the site, I purchased the carbon filters for people with pets.

I received both units & they immediately detected an AQI of 00. I ran them on “automagic” mode, figuring since 2 units are working to clean a small area, it should take no time. 3 days after receiving & running the units, I wrote into support because AQI was still indicating 00 on both units & I wasn’t noticing a change. They suggested I turn the fans up.

On Monday, I turned the fans up to 50%, which is what they have been running at since. They had me test the AQI on the units by burning toast & blowing out a candle. The AQI changed for both of these events, but not for the 2 days I had all the windows open. I don’t want to turn the fan up any higher because they do get fairly loud.

Since I still haven’t had a change in my air after running both units at 50% since Monday for 24 hours a day in a small area, I wrote support again. My current options are to spend more money to buy even stronger filters, with no guarantee, turn the fans up even higher to a loud volume, or pay to send the Milas back to receive a refund. The units are not small & I expect shipping will not be cheap & I haven’t heard yet what will happen to the $50 box of extra Mila socks I bought.

If you are purchasing an air purifier to help with pet odors, choose a different brand as these units do not help. 2 units rated for 1,000 sq feet each are not helping to clean the air in approximately 500 sq feet.

Not happy that I spent over $700 on these.

**Update - I shipped both units back. I believe the shipping was around $20 per unit. It’s been a while. I also had to pay to ship the additional unopened socks back. I would not have ordered the extra socks if the site had been clear that the filters I chose came with socks. So that was an additional waste of money. Buyer be warned.

title: Three Words - Save Your Money
text:
The only thing that Dave Oreck has succeeded in with these filters is a marketing gimmick. There is so much blow by in this thing that there seems to be more dust around it than in it. I love the demonstration where the unit cleans up the smoke in the little test chamber. Unless your room is this size, don't bother with this filter. Check out Consumer Reports review on the Orecks.. .dead last.

Doesn't it seem to be a dream that you can dip this thing into water and a little soap and it magically comes clean? Don't count on it. Next to industrial strength oven cleaner, NOTHING will get this clean if you smoke or cook within 30 feet of the thing. I went into my local store to ask about this issue and was given some simple steps to remedy this until I pointed out that the cell they had on DISPLAY showed the deposits in the center that I spoke of... oops!!!

The plus is that it does capture SOMETHING from the air but is a CADR of 30 REALLY worth the price? I think it would be more effective to put a fan in the window on the exhaust setting than to waste your money on this thing.

The ionizer? lol.. what an ionizer ACTUALLY does it dull your sense of smell.. So that fresh smell you THINK the machine is producing is actually in your imagination.

If you really feel the need to drop the cash for this, I have two that I would be willing to sell and include the Asail-a-Cell cleaner and replacement charcoal filters as a bonus. Never mind I wouldn't even do that to a stranger.

The certification this machine carries can be had for 500.00 I believe and the organization is not offering a seal of approval on ANYTHING. I guess maybe I should get one and stick it on my tailpipe.

title: Clearer Air in Just a Couple of Hours!
text:
The only other air purifier I have ever had was about $100 from Costco - and I didn't notice any differences from it, but I kept using it anyway.

THIS Flex air with the silver filter is very obviously making a great difference in a short period of time.

My new bedroom is small (about 180 sq feet) with two big, old, drafty windows and tall oak trees all around. When I dust, surfaces are dusty again within 24 hours. After noticing the dust accumulation and that I haven't really been feeling rested when I wake up in the morning, I decided to research and purchase an air purifier.

I plugged it in for the first time about 3 hours ago (that whole process took about 45 seconds after the box was opened - It's super easy to put in the filter.), closed the doors and windows to the room and left home.

I have just returned and the air in this room is cleaner! Absolutely!! It feels fresher somehow. Things actually look clearer, too. Maybe there was so much dust hanging in the air that it was actually kind of hazy in here before?

This is a slim machine, smaller than I imagined. It has a clean look to it that allows it to blend well into the background.
I really like the brushed bronze cover.

It is very quiet on the lower settings, but I have it on Turbo.

Turbo is pretty loud, actually. However, it's a white noise with a 'surf' like quality.
The Turbo sound doesn't bother me ... much. It's worth it for the benefits I'm already feeling.

Actually, it would be great if they would just 'go for' the surf sound on Turbo and give it a random, rhythmic quality - rather than the steady, rushing sound of a river over falls. I think it would be more soothing.

4 hours in and I KNOW this machine is doing what I need it to do - clean the air.
I know I can lower the setting to make it run quiet, I'm choosing Turbo because I'm tired of the dusty, pollen filled air.

I am very happy with this purchase!

I'll be sure to update this review after a few months - but, unless it breaks - I'll be ordering one for each of the other bedroom in the house.

title: If you want it to be worthwhile, run at least medium speed. Any less is near useless. Runs quieter than most cheaper filters.
text:
When I bought this, I bought it because I heard it's silent, hence it being in the title "Ultra Quiet", it's one of the selling points. Though it is near silent, it also makes it near ineffective. I use it as a general air purifier for about a year now. I just need it to pull the dust out of the air so I don't breathe it in. Truth is. if you want it to be worth the space, it is just a bit more silent than your cheaper air purifiers, but it will be heard. It's just the natural order of things. So for those of you that think "Ultra quiet and it still filters the air? WOW!" it's ultra quietly insufficient for what you need and if you want it to make a difference, you must turn it at LEAST medium if not high or turbo most of the time, ignore the automatic feature. And I'm in a CARPETED 200~ sq feet room (which makes it a bit more dusty), not the advertised 700 sqf that it's supposedly able to cover. A lot of air movement is needed to circulate that much air volume and there's no way around it, you can't have it be very quiet and still do a good job. That is, if you're going for the portable air purifiers.

The durability so far is fine, but I've never kept it on high or turbo for more than 3 hours at time. I don't know if it can handle that.
In automatic mode, it does a better-than-nothing job, my PC that's about 5 ft away still gets dusty as usual though, so I'm definitely thinking that it just doesn't push the air enough to make a significant difference.

For five hundred bucks, I'm not entirely impressed, however, I'll increase the stars if I can keep it on medium to turbo all day long without failing.
As for the smell, it does an OK job, again, not too impressed. I don't smoke or anything so I'm just dealing with the usual college guy room smell.
I've looked at this filter and the setup is pretty simple.
The ionizer I have off because I THINK it causes me to have lung problems, I remember the last time I had it on for two weeks or something, I was coughing a lot. Really bad coughs that goes into the night. Let me try it again, if it comes back I'll update. I mean, I heard that this thing emits an extremely low level of ozone that even parrots are okay with, so I don't know.

title: so far so good
text:
I didn't buy this from amazon, but ordered directly from the Rabbit Air website. I got one with the tree of life artist cover. The cover is very attractive with a thick shiny finish and appears it will hold up to being wiped down without getting ruined over time.

I won't go into extreme detail as I agree with most of the comments, just wanted to add some extras.

I'm not sure if the ones in Amazon's stock are a bit older, but the one I got has all the features.

It has both the particle sensor on the side, and the odor detector on the front. I read some reviews saying the odor detector wasn't on their unit, but perhaps it is back due to popular demand. It also includes a feature to disable the negative ion emitter as well, although I like to keep it on. Not sure if it is just my imagination, but any dust in the air seems to fall very quickly now. The unit gets dusty pretty fast as it is sticking due to the ions I guess.

Despite what I read online, it also has an indicator light for when to change the filter. The instructions show how to reset the indicator light which probably means it is just programmed to turn on after a year, although I can't confirm that. It has enough other sensors maybe it checks for reduced airflow but that seems unlikely to me.

If I blow into the odor sensor the light turns from blue to purple. heh, uh oh. Also, I made some toast this morning and it went from blue to purple, so it definitely works. I patted a pillow in front of the particle sensor and the light turned purple as well and kicked up the fan until it was happy. This morning I pulled the cover off and there were chunks of dog hair and other stuff on the first filter. I have the unit on a counter top, had no idea that stuff floats that high in the air.

You can adjust the sensitivity of the sensors low, medium and high. I changed it to high personally. They don't seem to be extremely sensitive, I tend to manually keep the fan on medium or higher, otherwise it will stay on silent or low mode if set to Auto. I guess my air quality is pretty good already, but I have the unit in a large room and I want it to keep pushing a lot of air around.

That would be my only con so far is that I don't think it will be very effective in a big open area if it stays on low. I noticed that when on silent mode, it is barely sucking any air. So the particle detector which is on the side will only kick the fan higher if the immediate surrounding air is dirty. I found the air quality indicator would be solid blue, but when I turned the fan to high or turbo, after a minute it turned purple as it moved much more air and started bringing some dustier air to the unit. That kind of irritated me but I'm sure it would do the job if I just left it alone rather then stand their and obsess over the sensors. (It turned bright red when I held a really stinky garbage bag in front of it, lol)

Having used a Austin Healthmate which is quite noisy, this thing in comparison is whisper quiet.

It is almost totally inaudible on silent mode and low mode. I don't have to turn up the TV at all on medium. Even on high it is amazingly quiet in comparison to the Austin. On turbo mode it is louder but about the same noise level as the Austin on medium. Granted, it doesn't push nearly as much air either, but it does a solid job, especially on high or turbo. You don't really hear the motor, just the whooshing sound of air.

The instruction manual now does not mention anything about 2 year filter. It instructs you to clean the permanent filter and replace the other ones every 12 months, and run it 24/7. To me that says the company is more interested in being upfront about the facts rather then try to trick you into thinking it is a 2 year replacement and then say in fine print only if you run it 12 hours a day. Could get expensive though.

About smoke. My girlfriend and I smoke in the garage, and it seeps into the house when we open the door to go in and out. The filter is doing a great job removing residual smoke smells in the house. For the custom filter I chose the charcoal one for this exact purpose, and it seems to really work well. Time will tell if it gets stinky before the year is up.

text:
