I had multiple interactions with their customer support and they were fantastic! After a short back and forth they sent me a new one. I've now had that one for about seven months. It's on 24/7. And, it still works just like it did when I first received it.

We had a cat adopt us late in 2018. We've had other cats in the past but have always kept them outside or in the garage due to my severe cat allergy. This time I wanted to keep her inside. So, we started looking for filters we could use to help mitigate my problem. We've had this in the kitchen dining area between the kitchen and the family room. About 600-700 sq ft total. To say it has worked is an understatement.

One of the best (most enjoyable if you get my humor) parts of this filter is when we're cooking something in the kitchen that puts off extra fumes or something comes in from outside, etc. The filter will automatically increase the speed until it's satisfied that everything is back to normal. Then it goes back to the lowest speed. It's amazing how quickly it responds to odors and smoke, etc. And, it never fails to bring a smile to us.

Just replaced the filter set for the first time. We keep it vacuumed up once a month. It's hard to say whether or not it's had any effect on our electricity bill but I suspect not.

Again, I can't say enough about the people at Hathaspace. They really care about their customers. And, with products like this, that's the most important part of the sale.

title: Stylish, a little pricey, a lot of filter layers, thicker than it looks
text:
We've used the Blue Air Purifier in our masterbedroom for years now. And while I don't change the filters every 6 months, I do every 12 months. We literally turned it on in the corner of the room and occasionally vacuum it, but we practically forget it's there. It runs quiet and moves a lot of air. And definitely cuts down on the dust in the room.

We're redoing our kid's rooms and the appeal of this unit was that it could be wall mounted, off the ground and away from little curious hands. So, it's a bit annoying you have to buy a $10 wall mount kit separately, but it's no biggie.

The unit comes well boxed, with your choice of personalized filters. When you unpack it, you have to open up and unwrap each filter layer. It's then that you appreciate how many "filters" are involved in the process. It's a well made item. I kinda ignore the "mood light" verbiage and view it as a night light. In Auto mode, it does a great job of sensing lights off and, overall, runs very quietly (occasionally ramping up the fan when it "detects" more stuff to filter).

It's an attractive unit. Now, it's deeper than photographed. So, wall mounting it, is not as sleek as the photos would have you believe. That said, it's nice to have the option to wall mount it, as many/most don't.

I think the Blue Air could learn a few things (they are reminiscent of the Beige computers of old) from Rabbit Air (which is more like an iMac). I think the Blue Air's do a lot more room air exchanges and the filters are thick bricks. But, they are definitely big, bulky, beige boxes. The Rabbit Air doesn't handle the same "volume" as effectively, but are comparably priced and ultimately a better looking unit with the option to wall mount. Though, the wall mounting isn't the most practical given it's size and then, there's handling the power cord.

I hesitated when I bought this, as I was curious about the Asthma and Allergy certified unit, that was more expensive, turns out, that's just an "Odor removal" filter on the same unit, with which you pay a premium to be certified for...here's from their website:

What is the difference between the MinusA2 Asthma and Allergy Friendly(tm) Air Purifier and the standard MinusA2 air purifier?

There is no difference with the air purifier itself, although the MinusA2 Asthma and Allergy Friendly(tm) Air Purifier has been certified by the Asthma and Allergy Friendly(tm) Certification Program to show that it is both asthma and allergy friendly for our customers. The cost difference goes towards the Asthma and Allergy Friendly(tm) Certification Program, which is the oldest and largest not-for-profit, asthma and allergy patient advocacy organization in the world.

When you purchase a MinusA2 Asthma and Allergy Friendly(tm) Air Purifier, you will automatically receive the Odor Remover customized filter. This is the specific customized filter our Rabbit Air team chose to use while we conducted the testing with the Asthma and Allergy Friendly(tm) Certification Program. If you wish to choose another customized filter, please purchase our standard MinusA2 air purifier where you will have a choice of 4 customized filters to choose from.

Up to you if you want to pay more for the certification or not.

title: Technology that really works!
text:
We recently acquired the newest air purifier made by Alen called the BreatheSmart. It has a number of Smart features that makes it effective and user friendly. In short it is wonderful. We have an open concept home, so it is kept in our living room which also opens into our kitchen and it has done a superb job covering the area which is probably a little over 950 Sq. Ft. The air is noticeably fresher and cleaner, and my wife's stuffy head seems to have been relieved. As an FYI, We also set up an additional Alen Air Purifier (T300) tower in the bedroom. I would definitely recommend getting the new Breathe Smart.
Visually speaking, the Breathe Smart is a super clean modern looking device that does a decent job blending into any decor. It is easy to to set up and the controls are intuitive. Filter changing is about as easy as it gets and anyone can do it. My favorite feature is the air quality monitor that uses simple colored lights (blue=clean, white = so so, red=dirty) to let you know how dirty your air is. If you set it to automatic, it will increase the airflow when it senses that your air is dirty. Once clean, it will turn itself down. It really seems to work. For example, when someone sits on the couch, or when the AC kicks on the unit goes to red. In the morning when I come downstairs the unit has had all night to clean an empty room and it is on blue. I really like knowing when the air has been "cleaned." This takes all the guess work out of when to run the unit and when to turn it up or turn it down. This is really GREAT!
We have owned other cheaper Air purifiers that we have purchased at big box stores, and are glad that we switched to the Alen units. Their machines have a lifetime warrantee and are significantly quieter than the ones we previously owned. Noise can become an issue. Lastly, this air cleaner has a filter change indicator light that tells you when you need to replace the filter cartridge. I do not know how long it will last, but our bedroom unit has been running on and off for more than 6 months now and we are only on bar two which is half way through the filter life, seems reasonable.

title: BIG BEAST PURIFIER
text:
The EnviroKlenz Air Purifier Plus is a LARGE, commercial grade air purifier. This puts my little Honeywell. Rated at up to 1000 sq ft., this will handle an entire modest sized house and at least an entire floor in a bigger house. The specs all speak for themselves and it is USA made. A rarity in today’s world.

This is obviously the top of the line here. I cannot think of another purifier that’s close in price or performance. With that said, something of this size and price, you really have to need it. It’s an investment. Not only to initially purchase but to maintain it as well. It would be ideal for someone with severe allergies or compromised breathing. Would also be great in an office complex or other commercial environment.

Let’s get to my thoughts:

Performance: I have to rate it a 10. With two stages of filtration and UV bulbs, basically nothing escapes it! And it is reasonably quiet, especially on the lower settings. Certainly fine to live with, even in a den or bedroom. Ours is in the dining room we don’t use, and adjacent to a litter box. It has done a TREMENDOUS job reducing dust, hair and odors not only in that room, but the whole house! We do not smell like a cat house anymore!

Appearance: Quite frankly it’s a industrial looking and almost ungainly given the size. The wheels work to move it around but I just picked a spot in my dining room and left it there. You wouldn’t want to move this around daily. And probably wouldn’t want it somewhere extremely visible.

Value: It’s expensive, as are the filters. Does that make it a bad value? No. But I think it narrows the market down quite a bit. You want the best, you buy this. No doubt. But if I’m being honest, there are options for less money that do most of what this does. In the end you get what you pay for.

title: After 3 Months of Constant Usage, The Avari AV600 Has Greatly Improved My Sinuses! Customer Service from Pado is Great!
text:
The Avari AV600 Air Purifier is small and extremely portable. I kept the box that the company shipped it in and took it with me when I visited my elderly parents in Tennessee during the 4th of July holidays. I was there for nearly ten days and kept it operating in one of the guest bedrooms. I did this as a trial run. It didn't keep me awake. In fact, I couldn't even hear it. I took the AV600 back home with me to Chesapeake, Virginia. I unpacked it and put in my bedroom.

I must be honest and I say I don't dust my bedroom as often as I should. I am busy working two jobs, singing in the church choir, and taking care of a family of permanent "house guests." Normally, in October, when the weather changes from spring to fall, I get serious sinus congestion that often leads to at least a cold or a mild-to-serious sinus infection. In 2017, for the first time in many years, I got through October with only some mild sniffles. My girlfriend, Tammy, can vouch for this. In fact, she was the one who first introduced me to Mucinex D.

The AV600 is easy to unpack and operate. Simply insert the cord of the DC adapter into the adapter port on the back of the AV600 and then plug the adapter into a power outlet. There is a small but detailed, easy-to-read owner's manual that explains everything that you need to know. I thought I had lost mine in all my clutter and was panicking. I called the customer service for Pado, Inc., the manufacturers of the AV600. I quickly was connected to a customer service representative, Sarah, who was very friendly and cooperative. Within twenty-four hours, she had emailed me a link that took me to the manual. I was able to easily download and print it out. I was very thankful. I didn't have to give Sarah any personal information; only my email address.

The replaceable filter needs to be cleaned every month, which is reasonable, and replaced every eighteen months. I have already checked and the filter can be ordered directly from Amazon. The filter is easy to clean. Simply push open the top, and insert the suction tube accessory on your vacuum cleaner, and suck out the dust from the filter. The filter always looks very dirty, which tells me that the AV600 is working. (Make sure the AV600 is turned off and unplugged when not in use or when the filter is being cleaned or replaced.) The adapter cord leading from the electrical outlet to the AV600 looks like the type found on a small electronic item and is very delicate. It is not your standard electrical cord. It is fragile. Once, I accidentally stepped on it and pulled it out of the device. I quickly plugged it back in, forgetting that you are not supposed to do that. The cord goes first into the AV600 and then into the outlet. I don't believe any damage occurred.

There is a little blue mood light that shines when the AV600 is operating. Some owners may find it annoying but I don't. (It can be turned off.) I have several night lights in my bedroom. The blue mood light keeps me from stepping on the unit when I have to get up in the middle of the night to go use the bathroom. The AV600 is very decorative and stylish. It doesn't look like the old air cleaners that I've owned in the past; they were huge and bulky. The AV600 is very lightweight and easy to move from one room to another.

I seldom ever run the AV600 on high speed mode (turbo mode), probably because it will only stay on high speed mode for two hours before switching to low speed mode. Therefore, what is the point? Also, I noticed that whenever the electricity goes off in my condo and then comes back on, I have to manually turn on the AV600. With my older Whirlpool air cleaner, it automatically comes back on. The AV600 is more complicated to operate. I wish it had separate buttons for low, medium, and high speed like my Whirlpool does. Instead, with the AV600, I must push the same button several times to switch functions. It can be confusing. Unless you have a great memory (and I don't), I recommend storing the operator's manual in a safe place.

I would also like to add that the AV600 uses very little power. Cost of electricity for running it for a month is less than a dollar. Someone like me, who is very allergic to dust, should have an Avari AV600 Air Purifier in their bedroom. It would make a welcomed Christmas gift for someone who suffers with allergies. My only suggestion is that you keep its operator's manual in a safe place because you will probably need it.

We have six cats and six litter boxes, including one tucked away in a corner of the living room for an elderly feline who isn't always willing to trek to other more distant boxes. (Other lazy cats frequently use it, too.) We use a fairly dust-free clumping litter but even so, after a few weekly box changes, there's a fine sheen of dust on everything, including our TV screen and other electronic items. While we dust the obvious, we know there's lots of dust (and cat hair) in the room.

The Oreck Air Response has proven to be a godsend. When set on automatic, it kicks in on high when particulate is heavy - and since we've been using it, we don't have a dust problem anymore. Because it's lightweight despite being an armful size-wise, I've been carrying it into the laundry room, to the hall outside the bathroom, and to a spare room whenever I change those boxes. No more dust. It's simply fantastic.

When not on automatic, you can set the filter's fan to low, medium or high speeds yourself. Low and medium are exceedingly quiet, but on high, the Oreck moves so much air that you might compare it to a quiet air conditioner. The sound isn't - to us - annoying in the least.

We were away for a couple days and when we came back, the air was stale from the house being shut up, but we turned the purifier on high and it freshened the house very quickly, even before we scooped the boxes. We were very impressed.

We are currently painting the walls and woodwork in the house and keeping the purifier on full time while we're working and on automatic at other times. It clears the air and the odors in record time. We also removed tile board from the bathroom and found a little mold. We instantly put the filter in that room since my husband is very allergic to mold and fungus. After removing the old tile board (wearing masks) we set the purifier to run for two hours before resuming the remodel. It helped tremendously, letting my husband continue working without a mask.

Another thing it's great for is cooking odors and smoke when you get the burner too hot while grilling burgers or you burn toast. It clears it up fast!

The purifier has a HEPA filter and an odor filter that must occasionally be replaced. The HEPA is rated for a year with twelve hour a day usage, and the odor filter for six months. I doubt they'll last that long in a multi-cat household, but the cost of replacement is small compared to the freshness of the air and the lack of dust.

The purifier lights up (if you want it to) to show you if it's running on low, medium, or high speeds (blue, purple, or red, respectively) and also lights up to tell you when the filters need replacing. All in all, it's the best purifier we've ever had. I'm looking forward to buying a second one so I don't have to carry it from room to room.

The purifier works best in small rooms - not big open areas - but it's fine in our living room since we keep it near the litter pan. It does its job and it does it well.

title: Quiet Air Purifier With Lots of Convenient Features
text:
The Oreck Air Purifier is easy to use and is good looking too. The packaging provided great padding and once out of the box, no assembly was needed. Setting it up was pretty straightforward and took hardly 5 minutes.

Oreck purifier was lightweight enough (14 pounds) and easy to move around. It is not on wheels, so you have to pick it up to move it, but it can be lifted easily with handles on the side.

This air purifier has a very nice feature called "Dust Sense", which automatically detects the particle level in the air, and adjusts the fan speed accordingly. Color lights tell you the level of dust particles: blue, purple, and orange when the levels are really high. We run it on automatic mode most of the time. Timer feature is also very useful when you only want to run it anywhere between 2-8 hours. Additionally, you can adjust the fan speed manually should you want to run it on low or high yourself. This purifier covers approximately 300 square feet. But it comes in 3 sizes.

Our son suffers from allergies and asthma and this air purifier works so well for him.

Warning light lets you know when the air filter needs replacement. It comes with 1 extra odor filter as well. Cartoon instructions are located inside the front cover in case you forget what goes where. Overall, we are really pleased with this Oreck air purifier.

title: Sleek, Modern and Large
text:
The Oreck’s fan motor is virtually silent on setting 1 and 2, but it’s fairly loud on setting 3. The purifier is large but the design is sleek and modern. There are indentations on the side for picking it up and moving it, but because the front cover opens outward, I got a nasty pinch picking up the Oreck to move it. Using the side handle indentations puts your fingers at the seam where the front cover meets the back. Ouch.

I’ve had no issues with odor from the Oreck. The filters are easy to access and therefore I will assume they are easy to change. So far, I like the machine, although it is a lot larger than I had anticipated.

We have 3 large dogs and I will be interested to see how it handles the dog dander issue and dog odor. Will check in again when I know for sure.

title: I like it but....did the air really improve? or not?
text: I have a couple other HEPA filters but here in Florida, they get used a LOT. First, we have sand and high humidity with open doors and windows frequently throughout the day. I also have pets that come and go via a pet door. I live under an oak canopy so pollen is rampant and in general, it's safe to say air filters get a serious workout. I currently have been using a larger PureBlue filter for the main living area - it does a decent job but has struggled to keep up and I'm replacing the filters more frequently. It's also really loud so I tend to turn it down or off. This was tooted as quite with a new HEPA tech so figured it was time to update and give this a try. It is quieter - even on max setting it's substantially quieter. I really enjoy the automatic feature which is something my smaller bedroom filter has but the big blue was lacking. This is nice although admittedly, there are times when I don't want the extra surge however it's easy enough to switch to manual adjustments. Now, for the actual results - I opted to try this out in a bedroom/master bath setting rather than main room just to see how well it reduced ppm etc...I have an air quality sensor set up in that room with several months of average readings. I set up the filter and allowed it to run in the large room for a day or so then moved to the small closed room, set on auto and let it run a couple days before reviewing the actual air quality data. My personal impression was a feeling of better air quality and easier breathing the first night or two which then seemed to level off without any major difference. I compared the data - while it did seem to go down, it was a minor amount. Far less than I'd actually expect. However, I have to give it a longer trial run because we are experiencing an early spring here in Florida with super high pollen counts so the data is probably skewed when compared to the prior months. In short, the jury is still out as to the actual air quality improvements.

title: Great for office air
text:
Coupon code resulted in low/no price purchase for evaluation. Maybe it's me but this is one of my favorite new items to come around in ages! If you are stuck in an office all day then chances are you might appreciate this more than usual...it's a simple but effective and beautiful solution to something few people give much thought to...the air quality inside.

Years ago I was stunned to read that indoor air quality was actually even worse than outside pollution but then it made sense. Computers, carpeting, perfumes, printers etc all give off volatile compounds that compromise the air quality indoors. The problem with air quality is that it's hard to improve...it's easy enough to make a room smell good but usually that worsens the actual air quality by tossing more chemicals into the environment. Essential oils are a nice fragrance but again, they mask odors but don't actually clean the air. Plants do! It's part of their job in nature and it only makes sense to use them in an office....but there is the mess, dirt and need to maintain. You know what's next...a dead plant stuck in a pot of dirt.

Fast forward to this nifty product - yeah, I'm excited but it's such a cool idea. This allows easy maintenance for your favorite plant (which is basically anything green) and then increases the purifying qualities by increasing airflow. It's quieter than HEPA filters, a lot more attractive than some ugly machine sitting in the corner humming away while collecting dust and whatever germs are floating around the room. Very subtle styling means this can fit into an office or home with ease - neutral yet attractive. Coupon code resulted in low/no price purchase for evaluation.

I put this little purifier down in my guest area bedroom before my guest arrived. I placed the Oreck purifier down there about an hour before he arrived and by time he got there, the room did smell noticeably fresher. I like that you can turn off the light - my other purifier does not have this function, so if I use my other one at night, I have to cover up the light with a cloth (I took a photo of light on and light off).

I wish it were a little more attractive, but my other purifiers aren't attractive either. But a little more thought to design to make these purifiers better disappear in a room would be nice. This one is not only the size of a garbage can but sort of looks like one. It is a little "sleek" looking but I hid it where it wasn't as visible.

It comes out of the box ready to go, except that you must take off the front cover (grasp at bottom and pull it away -super easy) and take the plastic off of the filters - you must do this before you use the unit. There is a tab to 'warn' you of this.

At time of this review, the unit is about $179. That's a little pricy, but most hepa purifiers are pricy. However, that price for such a small unit does make me hesitate to think about purchasing another one.

Overall, I'm pleased with the unit.

title: The only one to get rid of SKUNK odor this effectively
text:
My dogs wound up on the losing end of an encounter with a skunk. If you never had the smell brought into your home then I have to warn you it can make your house unlivable for days or much longer unless you work on it immediately. Bad news is it is an oil based pheromone and it moves, so unless you get rid of it or neutralize it then you will smell it for weeks. You can pay thousands for a service to come get rid of it and basically they will do what we did for much less. We cleaned all surfaces we could easily clean and mixed an enzymatic solution that attacks this particular pheromone (We got this from petsmart). We ordered this unit via over night delivery and ran it in every room of the house moving it from one room to another. Every room still stunk and it took about 2-4 hours to fully freshen up. You could smell the exhaust from this air cleaner in a room full of skunk smell and it was neutral is how I would describe it. From awful skunk smell to neutral, I would have to say that is a very good real life test! The smell has not gone away from the house entirely. I expect the odor is on the walls, celling and any other place we did not touch. Each time we move the cleaner around the smell gets better which is promising. The product description says it cleans ~800 sq ft and I feel that is realistic.

I purchased two ion type air cleaners from a local store because I read ozone will break down the smell. In fact if you put your nose right up to the unit it did smell much better, although the smell was NOT neutral it smelled of ozone. The amount of air coming through however was barely enough to move a feather. I also purchased two ionic ones from sharper image that have not come in yet, I might just return them and get another one of these units. I know this one unit costs as much as two ionic ones but I am really happy with this one and you won't have to clean the filters weekly like I read on sharper images own website's reviews. You have to clean the ionic ones in the dishwasher since the screen is so close together on the high end model. The plus on the ones from sharper image is that they have 4 little fans to assist air flow. I will give them a try and I will update this review for a comparison test.

This is my second rabbit air unit, I really wished I had purchased this one first. The filter pack is better and I like the features on this model better. I am pretty sure that I would not have spent this much money if it was not for the first purchase though. I originally purchased the first unit due to dust and allergy problems, which it does a great job at making me comfortable. I expect this one to do the same and better when spring comes around next year.

***Update, I have had the ionic Breeze from sharper image for over a week and I have to say I am disappointed with them. I bought 2 units from SI, the ones with little fans to boost the air flow. Unfortunately the fans are noisy even at Medium speed and the ionic part does little to get rid of odors. I am returning them and have already purchased another MinusA2 (it has already been delivered) and I am much happier using 3 Rabbit Airs in my home. We still have a little skunk odor hanging around even though we have washed everything in our closets and wiped down the walls in most of our rooms. I think after you get the full experience you get hyper sensitive to it and it bothers you more than it would others. 3 Rabbit Airs might sound overboard but we have a 3500 sq ft house and just want our bedrooms and living area clear of allergens and dust. We feel this should cover the areas we are in most of the time and give us relief in the spring. 5 units at $5 bills plus each is going a bit overboard.

***** 2nd update I have cleaned the units twice so far using a good HEPA vacuum and I must say the junk on the pre filter is down right scary. I cleaned the other filters too and they are appearing to darken which tells me I will have to replace them pretty soon. I really took the red light feature (Odor sensor) to be a gimmick but it seems to work very well I have walked by and noticed the light was red or partially red and wondered why then when I left the room it was obvious. Outside my room I could smell the dust from my daughter changing the sand in her lizard tank or that my wife had just cooked something. I farted next to it as a joke then the joke was on me when the red light came on and the fan ramped up.....

title: ************UPDATE***************  August 2017-2021
text:
*********UPDATE********** 2017 -2021
****************************************

We've had our Green Air Encore since 2017. It has proven to be one of the best investments we have made in Amazon purchases, ever. It is STILL quiet, efficient and EFFECTIVE. This is a solid 5 star product if I ever saw one. If you are on the ropes about it, dont be. I have years of ownership experience with this air purifier. Both me and my son have seasonal allergies and we have two dogs. The difference between being outside in the air in spring and summer, and the difference with all of the fires in the summer here in the pacific northwest and being inside with this monster are night and day. Buy it.

**************************************************************************************************************

1.)Just received this last night. It was packaged well and well protected. No damage.

2.)First thing I did was read the instructions in the users manual. I think a lot of people aren't doing this. You can just plug it in and put it on auto but you are missing some really key features if you do this. I think one feature that took me a bit to understand was the sensitivity feature which, if you just read the manual, is confusing because you are led to believe that adjusting the fan speed also adjusts the sensitivity...it doesn't. You have to unplug the device, wait a few seconds (manual says 2 minutes but its not necessary) then hold down the air quality button as you plug it back in....now when you use the fan speed button, it actually adjusts the sensitivity! Then when you have it where you want, just hit the power button and put it on auto. Works great.

3.) This thing is quiet as a mouse when running on auto and the air is clean. This unit as well as any other will make some noise when the fan kicks into high gear as it is responding to particles in the air but even that is very reasonable...then later it will go back to eco mode and you almost don't know it is running, until you put your hand above and behind it and feel the air coming out! Case in point...our unit is right next to our entertainment center where our tv is located and it cause no issues at all.

4.) Love the design, it just fits our home well. We have wood floors and earth tones through out and this just blends well.

5.) Ease of access to filters. The panel is held on magnetically so not clips or parts to break or wear out when removing and changing filters. This is good thing.

6.) Price. This thing is the same quality and functionality of 500 dollar units. I know, I've seen a few others at store on display and at a friends house who owns a 450 dollar model made by another company.

****UPDATE****************************************UPDATE****************************

So we use a lot of scented candles in our home...well you better turn this unit off if you want to experience your scented candles cause this unit will literally kill the odor so it doesn't permeate through out the house. Yeah, this unit definitely is doing its job and then some.

**********************UPDATE #2*******************************
It has been since 2017 since we bought it. Still kick butt and taking names. No issues, no failures.....it is the king in my book at this point.

I did this because I read reviews of people saying it takes smoke and shoots it back out the sides. That wasn't the case for my testing and it sucked 98% of the fog/aerosolized water vapor through the filter. While the replacement filters are insanely expensive, I'm hoping they last long enough for that cost to be on par with the other filters in my home and I recommend this for people who need consistent good quality air to improve their quality of life.

title: Great for pet allergies and asthma !!!
text:
We have had the 780A model in our bedroom for over 10 years now (!!!) and are very happy with it.

We got it because my wife has some serious cat dander allergy and asthma, and we had 5 cats in the house! Well, something had to be done, so after extensive research on air purifiers for cat dander allergies and asthma, I selected the Rabbit Air 780A. (Edit: we now have only 2 cats and with the Rabbit Air A2 780 the air quality is quite good. Still 4 stars since the light issues persist, and the model hasn't changed in ten years making me think they have yet to fix them.)

We recommend Minus A2 780A highly, with two caveats.

We are still using the original filter after more than a year, and have cleaned the pre-filters exactly two times. We run it most nights, 8 to 12 hours while we are in the bedroom. We turn it off when we aren't in the bedroom or aren't home. It still seems to be working great, and I don't feel like we need to get a new filter yet. My wife has commented that it makes a huge difference in her comfort level and ability to sleep. She uses her inhaler a lot less.

There are several downsides: We have the unit in our bedroom several feet past the foot of the bed where we both sleep. But the problem is, and it is kind of a serious defect, the front of the thing is covered with Green LEDs and a large LED light that changes from blue to red and back, to indicate the level of cleaning that needs to be done to the air. It is not possible to turn these lights off. They are very bright in a dark bedroom, and interfere with sleep. I've had to cover them with several layers of tape, which helps, but isn't pretty. Also, it has the moronic mood light function in a wide band across 3/4 of the front panel. This "feature", actually it is a huge FLAW, is supposed to improve your mood by changing from blue to purple. Well, it doesn't work to improve my mood. Actually, it has the oposite effect. It makes me angry at how stupid and obnoxious it is every time I see it. Luckily, it can be turned off permanently. However, one of the main benefits of the Minus-A2 line is the option to get a designer panel for the unit. We have the super cool Mount Fuji Wave image, and love it, except that it is partly RUINED by the stupid and ugly translucent plastic bubble for the mood light right through the middle of it, and the less obnoxious, but still stupid and objectionable small black and silver accent "tab" or whatever it is on the left side that cuts into the image. I've deducted one star because of these two light issues. The designers should be more sensitive to those who want the unit in their bedrooms and want to sleep in the dark.

HELLO, Mr. Rabbit Air designer, please make the stupid, obnoxious and ugly mood light bubble in the middle of the front panel optional!!! That way, those of us that don't want it don't have to be annoyed by it every time we see it! Also, please put the LEDs on the front behind some sort of panel or door, or provide a dial or some rocker switch to dim them all the way to zero, so they don't disturb our sleep at night. That would make this unit close to perfect.

Other than those two mostly aesthetic complaints, it is a great unit, although pricey, and we are glad we got it.

title: Not the ozone level I wanted
text:
Vivitar Quiet Desktop Air Purifier (hereafter "Vivitar") is as it says, quiet, because it doesn’t move large amount of air like other types do. (As many observed here, the two settings show little difference, although if you listen closely, the "Whisper" setting is even quieter.) My unit's package says nothing about being an ioniser, yet it clearly is one as described here. (As such, it uses no filter, contrary to a claim on one of its cover panels.) The smell many people notice is from the ozone that is generated as a byproduct. (The smell should be familiar to anyone going close to an operating office copier or laser printer.) Because of ozone, this kind of device should be used in well ventilated area, not in closed space.

Theoretically, negatively charged air ions attract pollutant particles, lumping them toward nearby surfaces, thus "purifying" air. Additionally, negatively charged ions are reported to neutralise certain pathogens. I used to be skeptical of such hypes that my brother listened to. But desperate times call for desperate measures. When my daughter's asthma worsened as air gets horrible from nearby fires, I rushed into Fry's like many in the area. I needed something then and there, and Vivitar was on discount at $30. So I bought this together with one with a HEPA filter. Though the filtered air purifier was much larger in size and gave an effective area of 8m^2 (80 sq. ft), Vivitar's claim of 30m^2 (300 sq. ft) coverage made me want to test it out.

Due to smoke in the area, my windows were closed. So the first thing I noticed was the ozone smell. There is no standard to verify "Up to 300 sq ft coverage" (~30 m^2)). But over time, the smell does spread to a large area despite Vivitar’s weak fan. And the extent of ozone smell is not what I have in mind when I think about air purifier’s "coverage".

If I open the windows, the smell becomes barely noticeable. Then, I did more research. I bought this in the hope to help my daughter cope with asthma. But FDA sees no respiratory health benefits in ionisers. Even though I believe that Vivitar's ozone level is acceptable, I do not need one more device that does not help and generates ozone. So I am keeping the HEPA filtered unit and returning Vivitar.

To answer another user's comment about not finding evidence of use of UV, it is perhaps a good thing. Because according to literature, use of UV optimises generation of ozone, not negative ions. (This type of device uses high voltage between metal plates. Any ioniser will always produce some ozone. The kind used in hospitals will have some mechanism to neutralise ozone, but cheaper devices like this one do not.)

title: What HEPA filter does your allergist recommend?
text:
As a board-certified allergist, I'm often asked, "what air filter should I buy?". First of all, do you need a filter at all? If you're allergic to just dust mites, don't bother. Dust mites are carried on large particles (10 micro-meters, or microns), and only stay airborne for 15 minutes after being disturbed (such as making the bed or running a vacuum cleaner). They won't even get to the filter, so no matter what filter you buy, it can't filter something that doesn't STAY airborne.
But if you're allergic to something carried on tiny (~ 2 micron) particles, such as cat dander or grass pollen, then by all means consider getting an air filter.
My household owns 2 Rabbit Minus A2's. That's the bottom line, but here's the long explanation:
1) I ask my patients who need a filter, 'what is your budget'? If it's $200, get a Honeywell. They're inexpensive and work well. If it's $500, get a Rabbit (details below). If it's $1,000, consider getting an IQ air, Blue-Air, or Austin. If cost is no object, do what we did with our previous home. I bought 3 hospital grade IQ Airs and put 1 of them inline with each HVAC unit in the house (I know, I know, 3 HVAC's must mean a big house, buy hey, I'm a doctor in practice for 25 years, and besides, the financial guy down the street has a house twice as big). We spent about $12,000 on that upgrade. All so we could have our cake and eat it too (not get rid of the cats). Or is it EAT our cake and have it too? The super-fancy filters lowered the airborne allergens to next-to-nothing, but if my daughter still slept with the cat...
2) Why do we own 2 Rabbits? I really like the idea that Rabbits have 4 separate filters, and you can customize the 4th filter (germ, pet, toxin or odor remover).
3) I am totally inept when it comes to mechanical aptitude, but I am able to order the $85 filter pack once a year and make our Rabbit as good as new. All you have to do is unwrap each filter and keep them in the same order.
4) We have one of them in our bedroom and one in the allergic kid's bedroom.
---Other hints about getting any filter
-High speed equals better filtration, but the 'turbo' speed on Rabbits is pretty loud. Maybe run it on high speed when you're NOT in the room (especially if the cat goes in the room---Whiskers doesn't mind the noise--trust me on that one), and turn it down to low speed when you're in the room.
-Priority #1 is to put one of these in your bedroom--that's where you spend (hopefully) 8 hours a day while you're asleep.

title: Fantastic product, a must-have!
text:
My wife & I live in Hollywood, where air quality is always an issue but has been particularly terrible lately due to the ongoing wildfires. The combination of LA smog, wildfire plumes of smoke, & COVID-19 pandemic led us to seek out an air purifier for our home, and thank god we settled on this Air Choice model. It's relatively light weight, small enough to fit comfortably and unobtrusively in the corner of any room -- the sleek design actually makes it look like a fancy speaker or internet server.

It stands just over knee-high on an adult man, it's extremely easy to use and move from room to room (more on that in a moment), and once it's cleaned out your home's air on the higher fan settings it settles into a nice, quiet fan to maintain the good air quality. And boy does it ever make a BIG difference. Being indoors with windows and doors mostly shut because of COVID, wildfires, and typical LA summer heat, it can get musty sometimes.

This air purifier has improved the air so much that our apartment smells fresh all the time now, the air is visibly clearer, I don't have to clean dust off my TV every few days anymore, my sore throat from the smokey air has cleared up, and we haven't even had to move the air purifier yet.

Which brings me to a point about it's overall capacity -- we have it in our living room, and we took turns opening doors to the two bedrooms and bathroom in our home, and it seems to have completely cleared up the air everywhere in the apartment and is maintaining good quality air beyond the advertised 495 square feet capacity.

I recommend trying it in a few different locations to see how the sound and air quality is in your home and where the most efficient location is for the air purifier. When your air quality is bad (indicated by red circle of light on the device), the fan is loud enough you'll need to turn up your TV if it's in the same room, but once it's cleaned the air to a mid-range level (green lights on the device) the fan's sound is lower and less intrusive. Once the air quality is good (blue lights on the device) you'll barely even hear the soft blowing sound of the fan as it continues to maintain the "good" level of air quality.

It took about two days to clear out the air in our apartment completely to a consistent "good" air quality, including shutting the device off overnight while we sleep.

We looked around at various air purifiers, and what we found is the cheaper devices filter less from the air and only cover a smaller space (less than half the space this Air Quality device covers), while more expensive devices seem to either be doing the same thing without apparent increased quality, or they use technologies that aren't deemed safe enough under more strict state regulations in California. So, even if your state allows some of those devices to ship to you, be aware that other states might ban the device because of certain ozone-related safety issues. So a good way to consider the safety of the devices is to put in a California shipping address and see if it will ship there -- if not, then the device probably uses some of the prohibited technology considered unsafe in California.

All of which is to say, this Air Quality device seems to be a perfect balance of best quality within acceptable safety guidelines, for the best price at that quality level. Highly recommended.

title: It’s pretty, so it gets away with murder
text:
It took me a long time to buy this fan. I was very on the fence. Looking back on it and to not bore you to death, my take away from owning one for a few months is this:

1. It’s quiet. Below 5 it is extremely silent, and the best part is that the oscillation is silent; Every single tower fan I have owned creaks when they oscillate. To get technical - it’s mostly because the other fans have blades that sit upright, so when the fan turns from left to right, the blades jostle around and shudder a little. For $400 this one absolutely does NOT do that. Fan is mounted at the base, and spins on the same axis that the fan oscillates on. So that’s a win.

2. It is an air purifier. Can’t say I really care too much about this, because I actually got it almost exclusively because-

3. It’s good looking. Honestly it is a striking looking piece of fan art. People notice it, and although it’s not quite as shiny and glossy as the ad pictures, it’s a Dyson. And in the world of fans, the Dysons are like the Kennedy’s. High echelon and seemingly always in vogue. Doesn’t matter why they’re top tier, they just... are.

It’ll strike a discussion for sure once someone sees it - so don’t hide this thing! You’re paying top dollar for it.

So, it blows air and it’s quiet. It supposedly cleans air too. But honestly, there are 50 dollar alternatives. You know that. I know that. This fan even knows that - but who could really say no to this thing? It’s a charmer. If you got the money to blow and you’ve always wanted one, then save up a little and give it a shot. You won’t be surprised, but won’t be disappointed either.

title: Regales with beautiful air and stylish attitude
text:
We are using this in a roughly 250 sq ft area and in nearly every aspect it shines like a champ.

It's incredibly quite on low, and reasonable at med and high - I would imagine that if you live in any sort of city or suburb the ambient noise would be well above what this puts off. We live in the woods, and have found that the noise it does produce is quite enjoyable (something akin to the soothing breath of a sleeping baby that only ever exhales).

The buttons on the unit itself require a little more force to push than really seems necessary (sometimes you have to place a reassuring hand on it's back so it doesn't topple over in protest to the aggression it's subjected to when fumbling for sleep mode in the dark). On the other hand the controls do seem quite stalwartly constructed and offer impressive fortification against all wine like assaults that might occasionally drift in it's direction.

In general, the auto detect system appears to have the nose of a seasoned bloodhound, both for particulates (dust, etc) as well as odors (even those produced by fragrant mists and the like). It sometimes seems as though the poor little guy is under equipped by it's limited little three bars of communication to adequately convey the vast bouquet of scents that it delights itself with.

We have noticed that it tends to better detect air quality when it's running on high or medium (probably because it seems to become considerably more excited about it's job when larger volumes of air are gusting in air towards it's sensors) but if in doubt, more voracious suction is just a button press away.

We've found this neatly dressed little robot butler to be a stand up addition to the household - I would certainly and enthusiastically recommend one for every human who finds that they tend to breath, and enjoys doing it with nice clean air.

title: Quiet and Clean!
text:
Superior purifier.
Very quiet performance compared with all other purifiers, even at the highest setting. I tested the decibels and confirmed the manufacturer specs. Purchased over one year ago, this purifier has remained on the highest setting for nearly 24/7 for the entirety of the last year and still maintains the same low volume it had when it was purchased.
In the Central Valley of California, our air quality is rated among the worst in the nation. Pollution from the Bay Area gets blown southeast into the valley where it gets trapped against the Sierra-Nevada Mountains to the East and the Tehachapi Mountains in the South. The poor air causes bad allergies and asthma in the general population. With this purifier (using the standard filter) working continuously in our house, our inside air smells clean and my wife, who has bad allergies and cannot breathe well outside, has no respiratory issues inside our house. The house was also much less dusty than before we purchased the purifier. Our house is larger than the 1100 sqft for which the BreatheSmart is rated. However, by placing the purifier in an area with significant air movement, the BreatheSmart performed well at keeping the house clean. If you don't have good airflow throughout the area where the BreatheSmart is located, I would recommend running fans or purchasing multiple purifiers.
The clean air sensor works well and will typically show that the air is clean when there is little to no air movement (fans and HVAC off) and will immediately show that the air is dirty when the ceiling fan is turned on.
The large particle filter on the front of the HEPA filter has to be vacuumed about once a month and the HEPA filter does need to be changed at or before the 6 month point that is recommended by Alen.
As for the Ionizer, it is hard to determine whether it does that much. The filter on the whole does very well at cleaning the air so in the end, I am not concerned about the performance of this particular feature on its own.
If there is one negative to highlight, it is the size of the BreatheSmart. It will take up the entire surface of an end table or occupy an equal amount of space if placed on the floor. To get maximum cleaning, the BreatheSmart must be placed in a well ventilated area. This generally means that the purifier will be in a fairly prominent location. Its size and shape are not the most pleasing to the eye when you basically have it as a piece of furniture.
Overall, even at the $600 price point, the BreatheSmart is well worth the cost. I would definitely recommend it to anyone that is battling allergy and asthma concerns and still wants to be able to hear normal conversations above the sound of the purifier.

title: best of the 4-5 purifers I've owned
text:
First, it comes really well packed- I was very impressed at the care the seller took when packaging this item. I have several purifiers (one in each room) but these folks make absolutely sure the item comes intact. I'll give it an A in this respect.

Second, it's a sleek looking purifier; square at the bottom, cylindrical at the top -- about two feet high and 6-8 inches wide. It's dark gray and I'm very happy with the appearance. Grade: A

Noise: on Auto & Fan 1 -- barely audible at all; I keep it in fan speed 2, and can barely hear it. Fan speed 3 is a acceptable, 4 and 5 -- which I'll rarely ever need -- are noticeably loud. But if you ever do need speeds 3, 4, and 5, you can rest assured that this purifier will clean your air well, and it does it fast.

Energy-efficiency: it's energy star certified, so I am confident I can run it 24/7/365 for next to nothing.

Laser sensor: I believe it, but I have another purifier with a PM 2.5 sensor and sometimes that purifier registers red whereas this one continues to indicate that air quality is very good (under 5). I know for a fact that the other purifier I have is 100% accurate. I believe this one is too (I think) but can't be sure. It's definitely a cool feature and more typical of purifiers at or above $300. Grade: B+

Cleaning capacity: when I walk in to my place, the air is never stale. I've only had this 2 days but the air feels clean and crisp and I know this device is definitely cleaning the air. Grade: A.

It's AHAM certified at 455 square feet and has a CADR of 290. Which more or less means that it will clean the air twice an hour in a room that's 900 square feet (assuming ceilings are 10 feet or thereabouts) at top speed (which I'll rarely ever use) My living room is about 300 square feet so my calculation is that it replaces the air 3-4 times an hour on speed 2 (barely audible). It's super efficient and has the cleaning capacity of $300+ purifiers by other well known brands. By this costs $233 (plus tax), so I'm thrilled.

Cost of filter replacement: I believe it's $69, every 6-8 months. On par with other large room purifiers. I wish it was $20 less, but what can you do.

I like that it's quiet (less than 25 decibels on fan speed 1 and sleep), cost-effective in that it's energy star certified, I like the laser sensor which gives me real time numbers on air quality and I like the ability with which this device cleans air. And it looks sharp.

I've had 4-5 purifiers in my life, have one in every room, and this is by far my favorite. And I've only had it a couple of days but definitely think it's a keeper.

I'll provide updates as necessary if I think they'll be helpful.

text:
TLDR: If you have the means to buy this, and you are considering buying it. Absolutely go for it.

For people wondering about noise, at the lowest setting it was at 45dB which is quieter than my keyboard which at the same distance was around 70 dB
Medium setting from 7 inches is 50dB and high around 57dB
For air impurities detection I used Febreze as a stand-in. Spraying for 5 seconds 10 feet away it took the purifier about 13 seconds for it to bring the speed up to medium, and 2 seconds after that it ramped up to high.

My wife and I bought this to keep in our room. I suffer from terrible allergies, which causes frequent migraines. We were skeptical about just how affective this would be for us, due to the price and the defined square feet. After about a month of use I can confidently say this is one of the best air purifiers I have ever used.

The compact size of it makes it very convenient to be stored under our desks for as little intrusion as possible. This purifier has made a world a difference for me, helping with my allergies immensely. We also have two cats and a dog and I have noticed that the room doesn't have a stale animal smell.

Now about that smoke demo. My wife was going to make something in the oven about a week ago, and we had a pizza box from lunch sitting in the oven(ya know, to keep it warm) and she turned the oven up to 450F. I smelled it before I saw it. The pizza box had caught on fire and smoke began to fill the room. I got the pizza box out but the smoke was still a problem. I took the purifier and set it on the counter in the kitchen to try to get some of that smoke taken care of. It took 3 minutes for all the smoke to be gone. title: Overkill unless you live in a very dirty environment
text:
I've owned this product for about 3 months and only the prefilter has gotten a little bit of dust on it despite running it on high/med 24/7. I think it's a very well designed filter but it's simply overkill unless you live in a very dirty environment. I purchased the filter to control my allergies which are related to dust. While I understand I can't blame the filter completely if my allergies don't go away, I still see dust on the table, floor, etc... The filter does a great job of working of cleaning the air that goes through it compared to other air filters, but I think you can't expect an air filter to remove all the dust in a room unless you live in a very dusty environment with pets and lots of indoor activities.

Lots of people have rated this product very highly possibly because they do live in these environments. But also 80% of what I see people write in the reviews here considers things aside from the main function, things such as aesthetics, noise, technologies used, #filters, air flow. If you have allergies and are very sensitive to dust/mites/etc.., all you care about is what is trapped on the filters themselves and I don't think this filter removes those minute traces of dust and particles in the air FAST ENOUGH before they go through your nose or fall to the ground and other surfaces.

So the 3 stars is because while it's a great filter (compared to other filters and considering all the miscellany features), it simply does not provide the service I expected for $600. Again, aside from the pre-filter, none of the other filters have any particles/discoloration/smell on them whatsoever and my allergy symptoms to dust while at home have not improved. I'm returning this to rabbitair within the 90 day guarantee. Too bad they don't refund the cost of the expensive filters ~$100 altogether.

So let me wrap this up with a simple equation:

Services Rendered - Cost of Purchase = Was it worth it???
A little bit of dust particles on the prefilter after 3 months - $600+ (after tax) = NOPE!

title: Doesn't work...Update: figured out WHY it didn't work, a sort of user error
text:
I'm a smoker. The last air purifier that I bought cleared the smoke completely from my 144 sq. ft room in about 15 minutes. I chose this one to replace it because the other brand's filters have gone from $60 per filter to $90 per filter in the last year. This one costs a bit more than the other brand does. It WILL clear the smoke from my room in about 8 hours but only if my fan is also running. However, it did work okay the first day, it's really quiet, and it does help with the smell from the smoke and my dog.

UPDATE: I'm changing my rating from 1 star to 4 stars because after I received a refund from this company without any trouble, I bought another brand of air purifier and realized then WHY I had a problem with the Hathaspace air purifier. I thought this might help the company and future customers.

The problem wasn't the appliance. When I had the air purifier before this one, we adopted 3 new pets and that air purifier gave up the ghost. I thought it was due to the age of that one, appliances are no longer built to last (on purpose) and I'd had it 2 years.
Then I did a lot of research and settled on the Hathaspace. The Hathaspace worked really well for the first day but was useless thereafter. So I thought there was a design defect or something. The real issue is that the increased animals meant feathers, a lot more fur and dander/dust. It took less than 24 hours for the filter to become completely clogged and no air could get through and so the bad air quality didn't register and it didn't kick in to the higher speed. I had the exact same issue with my current air purifier but it took longer to clog because the Hathaspace had already done a fairly thorough cleaning. It took me a bit of problem solving to figure out the problem. Now that I know.... if you have an issue with the machine working great soon after you get it and then rapidly stopping cleaning your air, check your filter. If you can see the dust and fur/feathers, vacuum the filter with a handvac and that'll fix it right up. I recommend vacuuming the pre-filter once per week in between filter changes.

I apologize to the company for not figuring out the problem sooner and leaving a poor review through no fault of their own. The only reason I give it 4 stars instead of 5 is because it really did take longer than my previous air purifier to filter the air. But I do want to say that the quietness of this product was fantastic and when my current machine, which also struggles a bit with circulating the air, goes out...if the company doesn't raise the price beyond the $200 price point, I would definitely purchase it again.

text:
[[VIDEOID:83e018e0a05b0fb4ea109ff3fe083be9]] My Boreas Portable Air Purifier made our musty root cellar smell like a fresh breeze in just an hour. We air out the room where we store our harvest for the winter, but even after a week it still has the earthy odor of the previous year's potatoes, onions, carrots and other crops. The Boreas quickly and completely overcame these odors and, presumably, any airborne mold or mildew. Our Boreas air purifier also freshened an RV we had closed up for some time, leaving it smelling better than new. We've also tackled - and beaten - cooking and pet odors and the unpleasant smells of construction adhesive, caulk, and fresh paint with this device. We'll use it all winter to help fight off flu and colds with its antiviral properties.

It took me only seconds to set up the Boreas Portable Air Purifier; removing the bottom, I inserted the charcoal filter and the viricidal air treatment cartridge (which must be unsealed to activate), reclosed the bottom cover, and connected the USB power cord. Although very portable, this purifier does require an external USB-A power source such as a phone charger. I've used it with a lithium power bank which works perfectly where mains power isn't available. The viricide cartridge and HEPA filter are easy to replace. I'm delighted with this air purifier and recommend it.

title: Ignore the daunting price... well worth it!!
text:
I've had a string of moderately priced air purifiers over the years and all of them left me wanting. They would chug away, becoming noisier with time, and do a questionable job cleaning the air. The filters were often as expensive as the entire unit, which sucked. When I tried a more expensive, filterless unit, I really didn't notice a tangible difference in air quality. The one I had just seemed to run and run with no real indication it was doing anything but wasting electricity and costing me money. When I cleaned it, the amount of dust it removed from the air was kind of pathetic.

I wanted the performance of a unit with filters, but also the style and technology of some filterless air cleaners. After a lot of research, I found RabbitAir.

The reviews were overwhelmingly good, but I'd never dropped $500 on an air purifier and was a bit apprehensive to spend that much money. My wife had bad allergies, so in the end it came down to the reviews and the need for something better and I rolled the dice. Man, I'm glad I did.

This unit is quite simply fantastic. I ordered from RabbitAir online, and the purifier arrived quickly and in great shape. When I opened the box, I was extremely pleased. The purifier is sturdy, stylish, and it oozes with quality. Excellent customer service.

It was easy to assemble with clear instructions. It has like seven stages of filtration when assembled. The filters are independently wrapped to preserve them, so you have to unwrap them and insert them into the unit before you operate it. It only takes a few minutes, but it also gives you an appreciation for how much it actually cleans the air, as you insert filter after filter.

The wall mount was easy to install. Mounted on the wall, it looks more like a high-tech decoration than an air purifier. The "mood lights" are stylish and cool; they change color based on the quality of the air and power setting.

There are many modes of operation, but I choose the auto setting, which adjusts power based on detected air quality. This feature works like a champ. It even detects and eliminates odors (charcoal filter included). I regularly have an evening soak in the tub with eucalyptus bath salts, and the unit will cycle to a higher setting when it detects the "scent" of eucalyptus. Kind of funny...

I use it in my bedroom and haven't lost a wink of sleep. In fact, the barely audible hum kind of helps you sleep. It's whisper quiet -- soooo much better than the piece of crap air purifiers I had before that rattled and chugged along, constantly making noise. Also, don't worry about the lighting when you're trying to sleep. It automatically detects when the room is dark and goes into sleep mode, turning off the lights or dimming them so they don't distract you and/or keep you awake. It activates three minutes after the lights go out in the room, so don't freak out if it the unit's lights stay on for a bit. For the record, I'm an extremely light sleeper, and this unit has never woken me up.

The kit to replace all seven filters is like $70, and you're supposed to do it like every two years. To me, that's a reasonable maintenance cost.

Most importantly, it does its job! The air in our house is cleaner than ever. My wife breathes easier and her allergies aren't as bad. Mission accomplished.

RabbitAir is simply the best air purifier I've ever owned, or SEEN for that matter. I highly, highly recommend this great product.

title: After 2 Different Tries With Different Units, They Both Crapped Out!
text:
3rd edit: The company replaced the first defective unit after quite a while.
The replacement unit arrived and worked great for about a month. Then I changed the ozone plate. The ozone never worked again. I have used this type of purifier for decades so I am very familiar with how to clean them and how to properly change plates. It was definitely NOT user error.
I gave up even trying to replace it.
I have ordered a unit from a different company.

2nd edit: I did receive a replacement and it works great. They took a while, but finally came through.
My unit was out of warranty (30 days?) when it stopped working, but they eventually sent me a new one anyway.

The unit itself is doing the job, keeping our house from smelling musty and moldy.

Unlike what you hear, you CAN leave the ozone on all the time. It will not hurt you in small amounts. If you don't lock yourself in a closet with the machine running full blast, it can't make enough ozone to hurt you. We have run these machines continuously in our house for over 20 years.

Here's how to do it. Turn the machine on and start the ozone at the lowest setting. Leave it for a day or two. Gradually up the level of ozone over the next few days. When you start smelling the ozone, back it off a little bit. There is a perfect spot where your air will smell like a fresh spring day...that's what you are after.

The level may change with the weather. Humidity soaks up ozone, in dry air, a little goes a long way. So feel free to adjust it with changing weather.

These devices usually last for several years, but mine stopped dead after 2 months.
1st Edit: I emailed them (not easy to find) and they agreed to replace my unit. I took it to the return around Sept 11. Had not heard back from them, so i emailed again.
They had received the unit quite a while back, but did not start the process of shipping my replacement until I bugged them on Sep 25. Acted like they had forgotten about it.
NOT impressed with their response.
Meanwhile my house smells.

title: Died in 2 weeks. I have to pay to ship back. Terrible Warranty Fulfillment.
text:
I hate to doing these one stars, because it might be a good product, but I got a bad one and was basically told, "Too bad". Yes, I can go to the shipping place and send it back at my expense. I could even understand that attitude if it ran for 8 months and then died,
But this died after 2 weeks. The ultra violet light went out. Also, I don't think the ozone ever worked. I have used Alpine air purifiers (the model these knockoffs are copying) for probably 20 years. I am fully aware of how they work and smell. This one never produced any ozone smell.
I knew this wouldn't be a lifetime investement. I was just thinking, if I get a year out of it, it will be worth it, because Alpines cost about this much to get repaired. But 2 weeks? And then I'm told I pay to ship it back under warranty. That's crap and It's not even worth my time and trouble.
Horrible attitude by the company.
On a related topic, ozone is NOT dangerous to your health in small amounts. It is one of the main ingredients in healthy outdoor air. If you have a fire in your home, the restoration companies use ozone at MASSIVE levels to get rid of the burned smell. Those levels will HURT you, but they are thousands or millions of times higher than normal. But tiny levels where you can't quite smell the ozone, but the air just seems fresh are good for you. It's like saying water is really bad for you because people drown. The right amount of water is necessary for life, too much and you die. Ozone is natures white blood cells of the air to break down impurities in the air. I have been living with low level ozone for decades because our house is too musty to live in without it. No problems at all.

title: No fake "ionization"; just good old filtration
text:
In car and most in home "ionizers" are worthless. They lack the power and capacity to ionize and deposit any meaningful percentage of suspended particulates. And even if you had an ionizer with sufficient power to make a dent in particulates, ionization does little to keep grounded particulates from becoming airborne again if disturbed.

For that reason I was looking for a compact in car filtration-only system to help reduce the amount of smoke particulates in the cabin air from recent wild fires in my area. This unit is nice and compact (akin to a "Venti" sized coffee cup, fits in a cupholder, has it's own rechargeable internal battery, can be recharged with the included cable from a vehicle USB port, and on higher settings (adjusted by rotating the top of the unit) does a credible job of filtering the air in the front seat area of a vehicle.

Downsides? Sure, a couple. When set >50%, which seems necessary in order to recirculate enough air to make a dent, it's pretty noisy. Not an irritating noise, but a medium pitched buzz that can be heard over normal spoken word volume levels (conversation, audiobooks, my normal music listening volume levels, etc.). The filters are replaceable, which is great, but replacements are pretty expensive for cheap-to-make, simple, paper cylinder shaped filters (like the innards of an oil filter); filters cost a significant percentage of the price of the unit itself and the included filter. That said, I've used mine daily for three months on both short and extended drives, and the original filter is still relatively clean (grayer than the replacement filter, but not so dirty I feel tempted to replace it at this point).

I also don't think this would be useful in an office or home setting. It certainly doesn't have the oomph to process room-sized air volumes even on the highest (noisiest) setting. But for in car use it's pretty good.

title: A good air purifier at a decent price
text:
We've had this air purifier for one week, mostly to reduce the impact of pollen allergy. It's been installed in our bedroom (over 450 sq ft) even though it's said to be most efficient under 350 sq ft.
Here are some facts:
- my wife already stopped taking Zyrtec
- I'm not a big fan of ionization because it produces ozone, so we closed this function, but we kept the UV sterilization on.
- I tested the sound level with a dB meter. It gave 20 dB at 10 feet in sleep mode. Actually the fan is hardly audible. At full speed it's still a whisper and it's not a nuisance at all.
- I had a (minor) problem with the delivered purifier and I contacted Hathaspace Customer Service. For many years I have not seen such a quick, fair and efficient reaction. We found the purifier so efficient that we did not want to return it, but they found a solution beyond our expectation.
Overall, we are very satisfied and we won't hesitate to buy again from them.

text:
Grandma and I bought this air purifier because our French Bulldog farts all the time. Before we bought it, our house smelled terrible - talk about silent but deadly. That little dog can generate some methane. We've tried different dog foods but nothing worked. We talked to our vet and she said there was nothing we could do except to get rid of the dog. But grandma wanted a lap dog and so we kept him and got this air cleaner.

But, to tell you the truth, I've been wondering if it is the dog or grandma. The dog sits on grandma's lap so it is hard to tell. When I ask her about it, she turns red and tells me not to ask that again. Grandma and I are 82 so we are at the fartin' age. As I think about it, I remember foul smells before we got the dog but certainly not as regular as now. So, is it my wife or the dog? I don't know but I have my suspicions.

title: It purifies the air like it should
text:
I have 3 different air purifiers, one of which is the Hathaspace 6-in-1 Large Room air purifier. I have them in different locations in the house, and all of them work well at reducing my allergies. I haven't really done a comparison of air quality between the different brands, however, this air purifier stood out based on the filter design, which appears to have the most features of all 3 units I own and is the reason I gave it 5 stars. There is a small flaw in the design (in my opinion) that does not materially impact the quality of the purifier. I really hate the retaining tabs for the filter because the filters fit snugly on their own and the retaining tabs do not stay put while trying to put the filters in.

Compared to my other 2 air purifiers:

The unit is a bit smaller and has a little less air flow than the Winix 5300-2, but the filter design does not appear as high end as the Hathaspace. All other features are similar. If the filter design was the same, Winix would be my preference because of the increased surface area of the filters.

My PureZone 3-in-1 True HEPA Air Purifier is much smaller than the Winix and Hathaspace and lacks the air quality monitor that both Hathaspace and Winix have. At about $100 for the small size of the PureZone, I would not recommend buying the PureZone unless the small size is your primary interest. Running one of the bigger air purifiers at a slower speed results in a near silent air purifier for a small room and the filter life should be better (although the filters are cheaper for the PureZone).

title: Finally an air purifier that actually works--you get what you pay for!
text:
I got this air purifier for the room I keep my camera gear in so that I can change lenses or clean my sensor without lots of dust immediately getting on the glass. I tried two cheaper air purifiers from Amazon, but returned both of them because they did not work well, if at all. I use the "flashlight test" to see how well an air purifier works. At night, I turn all of the lights off and shine a bright flashlight in the room the air purifier has been running in and compare the amount of dust I see with another room. The Alen 45i passes that test, as there are noticeably very few dust specks floating around after it has been running and the indicator is blue.

Now, when I clean my camera sensor, I can inspect it for 20-30 seconds with a super bright LED headlamp, usually without even getting one tiny speck of dust on it, as long as the indicator on the Alen 45i is blue and my HVAC is not running at that time. Without the Alen 45i, at least 4-5 tiny dust specks get on the sensor while inspecting it, which makes sensor cleaning like whack-a-mole. I keep the ionizer on, which is a feature that led me to choose this over another air purifier I was considering. If I understand the ionizer feature correctly, it ionizes the air so that particulates that haven't yet been filtered out coalesce and therefore are more likely to fall to the ground.

Overall, I love this air purifier and think it is worth the premium price compared to cheaper brands. I actually ordered two more--a 75i and another 45i--to use throughout my condo because I am so impressed with it's ability to clean the air. One last point: as others have mentioned, in order to extend the warranty to lifetime warranty, you have to sign up for a filter replacement subscription with Alen, which allows you to choose an interval (up to 15 months) at which the replacement filter of your choice will be delivered to you. With this service, you get a small discount on a filter you need to periodically replace throughout the life of the air purifier anyway. You can also modify your schedule or skip a delivery if you wish. Therefore, I don't think enrollment in the filter replacement subscription is a big deal. Even if you don't enroll in the filter replacement subscription (which I don't see why you shouldn't), you will get a 5-year warranty by registering the unit with Alen.

text: My 13 week old tested positive on her NBS for GA1, if she gets a fever it can be fatal, so with other children (10, 8 and 3yos) we decided we needed to help keep everyone especially our newborn healthy. So off I went to Amazon to search air purifiers with reviews in regards to those with actual immune issues who could attest that what they purchased made a real difference. I didn’t want to end up buying some “fancy fan”. This gem most definitely works. My husband tried to say otherwise bc, yes, there has still been sick kiddos, but I know it works from it detecting issues in the air. For example, we have a wood stove and every time we open it to load or restart the fire, this air purifier kicks into high speed. If for some reason we are using a chemical nearby, it kicks into high speed. If there’s a lot of traffic into the house, again, high speed. I also have to vacuum the front filter frequently from all the dust and hair it pulls in. Our home smells fresher and when we first got it I could definitely smell a very slight ozone smell. We used to have an ionizer, and I’m sure if it wasn’t for using that in the past I wouldn’t have picked up on the ozone scent, and now I don’t smell it anymore (perhaps accustom to it), BUT, I appreciated being able to pick up on that scent so I knew it truly did have the ozone feature. Had I never owned an ionizer I’m sure I never would have picked up on it, so it’s not a lot, which is how it should be for everyday use. With an ionizer you can’t have anything living (people, plants or animals) in the area and even after for a while.
