title: Exceeds expectations
text:
*** 1 MO UPDATE ***
Still going strong. My master bedroom is quite large (~2128 cubic feet) and this unit will do 3.2 to 4.5 air changes/hour (ACH) on med/high setting and 6.2 ACH on turbo. On medium setting the noise level is whisper quiet.

Rabbit Air is one of the ONLY companies that I have seen post their sound levels (dBA) AND air flow for EACH fan setting!!! Most companies will tell you their CADR (on max fan setting) and how "quiet" their unit is (on lowest setting). This is pure deception. I hope RabbitAir continues to post these specifications and have a level of transparency unmatched by their competitors. I'm buying another unit now for the living-room to replace a different model.

My air quality on medium setting (note my meter is sitting about 6 feet away from the purifier for these values)

PM2.5 = 1 ug/m3 (I suspect lower, but 1 seems to be the lowest my Temtop M10 goes)
HCHO (formaldehyde) = 0.07 mg/m3
TVOC = 0.37 mg/m3
AQI (air quality index) = 4

In case you aren't an air quality expert, these are all well into the recommended "healthy" levels.

*** INITIAL REVIEW ***
This thing is very solid and thoughtfully built. I rarely give a product 5 stars, but this earns it so far.

Purchased a Temtop M10 Air quality monitor and blowing directly out of the unit it shows (on lowest setting);

PM2.5 = 1 ug/m3
HCHO (formaldehyde) = 0.11 mg/m3
TVOC = 0.54 mg/m3
AQI (air quality index) = 4

I wish it had more details on the built-in air quality monitor (the app just tells you generally if the air is bad/ok/good/best), would love to see what it measures and what the values are.

I had issues with the WiFi connectivity out of the box, blamed the tech, but found out it was my router that was being problematic. Worked around that and now haven't had any issues.

Have this in the bedroom and I turn it up to the 2nd highest setting for a "noise machine" at night (pleasing background noise). Turbo mode (highest setting) is of course loud, but meant to move high volumes of air quickly. On the lower settings I do not hear it above the ambient noise in my room.

I made sure to research a machine powerful enough to turn the air in my room over ~4x/day on low.

5 year warranty, solid build, actually does what it is supposed to do? Rare for a product these days. Of the last 30 things I've purchased only 3 items had over a 3 year warranty, and that was cookware, a garbage disposal, and a mattress.

I am looking to buy another to replace the Sharp Plasmacutter I have in the living-room. If you care about indoor air quality (and you should) then buy this.

text:

I am beyond happy with this air purifier! To start, it is large and powerful. You can feel a difference in the air quality pretty quickly. The thing that immediately popped out at me is the care put into designing this. text:
I have severe allergies and chemical sensitivities, so we own three units: a Jr for the bedroom, and a full-sized unit for each level of our house. They have made my life bearable and I never want to live without them again.

FILTERS
After five years, we have just bought replacement filters for all of them, and I realize by how good I feel that I should’ve replaced them a year ago. Austin offers discounts on replacement filters if the previous one lasts less than five years. FIVE YEARS! I love the incredibly long filter life! Replace the pre-filter annually and vacuum the outside of the unit once a month. That’s all the care there is. Way better than messy and costly monthly filter changes!

SOUND
Low is barely audible; even right next to the machine, I have to strain to hear it. We use this when we are in the same room. High moves a lot of air very quickly and so is quite loud; we use this when away from home, not in the room, at night (units not in bedroom), and when we have fumes or allergens to clear quickly. Medium speed is closer to low speed in loudness. I don’t find it bothersome unless I pay attention to it.

text: After researching over a week I got two air purifiers to test out 1) Alen Breathesmarte Classic and 2) Dyson HP06. Both are similar in price (when you consider the $99 add on for the FreshPlus filter for the Alen). At first I liked the Alen because it was easy to set up, not too noisy and super easy to use (not easy to move around if needed). But I noticed pretty quickly that the air quality sensor light was almost always red. Sometimes after being on for an hour or hours it will go down to orange/yellow which meant moderate air, but I could have it on all day and it would never go down to blue. Then for two days before we decided to return the light stayed on red. Even on a day when the air was supposed to be clean outside the light remained red. We thought it was weird so we tested it side by side with the Dyson (which shows the AQI level go up or down ever few seconds to show real time) and as expected the Dyson was showing green/clean air in the room when Alen was remaining at red. When we decided to return the unit Alen suggested that they send us a replacement, that they used to have this problem but that they fixed it. Hmmm..then I'm not sure why the new unit that we ordered less than one week ago was the one with the "old" problem and not the new "fixed" one. We lost faith in the product and decided to return and get another Dyson. So far we like the Dyson a lot~ many people have issues with the phone app for the Dyson so you should read these reviews if phone app is important to you. I just use the remote control and don't need the phone app so it hasn't been an issue with me.

title: Great Customer Service, Not so Great Air Purifier
text:
I bought the SPA-780A in Black with the Odor Remover Filter. I received it in November 2012 and promptly put it to work. I was looking forward to smoking a cigar inside a room in my home without the doors and windows open. It just didn't do the trick (i.e., remove the odors). After having a friend over and leaving the unit on Turbo for 4 days, the "next day smell of cigars" was still present. Now I like that smell. A good hint of vanilla & coffee from a good cigar. However, my wife doesn't like it. I called Rabbit Air and told them I would like to return the unit. They couldn't have been more pleasant. They were said they were surprised but that it doesn't work for everyone. They did say that some cigar bars in NYC use it with good results. Customer service suggested I give it another shot and put the unit closer to me. Well, I did, but it wouldn't have mattered if it was in my lap. It just didn't work. While putting together the unit I did notice the charcoal filter is very thin. It didn't seem like there was much charcoal at all. Now there are a bunch of other filters that go along with that so I guess that is their design.

In the end, I bought a set of new filters for my 10 year old Sharp Plasma Cluster. That unit comes with a thick charcoal bag type filter. It cleaned the room up in about 8 hours.

I will say that the Rabbit Air is a really good looking unit. There was no problem with them taking the unit back and refunding my credit card. I did have to pay $35 to send the unit back. I gave it 2 stars because the unit was really just 1 star but they had 5 star customer service. In the end though, I am buying the unit not their customer service. I am very happy with my old Sharp Plasma Cluster and will buy another Sharp when this eventually dies.

There is far less dust on the bedroom furniture now than before we began, but it's not a full solution. I didn't include a pic, but dust literally settles on top of the purifier on the control panel. As far as a smoke eater it's awesome, but it's not a smell eater by any means. I smoked one small cigar in my office, with the purifier next to me on auto setting. It ran full bore and the room wasn't smokey at all (12x10), and I couldn't smell cigar just outside the room. That was all good... I thought it was a winner for this purpose, then my wife came home 4 hours later (with the machine running full blast in the closed small room). She went into my office to grab something, and I thought I was surely a dead man. After she was done chewing me out, I went to my office and noticed that though there wasn't a hint of leftover smoke, but the cigar smell was still extremely strong. Fail, and I'm in trouble. To further the problem, I moved the purifier back to the bedroom that night, and it proceeded to make my bedroom smell like I was smoking a cigar in there. If you want to have clean air and smoke, this machine sucks. If you want to cut airborne dust, it's okay. I still give it four stars, because my wife vapes, and I watch the machine deal with it in real time and I can't smell a thing, so at least I know it's working as it should...I just had higher expectations when the machine costs triple what similar machines on the market do.

title: Product changed - doesn't work
text:
I've owned 3 of these in past years, purchased at Home Depot and Walmart. Until this recent purchase (May 2010), I hadn't bought one since 2007. They are no longer available in retail stores, probably because a couple years ago the EPA asked retailers to curtail the sale of ozone-emitting devices. They didn't ban them outright, they just said that too much ozone is unhealthy and could you please make it harder to buy ozone generating gadgets, pretty please?

Enter the new, dis-improved Ionic Pro. The reason I used to like this little device is because it used to make a lot of ozone. Plug it in for a day, and there was plenty of ozone to deodorize a cat box contaminated room, or a smelly closet, or a living room after a party. Now it takes 3 days to get enough ozone generated to smell it in a closed closet. The device appears to have been neutered in order to generate a minimum of ozone.

This reviewed product is small (about 10" x 4" x 3"), plugs into a standard U.S. 120V outlet, and includes a night light that cannot be switched off when the device is in use. It has somewhat complicated maintenance instructions for cleaning, because the tiny wires used for ozone generation must be kept clean, pretty much on a weekly basis, in order to work at all.

For those of us who want to use ozone for its deodorizing and disinfecting properties, these products should not be difficult to obtain, since they are legal and effective. Unfortunately, the EPA polite semi-ban means that you are now forced to buy such things from scammy, overpriced multi-level companies and individuals, rather than from retailers. I am unable to find this device or similar ones from any other online retailer than Amazon.com. I will be returning mine, because it doesn't work as advertised.

As a point of education, the technology used in ozone production is very simple and cheap and has been around a long time. There is no reason why you should pay hundreds of dollars for an effective device. Another point is that ozone is a respiratory irritant in sufficient quantities. So if you use an ozone generator, you should only use it as needed, and you should air the room out with fresh air between uses.

title: They work, but Ozone gets weaker after about a year of intermittent use.
text:
I bought four of these about a year ago. When they work full strength, they do appear to eliminate odors, by my observation, in small spaces such as bathrooms or closets. For larger areas a much larger unit is required.

If using it for mold or fungus or mildew, in order to permanently eradicate the odor of a mold or fungus you would need to remove it at its source. If not, the odor of course comes back as soon as the mold or fungal spores repopulate the room. Continuous use of ozone might however prevent further spread of the existing mold or fungus, IMO, if the source can not be reached and eliminated.

In rooms where the source of the odor was eliminated, ozone units do appear to eliminate the residual odor permanently, after a few weeks of use, within the square footage specified.

I also use much larger ozone machines, and those also appear to work to eliminate a damp odor that always seems present at our 4000 square foot house on the bank of a river, when used intermittently. I place the larger units on each floor of the house and they appear to keep the odor at bay. Those larger units typically have ceramic or metal plates that can be changed when the ozone released appears to weaken.

I like these units, but my main issue with these particular plug in units is that after a year they appear to have lost the powerful ozone odor they once emitted and there is no way to replace any part in order to regenerate the ozone to full strength.

I cleaned out the opening from where the ozone is released gently with compressed air and an alcohol swab. That did help somewhat. Still, the ozone odor is not as strong as it was when the units were first purchased.

I do NOT use the units 24/7 or even daily. I turn them on for several hours if I have an odor problem and then turn them off.

IMO, the units are best treated as somewhat disposable due to the fact that the ozone seems to become weaker over time. Perhaps internal parts are corroding, but I am not sure what the issue is. Because of the loss of ozone, and the inability to replace a part that would regenerate the ozone at full strength, I personally think they are somewhat overpriced. IMO a disposable unit of this nature would be worth about $20 for my intended use.

With that said, they are easy to use and easy to move from room to room. They are also very convenient to use in small areas.

title: Unsatisfying Dispursement of Air, Poor Range
text:
You know you look at a fan and the air is concentrated in some square or box shape corresponding with the fan? Well, this is basically the same... but instead of consolidated footage, it's two parallel streams of air at you. Which, I don't know why I thought it WOULDN'T be this, looking at the design, I'm just perplexed why anyone would find this type of disbursement of air superior in absolutely any way from a box fan. Two, thin streams of air at you, even when the fan is oscillating, actually just frustrates you more than relieves you.

I somehow thought the streams would meet in a way to feel like a cohesive sheet or box of air, but it doesn't. Perhaps it's meant to be experienced further away from the machine so that, across enough space, that IS the experience you'd have.

But the fan has such a short length, if it was further away, the air would feel weak and therefore provide little extra comfort. So you put the fan just next to you and suffer through a stronger "wind" but dispersed in a baffling and frustrating way (and I'm holding back. I'm actually infuriated, but I attribute that added bit of emotion to the heat that has been driving me insane this whole summer). I'll be reselling it, and buying better, more effective fans, and with the money savings, more of them!

Also not sure why sometimes it will change to "Red" for no apparent reason despite running for days at maximum turbo in the "Yellow" zone and no change in surroundings.
Air is taken in along both left and right sides and pushed out in an upward direction.
Keep in mind that when purchasing be aware that there are multiple choices from 4 filters, but you'll only get that one filter.
This being a Hepa purifier it claims to be limited to only 0.3 micron particulates and larger, so anything smaller (such as viruses) that goes in very well likely will come back out.
I like that it has an auto setting to allow the unit to adjust based on surrounding air quality.
The description claims to be sufficient up to about 1100 sq.ft but that would require using turbo (the loudest setting) and what you really need to know if the volume of air, i.e. cubic feet per minute rather than just the rooms sq.footage. For this reason, I determined after a few days, using it's own reporting of whether air was becoming cleaning that I would need an additional unit since I have very high ceilings.
As much as I like this product, I did not purchase a second but rather opted for a purifier by a different manufacturer that could trap much smaller ultra fine particulates.
Both products have pros and cons but in general I like them both for different reasons.

title: Highly Effective and Well Made
text:
I was put off by the price, but I really needed a miracle. I think purchasing a second unit might achieve that result. The house here has been smoked in for decades and has a horrible musty basement smell throughout, that clings to your clothes and hair. The smokers are now going outside to smoke (despite arctic winter temperatures which prevent opening windows) but bring traces of residual smoke back inside. Ultimately as heat rises, so do the odors. So, I decided to place the air filter near the stairs in the open upstairs/attic. This is not a large house, and it is heated by a single wood stove (which adds to the indoor pollution). Air circulation is an issue here, and having a fan helps. This filter is amazing at eliminating the odors when it comes in contact with them. Sometimes I have to move the unit around a bit to catch the drafts though. An oscillating base would have been a nice option to have for my particular situation.

As far as performance, I have not been having headaches from residual cigarette smoke, and I have not been waking up suddenly to the stench of cigarettes drifting in the air. Even the smokers here - one of whom has COPD - have not been hacking and coughing at night. When I first turned the filter on, the light was red and it ramped up to high speed. It wasn't long before the indicator light turned purple, and later blue. It has now been one and a half weeks, and the air is appreciably better. I can still detect the (now faint) mustiness even upstairs, but only after having been out for some time. That is clearly a separate issue, and I'm sure a second unit on the first floor would help significantly.
This filter is a little slower on clearing cooking odors, but that might be because the added-on kitchen is so far away from the filter that the food smells dissipate into a greater volume of air. We also have no fan or vent for the stove. Technically there should be a second air filter for the square footage of the kitchen, but this filter still handles all the air in the house impressively.

The sound of this filter is perfectly silent on low for sleeping a few feet away. I am as hyper-sensitive to noise as I am smell, and this is how I even discovered RabbitAir filters. Due to my air circulation problems here - having no central air - I have opted to run the filter on medium through the night. I am usually not a fan of white noise, but that setting is tolerable for me. It also guarantees that early morning smoke wafting in will be caught before I detect it. I chose the slightly less expensive model because I didn't want to ever hear the filter switch itself on turbo. Even when I have it set to regulate its speeds automatically, I have not heard it go to the highest setting, even with a red sensor light.

One more note: the customer service/support is second to none. I unfortunately did not get the unit delivered on time as quoted to me, and that turned out to be a UPS issue, rather than a problem with the seller. They were genuinely concerned, very responsive, called to follow up, and even sent a complimentary replacement filter kit for the inconvenience of having to breathe this horrible air for the weekend before the filter arrived.

Update Nov. 2016: I am still really enjoying this air filter; it is easy to clean too. The house smells remarkably fresher than it did almost a year ago. In order to maximize air circulation — because we do not have central heating — I run a personal-sized fan to move the air a bit. A ceiling fan would work even better, but we don't have one of those and the ceiling is a very steep pitch story and a half with no electricity routed up there.

title: Works on Vog and Pet Smells
text:
After much research on air purifiers, I decided to purchase the Rabbit Air MinusA2 for our condo unit. My family and I are sensitive to dust and the volcanic haze known as "vog" (sulfur dioxide gas & sulfate aerosol) that floats over the Hawaiian Islands from Kilauea. Our normal cooling northeast trade winds often changes to a humid southeast direction when there is a weather system passing over the islands. Many in Hawaii suffer from the vog with respiratory problems and headaches. I normally begin coughing and will often develop a migraine from the vog. Asthma sufferers are encouraged to stay indoors with the A/C running since the A/C will filter out some of the vog. We have a central A/C system in our condo but it doesn't do enough to clean out of the vog. I decided to look into hepa air purifiers to help keep our condo air clean during the voggy days.

The Rabbit Air units really stood out from the rest for its performance and good looks. They did cost more than the competition but the lower long-term cost of filters and the 5 year warranty make up for it. Their customer service is supposed to be excellent and their 24/7 service representatives are right here in the USA - not India. They can be contacted by phone, email, and through a live chat on their website. I had a shipping problem and they were very friendly and quick to respond and resolve the issue. They even sent me follow up emails to make sure everything was ok. For us in Hawaii, the 24/7 service is great since the time difference often means mainland customer service is available only in the morning.

I've been running the unit for about three weeks now and I can already tell the difference. My morning allergies are much improved. We also have two small dogs and although I try to keep the condo clean by vacuuming weekly and shampooing the carpet monthly, I've noticed that our place was starting to develop a slight smell, similar to that of a pet store. After running the purifier for a few hours, that smell was completely gone. I really noticed the difference when after running it for 2 weeks straight, I decided to turn off the purifier during the daytime when were at work. When we returned, the pet smell had returned. Running the purifier for a few hours help get rid of the smell again. We just recently had two days of vog and I didn’t wake up with any cough or headache so it seems to be working. I did however, go outdoors during the day with my kids and ended up with vog symptoms. At least I can breath easy while I’m at home.

title: Most quiet HEPA air purifier I've ever owned!
text:
So far this has been the quietest HEPA air purifier I've ever owned. I am moderately asthmatic, severely allergic to envronmental allergens, mildly VOC sensitive, and Autistic, so I'm very picky concerning my HEPA cleaners in terms of cleaning and noise. For those concerned about Styrofoam gassing (VOC), I can attest that there is a moderate chemical smell from the packaging (open cell polystyrene and cardboard) which dissipates after 6 hours of operation. Inside the Oreck WK16000 there is minimal, if any, closed cell Styrofoam in the baffling-- mostly hard plastics and a few neoprene seals. The HEPA appears to be approximately MERV-13, given the density of the material's weave and airflow output. The carbon prefilter is thin (1/8-inch thick), which is easily replaced with the standard 1/4-inch stuff that is readily available in big rolls. I took an average of my own HEPA air cleaners' decibel ratings at different distances and heights for comparison:

Oreck WK1600 (Small Room) CEDR= 100; Low= 10 dB; Mid= 28 dB; High= 49dB.
Hunter 30090 (Small Room) CEDR= unlisted; Low= 36 dB; Mid= 42 dB; High= 48dB.
Whirlpool Whispure AP51000K (L.R.) CEDR=315; Low= 41 dB; Mid= 47 dB; High= 51dB.

***CONCLUSION:*** So far the Oreck WK16000 meets all my stringent demands for air purification, and is by far the quietest small room HEPA I've ever owned. It has become my HEPA of choice for my bedroom. Filters and pre-filters are priced economically, compared to other HEPA's of similar size. Simply put, I'm amazed and pleased. I intend to eventually replace my other household HEPAS with Oreck WK16xxx Air Cleaners.

title: 12/10 would recommend!
text:
I can't begin to tell you what a life changer this has been. With have lung disease with chronic asthma, I had 38% use of my lungs. Needless to say, inhalers and nebulizer treatments were part of my daily routine. 2 summers ago, the fires in NorCal were so bad, air quality was >150 for months. So the following summer, I purchased this bad boy in preparation for fire season. And while the fires never came, I could immediately feel the impact this purifier made in my home. Within a few days I noticed I wasn't coughing as much. I'd reach for my inhaler out of habit and realize I didn't really need it. I used to use it 3-5 times a day, now I use it maybe once...some days not at all. Now I only have to use my nebulizer when I'm sick. My lungs don't fill up with as much lung-butter as they used to. I don't wake up with headaches anymore. I just got to the part when I had to change my filters and the machine pretty much shut down until the new filters got here (which I ordered through the app and got here within 4 days....pro-tip schedule a reminder for yourself to order filters in advance so you don't have to wait). Within a day or 2, I was back to using my inhaler 3-4 times/day.

I also find it amusing how well it works sometimes. I have a smaller apt (650 sq ft), and most of it is open concept so I just have the one purifier in the middle. I keep it on auto so it will adjust as needed. I'll spray hairspray in the bathroom (down the hall about 8 feet away) and within a few minutes, I can hear the fan increase. It works quickly, too! Within maybe 3 or 4 minutes, the fan goes back down. When I cook on the stove top, it'll increase. I have cats and when one of them has a particularly rank poop, the fan increases haha. It's amusing.

Anywhatsit....it's a pricey investment but by far one of the best investments I've made for my health. I've probably saved more than what it cost to buy this thing just for the fact that I rarely have to buy nebulizer medications anymore. Good job, Rabbit Air. You have a customer for life!

title: Update - five stars - great customer service!
text:
The company responded right away and is sending two additional filters free of charge and they have already shipped. Also they let me know the smell is typically the charcoal filter and typically means it needs to be replaced. Mine were faulty (as they were new).

Sooo I can attest that I also had a moderate chemical smell in the first two to three weeks. I figured this was the hepa filter "kicking in", which means with zero scientific actual data (just a guess-timate on my part), but with good intentions to test it fully for longer than a week before returning if the smell continued. That said, almost four weeks in now and the chemical smell is sorta gone - I catch whiffs of it occasionally.

Here IS my actual data for what smells the unit is effective for / works on in a multiplex unit with a lot of character and not much installation between units (so - excellent test case) - works on - highly flavored vape oil, followed by incense and air fresher to "hide" the smell (it is a non smoking multiplex). Also fire place smoke from chimneys outside, and BBQ smoke (ditto) before I notice and close the windows. And because we just had Independence Day, gunpowder in the air from fireworks

I am going to contact the seller and ask if the chemical smell means I should return the unit - like the other reviewer ... but one way or another I'll be keeping it and I can verify for others that it's worth the cost.

Also the no light feature - eg to kill the many colored light display - is awesome and the unit is so quiet that I set a timer to remind myself it's on.

If you're having issues in buildings with your neighbors smells - especially when we are all mostly inside and WFH - I say go for it - you will be a whole lot happier.

title: a capable air purifier, but too expensive
text:
I've been upgrading my air purifiers to ones which have more capacity, better filters, and more features. This unit from Hathaspace seemed interesting.

I have said in other AP reviews – air purifiers are very simple machines – they just pull air through a filter. The better ones move a lot of air and do that quietly. The other features – like sleep, timers, and apps just make the unit more convenient in different circumstances.

With that in mind, this is a very nice air purifier but way too expensive for what it does.

It's a great, medium sized unit with a terrific fan. The fan creates a nice, smooth airflow and noise is inaudible at low levels. According to the company, it can clean 1500sq ft in an hour. (They don't ever mention the CADR – CADR measures an air cleaner's effectiveness based on room space and the volume of clean air produced per minute. I looked through this product page and on their website, but this unit isn't even listed nor is CADR on any purifier there!)

= Here are the things I especially like about the unit:

* sleep light

This is the only unit i own which allows you to choose the level of the light – from OFF to 5-levels of brightness !

* large vent holes

Larger and more holes means it's easier for the fan to pull in air, which translates to capturing more dust particles, etc.

= Here are the issues I have with the unit (aside from price)

* fan speed

It has four fan speeds (not incl Sleep mode) as indicated by dots on the display. I feel like speeds 1 and 2 are too close together in sound level. As it is, they are both almost inaudible. But the sound-level on 3 is more than just background, ie, too noisy. So 2 would be better moving faster (more noisy) and hit within the "background noise" sweet spot. Here are my measured sound levels:

Sleep – 34 db (inaudible)
Auto – 35 db (inaudible)
Lvl 1 - 35 (inaudible)
Lvl 2 - 41 (barely audible)
Lvl 3 - 68
Lvl 4 - 71

Lvl 2 should be around 50-55 db.

* button lights

The control buttons aren't backlit (note that this isn't the only brand with this issue). So in low-light situations it's hard to know where the buttons are. The situation is even worse when the air-quality light is up full-brightness because you're staring into a light.

The picture I included was taken when the room was illuminated by my monitor – so low light, but definitely easy to navigate when walking around the room. But couldn't find a single button on the unit's display about 8 feet away.

= summary

This is a capable air purifier – it's a good size, has great fan flow and it's very quiet when it needs to be. But for such a premium price ($350!), it's not perfect and I would expect perfection – it doesn't have any app capabilities, no remote, or any special features not found in many other, lower priced units.

At this price I would not recommend this to anyone. 2.5 stars rounded up.

I hope that you found this review Helpful !

text:
I try not to write reviews until some time has passed and it’s been about 8 months since we purchased this and couldn’t be more happy.

It was odd because we loved to San Diego which has much cleaner air and tested this in small isolated rooms showing the same issue. Upon contacting support they confirmed that some of the 45i units had an issue with a dirty sensor and would send a cleaning kit free of charge. We received the lot within a few days but it was still having the same issues. What did they do??? They offered us a free upgrade to a 75i!!! WHAT? This was by far the best warranty (at no additional cost) I’ve ever seen. The new unit arrived within a few days and here we are happy as can be with a fast/stronger device cleaning our home.

Conclusion:
I’m so happy with this purchase that I made this loooong review just to make sure any potential buyer knows it’s worth! Our medically fragile toddler sleeps so much better with this in our home and the same goes for my allergies. Definitely worth spending the extra money!

title: Smart Air Cleaning Robot!
text:
I read some reviews on here that think the air quality sensor on this unit "is a scam." I have one thing to say to those people, "READ the manual." If you read the manual it says upfront that the unit cycles through red, yellow and green for the first several minutes and does so anytime you reboot (unplug) it.

Anywho, on to my review. I just got 2 of these units yesterday. I bought a new comfort UV, ozone generator/ air purifier over a year ago. We noticed drastic improvement in our allergies. I keep the new comfort in my studio where I make music because I spend a lot of time in there and that room is carpeted. Not to mention, I also have a Pitbull and a SchnauMation. Both dogs obviously produce some dander even tho they are indoor dogs and bathe once or twice a month depending on how much time they spend outdoors.

So obs the air in our house has some stuff's floatin around. The new comfort treats up to 1300 square feet but I have to tell ya. If it's in my studio the air in the rest of the house doesn't cycle through it. So I decided we would get one for the living room and one for the bedroom where my wifey, dogs and I sleep.

First thing I noticed yesterday. By the way, I sort of freaked out when I plugged it in for the first time and saw it in the red. So I READ the manual and realized that's normal. Once the unit stabilized we proceeded to clean our house. We use vinegar to clean the floors and surfaces because bleach is too harsh for both my wife and I. While my wife was mopping the living room I was cleaning the kitchen. When I was done in the kitchen I went to clean the bathroom and I walked through the livingroom. I looked at the air purifier and noticed it had gone from green to red! It smells the vinegar in the air lol. Best part of this is, the smell of vinegar usually lingers. I know because my buddy came over last week and I told him, "sorry about the vinegar smell." He just giggled and said, "dude your house always smells like vinegar, I usually smell it from the car when I pull up." 😒

Well, yesterday the vinegar smell was gone within 10 minutes and when the smell dissipated the Hathaspace went back to green.

Later that evening I had a BBQ with real mesquite wood in the front yard. I usually leave the sliding door open with the screen closed. The smoke usually gets in and yesterday was no exception. Again, I walk in the house to grab a probiotic soda and look at the Hathaspace, its red again. It smells the smoke and works on clearing the air of it.

It smells hand sanitizers and pretty much anything you can think of. If you run it on auto, it works harder when it smells something. This is great. I'm thrilled to have two units in our house! I totally recommend getting one if you want cleaner air in your home. Last bit of input from me. If you have allergies to dust, pollen and other floaties you likely have some food allergies or sensitivities. With that being said, if you eat something you're not supposed to you will have hayfever type symptoms.

title: Air Putrefier
text:
I don’t enjoy writing scathing reviews, but some companies seem to be working hard to earn them. I’m posting this in the hope that it will spare someone else the lousy experience I had with this product and the disingenuous company that makes it.

The Molekule Air Mini emitted an offensive chemical smell out of the box that persisted for hours, at which point I turned it off. After contacting Molekule support, I got this reply:

“As with any new product, your Molekule air purifier will have been exposed to dust and other contaminants during the warehousing and shipping of the device. When you first turn on the device you may notice a slight odor as it starts to run. This effect is called offgassing, and is caused by the release of gases that have been trapped or absorbed in the device during this transit period. Please note that Molekule’s technology is capable of breaking these things down, and we aim to minimize this initial offgassing as much as possible. If the smell continue (sic) after the initial period, we can always replace the PECO-Filter for your Molekule Air Mini for free, which we believe should remedy the issue.”

I was creative director of a leading advertising/marketing/PR firm in Orlando for years. I know damage control when I see it.

“As with any new product?” I have never bought any new device, including any air purifier, that produced a smell so noxious, it probably could be weaponized—what Molekule refers to as a “slight odor” I “may notice.” “Dust” does not produce off-gassing. Furthermore, there was no visible dust on the unit or even the box, and the filter came sealed in plastic. What sort of gases would be ”trapped or absorbed” in the device during warehousing and shipping? And 24-48 hours for this to clear out? Most likely, the odor is caused by the PECO technology, which is at best controversial, the hype notwithstanding. (“Hype” is not an overstatement. According to the New York Times, Molekule was challenged before the National Advertising Division in a case brought by Dyson for making 26 false claims in their advertising. Dyson prevailed, and most of the NAD’s findings were upheld on appeal.) Finally, wouldn’t a replacement filter also have gases, dust, and other contaminants “trapped or absorbed” during warehousing and shipping?

Off-gassing can be toxic. This is supposed to be an air purifier. It’s hard to imagine an engineering/manufacturing failure that rivals production of an air purifier that stinks up the room and leaves you breathing in god-knows-what. My concern is that the Air Mini poses the same health risks as any product that off-gasses—and I’m supposed to leave this thing on, spewing nasty air, for 1-2 days in my house? Yes, the design is standout, industrial, minimalist, Apple quality, blah blah blah. Don’t be fooled by the pretty face. It only makes purchasing and having to return this debacle all the more disappointing. People who invest hundreds of dollars in air purifiers take air quality seriously. They deserve a far sight better than to find themselves dealing with foul, noxious vapors and a company that unabashedly tries to spin this deal-breaking defect into business-as-usual in a tour de force of “alternative facts.” Buyer, these days more than ever, beware. Returned.

title: Gets ride of stink.
text:
I use this purifier for a 12x18 foot bedroom. It is a cute color, the lights on it are not bright enough to disturb my sleep, and the high setting is conspicuous, but I wouldn't call it loud. I actually find the noise soothing, and my brain is picky about the types of white noise it can or can't tune out. The high setting on the purifier does move the air about as much as a little desktop fan would, so it does actually make a portion of my room colder. I haven't really used the purifier on low or sleep, so can't comment on how those settings affect air quality.
I own a large bearded dragon, and when she poops it makes my whole room stink. This air purifier significantly reduces the smell! I used to be able to tell the lizard left me a present just by walking past my door. Now I don't notice unless I'm within a couple feet of her tank.
I also hoped the air purifier would help my allergies at night, and I have been waking up feeling a little less congested and my eyes are a little less puffy and itchy. I think it will be more helpful just as maintenance after I give the room a deep clean.
I took off a star because the red warning light to indicate it's time for a new filter comes on arbitrarily. It was on the first time I plugged it in straight out of the box, and it has also come on twice more just within the week I've had it. My room isn't THAT dirty and the filters still look totally clean, and I know from the instructions that I've put them in correctly. Luckily, resetting the light back to white is quite simple (you turn the purifier off and then hold the button down for 3 seconds). It's just a feature that isn't serving it's purpose correctly.

title: Finally, an air purifier that lives up to expectations.
text:
The Air Rabbit MinusA2 is a very solid air purifier. The unit itself is modern looking and attractive. I like the option to wall mount the unit. It mounts easily but be aware that, while it does include a mounting bracket. it does not come with mounting screws or drywall anchors. You will need to pick those up seperately. Make sure to have plenty of clearance if you wall mount. It sticks out 7 1/2 " when mounted and probably would not work well in a hallway or a high traffic area. The unit is reasonably quiet for what it does and seems to be very efficient. I ordered the odor filter in my kit since I have a dog and I have had people tell me that there is a noticeable decrease in dog odor since I installed the Air Rabbit. Also, I have asthma, I actually purchased this unit on the advise of my doctor. I have already noticed an improvement the breathability of the air in my home.
The only cons I have were:
1) I did not care for the remote. It is worthless unless you can aim it directly at the front of the unit. It wont work from any angle at all. It must be pointed straight on or it will not work.
2) The front panel controls do not light up so if you want to adjust the unit in a darkened room, you either have to memorized the button positions or turn on some lights. This is in regards to the control buttons themselves, there are indicator lights to designate mode and speed.
Both of these are minor complaints regarding convenience and do not affect the functionality of the unit, which, so far, seems excellent but it is something the company may want to consider in future models.
Finally, it would be awesome if they added Echo compatibility to the unit. That would solve the remote control and button issues in one move.

I included two pictures of the unit, mounted. Dont mind the cord dangling, that will be hidden once I get a cord organizer for it.

This is an excellent fan and air filter combo but it does come at a price. This is extremely easy to follow, you really do not need instructions but they are nice to have to confirm you did it right.
Now this stands over 4 feet tall but is very slim so it will easily replace any floor fan you might be using. The breeze created is very nice and should be cooling during the summer. The air is pulled in through the base (air filter) but after that it is a mystery on how it works.
Friends have told me it is very easy to keep clean, so that is also very nice.

title: Solid, sleek choice for bedroom air cleaner
text:
This is the perfect size air cleaner with a slim, sharp black design for normal sized bedrooms. I say normal because I have a larger unit I use for my master bedroom. After the first two days, the air quality is noticeably cleaner, especially considering how allergic my family tends to be towards pollen, dust, and pet hair, for which we have two dogs. The readings are intuitive to gauge overall air quality.

The only downsides are that the higher fan speeds get distractingly loud so we keep it at sleep mode for ghe most part, the lights are bright at night for a bedroom if you’re used to sleeping in a blackout environment (alternatively it’s a good night light if you want one), and the replacement filters at $35.00 are a bit pricey. Overall, it’s a good choice.

title: Cat allergy vanquished!
text:
Our granddaughter is allergic to our cat, and we decided to try this air purifier for use whenever she visits. So glad we did, because by running it for a couple of hours before and during her visits, her symptoms have disappeared! We’ve been satisfied with Dyson products before, and this one is no exception. It was quick and easy to assemble (only two main parts with no fasteners needed ), and the remote is very handy. It can also be switched on and off by hand. Removing the filter for cleaning is also a simple task. Finally, it produces only a low sound, sort of like a fan, while operating; the sound is imperceptible when running on a low setting, but if you want it to function as a fan, it can be turned up. There is even an oscillating feature. The whole appliance stands a bit more than three feet tall, and less than a foot wid and deep.

Quality product that functions well.

title: Big fan of this fan
text: This is a great fan and gives a nice breeze. Night mode works pretty well as I can not hear it at night. The air purification’s works great as well and I feel a big difference with it in my life. There was no hassle to build the fan and it was quick and easy to understand.

title: Excellent air circulation and filtration
text:
The Dyson Pure Cool sits in my workout room and does two things perfectly. First, it keeps me cool when I'm on my exercise bike or treadmill. It provides a nice strong breeze that keeps me from overheating. Second, it keeps my workout space from developing any sort of unpleasant odor, which has been an issue in the past.

Both are simple enough tasks, but standalone fans and air filters can't do them while looking good. My previous fan/filter setup was both ugly and took up far too much space. The Dyson combines clever engineering and excellent design. It moves an impressive amount of air for its size and does so in relative quiet. It doesn't overpower the music from my workouts, which allows me to keep the volume lower and not disturb the rest of the house. The noise from the fan is also a nice medium frequency white noise that would make this a great tower fan for a bedroom and sleeping.

The remote and other controls are easy to use. The face of the fan and filter are easy to clean and service.

The Pure Cools seems sturdily constructed and I fully expect that it will prove as durable and long-lasting as my Dyson vaccum, which is going on ten years old.

title: Works well, but quality of material and craftsmanship is poor for price
text:
I have always wanted a Dyson blade less fan, especially being someone that has young kids. But I could never justify the crazy high price point. So when I came across this AIRMATE Bladeless Fan via the vine program, and realized I could get it for about $140 (vine items may say free but we do still have to pay taxes on the full retail value like it is cash income) I figured it was definitely worth a try!

Being totally honest, if I would have paid full price for this I would have returned this. It’s not worth the $460 asking price and your definitely better off going with a Dyson or something of that nature.

It’s not that it doesn’t work, it does and actually does a good job. But the overall quality of it is not durable or made with quality materials. Its really flimsy and lightweight feeling, and there are some clear areas that you can tell the pieces don’t quite match up correctly like they should.

But as far as how well it works, I really have no complaints about that. There are a crazy amount of settings on it, honestly a bit overkill in my opinion. None the less they all do work and the higher settings put out a really good amount of air.

Maybe if this were closer to $200 I would be more forgiving. But the fact that it’s priced like a Dyson just makes the poor quality of the materials and craftsmanship all the more ridiculous in my opinion. I give this 2 1/2 stars. If it were in the $200 range I would go with 4 stars.

title: Purifier is cool, tracker seems suspect
text:
The purifier, for what it is, is a nice little device. It obviously isn't going to compete with a large room unit, but its portable and intuitive.

The tracker is more problematic. It seems to routinely report AQI numbers 100 higher than my AirVisual Pro sensor (which has been rated reasonably well in EPA tests) and than other publicly available outdoor numbers near it. It definitely is measuring something because putting it near the air cleaner causes it to report better numbers, but it seems like more of a novelty than a useful measurement tool. Although this is disappointing, most other PM2.5 sensors run $200-$300, so it shouldn't be that surprising.

Bluetooth on both devices is a little unreliable. On the purifier, this is less of an issue as, from what I can tell, the only things you need the app for is filter life and battery level. The sensor, on the other hand, is much more useful when you can get numbers off it rather than the 6 color revels it gives you. On the whole, I have not had too many issue with Bluetooth though.

title: Great tool for ridding odors once and for all, but use correctly
text:
I purchased 3 of these mini units from 3 separate brands ranging from $39-$55 They are all EXACTLY THE SAME UNIT, just different boxes and labels, so go with the cheapest one you find. This little unit packs a punch and really does work! Ozone is the same thing used to treat mold houses and fire damaged smoke houses. Just remember you want to use it as a shock treatment not an ongoing all the time treatment.

THE PROPER WAY TO USE:
Plug it in to the wall, turn it on max, shut the room door. wait 6-12 hours for it to fill the room with ozone, come back, unplug the unit and air out the room with fresh air from outside, your room will no longer smell. Repeat this process every 2 weeks.

PROS:
- works realllly well, it will totally knock out and destroy whatever smells are in that room.
- You can buy a 12v-110v adapter and use this over night in the car. It made my car smell new again.
- on max setting it really pumps out a good amount of ozone, much higher than I had expected for such a small unit.

CONS:
- NOT an air purifier or air filter, it should not take the place of one.
- NOT for use in an occupied room, Ozone will irritate your lungs and throat, so don't use this in place of an air purifier.
- Use as a one time shock treatment, not as a unit that you can leave plugged in always.

*Note, for basements or litter box rooms, you might be able to leave this unit plugged in and set to lowest setting. I would only recommend this if its a room you will not spend much time in. After 10 mins your throat and lungs will feel a little irritated.

If you use this the correct way, it is a super investment and will add value to your home and vehicle.

title: Well designed and executed, nonwashable filters
text:
This machine is simple to operate and maintain, and it has features that make it fit well in any kind of room, bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, living room (if appropriately sized).

Filters 145 cubic feet, i.e. over 5 x 5 x 5 feet, per minute on the high setting, which is the industry recommended amount for up to 225 square feet (with an 8-foot ceiling).

The auto sniffer really works. If I put it in my kitchen and start to saute onions in butter, the machine quickly turns itself on and starts filtering.

There's also an easy-to-set timer for 2, 4 or 8 hours.

It's quiet, almost inaudible on the low setting, like a quiet room fan on high.

You can set it so the lights on it are dimmed for the bedroom.

The filters fit snugly without space for air to get around them. They're easy to change. The machine will let you know when they get too plugged up to work well.

The filters that come with the machine are supposed to last a year with 12 hours daily use. A replacement kit for another year costs $30 plus $5 shipping from Oreck, though it isn't yet in stock.

Oreck tells me the filters shouldn't be washed. (Their email support was fast, took about an hour to get a reply to my question.)

Two-year warranty against defects with proof of purchase.

title: Household desperate for good air purification to reduce Allergic Asthma in several family ...
text:
Household desperate for good air purification to reduce Allergic Asthma in several family members. On reading numerous reports, I bought one of these from Costco, ran it on high all night. It did reduce allergens Somewhat; that is, better than nothing. But unit is incompetent to adequately reduce mold, dust, dander or VOC's, in our area [next door to a commercial mushroom farm]. Granted, unit is too small for our house, but it should have done better in the room it was in; Therapure claims on the packaging, seem inflated.
The unit immediately smelled of new plastic [VOC's Not abated, right at the machine!].
The "Ionizer" smelled more like ozone than Ions: Question the company: is it really an ionizer, or is it really an ozonator, as some companies do this?
The HEPA filter is the only thing doing much work, but it is too thin; it will need cleaned frequently.
The air passes the UV light too fast to do useful germ killing; the faster the fan runs, the less contact with the air and the less germ killing via that UV light.
This unit MIGHT do well in a Small room no more than about 150 sq.ft., and only in an area not too heavily dusty.
This unit could do better, if it had a washable pre-filter, and an activated carbon filter.
We're returning this, today.

That said, looking at the specs, many modern units have higher filtration at half the size, half the cost (or less) - just check out the CADR rating, which you can find in some $200 units, that are more aesthetically pleasing. title: Very effective air-purifier at an inexpensive price.
text: The Hathaspace Air Purifier is very quiet at low speed and there is not much discernable noise at the highest speed.  The Air Purifier really works well and it does a great job of filtering the air in a 450 sq.ft room and making it feel fresher.  It has a built in sensor to detect air quality and change the speed of the fan, supported by a color indicator for the current quality of the air.  This Hathaspace Air-Purifier comes with an anion mode feature that works great and also appears that it cleans the room of gnats and other small flying bugs. There are versions, although no longer offered according to Hathaspace, that also come with a UVc feature. There is an "Auto" mode feature that works great and it adjusts the product function to filter the air as necessary which is evident by the change in the color indicator. The filters are easily obtainable and inexpensive.  The filters are easy to replace. Care should be taken to replace the filters as removed or as noted in the User Manual or there would be strange smells coming from the device. The design is pleasing to the eyes and makes for good room furniture.  The remote control is a plus and makes handling the controls very easy since the manual controls are on the side of the unit and are difficult to see and use. It will connect from across a 450 sq.ft  room. The "sleep" feature is great too and turns off all the LED lights and sets the product running at minimum noise.  Hathaspace's customer support is stellar.  Hathaspace's customer service does strive to make things right when there are discrepancies with the product.  This is a very efficient product that does what it is supposed to do at an inexpensive price and very competitive with higher priced products.

title: Successful cooking odor removal!
text:
I purchased Hathaspace mainly for odor removal in my small apartment of 600 sq feet. In NYC during winter when windows are shut, even the most alluring cooking odor gets old after a day!

I placed my unit which is sleekly beautiful and quiet, in my bedroom, 9 ft x12 ft. After several hours, I could still detect odor!

I was alarmed and wrote to the co; their email address is in instruction booklet, not expecting answers right away.

Lo and behold, I’ve got a reply within an hour!!!

There were many suggestions and explanations in the reply. As well as reassurances that I can always return my unit if I’m not at all satisfied!

I decided to give a “fairer” test based on the gas law of diffusion: Gas moves from higher concentration to lower concentration until it reaches an equilibrium. I plugged the one inch gap at the bottom of my bedroom door with a beach towel and left my apt for 5 hours with the unit running and anion turned on.

To my absolute delight, I found no odor in my bedroom upon my return and linger odor still in the rest of my apartment!

Since then, I have the unit on continuously in the main part of my apartment, near the kitchen area where most of the odors originate. I knew the unit is sized for a space of 250 sq ft; it takes longer to have a complete air exchange in my 600 sq ft adobe !!!

I recommend my air purifier, Hathaspace, unequivocally to anyone for odor removal! (I don’t know about its other functions at this point since I only had it for 3 weeks and I keep a superbly clean house, I’ll report about that later when I need to change filters.)

I salute the personnel in the co for their prompt and congenial helpful correspondence! It is extremely rare for the after-sale support to be THAT comprehensive, from offering tips of operation to suggesting buying another brand and trying them side by side, to returning the unit if not completely satisfied....., etc. everything they can do to make you a happy customer!!!

I have to say I was quite shocked, pleasantly, of course!!!

title: Could not be happier with my Hathaspace
text:
[[VIDEOID:cebcb0fcbfae2162bf64d2e0bfcf1b0a]] Absolutely works to clean up the air quality in our 1600 sqft 3 bd 2 ba Florida home. It’s super quiet. So much so that you second guess if it’s still pushing air. I added a video with sound to give you an idea of how quiet it really is. With it on the low setting, air is still being driven at a good clip but you can’t hear it. If you stand above it the fan is blowing strong but it’s still silent. Medium speed you can hear air movement of sorts. On high you can hear it whispering low. So low that if your sitting on the couch next to it the sounds of the TV are never challenged. As for it creating better air quality, I can assure you it does. After the first 24 hours it was night and day in my home. Since turning this unit on 4 weeks back my nightly routine of allergy medication has gone to the wayside. All of our allergy eye issues along with mild respiratory issues are now gone. The air feels lighter and any of the Cat odors have left the building. I can’t stand the subtle odor of a cat and I’ve complained to the wife and kids for years about it since I’m rather over sensitive to smells of animals I’ve never wanted. But I can honestly say now with this Hathaspace Purifier when I return home after being gone all day the air smells and feels fresh. I’ve never been a fan of a home that hints of the smell of pets but the things you’ll live with to make your children happy. Right? Well now this machine has taken the hint of cat odor out of the equation.

Visitors to our home have also purchased one of these and they love it. The instructions say to change filters every 4 months and the backup filters were only $30 so that’s not that much of an issue. I’ll probably switch out mine every 2 months since we have the cat. But that’s just me.

If your on the fence deciding which one to purchase I can assure you this one works awesomely and it was half the price. Like I said, we have 3 bd 2 bath one level Florida home and it cleans the air for our whole house perfectly.

I do recommend for anyone with seasonal allergies that can get trapped inside the home or with anyone who has a pet they prefer not to notice through their nose and lungs.

title: +1 Star because it looks better than many of the other air purifiers out there
text:
I have two of these - I have had one for about 8 years, the other for 6 years.

+3 Stars because this unit does actually work well as an air purifier

+1 Star because the unit seems is well built, and one of them has lasted for about 8 years running almost 24/7 without a problem.

+1 Star because it looks better than many of the other air purifiers out there.

-2 Stars because you will spend an EVER INCREASING FORTUNE on filters. Go check out the filter price (I use camel), and realize you'll likely be changing them every 6 months to 1 year depending on how often you have the unit running. That's either 95 or 190 dollars a year on replacement filters at the current prices. The best part is, when originally purchased in 2010, the price of the filters was 75. In 2013, they increased it to 85. In 2016, it went to 95. I've no doubt they'll break over to 105 by 2019 if this trend continues soon, and then onwards from there. If you expect the unit to last a good 10 years (and it is built to last), you can expect to be paying 125 or more every time. Know what kind of financial outlay you're signing yourself up for.

title: -VERY- Silent
text:
I just received this unit a few days ago by mail. Although I cannot yet comment on the purifier's ability to purify, I can say that on the silent setting the unit is almost perfectly inaudible. Standing at least three feet away from the unit I was unable to tell whether it was actually on or off on the Silent setting. At higher speeds it is still relatively quiet as well. There are 5 settings - Silent, Low, Med, High, and Turbo. It wasn't until the mid setting that I could tell it was on while sitting nearby.

As for its aesthetics, the unit is pleasing to the eye. The construction seems to be durable and there is a nice glossy finish along the front end. The "mood light" on the front end lends itself to the refined look that Rabbitair was surely going for. All in all, the unit looks and feels classy.

In regards to maintenance, The air quality sensor and a few other parts have to be cleaned every few months with a cue tip, while the main filters have to be changed every 12 months under normal circumstances, according to the manual.

If its air cleaning quality is up to par with the design of the rest of the unit, I'd say this was money well spent. Time will tell. I will update this review as soon as I can comment as to its affects on air quality.

title: My breathe easy.
text:
This was my prime day miracle.
I have been looking for an air purifier for my house but I didn’t want to spend an arm and a leg so I figured I would wait for prime day. I decided to go with this one because I thought it was worth it. Inside our home we have the following:
1 long haired German Shepard
1 Big boy German Shepard
1 pit mix with dandruff
1 black cat
1 baby
This has been my saving grace. We have old carpeting we are waiting to replace. We live in a woodsy area. I can go on about the inside air quality and how poor it can get but we do not have that problem any more. This monster of a machine does as its advertised. We have clean air and I can smell the difference when I leave the house for the day and come back to it.
The ring has changed multiple times and after a week and a half of keeping it on, it finally went blue. It will go yellow when we wake up and walk around; and will go red when the dogs come in from being outside.

The only problem I had was when I received it, it came with a puncture in the filter, it’s the size of a dime and it’s on the charcoal side of the filter. It didn’t seem to affect the purifier and it wasn’t being sucked out when the machine was on, so I left it.

Overall this is the best purifier I have had. I have had 3 different ones. This one I believe is giving us the best bang for our buck because the filter will only have to be changed once a year where as the other one had to be ever 2-3 months. The chapter one would also get dog hair jammed in it and I would have to clean it a lot more frequently, other wise it didn’t work. I highly recommend this purifier if you own animals or live in an older home(or both!)

P.s. there was a little weird smell with the filter when I took it out of the bag but it didn’t last long nor did it make my house smell weird. It was like a factory plastic smell, not a toxic smell(and I’ve worked and write about hazmat) That was my concern when reading the reviews for this thing.

title: Very Good at Reducing Stuffy Nose!
text:
We purchased this air filter, HAP9240 about a year ago to begin purifying the air in my room. Dust is a common problem as well as pet dander.

The device is simple and easy to use. It has a "change the filter" reminder button, but I do not use it. Instead I just put on my calendar when the filter needs replacing, which can be every 4-6 months. I can tell when the device is not as effective because the filter needs changing.

There are three speeds (low, medium, high) and an off on the dial. The noise is moderate and does not bother me while I sleep, nor does the noise inhibit me from sleeping. This purifier takes Aer 1 filters, and there are a few to choose from. I found a lower price at Walmart.com and went there instead of paying twice the price on Amazon. Shop around.

The purifier does not completely remove my stuffy nose. It does, however relieve some pressure, clears both of my nostrils for breathing at night, and makes the air feel fresher when I walk into the room. It isn't the end all, be all utopia of allergy free living, and despite what reports say- it does allow me to sleep at night a lot easier.

I had a lot of beefs waking up with an itchy or stopped up nose with sinus pressure. The purifier, for the price does a good job and I am happy we purchased it.

title: Great so far!
text:
[Orginal 5/31/19]
I just got this, and was impressed, so I wanted to leave a review.
So, the only other air filter I have used is a GermGuardian AC4825. It's roughly half the price (I paid $80 for the germ guardian, and it's made for about 167 sq.ft). This one, I paid $144, and I think I saw this should handle up to a 400 sq.ft room, although the description says, "In an average 350 sq. ft. room, our air purifier will completely exchange and replace the air 2 times per hour."

Anyway, the Germ Guardian was good. it blows hard, and runs quiet, and these purifiers are so expensive, I thought I had found a good deal on price/performance/noise, because spending $100 on an air purifier seemed a bit much. One thing that bugged me though was how the grill on the front implies it will blow straight, but it actually comes out the corner of it. It works well, but I was hoping for one that would blow straight.

This one sucks in the front and blows out the top. I wish it sucked in the back and blew out the front so I could use it like a fan in my office. But I like that it doesn't use a cylindrical fan, it uses a typical pressure fan, and a nice wide filter.

This is expensive if it's your first air purifier, but I think it's worth it. I thought the other one was worth it, and this is less than double the price, and can clear more than double the room size, and it has more filters (the filters are clearly higher quality, I was impressed when unwrapping them). The air sensor is also really cool and one of the main reasoning I wanted to try this. The whole unit is just designed really well. I don't know anything about this brand, but it came across like a no-name Amazon brand, but I am very impressed with the quality. This is definitely a serious brand. The front panel is actually attached with magnets on the bottom and a half-hinge on the top. This was, it cannot wear out or break with repeated opening/closing like a pressure tab.

One thing is that the auto-fan is unclear. If you set the fan speed and want to switch back to auto, how do you do that? I'm guessing I have to just turn the unit off and turn it back on? I wish it would have a dedicated button to turn auto on or off, and then let the speed setting be a min or max if auto is turned on.

I will say about my old one, it must have been doing a pretty good job because I have a dusty office (attached to a warehouse in a very dusty/pollen field) and this thing ran on red for probably less than a minute before it went all the way down. Turning it off, then back on, it did the same process, so I guess every time it turns on it's red while it checks out the air.

If I place the purifier in a new room (large bedroom size) with untreated  air it only takes about 5-7 mins to eliminate odors using the ozone option. That said the ozone needs to be intermittent otherwise it is counterproductive (for breathing). I had tried a lesser air purifier (major appliance brand-nice quality around $400) and it didn't even come close to this one: If asthma or mold is a problem I highly recommend this appliance (fyi-ALENCORP offers financing if you buy direct from their website).

I only gave this machine 4 stars because, while it happily does what I bought it to do, I think it is considerably more expensive than perhaps it needs to be. Also mine has a defect somewhere in that it refuses to use the batteries. The company was exceptionally helpful in providing an additional battery to see if that would solve the problem, which it didn't, and would have been happy to exchange the whole machine if I asked. In the end however I don't visualize why I would need this to be a portable machine and just run on batteries, so for my use I declined the vendor's offer to replace it and it sits on my counter happily sucking up smoke every time I decide to indulge in my burn coffee bean habit.

title: Most helpful with larger airborne particles like smoke
text: I made a simple air purifier "box" with muffin fan and hepa filter and added the pair of these ion generators inside the box by installing a standard wall outlet to the "box".  The air is drawn in over the filter, past the ion generators, and then over the muffin fan back into the room.  To date the muffin fan is still working fine so I'm not sure how much the warning about placing these ion generators near electronic devices is really necessary.  The muffin fan is a brushless 48Vdc model so I know there are some electronics inside.  Anyway, I used the fan/filter combo for a few weeks before I received the ion generators so I had an idea of how much "stuff" was in my home by the filter condition.  After installing the ion generators I continued using my homebuilt "air purifier" and noticed that the filter was getting much dirtier than before.  I'd read that use of ion generators often left black soot or dust that needed regular vacuuming clean up.  The ionizers were certainly were causing the inlet side of the filter to turn more black than I noticed without having them in the air purifier.  From my simple perspective, if the filter is getting dirtier with the ion generators, then they must be helping the filter to collect more "stuff" out of the air.  That's certainly better air for me.  So, I do feel they are helpful.  This design with the carbon brushes on the front of the unit (so my fan would draw filtered air over them) made more sense to me than the designs with the brushes on bottom of the unit (which would have been off to the side of the airflow thru my box).  The power consumption is so low it barely registers on an ampmeter when I tested them before installing so no worries about ramping up the electric bill from these devices.  Overall, I'm very pleased with these installed in my homebuilt air purifier.  I do believe having the fan drawing air over them significantly improves their performance vs just being installed in a wall outlet with limited airflow around them to circulate the ions they create.  In addition, I've put well over a hundred hours of use on my air purifier and the ion generators indicate they are working just like when I first installed them.  I have read that cleaning of the carbon brushes by lightly brushing them (and/or using cleaning brush wetted with some iso alcohol) will keep the ionizer operation at peak performance.  I do this simple cleaning whenever I replace the filter so it's a minor maintenance task.  Overall, I've very pleased with these ionizers and would certainly buy them again if I build another air purifier or if these should fail in the future.

title: Big downgrade for more money.
text:
So I used to have the AM05 but sadly it was one of the heaters recalled to possibly being a fire hazard. I sent it away and received this HP01 as a replacement. I definitely regret it and should have went with a differnt brand

HEATING - Im not sure if its the oval part being smaller than the AM05 or maybe its less powerful overall but I used to need the AM05 for a few hours at 72 degrees and it would eventually shut off for my basement area depending on how cold it was outside. Even on near 0 degree days it would eventually get there. Im writing this review now on a 40 degree day where the basement isnt that cold. Yet on the 72 degree setting this HP01 hasnt shut off after close to 6 hours of running. Still chilly down here as im sitting right by it. Im sure theres some tech sheet that says this is the same or better than the AM05 but in my case it definitely doesnt do as good a job as my old AM05.

REMOTE - So the AM05 had controls on it so you could easily change the temp or speed. Those buttons are gone and you need the remote for a similar level of ease. While on the remote topic they clearly downgraded something related to their remotes. I run this in the basement and if the kids left it on I could easily turn the AM05 off from the top of the stairs with its remote. This HP01's remote absolutely doesnt go that far. I have to walk halfway down the stairs for it to work. Maybe this isnt a big deal to most but if you plan to have this across a large room or far from you I absolutely wouldnt count on the remote working as well as older Dysons.

FILTER - Ah yes theres a filter now. I know hepa is the way to go for everyone but IMO the reduction in quality and functionality of this thing absolutely isnt worth the additional filter. Add on top of that the replacement filter itself is $70 and the generic knock offs are plagued with compatibility issues. This means youre locking yourself into some pretty high maintenance costs which Im sure Dyson is overjoyed to have people willingly line up for. Google about this filter and you'll see if you ignore changing it too long you'll get an error code and eventually it will stop working altogether.

If you're looking at this for its fancy look, high price assuming quality, or just Dyson name in general I think you should look elsewhere. This is a downgrade over their previous products. Offering less with higher upkeep with the addition of the filter. I dont believe this is an improvement to the hot+cool line as much as its a downgrade meant to milk more money out of people gullible enough to buy based on name and luxury price.

Maybe if you have a small room or office this could work out for you. Maybe if you dont mind around $70+ filter costs instead of running a separate and likely cheaper hepa air filter this could work out for you. For me this thing largely doesnt make sense and theres no way I could recommend you spend $500-$600 plus to lock yourself into a sub-par heating solution and the bragging rights of being able to overpay for a hepa filter.

title: My first air purifier and I like it!
text:
I was diagnosed with adult-onset (?) asthma about five years ago. I have experienced bronchitis, pneumonia, and now asthma. I have never been diagnosed with allergies but I notice that in the spring I always have respiratory issues. We also discovered black mold in the guest room next to a bathroom a few years ago and had to get rid of that.
I studied reviews and compared HEPA air purifiers before I ever finally bought one. I looked at expensive and cheap ones and all in between. I even signed up with Consumer Reports to help me decide. I knew I wanted a true HEPA filter and a charcoal filter. My room is large enough that I needed a certain size air purifier. I also was hospitalized for acute bronchitis for five days and figured I had better do something about the air in my bedroom.
I finally decided on the Hathacourt due to the size, the filters, and the price. I figured if it did not work well, I would move it to another, less-used room and order a different air purifier.
I am happy to report that the Hathacourt is doing everything I wanted in an air purifier. A big plus is the remote control that I can use from the bed in my room. Another thing that I have noticed but don't know how it knows - the air purifier seems to respond to levels of impurities in the air. Sometimes it changes the speed of its fan based on, I guess, what it senses in the air running through it. I basically leave the thing running all the time. I am still recuperating from the hospital stay but I am slowly getting better. I do not want to breathe in dust, mold spores, allergens, or fumes from the master bathroom. This air purifier is treating me right AFAIK.
I am happy so far with this air purifier unit.

title: My personal fortress of solitude
text:
As an adult suffering from allergies and other related respiratory ailments , I thought it was time for me to really analyze the air I breathe and ensure that it is healthy for me. So when I came across the Wynd Essential Mini Air Purifier, I was immediately impressed by the concept of being able to control what I breathe in everywhere I go. The Wynd purifier is very simple to use, One button powers it on and you twist the top to adjust the level of air filtration you desire. On the lowest settings, you will barely believe the device is on but on its highest settings, it is a mini white noise machine (which helps me sleep like a baby so that falls in the plus column for me) It paired with my phone without any issues and allows me to ability to control the Wynd remotely including being able to turn off the bright light on top of the unit when you are trying to sleep (this can also be done on the unit itself by hitting the Auto button twice) The app also gives you a filter life monitor so you will know when it's time to replace it. Filters pop in really easy like popping in a fresh battery on a flashlight. The essentials does not come with the air tracker of the plus model, so I can't attest to its capability nor does the auto mode on the device seem effective without it. The effective range is limited, but as long as you can keep it within a few feet of you, the air that it puts out feels cool and refreshing. As a Lyft driver, I love keeping this device running in my cup holder to circulate clean air inside my car cabin (without having to open the windows) It comes with a stand to tilt and point the Wynd in your direction however, the stand can bit flimsy as it topples over very easily. The price point may scare some away but, you get a quality product that will get the job done well as long as you don't push the device past its intended scope. I would look elsewhere if you need a more stationary solution or need to clean large amounts of air in a big space. Overall, I'm very pleased with the Wynd purifier and gladly recommend it to others with its unparalleled portability and performance.

Pros:
Fresh air wherever you are
Great battery life
Functional companion smartphone app with useful features
Filters are easy to change and are relatively inexpensive ($12.50)
USB-C charging
Essentials model is much cheaper than the Plus (excludes air tracker)

Cons:
Pricey considering you can buy bigger purifiers for cheaper
Limited scope of effectiveness
Flimsy stand
A little noisy at maximum settings
Auto mode/ AQI app features ineffective without the tracker in the Plus model
