title: Disappointing: Overpriced and Loud
text:
With all the fires and the resulting bad air quality in California right now, we bought the Molekule Air Mini as an additional air filter for our home.

The Molekule Air Mini looks sleek and sort of cute. However, that's pretty much all it has going for itself. It works ok in a small - and I mean less that 150 sf - room, even though it's supposedly designed for rooms up to 250 sf. If you really want to clean a 250 sf room, you'd have to run it at higher fan speeds. That would be ok, if the Molekule wasn't so noisy. If you run it at setting 3 and higher, it's annoyingly loud. Definitely too loud for my liking. We also have a Winnix 5500-2, which is much quieter, cleans rooms up to 360 sf, comes with a remote, and costs less than half of the Molekule Mini. Here's my overall review.
Pros:
- Sleek design

Cons:
- Noisy
- Inefficient in rooms larger than 150 sf. We have an indoor air quality sensor, so we were definitely able to see how well the Molekule performed in different rooms.
- Useless app (it doesn't do anything other than constantly offer you to buy replacement filters)
- No remote
- Expensive replacement filters

To sum it up - save your money. There are much cheaper and better air purifiers out there.

text:
This air purifier cleans the air fantastically, easily on par or better than the Blueair 603 I returned in exchange for it. It has far more features than the 603 and looks better (to me). The 603 had a "whistling" sound that drove me crazy, and more than a few reviews I read commented on that as well. Turns out the Alen has a similar issue...might be a thing with these air purifiers, though I have no idea why. I went through two Blueair 603s and also two Alen Breathesmarts, and they all "whistled". Many people won't notice it, but I've got sensitive hearing...if you do hear it, you won't be able to ignore it, definitely not if you're sleeping. Luckily mine is in the living room.

I'm going to stick with the Alen because I need a high quality air purifier, and the whistle is very low pitched and barely noticeable on the lowest speed. I feel like these are too expensive to have this kind of noise (the fan itself is very quiet), but that's the way it is, unfortunately.

It has completely changed my breathing and I no longer suffer from congestion and can breathe normally again!! I felt an immediate difference after I set it up (which was extremely easy as I am not good at setting things up lol). It really is a “smart” air purifier because it will tell you if your air is “bad” by turning red and if your air is good, it will be green. It’s not loud at all and there’s also a sleep option so it’s more quiet (although it’s quiet without the sleep option as well). My only is concern is that it says it covers up to 300 sq ft but my room is smaller than that but when I move it from one side of the room, the other side will be “dirty” and turn red but it takes literally one minute and I feel a difference in my airway. title: Expensive. Works well. Lacking some gimmicky features.
text:
I was not familiar with the Alen brand but they seem to have good reviews from customers so I decided to spend the extra money and give it a try.

We were all suffering from dust or whatever allergies. Coughing, sneezing, runny nose, etc. This machines does help a bit. We're experiencing less of those symptoms after using it. However, it gives out a plastic smell when we first turned it on and it still has it after couple days. I hope it will go away after it has fully broken in. It only has one big thick filter comparing to the Winix I have in my room which has a thin pre filter, a HEPA, and a carbon. (The Winix is very good, too but it's for a smaller area). But the Alen is still very effective.

This might be the smallest BreatheSmart series air purifier but it still quite large. And it does move a lot of air. Also note that it says it will cover 700 sq ft on highest fan speed only. It has 4 fan speeds and the manual states that it will cover 200, 300, 400, 700 sq ft respectively.

I should've read the description more carefully but unlike its bigger BreatheSmart siblings, this FLEX does not have an automatic mode. So it does not have sensors that detect air quality and the ability to adjust fan speed itself. It does not have blue, yellow, red lights to tell you the air quality. Only a on and off button, fan speed, timer, and child lock button. Also no remote control but that I don't mind.

Initial impression is good. Still quite pricy for my taste. We'll see how it performs long term.

text:

I couldn't believe all the crud that this thing got out of the air. (Actually, I couldn't believe how much crap just floats around in the air like that, that we breathe in!) Actually seeing everything that this thing captures is amazing, and I'm so glad I can breathe clean air now.

The high setting is a little loud but I only use that when I first turn it on. The manual recommends to use this setting when you want to clean all the air in a room in 15 minutes. So after a while I turn it on to whisper mode and it's pretty quiet. Of course you can tell it's there.. just like a whisper.. but it's not reallllyy noticable.

Great product, & I love that the hepa filter is permanent and easy to clean, and you can actually see that it works. (and I think it's worth mentioning that this is the first product review I've ever written. That's how much I like it!)

title: Surprisingly great!
text:
This air purifier is surprisingly really great, and I have been pleased so far with how it is working in my home. I have four dogs - two with medical issues that require fairly consistent cleanups - so the house pretty much always has some sort of odor to contend with, and this small but mighty purifier has managed to take on animal smells with ease.

I will say that I am not giving five stars though, and that is for several reasons. First off, I found the instructions on use a bit confusing. I also still have no idea how to activate the “odor free” capsule. I think that’s something that you use only when there are additional odors…or maybe not? Honestly, I have no idea if it’s optional in terms of refillable - it’s in the bottom of the purifier - or “optional” in terms of being able to turn it on and off. Really, I have no clue because that part is unclear in the instructions, among other things.

The purifier does throw off a bit of heat into the air itself when sanitizing the air, which warms up the room. I haven’t noticed that it makes the room uncomfortably warm, and it hasn’t been long enough to notice if it has made my electric bill go up an unusual amount, but that IS something to take note of. Overall though, since this little machine is making a difference in the air quality in my home, I’m still giving it four stars and saying it’s awesome. If you’ve been looking for a purifier where you don’t have to constantly buy and replace filters, this is the one for you! Highly recommend.

title: Powerful purifier that does what it says
text:
I am quite pleased with this dual filtration air purifier. I am using this air purifier in my home, and technically this one air purifier should be able to filter all of the air in my home, although I am using an additional purifier upstairs in my bedroom since I have four dogs my my home.

This HATHASPACE purifier is downstairs. The main reason I got this is because it claimed to eliminate odors, and while it focused on odors such as smoke, I was interested to see if it was effective on pet odors. It does do a fantastic job on pet fur, dander, and dust. I have noticed considerably less pet fur floating around the house since I got this. I am also sneezing less as a result of pet dander. Additionally, I have an actual allergy to dust, and I have noticed MUCH less dust on the hard surfaces of my home since getting this air purifier, as well as having much less reactivity to dust, both in terms of how much my lungs react as well as how much skin reaction I have. That’s truly remarkable!

As for odor elimination, this air purifier does a pretty good job; I’d give it four stars out of five. I have an elderly dog who is frequently stinking up the downstairs of my house (she isn’t permitted upstairs). I can still smell her stickiness every once in a while now right after she makes a mess or gets an upset stomach and has problems, but the issue isn’t nearly as bad (or potentially embarrassing if I want to have guests over) as it used to be before I got this air purifier. Plus, my elderly dog was my one dog who gave me a lot of problems with her dander, and this purifier filters out the pet dander so well that it’s much, much easier to breathe around her.

This air purifier is really a great value when you consider how much it does to clean the air in your home. It’s a bigger cost up front, but the power it has in purifying the air is amazing. A+++++, definitely highly recommend, especially if you have serious allergies or medical conditions and you need a powerful purifier to clean the air you breathe.

title: Quiet, Easy To Use and Cleaner Air :).
text: [[VIDEOID:df85a2a7c3091f74f7ef9bbbbfbbdf40]] This little 8"x12" Happi Air Purifier is very easy to setup and use by the way so you don't have to worry about reading the User Guide or anything with just only three simple buttons. The ON/OFF button is located in the middle, with the UV Light ON/OFF to the right (when facing it) and the Fan Speed button to the left. There are three Fan speeds with one being Low, 2 Medium and 3 High. The noise level is not that bad at all as seen in the attached video. Very important to remove the plastic bag from the filter before turning on the fan :). Just slight turn on the base to open up and remove or reinstall the filter back into the unit. The filter itself seems to be very well made and solid with multilayers including the carbon as well as HEPA layers. If you look closely at the bottom of the unit after removing the filter there are two little UV LED bulbs just above the filter located at the center shinning down at the core of the filter. Now the big question we all wanted to know is how effective is the UV light. Unfortunately, I do not have one of those UV light test card on hand, however, I did tried out the banana skin test and the result was....... well, not quite as I was expecting. So I removed the filter and with the lid open, I placed the banana directly under the unit in place of the filter (not recommended by the way:) with portion of the banana covered up. After running the purifier with UV light ON for 10 minutes or so, the exposed skin of the banana to the UV light was just the same as the covered or un-exposed part of the banana. I guess, no sun burnt for the banana this time, hence I ended up eating the banana instead :). May be I should have placed the banana a little higher up nearer to the UV light next time. Anyway, UV-light or not, the benefit of having this Happi Air Purifier still out weights not having one. The air is much better, cleaner (down to level 8) and easier to breath in my little 120 sqft office after running this unit for about 20 minutes. With the current price, I hope the replacement filter will be a lot more affordable (if I can find one in about 3 months :). By the way, to reset or cancel the filter change alarm, just press and hold the ON/OFF and UV buttons for a few seconds after start and it's good to go until the next filter change. Hope this helps!

title: Fresh Air
text:
The Avari is a small and quiet electrostatic air purifier in a white housing that can be placed on the floor or on a tabletop. A major design difference between this and other models is the absence of facing vents as part of the intake design. In my experience, [[ASIN:B00FSRBZPE vents]] accumulate dust, a counterproductive feature of an air purifier’s purpose.

In contrast, the Avari draws in air through its circular top below which sits the multilayered filter (the motor sits below the filters and also functions as a base) releasing the cleaned air below. It’s taken me a long time to review this purifier (I received it July 19), because I wanted to see how well it performed over a two-month period of nighttime use. We don’t own pets, we don’t smoke, but we do keep the windows open during the summer. I thought that was going to negatively impact the filter, but the top wasn’t discolored. The real test may be coming up as ragweed season blankets Massachusetts, and the colder temps cause us to close the windows. I'll update in another two months.

Overall, I like this air purifier. It doesn’t have that weird smell that ionized air purifiers emit. It doesn’t have the facing vents. It’s quiet and simple to operate. The filter can be vacuumed. The rooms in which we place it do smell fresher. I’m assuming the quality of air in our house is already above average given the lack of widespread filter discoloration. We’ve used air purifiers in the past, and are glad to have this one cleaning the air in our home.

text:

In auto mode, the filter selects the fan speed based on air quality and in the 5 days that I have been using it the filter has kicked up to medium speed on three occasions when the air quality sensor detected something amiss. Twice from cooking and once when it sensed something that I did not. After a few minutes, the speed returns to low. We have 2 long hair dogs that spend approximately 25% of the day outside and I have ad fewer sneezing fits since we started using the filter.
Now on to the customer service part. When I received the unit, I removed the filters per the instructions to remove the plastic they are shipped in. While doing this, I broke one of the 4 plastic latches or buckles as the manual calls them. I used the Amazon link to email the company and explained that I had broken one of the latches and was wanting to buy a replacement latch if that was possible. They emailed me back the next day wanting my Amazon order number, my address, and a picture of the broken part. They also stated “As soon as we get this I will send out the replacement and follow up via email with you. Once you send me this, you can dispose of the broken unit in the manner most convenient to you.” I sent the requested information and received an email stating that my filter had been shipped and the statement “you can still use the purifier that has a broken latch - no need to return that to Amazon or to us.” I received my new filter today. Now THAT is good customer service.

title: Filter, yes; purifier, no
text:
Pros:
The speed settings run as wide a gamut as is needed. The sleep setting runs quiet enough to be in the room without adding much noise, and the high setting can be loud but will move through the most air. The unit is small and unassuming enough to be placed almost anywhere and fit in.

Cons:
When something claims to be a purifier, I expect there to be more than just a fan and HEPA filter. If you're looking for something to move air through a filter, this will do the trick. Even on the highest (and loudest) fan setting, however, the device won't change enough air to make a meaningful difference in anything bigger than a bathroom. You could use this as a desktop filter if needed, when not aiming to clean air for the entire room. There's no mention of how to clean or replace the filter (since this is a HEPA filter, cleaning isn't advised and the filter should be replaced instead).

Overall I wouldn't recommend this unit to anyone that needs to purify air, but maybe for the area near a litterbox or any small area where a lot of dust is present.

title: More sleeping, less sneezing
text:
It was summer in Seattle and the blooming things were exploding with delight, unleashing a blanket of pollen on the city and providing job security for the makers of Sudafed. I'd grown weary of sneezing myself to sleep at night and of constantly vacuuming up dust. It was the summer I turned to air purification for my salvation.

I bought the Alen 45i on the recommendation of Consumer Reports. After a few initial hours on turbo, it settled into a quiet cycle on auto mode and I haven't had to touch it since. Pretty quickly, my dust level was significantly diminished and I was sleeping better. I found that when I walked downstairs in the morning I would immediately start sneezing, so I ended up purchasing the larger 75i for my living room (probably overkill for my space; it's a gigantic beast). Both units are extremely quiet unless they're on turbo — but they call it turbo for a reason — and they're super-easy to setup and use. They also look nice, and I like that you can turn off the display light on the 45i so it doesn't cast unnecessary light in the bedroom at night.

So far so good on the filter, though I haven't had it long enough to say whether it's as long-lasting as claimed. Assuming it continues to perform I think it's worth the investment for cleaner air and better sleep.

I don't like that when it's in "pollen" mode, you can't also manually shift the fan speed to "high". The air filter commandeers the controls and automatically puts the fan in the mode it thinks it should be (which seems to mostly be Low). We might kick it out of "pollen" mode and try the filter manually on High or Turbo, and see if that helps.

title: Hathaspace HSP001
text:
Just got this in a couple of days ago. I've been looking at air purifiers for several months and after the wife recently had a friend come clean the house, realized just how dusty our house had become.
Living a few miles out of town in SW Oklahoma and it's WAY dustier than when we lived in town. So anyway, after the cleaning gig, decided it was time to get serious about choosing a purifier to try.
Of course, there are literally HUNDREDS of them on the market so I've read many, many reviews. I kept coming back to 2 or 3 and then I noticed that Amazon had this one on sale at, what seemed to me, an affordable price.
So, with the sale price, the features listed, and favorable reviews I pulled the trigger on this one.
Took just a few minutes to load the filters and get it going.
It's a nice looking machine and seems to be built well. Nothing really flimsy feeling about it. The front is lock-hinged at the top and uses magnets to close at the bottom, so that's cool.
The filters are quality feeling and fit well. Nothing cheap-o looking about them.
The machine runs almost dead-silent on low speed. Noticeable sound on medium, and could probably be used as a white-noise fan-sound on high.
Using the remote is easy and you can switch through the options of having the status-display on or off, turn on the Anion ionizer or not, set the timer if preferred, and set it to 'sleep mode'. It also has an 'auto mode' for adapting to the air quality it senses by increasing or decreasing the fan speed on its own.
I've initially set it to low speed with the ionizer on, and that's where I've left it.
The wife asked me, "How do we tell if it's working?"............Ha, good question. I told her, "Well, I don't know, maybe we'll see less dust in the house at some point (with a shoulder shrug)".
So anyway, fast forward a couple of days and she remarked, "You know I was cutting onions for our soup (she is cooking ALL the time) and threw the onions in the trash, and normally they stink up the house, but got up the next day and couldn't smell them at all".
I got to thinking about it and she was right. No onion smell at all in the house. So maybe that's a clue that it IS working.
So I've got it sitting in the main area of the house, which is the living room/dining room/kitchen combined. Probably about 600 sq. ft.
My plans are to have several of them throughout the house, maybe like one in each bedroom and so forth.
I have since found out, through searching, that the same model can be found on auction sites and other 'for sale' sites in various conditions such as 'used', 'refurbed', 'open box', etc.........and many can be found for half the price or less, which considering, is a GREAT deal.
So with that I've ordered 2 more and can't wait to get them all in and going.
Recapping; I think it's a great looking unit. I looked at another unit that was similar in size but watching the video it really looked cheap whereas this one does not. I like the fact that it has an ionizer and I can opt to turn it off if I want to. I like the other options of a timer and the sleep mode if I need it. And it does have an 'auto' mode that works off of a sensor to automatically change fan speeds as it sees fit by testing the air.
About the only knocks I could give it are the status display is a little much, especially at night time. However, if you turn it off and the unit is on low speed then you really can't even tell that it's on and working. That happened to us, I turned the display off and wifey wanted to know why I had shut the machine off. So.........It'd be nice if the company offered a simple green light to let you know it's on if you didn't want to see the status.
The other knock would be that a lot of other machines out there have a washable pre-filter whereas this one does not. Is it a big deal? Can't really tell for now.
I'll update this several months down the line when it's time to change filters.

title: Practically Eliminated Parrot Dust
text:
I finally pulled the trigger on a Rabbit air purifier for my home office/bird room and I am so glad I did. I share my very small (7'x16') home office with an African Grey Parrot. Greys are dust birds, their down feathers are designed to break down into dust and that is the bird's lubrication, which is great for the bird, but not so good for my lungs or my electronics, spending 40-50 hours a week in here with him. Usually I would be dusting weekly, but I haven't dusted since I got the Rabbit. I haven't needed to!

The auto-sense feature works amazingly well. When I first plugged it in, it went to red/high and stayed there for a good 20 minutes or so. Since then, it's typically at blue/low. When I uncover him in the morning, it briefly goes to purple/medium. And when he flaps his wings for exercise, it goes straight to red/high. At high, the Rabbit can turn the air in my office over completely 18 times in an hour, and at low, it turns it over 4 times in an hour. Pretty impressive!

Mine came with the toxin filter, which is working great, but I'm looking forward to trying the pet filter in a year when I need to replace it.

Setup was incredibly easy, with quick setup instructions for those of us who are impatient in addition to full instructions. The filters are all clearly labeled, and it's been designed to make it difficult to install them in the wrong order and easy to install in the right order, which is very much appreciated.

Finally, mounting it on the wall was easy. I used a mishmash of wall anchors and screws that I had on hand to put up the metal mounting bar and then dropped the Rabbit right onto it. It sticks out further than you might expect at around 7", but I just mounted it in a place where no one looks at it from the side and visually it doesn't bother me.

Bottom line, this is a GREAT product that does what it says it does, and I was easily able to justify the cost since it was roughly the same amount I paid for an x-ray when I got walking pneumonia last winter. Hoping to avoid that happening again by inhaling a lot less bird dust now that I got the Rabbit!

Shine a sunbeam or a flashlight through the room and the dust particles are far fewer. Everyone’s breathing better. And you can see the hoards of dust on the device filter when you take off the cover. And yet, we haven’t needed to replace the filter yet, and it looks like we should have several more months to go. On the high setting the device is pretty loud, like a room fan on medium or high, or maybe a car AC fan up pretty high. On the low setting it’s barely noticeable. So you can control how loud the device is. When company’s over we have it on low; otherwise we leave it on auto so that it can change its own speed based on how dusty it senses the room to be. For the improved health and comfort, I’d say this is well worth the cost.

title: Sleek and effective
text:
I bought the 780N from RA directly, due to California law prohibiting it to be shipped by Amazon for some reason (called Amazon twice trying to find a definitive answer why, but no one had info to specify the exact cause.) Anyways, I contacted the manufacturer through their web chat (which is insane an air purifier company has 24/7 chat support when most cable companies don’t even have this.) I expressed my frustration not being able to buy the product from Amazon and left only with the choice of waiting for a backorder not set to ship for 2 weeks. The next day I received an email that they found a “reserve” unit in warehouse. I received it the day after paying for the item (shipped from Cerritos to San Diego.)

The front panel came really scuffed, but who knows how long it was sitting in warehouse so I kind of expected this. Nevertheless, I contacted customer service and provided a photo of the issue, and was sent a replacement, so they made it right no problem.

The unit is very easy to install on the wall, and looks gorgeous. I’ve gotten many compliments on the unit. The black one looks like a thick flat screen tv, like others have said, but almost looks like a neat server which is cool for a geek like me.

When the fans are up high after detected odor or contaminants you can hear them pretty well, but it’s not overwhelming. Turbo can get a little wild, but on “Auto” the unit has only ever gone to “High,” which is quite bearable.

I gave four stars on the “Sleep Mode” only because the timer after detecting a change in lighting takes like 15 minutes it seems. I haven’t measured it, or found any info in the manual about how long it takes to switch modes. So, if you’re laying down for bed with the unit in the room you’ll either need to turn the lights off manually or deal with a blaring bright blue bar for a hot minute. After which, the fan switches to silent (which truly is silent unless you really get close) and the lights switch off. Minor inconvenience.

Overall, I’m extremely happy with the performance, and haven’t noticed any issues with performance or improper deal with the filters. They seem pretty snug to me. Overall great product imo.

It just gets stuck on whatever the fan speed was when you turned the lights off. So in the shoulder seasons when the people across the street who heat their house with wood stove are dumping a bunch of smoke into the air, and we want to keep the windows open to keep the CO2 from getting too high, this filter doesn't ramp up and clean out the smoke like we bought it for.

I called Alen customer service about it and they didn't offer a solution, nor a replacement unit. They just acted like they knew of the issue and didn't want to deal with it. Said that it would still filter the air, just not as fast.

This is definitely just a firmware issue. And an unacceptable one for a $450 filter. It renders the feature that's most important for us totally useless. Unacceptable

I write this embarrassing story on myself to point out that there was nothing in the instructions that said the control panel would appear only when plugged in. Just remember...

But when I'm done, if i leave it running, the fan actually puts out a very stale cigar smell, worse than the smell of an actively lit cigar (regular smokers can tell the difference). I cleaned it regularly as recommended but no change. I contacted Rabbit air about the issue and they came back saying that its 'not meant for smoke'. Then why advertise as a smokers solution? After arguing a bit they sent me a new set of filters. They also recommended i leave the unit running 24/7 (didn't want that electric bill). I changed it out but even with brand new filters, it still pumped out a smell, although much lighter. I thought that was odd, if it's not the filters, where is the smell coming from? I have tried to let it at least run overnight but when i come down to the basement in the morning, the smell is worse than if i had just turned it off the night before. I don't know what else to do other than look into something stronger like a ventilation fan system in my drop ceiling. In summation, if you're a very casual smoker in a small room, then this may work for you. But if you're a regular/daily user, then put the money into something more powerful.

title: It does work, in my honest opinion
text:
During the forest fires of 2020 in Oregon our AQI hit 600 at times. I purchased a molekule mini as a knee jerk sorta purchase without doing too much research. By the time it made it to my house I had read up on it and was already extremely skeptical of its abilities. Many online review sources hate these things, and I suppose if their tests are true I understand their opinions.

That said, when the air in my home was stifling with smoke, it did really help- and now many weeks later we continue to run it in our infants nursery and his room has the easiest to breath, cleanest, most pleasing air in the house. I have a Blueair fan in our bedroom now as well and it helps too, but the molekule seems to do a better job. It’s not a scientific review, just my own observations- but their is something to the molekule. It really does seem to clean the air. I don’t know much of the science behind it, their seems to be quite a bit of controversy about how it works, or if it works... I will say, that in my experience, it works.

It’s initial first day or two it sorta released a plastic smell. If you are sensitive to that sorta thing, well, maybe don’t buy one. Didn’t bother me, but I was also living in some of the worst air pollution the US has seen, so... Also initially the setup was really stupid and my wife had to call the company to get them to help her get it running. Apparently you have to screw it together REALLY tight to get it to run, and that leads some people into believing they got a defective unit. Also the fan in it, when you turn it way up, is unbelievably loud. So we leave it right in the middle on fan speed and it’s fine. Also, this thing isn’t cheap, and you can get a whole bunch of other air purifiers for less. However, I think this thing actually does what they claim it does- though my claims are just anecdotal based on my experience.

title: Deceptive Marketing - be warned!
text:
First, what I like about this: it's attractive, relatively easy to set up, and seems to be well manufactured.

Now to what I do NOT like:

- Filter life: what they do not tell you is that their 6 month recommended replacement interval is actually a requirement. I used my Mini when I first bought it a couple of times, then for some remodeling reasons it got unplugged and put in the corner. 6 months later, I turned it on again, basically brand new, and the filter LED was red and it wouldn't work. How could this be? The filter has been used maybe a total of an hour?! So I contacted Customer Service, and while they're looking into it, and it may get resolved somehow, what i learned from them is that as soon as their PECO filter is exposed to the UV light inside, it starts degrading. ANd it only lasts 6 months. So what this means, is that regardless of how often you use it, they're essentially forcing you to change this filter every 6 months in order to keep using the product. That is just BAD product design, and borderline unethical. At a minimum, this should be made very clear to purchasers, that you're signing up to buy their expensive filters and replace them every 6 months if you plan to run this rather expensive little device.
- Aggressive Marketing: I downloaded the app, and I had to persistently click "NO" to avoid signing up for filter service. It's very clear what they're trying to do - they want you to put recurring filter sales on your credit card, so you will hopefully forget about it, and they'll get this lovely recurring revenue from you every year. Their Marketing team must be cackling with delight looking at their filter signup data. BEWARE. Also, I've seen aggressive online ads before, buy they are ridiculous. After I bought my Mini on Amazon, I was haunted by Molekule emails and online ads everywhere I went on the internet!! Advice... after reading this, and clicking away from their product page, clear your cache, delete your cookies, etc or you'll have a Molekule tail forever.
- Questionable Performance: I've done a lot of research into PECO, UV and ionization related technologies, and while they work ok in lab settings, in real world tests the results are questionable at best. The reason is that for all of these, to be effective the all need a lot of time immersed in the light, or rely on particles in the air floating around hopefully attaching to bad things and neutralizing them. Like shooting a bullet with a bullet. They make it sound like they've solved the world's air problems. Do your research, read third party tests and reviews.... honestly, I think we're all better off taking the $400 plus $100 a year filters and buying a decent HEPA air purifier with activated carbon, and cheap replacement filters, and call it a day.

In short, don't take their slick marketing and fancy science words at face value, do some homework.

text:
I wish I would have read the reviews before buying this product. I turned it on and the smell was horrible! Respiratory distress! I called Molekule Phone Support. The guy was kind and sorry for my distress. He spoke with me and then sent this follow-up email: Molekule Air Mini or Mini+ will have been exposed to dust and other contaminants during the warehousing and shipping of the device. When you first turn on the device you may notice a smell as it starts to run. This effect is called off-gassing, and is caused by the release of gases that have been trapped or absorbed in the device during this transit period. Please note that Molekule’s technology is capable of breaking these things down and we aim to minimize this initial off-gassing as much as possible. Please run your device for 24-48 hours to allow the device to break down any contaminants that may have settled within the device and on the PECO-Filter, and reach its full efficacy. Running the device will break down any compounds that were picked up in shipping and once they are eliminated any resulting smell should be reduced.

title: Loud and a bit smelly
text:
We got the Molekule Mini in a hurry when Seattle got blanketed in smoke this summer. We have a toddler and were hoping to at least keep her room's air quality good since she spends the majority of her time sleeping in there. The Molekule was the one purifier we could get within a day or two, so we went for it.

The unit looks great, fits nicely in a corner of her room, and is easy to set up (as it should be). We turned it on full blast (setting 5) - and it's loud. Really loud. It's hard to have a conversation in the same room loud. Cycling through the settings:
1 - silent
2 - barely audible
3 - tolerable in the same room
4 - annoyingly loud
5 - intolerably loud

We've kept it on the 2 setting in her room, and I can't imagine it's doing much because I can barely feel the air it's moving. I should have returned it, but I did use it on 3 and 4 for a couple days in my tiny home office when I was getting headaches. I think it helped.

In addition to the noise, it also emits a noticeable smell. It mellowed out after a couple days, but a month later it's still there if I put my nose pretty close to it. It's not exactly the smell of clean (after some rain, our aqi was 1 outside, and I know exactly what the smells like), but rather of something synthetic. I'm not going to claim it's harmful but it is a bit off-putting.

We've since purchased two Blue Air 411 purifiers (3 Blue Airs cost less than one Molekule, and the replacement filters are similarly cheaper too) and they have none of the smell. They're comparable on sound volume, though the quality of the sound is better. The Molekule's has an extra high-pitched whine.

title: Worth it if you have breathing issues!
text: I bought this air purifier about a year ago and do not regret it.  At first, I wasn't quite sure what kind to get with the plethora of models out there, but my Asthma doctor not only recommended Alen, but also suggested a HEPA filter model over the ion-only models.  I keep this filter on at night in my room while sleeping, but also move it to other rooms if I plan on being there for a while.  The controls are easy to use.  It has a simple on/off switch with the feature of shutting off the LED lights if you don't want it shining in the dark.  It has four speed settings with an auto-speed feature which adjusts the fan depending on the level of particles in the area.  It also has an ion option which works in conjunction the with EPA filter giving you improved filtration.  What's also nice is the timer feature allowing you to adjust how long you want it on if you leave the house or just want in running part of the time while you sleep.  It's not really loud on speeds 1, 2, and 3.  It produces more of a relaxing breeze just slightly softer than a fan.  The filter itself couldn't be easier to access: lift off the front cover and pull out the filter.  My electric bill does not seem to be effected much either.  There's no noticeable difference, so don't worry about it guzzling your wallet.  The only con I can find would be the size and weight of the unit: it is indeed big and bulky, about 40 pounds.  It's more designed to be stationary, but it's not real hard to move it either.  However, with this filter giving you 1100 cu. ft. of filtration capacity, it is necessary to have a purifier this size.  Sure, you can get those small space-saver models that will fit on top your dresser, but you get what you pay for.  They will only filter smaller areas.  I have a big living room and I'm glad I bought a purifier this size.  I have definitely noticed a difference since using it.

title: Good unit... with in reason.
text:
Ok... my 2 bits.
I have 2 of these units, have had them for YEARS. Don't know how many, all I know is I had them before I met my wife 8 years ago... they last.

First, these units are IONIZERS. Not air filters!

There is NO fan. Not necessarily a bad thing.I would recommend placing them up high, as there is no fan and the ions are heavy and only remain active for about 30 seconds. One less item to deal with. Like another reviewer said "if there was a fan in it, it better be sealed." These things attract and zap SMALL particles and it would destroy a fan. After shifting these things around I have found the best positions for them. I have one above my kitchen cabinets over the cooktop. We have a range hood that vents outside, but does not get everything. One of these on high ZAPS the stinky bacon odor at breakfast.

Another place I have found is NEAR (very near) and pointed at the HVAC air filter. You need a decent filter (not the super cheap fiberglass ones that only catch small animals and children) and I have noticed the filter get dirty faster. Again, not necessarily a bad thing. Before the ionizer the fine particles would/could slip past the filter. With the ionizer on, the particles a get charged and stick to the filter instead of passing.

Another use I have found, We have a tower Air Cleaner. I placed one of these on top of the tower unit, and just like the HVAC filter, it made the tower cleaner pick up more "stuff"

BE AWARE, because of the units ionization and some filtration, where you place it will be dirty. I had mine on a wall near the AC register, when I took the ionizer off to clean it, there was a very dark ring on the wall surrounding the unit. Kind like moving a picture on the wall at grandmas house that had been there, in the same spot, for 20 years.

These things are simple ionizers, NOT filters. For what they are they are solid. Another reviewer claimed the unit is LOUD. Yes and no. There is no fan, so no fan noise, however the sound of the 16 points electrically charging the air as is passes through, makes an electrical "zappy, fizz" sound. I use the sound as a sign it is time to clean the unit. When I can't hear the "fizz" sound, it means there is dirt on the points and time to clean.

Now down the the negatives. The only reasons I did not give it 5 stars.
The design of the unit does not allow very good air flow, it is a bit restricted. The unit I have above the cooktop, I actually have the top half of the unit removed. I DO NOT RECOMMEND DOING THIS. There is a serious "zap" factor with the plates and points charged and in the open. But I can say, the air flow is increased by 5x.

Cleaning, NOT the easiest thing to clean. The stainless steel points are sharp and close. I use a sponge soaked in Alcohol and rub the points and then stick the points into the sponge. The collection grid is fairly easy to clean, however when a big piece of dirt gets between the points and grid it can zap the dirt and cause an electrical arc (this is normal for units like these) But it can cause a build up of charred/scorched stuff on the grid. I have had to use a FINE metal file to scrape the fused on buildup. However, after doing this for YEARS (note years, these things just keep working)I have filed the metal back JUST far enough away that it really does not have anymore buildup. I don't believe it has affected the functionality of the unit at all.

I hope this helps. They are good units, for what they do. Please do not expect them to be room clearing, dust bunny destroying, allergy solving units. Frankly, without sealing up your entire house and spending min of $1100 for a crazy filter system you would find in a hospital, NO ONE UNIT does it all. But I can see these units being PART of an overall system used in conjunction with one another (quality HVAC filters, HEPA filter units, etc) inside a house to help relieve Odors, and fine debris

Like I said before, these are ionizers (purifiers) NOT filters. They make the air smell clean from the ions in the air and make dust clump together, get heavy and fall to the ground. These work best when used in conjunction with quality air filters

Hope this helps... I'm gettin' 2 more!

title: Product delivers, exceeds expectations
text:
I was skeptical about air purifiers in general, but after using this one for about 2 months, I'm no longer a skeptic. I used to be congested waking up, even though I vacuum often and my apartment is clean. I also had problems with cooking smells lingering for a long time from searing proteins and other stinky dishes. I noticed an almost immediate difference after getting the purifier, I woke up without congestion and the smokey pork chop smell from dinner dissipated noticeably faster. At first I thought it was just placebo, but now after 2 months of constant use I do think it works very well.

The machine is much quieter than I had anticipated. At first I used sleep mode when I went to bed, but now I just keep it on the standard mode as the fan is quiet enough not to bother me. I love the air quality test and adapt feature, the purifier adjusts to air quality by increasing and decreasing the fan level without you having to do anything. You can also keep it steady at one fan speed if you choose. At first I didn't think the air quality tester was real because it cycles on red for about 30 seconds when you plug it in, but after much use, it obviously works and legitimately adapts to the air quality. My boyfriend farted near it and the fan turned red, so there's also that.

The purifier is aesthetically pleasing and extremely functional, I certainly recommend it to anyone who breathes.

title: Bleach OK, beef not.
text:
I bought this to try and mitigate sudden, chronic, indoor allergies. $600 is a pretty penny to drop on a whim but after doing some research, it looked like this model held its weight. Unit arrived and was easy to setup. In a 600 sq. ft. room, it only took about 30m to purify the air, according to its indicator light. I suspect the impurities detected was the plastic wrap vapors that surrounded all of the individual filters inside; there's no way it cleaned my living area in that short of time... which told me my air was OK to start.

Regardless, I played with the different modes. Ultimately, I just have this thing run on medium 24-7. Noise level is equivalent to a desk fan on low. On the highest setting, turbo, it's loud enough that I have to turn up my TV to compensate for the noise. Overall though, white noise doesn't bother me so YMMV.

I also disabled the annoying blue bar light and turned off the ionizer (which required me to check the manual). I plan to move this unit to my garage after its remodel is finished because I plan to do some airbrushing there using the included wall mount.

As for my allergies? They're still there but not as bad. Did this alleviate them? I don't think so. I think I'm sensitive to superglue and that triggers allergy-like symptoms. If I limit my exposure to the glue, I'm OK. That said, do I regret my purchase? No. I'm certain it will be useful once the unit goes into the garage.

title: If you're on the fence, buy this now! Very Quiet!
text: I didn't want to spend this much on an air filter.  I already own 2 Holmes air purifiers that I ran full time in a one bedroom apartment.  I have asthma, seasonal allergies, and the standard list of ailments that plague a typical American in their 50s who doesn't lead a healthy lifestyle.  Then thanks to COVID 19, most of my neighbors were home more and to my dismay, I discovered that somebody in a nearby apartment must have reactivated their smoking habit because that was what my apartment began to smell like.  It was as if I was back in college when my roommate's friends would just puff away at all hours of the day and night, and no, management was not available to address this because it was not considered an emergency and the office was closed.  I woke up from a dead sleep one night because I had trouble breathing and suspected that it must be from the neighbor's cigarette smoke.  I tried keeping the balcony door slightly open, but the allergens that filtered in just made things worse.  So, I pulled the trigger on this product after reading the review about how one woman claimed that it detected the smell of her kid's farts.  The verdict: THIS AIR PURIFIER IS AMAZING!  Set up is quick and easy, and within 20 minutes, I felt like I had an extra lung!  When it finally cycled down to level green in auto mode (it has 3 levels of air quality, green, amber, red), I had to hold my hand over the output vent to make sure it was still running because IT WAS THAT QUIET.  As for odor control, the claim is true!  If I cook anything smelly, the odor is gone within the hour.  I cleaned my bathroom and this device must have picked up the chemical smell because it turned itself up.  I mopped my floor - same thing!  And when the AC kicks in (which is usually when I used to get the cigarette smell) this purifier validated that I wasn't imagining the smoke smell, BECAUSE IT TURNED ITSELF UP AND MADE THE SMELL GO AWAY!  I am am ridiculously happy with this product.  If you want cleaner air, especially these days when almost all of us are stuck at home, do yourself a favor and order this purifier.  It works.  You won't be sorry.

title: Worth the money
text:
My reasons for investing in a purifier at this price were for asthma problems. My boyfriend has allergies to cats and I own one. He would, on a regular basis, clear his throat or have frequent episodes of wheezing. Last year he was hospitalized for respiratory complications from two cats that he took in that were strays in his back yard, this is how he found out how bad his allergies really were. I bought two of these units from the rabbit air website. I choose to purchase directly from them to take advantage of the the costumer service and have my order on their records, was a little skeptical about paying $500 but made the purchase because of the great reviews this brand has received from multiple sources. I bought two, one for my place and one for his. I have mine in my living room close to the air intake vent for my a/c unit and his we put in his room. We run them on turbo with the ceiling fan circulating air during the day when we are gone and then turn them down to low or medium when home.
It has been about 3 days and I am not exaggerating when I say that his wheezing is completely gone and I have not noticed him clearing his throat like he normally does. I am shocked at how fast we have seen results. I even kept the cardboard boxes in my living room for ease of repackaging for return. I just now set them out in the garage for trash pick up! These are a keeper for sure.
They are pretty entertaining as well. The second day I had mine running I did some heavy cleaning. Lots of dusting and vacuuming. The sensor went from blue to red! I also tested it with perfume and had the light change to purple. The other entertaining part is watching my boyfriend try to set off the sensor by squatting over it and passing gas! No color change there but still funny to watch.

title: I spoke with two other industry contacts and they had really bad things to say about Aller Air
text:
I have two products from AllerAir, though not this one in particular & my comments are about those. However, I would not be surprised if the same can be said about all the Company’s products. When I was researching air purifiers specifically to remove VOCs from our house, I found the generally least controversial method is through activated carbon. Allerair had the largest carbon offerings and I contacted the Company to discuss the right models for my situation specifically.

We have several HVAC systems and the carbon purifiers were to be placed in the duct work, attached to the returns & were verified by their engineering staff to meet our requirements (provide appropriate levels of static and sufficient filtration to remediate the VOC issues we were having). I purchased & took receipt of two of their units. We set up one in the crawlspace and one in the attic. This was in March, 2015.

Upon start-up, we noticed significant odor coming from the ducts. We went through and did extensive sealing of all joints with Panduit, mastic, and tape and found holes which we patched. Additionally, we even sprayed Aeroseal (a chemical) into the duct work to seal leaks. However, the odors persisted even after all this work. So we narrowed it down to the purifiers themselves - the Aeroseal did not go into the devices but was instead for the duct work, and, as mentioned, we had already sealed everything.

To find the leaks in the devices/purifier, we initially put bright lights inside the units (see picture, difficult to see given lighting but you see a line, which was a lot bright in person) while turning off all lights in the crawlspace. It quickly became apparent the AllerAir unit leaked badly. There were lines of lights at the bottom of the unit (all the way across), at the door (which had no gasket) and through the myriad pop rivets used to patch together the cheap sheet metal construction. I informed the Company about this but they offered to do nothing to help me and didn’t even respond or acknowledge my communication. So I paid my contractor to seal these openings.

I thought we were successful because we could no longer see light. But yet, we still had the strong odor from the crawlspace coming through the duct work. At this point, I began doing testing to determine what was in the air. The crawlspace has been determined via testing to have severe levels of deadly radon gas (radon doesn’t have an odor but other odors from VOCs in the crawlspace do). This same odor permeates the house, making it unlivable. This is a huge problem for me as my family lives in another state and I’ve missed the precious first months and years of my two son’s lives and have had huge marital and financial stresses under these circumstances.

Anyhow, after determining the odor was still present in the duct work, I decided to smoke test the AllerAir unit. I pressurized it (pushed air through one side while sealing the other side) and smoke billowed out of it. The pop rivets and screws where the motor and wheels are all leaked heavily. Due to where the unit is installed, it is impossible to address/access/reach these problems as-is. I will have to relocate it to remove the carbon and get inside it and under it to seal. Additionally, in doing the smoke test, it fouled all the carbon. Now you smell the smoke bombs overwhelming the duct work. That’s strange because carbon is supposed to capture not emit the toxins. This is capturing and then releasing it. It’s the opposite of what it markets its capabilities as. So I’m going to have to replace all of this carbon ($500 worth) plus spend all the money required to fix the unit. I have communicated this to the manufacturer and they have simply responded that this is the first time they’ve heard this complaint and they’re not offering me anything in return because it’s not a motor or fan related issue, which is all their warranty covers.

It’s stunning that they haven’t offered to fix the situation. Why not. Because they don’t believe it’s a problem? Surely if they knew there was a problem, they’d offer to fix it. I can’t believe they specified this product for my house if they knew it had leaks. They’d know if it had leaks if they had a QA department. All they would have had to have done is a simple monometer test to figure it out. But maybe they don’t have a QA department. But if not, I can’t believe they don’t have a QA dept or don’t at least QA their product. Moreover, once they were informed of how diametrically opposed this unit is to the objective (ruins your air rather than improves it), surely they would’ve tested it to determine the veracity of my claims. All they would’ve had to have done is a simple smoke test or light test (if not the standard monometer test) that I did. Surely they did this. If they didn’t, then they should be put out of business. We’re talking lives here. They’re sitting around contently trying to preserve profits while I can’t live in my house b/c their product is sucking deadly radon gas into my house..

Finally, in continuing to chase my tail to fix my indoor air quality issues, I kept looking for new products (rather than fixing the existing). I spoke with two other industry contacts and they had really bad things to say about Aller Air. They stated the CFMs are not what they advertise and they under-load the carbon in terms of actual weight vs. marketing. They also stated they’re not UL certified. I don’t know about all this but I can say, they deserve their terrible reputation.

title: Great machine!
text:
Excellent! I bought this on a recent trip to Japan, and due to the currently weak yen, it came out to about $160 USD and I just checked it with my luggage for free. Figure another $100 or so for EMS shipping from Japan, and you've got a fair price.

It works beautifully here in my home of southern California, even without the use of a transformer. The humidification feature works great, and it can monitor the humidity level in the room and adjust it according the the optimum level for the current temperature.

Although the controls are in Japanese, the main button in the center is Omakase/Automatic, which runs the purification + humidification functions and by default adjusts fan speed according to the air quality per the sensor in the back. The sensors on these units are pretty decent, but by no means perfect (even on more expensive models) - for the best air quality, you'll want to simply up the fan speed to a level you find agreeable volume-wise instead of having it run on low all the time until it detects something. I will say that it's incredibly quiet on the low fan speed, though.

The Plasmacluster function can be turned off, which I usually do when I'm in the room. The jury is still out on whether such new technologies - while definitely safer than the older ozone-producing purifiers - are truly 100% safe.

The indicator lights can be dimmed or turned off, and it can also be set on a run timer. You can toggle between having it display the humidity level of the room, the temperature in Celsius, or the estimated electric bill (for 24 hours) based on the Japanese yen and the current power consumption of the machine. Of course, that is of little use here.

I only really run the unit at night when I'm in my bedroom, and the humidifier's water tank seems to be good for about three nights before refilling. It's easy to refill, and the maintenance of cleaning the humidification filter is relatively easy to understand from the manual's pictures, and should be done about once a month. The filter life estimates are all great on these newer Sharp models - 10 years for the HEPA filter, 10 years for the deodorizing filter, 10 years for the humidification wheel filter, and probably yearly for the water tank's "clean water cartridge". These are available from Amazon.co.jp for under $10. Just keep up on the maintenance depicted in the manual for each of the consumables and you should get a long life out of them. The machine does have an alert light that'll tell you when to clean the main filter.

Overall, great quality item from Japan that should work for a long while - even on the slightly higher voltage here in the US. I've run several Japanese appliances for years all without any problems whatsoever, but to be perfectly safe or for your own peace of mind, you could certainly buy a transformer of the appropriate wattage.

title: Well built, inside and out
text:
This is my second minus A2 now, this new one I got is the SPA780N which has the app support. Since most of the other reviews went over all the general information, here is a quick gist: This is one of the top of the line air purifiers on the market, made in Korea, not china, and is one of the only air purifiers that is wall mountable. In addition, it uses a brushless motor, this alone sets it apart from other top tier brands since everybody else uses brushed motors. A brushed motor has a definite limited lifespan as the carbon blocks wear out due to friction, rabbit air uses brushless motors which lasts longer (in order or magnitudes) and is more efficient.

The big shocker: I took it apart, just because I am a curious person, and saw that they used a very high quality Panasonic brushless motor. This was icing on the cake on an very well built air purifier, a motor that 99.999% of the customers won't ever see and they chose to use top tier motor rather than some generic Chinese one. Little details like foam gaskets on the filters, magnetic closing mechanism for the latch, and even the pleasant chime goes a long way in making the high price worth it.

The verdict is, if you have the money, you should very much get this because an air purifier is something that is run 24/7, might as well get the best.

The app itself while being version 1 works well, no bugs to report yet.

The last thing that is a bit bothersome is the magnet for the remote isn’t as strong as they would suggest. It’s pretty easy to knock off but I guess it does the trick.

title: Good for basic mold issues
text:
We bought this air purifier because we had a mold test done and had elevated levels of mold in parts of our house. The Alen BreatheSmart was one of the few air purifiers that has a filter dedicated to handling mold on top of the HEPA filter options. The filters are not cheap, but they sound like they will last quite a while. We have only had it a few weeks, but it seems to be helping with reduced coughing.

We initially had it on full power, but then switched it to the auto mode. In that setting it has an indicator of the pollutants in the air and increases the fan speed the more particles it detects. You can tell that it is working because it often jumps up a level when people walk by. The indicator also changes color with each level. Blue is for low fan, orange for medium fan and red for when it is on high. Even on high it is not as loud as other devices we have had. Currently it is located 10 feet from the couch where we sit and watch TV and we hardly notice even when it is on high.

We also had a $50 mail in rebate from our electric utility for buying an EnergyStar air purifier so you may want to look into that when you purchase as well.

title: Functional and completely useless at the same time
text:
I live in a house with lots of dust and pet dander. One of my dogs sheds hair and dander so much you would think someone is paying him to do this. This product pretended to function correctly, but didn't actually do anything. I set it up and made sure there were no obstructions around it or anything like that. Turned it on, it seemed to function correctly. It red the air as 'dirty' with the status meter reading red at the top. This thing proceeded to "clean" the air in 5 minutes or less, which is total BS. It didn't clean the air at all. Absolutely nothing was collected in the filters. If I turned it off and on again it would do the same thing, pretend to clean the air in 5 minutes or less and not actually clean anything. It kept doing this. If it had actually cleaned the air in 5 minutes or less in my house then those filters would be crying to be cleaned they would have sucked up so much stuff. The unit collected more hair and dust on the outside because of static cling than it did on the inside, which is to say it collected squat. I think maybe this thing got in my house, saw all the dust and dander and was like "Awww hell no!"

On the positive side, it has a fancy display and isn't overly noisy. Now if it had just actually done it's job.

Needless to say, it went back to the seller for a refund.

title: Great Price & Performance
text:
I was able to buy this model on Amazon for about $70 in March.

The unit is large, but is light-weight and looks good in any room. The HEPA filter does a wonderful job of cleaning the air. Our apartment is fairly old and does not have good air circulation, which resulted in isolated areas of mold growth during the winter. After a month of continuous use (low during day, quiet at night), the air smells significantly better and there have been no occurences of mold growth in areas where we ran the air purifier. The ionizer feature does a good job of restoring an ion balance to the room, and is easy to turn on and off separately from the fan. I've read that it's important to not operate an ionizer for more than 2-3 hours per day, so it was important for me to find a purifier with a separately-controlled ionizer.

Replacement filters costs between $28-$40 online, depending on where you look. I plan on replacing the filter every three months.

In all, I strongly recommend this air purifier based on its attractive price and performance.

Later I was asked for a video introducing pollutant/smoke to it directly. Placed a scented candle in front and it sucked in all the smoke when I blew off the candle. It stayed in "green" air quality. Support said the sensor is at the bottom of the unit and everything is working as it should. Are you kidding me? Definitely the unit is bad but I was not offered a replacement and they sticed to their claim that it is working properly so I should upgrade if I am not satisfied with this unit.

title: Breathe easy
text:
I've just finished writing a review for the replacement filters with the same title...and since they'll probably read almost the same, I apologize if you end up reading them both. Please note that I purchased the black unit, not the white.

I really love this unit. Yes, it was the equivalent of almost one month's rent for me. And the filters are pretty pricey since I replace them every 8 months (maybe less often now that I'm in a cleaner environment). But it's been SO worth it. Like I said in my filter review - I consider this to be a preventative healthcare investment, like the quote I've seen around: "Organic food might be more expensive a lot of the time, but have you ever tried pricing cancer?"

Again, I'm not sure if I'm allowed to upload links, but I've created an imgur album with pictures of the old medium particle (2nd of 5) filter and HEPA (3rd of 5) filter next to the new replacements (4 and 5 are dark colored and come after the HEPA so the difference isn't really visible and I think it's just that their effectiveness diminishes over time). These were being replaced after the unit ran continuously on auto mode, in my ~150 sq ft bedroom that was located one building away from Ventura Blvd in the San Fernando Valley over an 8 month period. This was the 3rd set of filters that have been through this unit (I purchased it in 2010). The bedroom door was always kept closed, but the windows were drafty old jalousie style windows. The album is here: [...] . Please note that I vacuumed the large particle (1st of 5) filter at least weekly, since it does a bang up job of collecting dust and pet hair. If they remove the link, and you'd like it, just let me know and I'd be happy to send it to you. I'm really, really glad it removed all that smog from the air! I kept it between the (blackout curtained) windows and my bed, as close to my bed as I could put it and let it still operate properly. My roommate was always hoarse with red, watery eyes, and a runny nose in the mornings, and he's not very sensitive. I hardly ever had problems and I've had severe allergies since middle school...they would only act up when I left the bedroom/went outside. My pets who slept in bed next to me in my room where I was almost 24/7 for several years (medical) also did not sneeze nearly as much as or wheeze like his pets did.

I'm in Phoenix now and not near a smoggy road (and it's not as smoggy here, anyway), so maybe next filter change, the filters will come up desert dust red instead of smog black? Now I'm in a one bedroom, and I keep it in the living room with me, next to my chair, then move it by my bed at night, so that my pets (who shadow me...they deserve clean air too!) and myself always have the freshest air.

Don't forget to clean the sensor every now and then...and don't be surprised if this kicks it into high for a few minutes when you do as you kick all the dust up around it. I would really get the (very lightly alcohol dampened) cotton swab all up behind in all the available holes near the sensor (if you get a unit, you'll see what I mean), at all angles you can get it in there, as deep as you can get it in there. I apologize for how dirty that sounded. I do this and I have pulled out sizeble pet hair dust bunnies since the dust accumulates behind and around the sensor area (it helps to spin the cotton swab as you do this to really grab the bunny and pull it out). Note: I'm sure RabbitAir would advise against doing this but I've always done it without shorting anything or electrocuting myself or damaging my unit, and I want to keep as much of that from getting deeper inside the unit where it could really potentially clog things up as I can. Just be gentle...like you're cotton swabbing inside your ears after a shower. Don't blow out your unit's ear drum.

It is noisy on high but it is very rare that high kicks on for me. It only happens if A.) I spray a perfume in the room (so I imagine if you use scented room sprays, it would definitely set it off) B.) an e-cig is used in the room (it really doesn't like that vapor), C.) I kick up a lot of dust somehow, D.) there is a fire nearby and it smells smoky or I extinguish a candle (it's fine while scented soy candles burn, however). It's actually kind of cool because I'll know if something funky is going on with my air before I can smell it, because the unit will kick on full blast and the indicator light turns scary red instead of healthy blue. Otherwise, it operates on low, and I think it's very quiet. I suppose at first you might notice it, since it's a new noise, but I never even notice that it's on now. I think this is a quality, nice looking unit (people ask me what it is) that's going to last for many more years, and I'm very glad I made the investment. If you have any questions, leave me a comment and hopefully I'll be able to answer it for you.

title: One MAJOR Downfall to an otherwise Amazing Air Purifier
text:
Would probably give a 3.5 out of 5.0. If it weren't for all four of my Mila units needing to be replaced under warranty (yes, all 4 out of 4) and the terrible customer service, this would be an easy 5 star product in every possible way.

Fantastic product when it works. 4 of 4 units I purchased all had to be replaced under warranty within 6-10 months after purchase. All experienced the same fan motor-based issued which caused a grinding sound that became progressively louder during use over time eventually becoming unbearable and sounded unsafe. My first experience with customer service went as expected and I received a new unit within a few weeks. Decent experience overall.

Unfortunately about two months ago I had to once again contact Mila customer service which was the completely opposite of enjoyable and helpful as the first. This was an embarrassing horror show on their part and would be happy to share my communications (emails) regarding this experience with anyone for Mila if reading this and interested.

My other three units also started to exhibit the same fan motor-based issue as my first unit. I was assured the problem identified, isolated and corrected in the latest model which I was told I would receive. Two months later I received three refurbished Mila's instead as "replacements". Upon attempting to work through this with the same individual at Mila's Customer service center the mistake was acknowledged, a few weeks later I then received 3 Mila replacement units which appeared new, but were EU models ( I live in the US), and the power cables and very basic filters were intentionally removed from the boxes of the replacements I received. I'd had enough by then, this CS representative was either messing with me or just incompetent. I kept my old US power cords, then sent the replaced units to Mila and have been using the EU units since basically convinced I'll run into more issues at some point. The three months of back and forth communication emails between myself and Mila customer support is extremely embarrassing and showcases incompetence, flat out disregard for customer satisfaction, a lack a providing prompt service, and multiple mess-ups. This is not the proper forum to share these emails in, but mentioning the extent of their customer service issues is. Customer service is terrible. The three months of back and forth communication emails between myself and Mila customer support is extremely embarrassing and showcases incompetence, flat out disregard for customer satisfaction, a lack a providing prompt service, and multiple mess-ups. This is not the proper forum to share these emails in, but mentioning the extent of their customer service issues is.

The software/app is what sets this air purifier 5 years ahead of all other air purifiers on the market. It's fantastic. It's easy to use, tons of sensor air data and history, awesome auto functionality, interconnected if you own multiple units, it's amazing and the one thing I expect from competitors very soon in the future, or they will likely miss out as other do.

Filters for Mila are expensive but in comparison to filter of the same grade its expected and comparable . Design is nice and compact with a powerful fan. It's impressive when it all works as it should, which is most of the time unless you have a deteriorating-based hardware issue, in which case ensure the customer service representative will send you a new Mila and the latest version/model as your replacement. You'll be able to tell if it's a new unit or not usually based on the packaging but also check for any nicks or scratches anywhere if your received a replacement.

For now I'm waiting for Mila's next hardware release to determine if this company had fixed up their hardware/QA issues, as this will determine whether Mila reaches greatness or sinks in the upcoming years. I do love my Milas though while they're working correctly! My wife loves them as well, especially the app.

title: Helped heal my sick house
text:
This product was a godsend! I had no idea I was living in a "sick" house until it got better!

I began reading about the effects of indoor air quality on humans, and after becoming concerned about that I looked for ways to improve the air in my home where I've lived for 13 years. That's how I stumbled onto this device. I'd already purchased one of the smaller air sanitizer units by another manufacturer, and I liked the modest effect it gave. So my rationale became, if a smaller machine can have that much of an impact, then a larger machine would probably be even better. I was right.

I've had mold issues in my basement that I've basically ignored for years, although somewhere in the back of my mind I figured leaving the mold there wasn't doing my health any favors. But because there was no coughing or anything like that it was easy to ignore. It was caused by moisture issues that I just recently finally addressed in the past month, so I figured since I eliminated the causes of the mold, I may as well start killing it so I bought the machine. Well, I didn't know how badly I was being affected by the mold, until I started running this thing.

I ran the o3 and ionization on the highest settings in the formerly damp basement for about 8 hours. The ozone, while very strong (this thing cranks it out), seemed heavier than the air so it only slightly made it into the rest of the house which was fine with me because I didn't really want to leave the house to do this. After that time, I went to retrieve it and take it to the second floor and give that floor the same treatment while I remained on the first floor. I went back downstairs to the recently ozonated basement after a couple of hours and I couldn't believe how fresh it smelled! The same thing happened on the 2nd floor when I went back up there to check things out.

I made sure to position the device near the vents so that the ozone could make its way into the ducts etc, and also distribute itself via the air conditioning. This was intended to kill anything harmful which might have been living inside the ductwork. I did all of this yesterday, and today I truly cannot believe how much better I feel. Even my plants (of which I have many, mostly spider plants which I procured to improve air quality) look perkier.

The weirdest 2 things which occurred have been these: 1) I normally have 3 cups of coffee in the morning, but since using this I only need 2 now and might even be fine with 1. My energy level just took a massive jump. 2) My sense of smell has definitely improved for some reason, along with my skin's sensitivity. This one was kind of surprising, but its unmistakable. I actually went outside and could evensmell flowers without actually seeing any nearby where I was standing. My sense of smell has never been that good, for at least as long as I can remember.

My guess is that I had been dealing with low level toxicity which was causing the symptoms that I had. I just had these symptoms for so long I considered them normal. Symptoms like loss of the sense of smell, brain fog, difficulty focusing, etc. These can all be traced to living in a moldy environment. Now, I've seen really bad mold before, and mine didn't appear to be on that level which is why I ignored it for as long as I did. But that's only the mold I could actually see. The rest of it that I couldn't see, like inside the walls etc., may have been what was affecting me. But no longer. I'll never be without a device like this again. I am strongly considering purchasing a few more of these for friends and family who might need something like this.

A very enthusiastic 5 stars!

title: Bought 6 in April 2029, 3 have already stopped working
text: Sadly we bought six of these at Costco back in April 2020. Since then 3 have stopped working without reason. Two simply stopped turning in completely and the third had two white lights in the air flow part start blinking. The carbon filters needed to be changed monthly just to keep up (instructions said every 3 months) and the main filter needed to be changed every 3 months (instructions said 6 months to a year). To get replacement filters you had to buy in a set with carbon filters and they were out of stock constantly. Lucky for us ours had a year warranty. We are waiting for the other 3 to also go out. Not sure if this is a design flaw, too delicate, but they break for no reason way too much. And it needs a better filtration system that can go longer between needing changing. Even cleaning the netted filter once a week (they said every 2 weeks would be fine) didn’t keep them from defecting. Customer Service for product was non existent. Never could talk to a real person about the product. All I can say is thank goodness for Costco having their warranty. Save your money until they improve on the device. Way to much work for them to just end up breaking anyway.

title: Great buy!
text: I started having asthma which I'd never before had.  I'd recently moved into a new apartment that smelled kind of mildew-y each time I walked in, so figured it was time to get an air purifier. I did a little research and this air purifier looked to be a t a good price point and had such amazing review, so I went for it.  I'm SO glad I bought it.  As the other reviews mentioned, it is super sensitive:  I was in the bedroom and it was on low showing good air quality and then suddenly the air quality showed it was poor and it went on high.  I was wondering what the heck had changed the air quality so suddenly and then realized that my husband had just come inside from smoking; he had come in the patio door into the living, a totally separate room with the patio door being at the far end of the other room from our bedroom door AND the bedroom door was closed, and he hadn't even been smoking inside, just coming inside after smoking!  Our apartment no longer smell mildew-y and my asthma is gone (I did take steroids for the asthma as well so can't say it was all because of the air purifier.)  Highly effective and very low-maintenance.  Highly recommend.

title: My air quality is terrifying and I had no idea
text: I live in Los Angeles and I literally had no idea how bad my air quality was in my own home. I thought I mightve been battling some mold inside, but didnt notice much of a difference the first month I had it. The thing I noticed the most was my dog's constant allergies seemed to get way better. He sniffs and sneezes less at home now. A friend asked me how I like it, and I said, "meh." She told me to wait until it was fire season... and BOY WAS SHE RIGHT. There's a color gauge on the device that corresponds to the air quality in the room... and once fire season started in California, that thing got CRANKING! It even turned purple one day, which is not in the user manual for this model... and I had to dig into the internet to find out that purple meant AWFUL. We've had so many fires and this thing is cranking all day every day to try and keep my air quality inside between ok and good. And now, I noticed a difference. When I leave my home, I'm immediately activated by the pollutants in the air. My nose runs and my eyes get puffy. It's made my grateful for this little fortress of good air I've created at home!
