title: Measurements don't lie- this thing works... graphical proof from my air quality meter
text:
Some time ago I decided to invest in an air quality meter by Awair to measure air quality levels (chemical / c02 / dust / etc). I did this as I recently moved to a well-sealed modern home -- and as such I wanted to keep an eye on internal air as we close up tight during winter.

Unsurprisingly - our dust levels steadily raised this winter as external and internal air was cycled less. This is despite having a Hepa system on the central air.

Since I like clean air, I had two choices: upgrade my central air for thousands of dollars, and hope that it works... or target specific rooms via in-room filters (like this one from Alen) and save $$.

Well, the results from my air quality meter prove I made the right choice. In only an hour after turning it on, I cut the levels in 1/3 down to nearly the same as exterior air.

My nose can definitely tell the difference. Inside air now smells like outside air.

My home is nearly 2,700 square feet -- open floor plan with very tall 15-20' catherdral ceilings. This units ability to cycle and clean the air (with help from my central air as well) brought my interior particulate levels down.

Here is a photo showing the graphed difference from my Awair air sensor the day I turned on my Alen BreatheSmart.

The air is clean and free of particulate and so pleasant that when you throw in a little Netflix and Chill, I never want to go anywhere any more; it's so nice at home!

Sound-gives a pleasant white noise hum that I find neither too loud or soft.

Price - worth every dang penny

Performance - Cleans my 1200 sq ft apartment (no walls, just one big loft) with no problem

Size - It's no small thing but even at its size, the design of the unit makes it easy to tuck against a wall and it doesn't feel obtrusive.

Filters - not cheap but if your buying a purifier of this scale then you understand its need for a high performance filter. I have mine for 6 months and am just now able to discern a difference in air quality and ready to buy the new filter.

Pictures attached - I put my office chair next to it to give you a sense of scale. Note the purifier is not under anything nor does it have anything around it to obstruct the intake/outflow of air. This is an important element of overall performance and should be considered before making your purchase. *NOTE-I apologize the pictures are sideways. They are not this way on my computer so I find it strange Amazon is incorrectly reorienting them.

Final Thoughts - It doesn't get any better than this for me. I absolutely and very highly recommend this product. You'll love it!!!

Pros:
Used electrochemical oxidation (PECO) to destroy the bacteria, mold, and allergens in the air. Works great in small rooms and apartments. I also love that I can connect it to my smartphone and control it remotely. It’s also quiet and portable. Recommended for someone with allergies to clear the air in their home.

Cons:
Regularly replacing filters--but that's normal!

title: Sleek, Quiet, and Easy to Use!
text:

The setup was very easy (a few pieces of tape, then removing the plastic around the filter), and the unit couldn't be quieter.

There's even a no-light mode to make sure it's not distracting while you try to sleep. It's hitting allergy season here in LA, so I'm very happy to have the thing in my room. As for how much it's helping, however, I'm still sneezing a decent amount, and after two weeks, the filter still looks fairly clean. Therefore I think it's worth moving the thing around to see where it's most effective. Either way, a great addition!

Not recommended

title: Powerful air purifier cleared kitchen smoke in less than 5 minutes
text:
This is a powerful filter that can move a lot of air. It has three fan speeds: low, medium, and high. If you set it on automatic, it will adjust the fan speed based on particulate count in the air. The low setting is very quiet. The high setting is very loud but it filters a massive amount of air and circulates the air in the room.

When you set the fan speed manually, you can also set the duration of filtration to 2, 4, or 8 hours, and it will automatically shut off after that time. A light bar on top of the unit will show either blue for low, purple for medium, or red for high speed. They were also kind enough to give you the option to shut off this light bar and dim the button lights.

When I installed this in my front room I thought for sure it would automatically kick into high gear because I live with multiple cats, but it didn't. But when I cleaned the litter box next to the filter, it went into overdrive. A few days later I was cooking bacon on a grill, and it was too hot. The fats burned and filled the kitchen with smoke. So I brought the filter into the kitchen, and within about a minute the filter automatically switched to high speed and cleared the smoke from the kitchen in less than five minutes. Then it went back to normal mode.

It's a very powerful air purifier, and I love it.

title: Quiet air filter
text:
This is an air filter that removes dust and odors from household air. The air filter measures 21x16.5x8 inches. The filter unit has an American electrical plug and runs on 110V service. The controls are on the top of the unit with touch buttons for Auto, (manual) Speed (1, 2, 3), Timer (2, 4, 8 hours), and Lights (on/off), as well as Power (on/off). Indicator lights to remind you to change the filters are also on the top of the unit. An air quality indicator bar (low/medium/high particle count) runs along the front of the top of the unit. The unit comes with a HEPA filter installed as well as an odor filter. In the box, you get an additional odor filter and a 30 page paper manual in English, Spanish, and French.

Setting up the unit is fairly straightforward. You remove the front cover, take the filters out of their protective plastic bags and reinstall them, then plug in the unit and press Power. It took me a few minutes to figure out how to remove and replace the front cover--it's not as easy to take off or put back as the covers on my Sharp air filters.

I was a bit surprised to read in the manual that the odor filter is supposed to be replaced every 6 months and the HEPA filter every 12 months, both based on 12 hours of use per day. 12 hours use per day? Dust happens 24-7 where I live. With any other air filter I've ever used, I simply turn it on and let it run all the time. The only time I ever turn my other air filters off is to clean the filters every 4-6 weeks. If I let this Oreck run all the time like I do my other filters, the filters will only last 3 months (odor) and 6 months (HEPA). Since the replacement filter kits for this model list for about $35, that gives a yearly filter cost of about $70. For my Sharp KC-860, which has a similar capacity, the HEPA filter lists for $110, but lasts 5 years, for a yearly cost of about $22. Thus, the Sharp machine has a much lower lifetime cost. The Sharp odor filters are also washable, but these Oreck filters are not.

Upon first opening the box, I noticed a chemical odor. While removing the bags from the filters and figuring out how to re-install them, I got a chemical headache. Thus, people with chemical sensitivities will need to have someone else unbox the item and then run the filter outdoors for a few days before they can use it inside. About 20 minutes after first putting the filter into operation, I began sneezing, but whatever made me sneeze went away after a few minutes and I haven't had any allergy troubles with the filter running since then.

After running the unit for a few weeks, I opened it up to check the filters. There is noticeable dust on the odor filter and some large particles (hair and what-not). The HEPA filter still looks pristine. Overall, this air filter seems to be doing a good job at cleaning the air. It's quiet and simple to use, but the filter costs make the machine rather expensive to use all the time.

title: Nice, But Expensive. Perhaps Worth Considering An Alternative...?
text:
We've had this air purifier running for about a week and it runs nicely/runs well. Does it do what it claims to do? I'm not sure I can tell, but I'll give it the benefit of the doubt.

I can say that this unit is very well made and thoughtfully packaged. It runs quietly while at the same time pushes quite a volume of air. It has (what I consider to be) standard features such as "fan speed" and a timer. All in all, quite nice.

But are you getting your money's worth for $395.00 (Amazon price at the time of this review)? Here's where I think the product falls from a 5-star product to a 3- to 4-star product. I also have a [[ASIN:B004VGIBZK Winix WAC9500 Ultimate Pet True HEPA Air Cleaner with PlasmaWave Technology]] and it has far more settings (and a remote) for substantially less ($217.74 Amazon price at the time of this review). While the Alen is a bit quieter than the Winix, a bit more modern looking than the Winix, and a bit smaller than the Winix I can't see the pluses of the Alen being worth almost $180 more. I guess you could say the Alen claims 700 square feet while the Winix claims only 283 square feet, but I'm not sure the apples are being compared with apples (in my very non-scientific comparison I think they both handle about the same volume). (I'm not going to address replacement filters because the prices are relatively the same (as best as I can tell).)

Not saying the Alen (this unit) is a bad bit of kit. It isn't. I rather like it. But I'm not sure I like it for $395. Especially since I already have a unit that I think offers more and does an equally as good a job as the Alen at a significantly lower price. You won't go wrong buying this Alen, but I can't help but wonder if you'll be paying more than you have to (aesthetic style points notwithstanding).

So let's go with 4 stars.

title: Great fan and purifier
text:
The Dyson Pure Cool TP01 is a fantastic fan and air purifier. It's an expensive device when you compare it to a simple fan. However, if you’re in the market for an air purifier, the cost differential isn’t as extreme. I have young kids in my house, and the blameless design of the fan is perfect. I don’t need to worry about a kid trying to put their hand in the fan.

We also have the Dyson DP04 purifying fan. The DP04 tracks the air quality in the room which was very handy last year when air quality was a concern due to the forest fires. TP01 has the same 0.3 microns and 99.97% of pollutant and allergen rating as the DP04 but lacks the carbon filter for odors and the air quality measuring.

My only complaint with the Dyson TP01 is that you need the remote to adjust the fan. You can turn the fan on and off on the device, but you can't change any other features of the fan without the tiny remote.

If you’re looking for a nice looking high-quality fan and air purifier, the Dyson is an excellent choice, and if you don’t care about the air quality rating, the TP01 is excellent for larger rooms.

title: This is our second Dyson Fan and already is part of my Smart home
text:
Overall: Dyson always produces great fans. Elegant design, pretty color, impressive functionality, straightforward user-interface, and fast WIFI connection.

Two remotes: My previous Hot+Cool Link comes with only one remote controller. Surprisingly this has two. Both remotes are golden color which matches well to the fan itself.

Smart App: Simply follow the popping up instructions to connect the fan to smartphone and MyDyson App. After connection, the phone serves as the third remote, and it can monitor and control the fan remotely. With Google Assistant enabled, I could automate the fan like other smart households items in my house.

Noise wise: below level 6, the wind noise is negligible. Above 8 and all the way level highest 10, the wind noise is audible and it may start to bother some sensitive people. I’m ok with it in day time. During night time, I’ll turn it to Auto Mode and it doesn’t bother me at all.

Wind direction: this is a surprise to me. The wind can be blown from either side of the fan. My older Hot+Cool Link blows only from one side, but this one has a button on the controller which the wind direction could be switched with one button push.

title: Definitely NOT a scam. lol
text:
This Purifier is well built, looks good is, quiet and so far works great. After running in for a while I re-entered the bedroom and did notice the air smelled fresher and felt less stuffy.
To respond to the negative review about it being a scam. I almost didn't buy it because of that negative review. I'm glad I tried it for myself.
The review said it was scam because after powering off and unplugging the unit while the air quality was on green (good) and then immediately plugging it back in and restarting it the air quality light was on red (bad). The reviewer was asking how could the air quality get so bad in one minute therefore calling it a scam. What the reviewer failed to realize (and is clearly stated in the manual) is that whenever the unit is powered on it automatically starts off as red by default. After a few minutes it will "read" the air quality and adjust accordingly. I think the reviewer should wait a few months and then check the filters see how much if any of the dust or particles the unit caught.

title: It works well.  I used to be very sensitive to allergens.
text:
I know this works well from personal experience. I used to be very sensitive to house-hold dust & other allergens.
Here's the thing I've discovered. If you have dust-allergies, and you have carpeting, you've got to vacuum at least once a week. If you do not do that, you're going to suffer, but, if you have one of these bad boys. He he he. It's more like once a month, if that. The unit works, and does a great job. My allergies cleared up, and stayed clear for a long time with this thing running.
You've got to put it up high, as close to the ceiling as you can. Just leave it on the HIGH setting, and do not shut your bedroom door if it's in your bedroom where you sleep at night. It needs plenty of breathing room, or it can overpower the air. If it's in a bedroom, I'd put it up high, near the door, and sleep w/ my head far away from it. It needs about 2 rooms, maybe 3, to have the perfect environment to be just right. It's very powerful, and not cheap, but back when I was doing price comparisons, it was the best for it's value.
Also, It lasted me about 5 years of nearly continuous operation.
I was told that I was allergic to it's negative ions, but, even if I was, the cleaning that it did to the air was worth it.
It can make some electric-static noise when it's very humid inside, but for me, that was not that common, & it didnt keep me up at night either. It's generally very quiet. It's cool to look at it's little blue lightning bolts inside also.
I love this machine and highly recommend it, especially in these times, when the air could be much better.

title: We love our Rabbit Air!
text:
We have had our Rabbit Air spa-700a for over a month now and we are very happy with it. We live in a basement with not one or two but three chihuahuas, one of which just had a litter so make that SEVEN chihuahuas ;). Since we got the Rabbit Air it no longer smells like basement down here nor does it smell like dog. We got the "pet allergy" filter in our Rabbit Air.

I really like the customizable filter option. I also really like that it has a 'pre filter' to trap contaminants from unnecessarily contaminating the more expensive filters. Since we got our Rabbit Air the air smells cleaner and needless to say, we are very happy with it!

I spent A LOT of time researching air purifiers before deciding upon the Rabbit Air spa-700a. I found the Rabbit Air spa-700a air purifier to be the best value for the price and was just what I was looking for. The Rabbit Air is quite small considering the amount of filters in it. It is capable of moving a ton of air on turbo mode and is pleasantly quiet in sleep mode.

Rabbit Air also did a geat job in taking air purifiers from bulky and unsightly to compact, stylish units. I proudly mounted mine to the wall.

I really wanted to comment on the price, at just below $500 I think it is a great value. No I'm not rich, $500 is a lot of money but think of it this way; how often do you breathe, and how important is breathing to you? For something that cleans the air you breathe in and out, all day, everyday, $500 is nothing. Air quality is very important and directly related to your health and $500 to me for clean air is a great deal.

I am very happy with my Rabbit Air spa-700a. I highly recommend it to anyone searching for an air purifier. I also recommend purchasing the wall mount for it, it looks great on the wall and keeps it up out of the way, saving space.

text:
Not smart at all. Smart is plastered all over the product details and description but its not. The Smart Air sensor is does not actually work. It is time based. If you unplug the Air filter and plug back in it resets and does not read the Air quality again. It turns on high as if the Air were dirty again. Reproduced this various times. Then I tested this in another room where I already have a Air filter going and it kept saying the Air was dirty when the filter had been running all day and I could feel the difference in the air quality.

There is nothing smart about this Air filter. It just has a timer and sleep mode. For that I could've gotten a much cheaper one. Also won't work with a smart plug because when you turn on the smart plug the device will get power but stay off until turned on manually or by remote.

Other than this complaint about false "Smart" claims, it does filter well and its pretty quiet. It does however have trouble with cleaning the air outside of its small general area. Meaning if you sit near it you will feel the air quality difference. If you sit away from it it struggles and keeps recirculating the same air it just cleaned.

To filter the small living room we have, we had to turn on the ceiling fan to get air flow in the room for it to filter the air properly. After this the air quality was definitely better but without the ceiling fan on it did not create enough airflow to filter the whole small living room.

We are unfortunately returning this.

title: Handles VOCs
text:
04/12/2023 - My wife and I purchased this unit a few years back, but it was through the EnviroKlenz website, not Amazon (Amazon didn't sell these at that time if memory recalls). This unit advertises that it can handle VOCs (Volatile Organic Compounds), which can affect breathing. When we purchased it, we kept it in the bedroom and I noticed that I was able to breath quite a bit better (didn't know we had CO2 or VOC in the house).

Before I begin the next part I must disclose that I had this unit turned off for several months while we were doing some reorganizing around the house. It was during this time that we had purchased a Smart Thermostat that detects VOCs. Pairing this thermostat with Home Assistant I was able to see that the VOC in the house (again with THIS air purifier turned OFF!) was very high (like 40,000 micrograms/cu meter high).

I installed a new filter in the unit and am going to run a test (pairing this with a smart plug that will turn on when high VOC is detected, also made possible because the controls of this EnviroKlenz are mechanical - knobs and switch, versus electronic), running it right next to the thermostat to find out how effective it is at handling VOC. I do expect it to do well, given how my breathing improved at night when it was turned on. Stay tuned for the results of that test.

All in all, avoid this product, the company makes it impossible to use the filter beyond even 12 months and honestly, I think the FTC needs to investigate this company and shut them down. title: Cleaner air comes out, but Auto mode is unreliable
text:
The HEPA feature works fine, according to a separate air quality monitor that I have. That is, the air coming out of the top of this device is clean.

However, the air quality sensor is not reliable. The air quality level shown on the display of this filter, and the associated Auto mode, which adjusts the power based on this filter’s sensor, are not reflecting reality.

At first I thought the sensor was great, because the lights showing the air quality level start out red when it first comes on, and then lower down to green after a while. They also change temporarily when the filter detects steam from a shower in the next room.

But today we’re on Day 3 of the SCU Complex fires (in California), the local AQI outside is 159 (“Unhealthy”), the air in my house smells smoky after we had the windows open all night (had to cool the house down due to the heat wave), but the air quality monitor on this filter’s display is showing green, and in Auto mode this device goes to a low fan setting. Whereas my other air purifier’s monitor is showing orange and the fan is on high.

I do like this filter (because of its output, and it’s pretty quiet). But you might need a separate sensor.

title: Fresh Air from Vocolinc
text:
[[VIDEOID:ce350ce42f6b90ffbe1183cab7c05f1e]] Affordable clean air from the outstanding company Vocolinc.
The Vocolinc PureFlow Smart Air Purifier is one of the best purifiers I've used and it's SMART!
Set a countdown timer, know the humidity, room temp (choose Celsius or Fahrenheit), choose night mode, lock the device, power on/off, and know air quality all from the overview screen on the Vocolinc app.
Choose to set the fan speed from levels of one to five or use the auto option (I use this option as I only allowing smoking in the game room. It's really cool how it detects the smoke so quickly, cleans and then lowers the fan speed after cleaning the air).
I also set the screen brightness and the indicator (really cool bar that changes color depending on the quality of air in the room. You want bright green).
Set a schedule and forget it so that you aren't using the device when you are away (helping to save power and filter).
Name the purifier what you want and tell your smart assistance to power it on/off.
The settings tab informs you of signal strength and the remaining filter life (very important so that you have filters when you need them).
Filters are affordable and costing less than my other not smart purifiers and can usually find them on Amazon on sale or using a coupon.
In the HomeKit app Power on/off is available as well as access to the Air Quality Sensor, Humidity Sensor, and the Temperature Sensor. Do some cool automations!
Another great product from Vocolinc. Say hello to clean air powered by your smart home.
Highly Recommend!

title: Made the difference for recurring health issues
text:
I purchased then received the MinusA2 on June 5th (2019) and installed it immediately thereafter. I purchased an Air Purifier after months of health issues, which I couldn't determine the cause. Aside from hacking (coughing) which seemed to also originate in prior years, this past January I got sick with Flu like symptoms, which lasted for about three weeks. After recovering, I strangely had a relapse every few weeks, and eventually started having symptoms almost weekly, which oddly only lasted a day (coughing, fever, body aches, etc), knocked down with over the counter meds. Had 3 different doctor visits during those months, two different antibiotics (which knocked it down for for a few weeks after completion, but relapses again thereafter), two chest X-rays (each clear), and though never having any allergies, have been prescribed and tried different allergy meds with no difference. I travel for work, but never seemed to have issues abroad. When not traveling, I office from home, so spend the majority of time there. Also, my other half occasionally started to get the single day symptoms (oddly at the same time I did) in April/May, but works in an office so isn't home as often. So during the last few weeks of May, I started doing detailed investigation at home.

What/How I tested:
First checked air quality constantly throughout the house with a tester (PM2.5/PM10/PM1.0 Micron Dust and Indoor TVOC and other sensors). Since it seemed the issues were related to chest symptoms, felt they were most likely the issues, but nothing resulted in out of ordinary levels. I then tested our water sources, though knowing we've always had poor water quality in San Diego, we've been buying/using Carlsbad Alkaline Artesian Mineral Water for years. I checked that water, our bottled water dispenser (to see if any contaminants through the system) and did a thorough cleaning of the dispenser, though found no suspect ppm levels or other detected issues on any of the sources. We have pets which are very clean, and were already vacuuming constantly (robot vacuum and manual). Did visual checks throughout the house for potential issues (mold, A/C system, filters, fans, etc) which should have been detected with the tester anyways. Still suspecting the air quality, I decided to try an air purifier. Aside from the thorough filtering and good reviews of the MinusA2, I chose it over others for the unique wall mounting capabilities (very few out there), auto-detection, and degree of filtering for the room & adjacent kitchen area I spend the majority of my time, which is approximate 730 sq. ft. (unit advertises coverage up to 815 sq.ft. with 2 air changes per hour; allergy sufferers rated for 408 sq.ft. w/4 air changes per hour). I selected the Germ Defense filter model over the other three customized filter options.

First Use:
Installing on that Wednesday on a living room table to the side, I unfortunately had another relapse on Friday, but chalked that up to already having been affected. Immediately after installation, the sensor immediately shifted to "red" for high detection (checked with the tester at the same time, and still saw minimal/acceptable levels) and eventually shifted down to "purple" then "blue" over the next few hours. It would shift between levels at different times during the past two months, increasing filtering as it did. You could see it shift to red when cooking certain things in the kitchen for sure. I circulate the air in the rooms with ceiling fans, so it gets a good degree of overall conditions. I think it very helpful to have an auto-detection unit, rather than manually determining when you might need better filtering. I can happily report, after that initial relapse, I haven't had another recurrence since, during the following two months, with very minimal coughing issues, if at all. I did the first pre-filter & sensor cleaning a month later as directed, and all seems to be working well (will clean at the start of each month).

Opinion:
The unit has been about 6 feet away from where normally sit (until I mount it). The noise level is minimal, even when the sensor goes red and the airflow increases. Silencing the room and setting the unit to the higher levels, the highest Turbo was only 60dB from that distance, High was 54dB, and medium fluctuated between 50db and below (my meter just reports LO when below 50 so didn't test Low and Silent settings). I didn't mount the unit yet, as I wanted to make sure it was making a difference (which it is, in my opinion), so I probably will within the next month. I purchased the WiFi model to see and control elements of the unit. I've left the sensor set to default medium sensitivity level rather than raise it, though it's nice to have the option to change as needed (attached a screen shot of the app from today as I type this). The app is decently rated on Android with a 3.1 as of today, though only a minimal 16 reviews. Most of the issue reviews were problems getting the app and/or WiFi working, of which I had no issues, or wanting to see detection level history, since it mainly shows current levels and provides control. I will say, Rabbit Air responded to every single review (good or not), which is nice to see (I haven't posted a personal review yet). Aside from the manual cleaning of the pre-filter, the 4 filters are advertised as only needing replacement annually, and a complete set is about $95, which I don't think is bad (good to figure annual costs). You can see the details of the 6 stages of filtering on the product page. It's nice the unit has covers available with different colors and designs to fit the decor of a room, though I purchased the plain white cover model, but when mounted, plan to attach my own artwork. I also purchased a recessed outlet box for where I'll mount the unit, so the cord is hidden behind the unit (the back is flush without a recessed area for a plug behind; also plug is straight, and not 90 degree). I haven't used the timer (since it's been on auto since installation), and have left the mood light off (though when first installed the auto mode nicely shifted things off at night).

My Pro vs Cons:
Pros: Wall Mountable (flush behind, no recessed area behind unit), 6 Stages of filtering, large area air filtering/air recycle, Auto-detection sensor, Ease of filter changes & annual cost, Mostly flat front cover with designs available or possibly own designs (some con below), Overall very quiet, 5 year manufacturer's warranty, actual performance difference it made (for me).

Cons (most minor personal wish-list things): Straight outlet plug - I purchased a recessed outlet box so won't be an issue but would be nice to have a 90 degree end, Front cover LED area is raised but flush would have been nice for designs, App needs detection history (at least for some duration; 24 hours, 7 days, etc), at 7-inches pretty thick mounted (filters box about 2.75in of it) but not bad considering performance needs.

Overall
I'm very pleased with the design and performance of the MinusA2, with some very minor criticism which wouldn't prevent me from buying the unit again. Hope this info was helpful to those making a consideration.

title: Worked wonders removing smell from our smoky house
text:
Nearly 6 months in and I can say that this ozone generator has made a significant difference in the smoke smell left in our house from previous owners. Along with cleaning and washing walls, windows, floors, carpets, and light fixtures and replacing curtains and (some) window fixtures, leaving this O3 generator on max power while we take weekend getaways has been more than enough to take that lingering smell of smoke nearly completely out of our house. We plan to repaint walls and ceilings throughout our entire house in the years to come, but in the meantime this machine has really done wonders....

A few notes:
-The in-laws also used this in a 100+ year old rental house with bug and mold problems. ~5 days of constant running at max ozone output had taken away a huge portion of the funky smell. Another few iterations of 5 days running at max power and the smells are almost completely gone.

-DO NOT USE THE OZONE AT ANY OUTPUT OTHER THAN 'LOW' WHILE YOU'RE IN THE HOUSE! I can't stress this enough. Ozone is REALLY bad to be breathing in. It's an oxidizer and a respiratory tract/ mucous membrane irritant. If you can smell ozone or if you're getting a sore throat or something, TURN IT DOWN/OFF!

-This generator completely saturated our 1800 SQF four-level split home with ozone when left on max over a 48 hour period. This little thing packs a punch.

-When returning home to a house filled with ozone don't forget to open doors/windows and let the house vent for at least 20-30 minutes. I basically just run in while holding my breath as much as possible and get as many doors and windows opened as I can. A few big whiffs of ozone is enough to give you a bit of a sore throat for a day or two. Be careful out there people.

-The smell of Ozone may linger a few days after a treatment, even after venting the house. This is normal, as far as I can tell, and hasn't been enough to cause any health issues due to the lingering ozone.

title: clean natural smelling ozone
text:
This O3 Pure ozonator makes the air fresh, clean, and natural smelling. Strangely, the smell seems "cleaner and healthier" than two other ozonators I've had. I loan the O3 Pure to a 94-year-old woman who had a stroke, and who was bedridden and partially paralyzed, and it rid the odor from her room. I also loan it to a woman who had allergies, who noted a positive difference in her health; she will buy one for herself. Then I loan it to a third woman who had asthma. I don't think she liked it. But it definitely helped my lung problems, and it's helped others get off their meds.

The fan was returned to me with a buzzing sound. I put a drop of "clean oil" (no smell, nontoxic) into the little hole. Perhaps it was coincidental, but the noisy sound disappeared ('though I wouldn't recommend doing it). The fan broke after I vacuumed it with my Dirt Devil--the devil was too strong for the little fan. I rate O3 PURE 5 stars for its clean ozone, and 2 stars for the fan.

I read of a study where ozone caused people negative reactions for about two weeks. This may be a Herx Reaction, a "detoxing" of their lungs, similar to taking "greens" to detox yourself of poisons. It's a healthy thing to do, and one often feels healthier after a detox cleanse.

Sadly, I can't buy what I want--the stronger ozonators. California has outlawed them. The ignorant California Legislature listened to the greedy lobbying of the Hepa filter people, whose business was probably affected by the growing popularity of ozonators.

title: Good but, missing some key features
text:
I'd actually give this product a 4.5-star rating if that option was available. First, the reason I like this unit: attractive (for an air purifier); low noise; high-quality filtering system; works well in a large room. Now for the annoying part: for the price of this item, Hathaspace really needs to step up and provide more 21st-century features. Essentially, all the timers are "countdown" timers, they go off, and then you have to turn them back on manually. For example, the "sleep" timer puts it to sleep, but does not automatically wake it up. The "auto mode" automates the monitoring of the PIM level (air quality), but doesn't put it to sleep or anything like that once a certain level is reached.

I can get a $3 tea lamp that has an "8/16" timer or a $10 smart wall socket that communicates with Google or Alexa. None of these features are present in the HSP002 unit, which, ironically, uses the term "smart" ??? Not! As some have pointed out, where's the remote? Again for a product at this price level, it needs to add these features--or stop billing itself as "Smart." Frankly, compared to many other electronics I've purchased in recent years--most a significantly lower cost--this is a rather "dumb" device. The Hathapace HSP002 does many things well, but being smart is not one of them.

title: Very effective on removing odors from cigarette smoke
text: I bought the Rabbit Air MinusA2 based on extensive research on my part as to the best air purifier for cigarette smoke. I have only had it a week but I must say that it does the job. My husband who is a non smoker says he does not smell any smoke whatsoever. It seems to be removing cooking odors as well. I previously had an Idlys air purifier which was quite good but the filters were costly and had to be changed about every 4 months. I replaced it with the new Idlys model which was supposed to be more powerful and it was terrible. It was only effective on the very highest speed and it was so loud that it made my ears ring. The auto mode didn't work at all. I returned it to the place of purchase and decided to buy the Rabbit. The Rabbit is very quiet even on the highest speed. It is very effective on removing smoke odors. There are 4 different filters (germ defense, pet allergy, toxin absorber, odor remover) to choose from so you can customize your Rabbit to your needs. This model covers up to 700 sq ft. The room I have it in is about 400 sq ft. It is a bit pricey at $500. but it works so I think it is worth it. The filters cost about $85 per year. I have only had it a week so time will tell if they last that long or not. If they do that is quite a savings compared to the Idlys which cost me about $250. per year. This model can also be mounted on the wall if you like. I did not mount it on the wall. It really doesn't take up much space and I wanted the flexibility to move it around if I wanted.

text: I recently purchased the Alen BreatheSmart with OdorCell filter here on Amazon. The Alen on the highest setting, turbo, is quieter than the Honeywell HPS 300 on its lowest setting. I am satisfied with both the Alen and Honeywell. title: Air sensor definitely works, but not as well as my nose
text:
I bought this unit specifically to deal with lease-violating neighbors who smoke inside their apartment. I've never been particularly concerned about the "quality" of my air day-to-day. I just don't want to smell smoke (tobacco or marijuana). I tried improving the seal around my door, which helped, but didn't eliminate the problem. The automatic mode on this unit really appealed to me, as I thought it would be nice to have the fan on low when there was no smoke, then kick into high gear before my nose picks up the smoke. I was concerned about the number of reviews here claiming that they thought the sensor was "fake".

I am here to say the sensor is definitely not fake. Yes, the auto mode starts in high then drops down when you first power on the unit. That is documented in the manual. I think this is needed to "prime" the air sensor. I have noticed the fan kicking up when cook, usually to medium, which definitely tells me this sensor is not random. I put on spray sunscreen near the unit and it almost immediately went on high. And just a few minutes ago, I saw it go onto High for something I hadn't picked up. I opened my front door and there was a strong smell of perfume in the hallway. The air purifier did a really good job detecting that.

Unfortunately, it does not seem to detect smoke too well. Remember that I am dealing with light wafts of smoke, NOT smoking in my own apartment. I abhor breathing smoke and I'm not willing to test how well this unit handles that. There have been a few occasions where I start to smell the tobacco or marijuana smoke, but the air purifier is still sitting on low. On low, it does not move enough air to stop the smell. I'm glad that there is a remote control so I can manually increase the speed. Once I do that, even just to medium level, the smoke smell no longer reaches my living room or bedroom.

On low, the unit is essentially silent. On medium, it's a little noticeable, and on high it's very noticeable. But not as bothersome as my air conditioners. I do not use the sleep mode. I do appreciate the option to turn off the LEDs, though I wish there was a light sensor to do that automatically.

title: Good, basic, no frills, true HEPA filtration
text:
I purchased this item because I had been looking for a reasonably priced true HEPA room air filter with no ionizer. I have heard conflciting information on the safety of ionizers which produce ozone in the home so I did not want that feature, though it is popular right now. I have pet birds which are high dander and wanted to filter the air in the room the birds are in, both for my health and the birds' health.

I have been really happy with this product. The box says it is for a 16' x 16' room. I am using it in a 12' x 16' room and it seems to do the job. It is compact and is designed to sit on its end or on its side, whichever you prefer. It is beige and unobtrusive. The item is ready to go right out of the box - you just have to install the carbon filters (HEPA filters are pre-installed at the factory). Installing the filters is a snap. The air filter is simple to use. There is power button to turn it on and off and it has four operating speeds, 1 through 4. You can also set a timer function that allows you to set the filter to run for 1-16 hours and then automatically shut off. Impressively, the unit comes with a FIVE YEAR manuafacturer's warranty, something you don't see very often.

I researched HEPA air filters extensively before this purchase. Some HEPA filters cost $50-70 each to replace! This unit's filters are readily available in Wal Mart and Target. Amazon sells a two pack of HEPA filters for this unit that currently costs $32 and a four pack of carbon filters that costs $12. The manufacturer says that the HEPA filters will need changed every 6-12 months and the carbon filters every 3-6 months. Keep in mind that this unit uses two HEPA and two carbon filters. The unit also has indicator lights for each filter to tell you when they need changed. I'll probably spend $88 a year on the filters but that is much lower than for many other HEPA filters I looked at!

I run the unit on speed "3" for about 12 hours per day though you could run the unit continuously. It does a great job of circulating the air. Within the first day I noticed a marked improvement. I can't see very much dust in the air anymore, even in bright light (when you can see the floating dust particles in a room). Also, lots of the bits of feathers and fluff from the birds that used to float throughout the rest of the house are gone. The room did not have an obvious odor before but I really think the carbon filters have made the room smell "fresher."

The only drawback I can think of is that is it somewhat noisy at speeds 3 and 4 which are the most effective speeds. I don't consider this a problem because I am fond of white noise in the background. Some people might find it too noisy at the higher speeds.

Update November 2006: After five months of continuous use this filter stopped working in September 2006. I followed the instructions for returning the item for warranty service which required me to pay for return shipping and also pay to ship the item back. Within about a week Holmes had sent me a brand new filter that is actually a newer, larger, model worth more than the one that had failed. They gave me no hassle and replaced the filter with a better model. This new model is working fine so far. I am pretty pleased with Holmes prompt replacement.

title: useless for PM2.5
text:
I live near Portland. There's literally a wildfire about 3 miles from my home. This air purifier is claiming that my air quality is fine. It is not fine.

I've got multiple air quality sensors in my home, and I've also tried a lot of different air purifiers. Watching the air quality sensor reports, it's pretty easy to see what purifiers work well, and which don't.

I am not sure in which alternate reality that any claim that this would help with allergens would be true. I've been using it for about 6 months, and it has never dropped the PM 2.5 levels at all. Not even during the wildfires, when there's a PM2.5 of 300 outside. The room where this air purifier is stationed is hovering with a PM2.5 of around 60, and this doesn't change if this air purifier is running. On the other hand, if I run my Coway, it drops to 10-15.

If you're looking for something to help you with air quality because of the wildfires, this is not the device for you. However, if you're looking for a device that removes smells very well, this one actually does a good job - better than my other air purifiers. That's the only reason it got 2 stars instead of 1. Weirdly enough, it does seem to make a slight difference with VOCs, which is rare. Usually it's only more expensive air purifiers that really do anything with VOC. It's a minor difference, but it exists, so I started mostly using it in a room when I was using polyurethane. The room was well ventilated, but this does help dissipate the VOC levels a little bit faster, and it does get rid of the smell.

It will fool you into thinking that it is helping with the air quality due to wildfires, but believe me, it is doing absolutely nothing but removing the smell. If you're very concerned with air quality, get a sensor that monitors PM2.5 and use it to help find an air purifier that works well in your space.

title: Excellent product
text:
I bought this air purifier just over 3 (three) years ago. It has been ON all this time non-stop. The only time it is OFF is when I clean the carbon filter which I do roughly twice a year. The unit is quiet and does exactly what I expected/hoped it would do.

Here are the Pros:

1. Quiet
2. Neutralizes smells and odors quickly and completely. My unit is in the room adjacent to the kitchen. Cooking odors are not a problem. Odors are not neutralized instantly, but it happens quickly enough to say that the unit does what I want it to
3. Carbon (odor catching) filter is washable and so far (after 3+ years in operation) I do not feel the need to replace it
4. HEPA (particle catching) filter never requires replacement (according to the user manual);
5. Though the unit is small and quiet I did notice a significant reduction in dust build up in the room where I use it.
6. The odor sensors are very sensitive and will increase/decrease fan speed as needed. One example (apologies for being graphic): Once, I came home after a long hiking trip and, naturally, my socks were not quite fresh. As I took off my boots and waked into the room, I heard the fan accelerate to MAX power though I was some 10+ feet away from the unit. (and no, it is not very loud even at MAX fan speed)
7. If I had a large place I would buy one of these for each room. Highly recommended.

Con's? None.

title: Buyer Beware: After a Few Years, Stops Working
text: All the people writing 5-star reviews after barely taking this thing out of the box are doing a disservice to folks looking for factual information. Have owned this air purifier for several years now (it's still within the warranty period), and after a few years, it stopped cleaning the air. It worked well for the first few years, but now it's less than a glorified fan. The unit is mounted on a bedroom wall three feet above the cat's litter box, and after the cat goes in the box and tangoes, kicking up dust and producing magnificent smells, while I have to cover my nose and escape the room, the air purifier won't react. It's set to auto, so when the cat tangoes, it should automatically kick the fan up faster into air-cleaning function. It does not. This fan, er, "air purifier" does not react to offensive smells at all. I called the manufacturer, and despite their courteous manner, they told me the air purifier "loses its sensitivity over time." I was told to press certain buttons to restore the unit's sensitivity, some ridiculous voodoo which I attempted, following their instructions, resulting in zero improvement. I faithfully keep the unit clean, including sensors, and replace their expensive old filter with their expensive new filters as directed. This unit costs a LOT of money, and when you include all the filter replacements, you are out one big pile of cash -- for a product that, in several years -- won't work. Not sure why people who've had this pricey product for only one week or one month write reviews. Because of all these just-opened-the-box reviews, the reviews of this product are skewed false positive. Despite still being under warranty, Rabbit Air will not replace this unit for me. People looking to buy this unit need to know this.

I also have a glass table that has a stand that lifts my tv up and normally it needs dusted every 10 minutes, since using this the dust has been cut down tremendously.  I plan on getting two more of these, one for an apartment off the back of the house and one for the downstairs.  I love it, my allergies are much improved and my breathing is greatly improved. title: Very nice, however needs a little TLC before use.
text:
This air purifier looks terrific, better than the pictures. Outstanding construction quality but with a critical flaw. My household air is now on a whole new level of sweetness. Functions great, looks great. A negative attribute is it is not completely silent. It is not loud, but it has a fan and the fan makes some noise (unlike a purifier like the Ionic Breeze and clones), as all fan based air cleaners make some noise. It is not silent and not abnormally loud. The amount of cleaning packed into this compact unit is outright impressive. There are several units similar to this unit in both function and design on Amazon and I cannot say if this unit is in anyway superior or inferior to it's piers, but this unit is remarkable.
The critical flaw to this unit is the HEPA filter on the back, there are 2 screws that fasten it at the top and 2 hooking latches that fasten it on the bottom. The hooking latches have too much play and the filter does not seal good to the unit, leaving an air gap that bypasses the HEPA filter. This air gap allows small particles to enter the unit and cling to the inner walls, which is very noticeable on this clear unit. It is easy to open up and clean by removing 2 bottom screws and removing the 2 control knobs, then the guts slide right out and easy to clean insides.
My personal fix to this flaw was to get insulating foam tape about (1mm thick) and place a 2-ply seal around the filter, a 2mm thick seal seems to be functionally appropriate. I suggest applying this seal before use, the tape is easy to find in any home improvement supply store and far more tape than necessary for less than $5.
A suggested fix for the manufacturer would be to revise the rear HEPA filter mount by removing the hooking latches and replace them with 2 additional mounting thumb screws at the bottom for a total of 4 thumbscrew mounting fasteners, this would eliminate the error.

title: Works very well for what it does
text:
It's very rare for me to spend the time to sit down and write a product review unless it's to warn others of a faulty product.
This Ionizer lived up to my expectations and more. I bought this because my girl and I have bad allergies in the heavy pollen climates of our area and it keeps us up late night with stuffy noses and constant snoring.
Since adding this to the bedroom, our breathing has been exponentially easier and vastly improved sleeping. The product has two settings, high or low. I've found High puts out a lot of ozone which is a sorta sickly sweet electric smell and I wouldn't recommend such a setting for small spaces while people are in it, however it does have the benefit of killing bacteria, odors, mold etc and so is actually nice to 'sterilize' a room when not in use by setting to the high setting and closing that room off. Ozone isn't actually good for breathing, but it has a relatively short lifespan in the air and is very very good at cleaning the air and sterilizing your space. The low setting does not give off any of this odor and is perfect for leaving on when your inhabiting those spaces.
This machine also has dust collection plates that might catch some stuff, but really the ions appear to be more airborne so you can expect your dust to settle faster than normal.
This is a side effect I don't mind since it means I'm breathing less dust and allergens and just have to dust the furniture a bit more often. I also find it helps to have a small fan in the room to help circulate the ion air for best results.
For the price and quality of the product I was happy with this purchase and would gladly make it again.

title: Medical grade or not?
text:
The Air purifier itself says it is not a medical grade device. The filter page says the filter is medical grade but the filter alone is not a medical grade device. When read separately, it sounds like that they together, become medical grade.
What is going on?
How can you call it medical grade if neither the device or the medical grade HEPA filter are medical grade devices?
This only makes sense in the case of double negatives. By this logic 1 non-medical grade device + 1 non-medical grade device= Medical grade filtration. There are HEPA 13 medical grade filters that remove more particulate than your test stated. It’s misleading. Just stop calling it medical anything.

title: Something about negative ions
text:
If you are purchasing this as an air purifier, please read [...] or just do an internet search for 'EPA and Ozone Generators' and/or 'Ozone and Your Health'. It really doesn't clean air, so much as it deodorizes, to a degree.

I purchased this item because it was relatively low cost, I like the clean smell of ozone, and at the time I'd been looking into things to help with SAD and something about negative ions possibly being helpful came up. I positioned it in our bedroom on the far side of the room and set it on one of the lowest dial settings. It can take a little while to get used to the ozone smell.

*If you have asthma, nonallergic rhinitis, or are very sensitive to fume-like smells (bleach, gasoline, strong perfumes...etc), then this product isn't for you.

As far as any positive results and changes in mood or mental status, the wife and I haven't experienced any that we could associate with this product.

The product, which I purchased in November of 2012, operated normally and was cleaned frequently and maintained regularly per the products manual. After about 8 months of use, the internal fan began becoming noisy and I couldn't get it to operate quietly. Eventually I took the product apart and thoroughly cleaned it; the fan is about a 1" x 1" tiny computer fan. This helped for a short while but wasn't a long term fix. Finally, I figured out that part of the noise was related to the pegs that the fan was being held in place by. Two of the four pegs were loose enough that they caused some rattling when the fan was operating. I fixed this with super glue. The fan still is significantly noisier than when we first purchased it, but now it is a more consistent and bearable sound.

The best thing you can do to keep your indoor air clean is to regularly have your heating/cooling systems serviced and cleaned, buy good quality air filters like [[ASIN:B0015U901E Filtrete Ultra Allergen Reduction Filter, 1500 MPR, 6-Pack]], (1500 microparticle performance rating (MPR) or better), and make sure your ducts and vents stay clear and clean.

title: Excellent product and even more amazing service backing it!
text:
I initially tried a purifier of different brand but it wasn't doing a whole lot and after reading the consistent reviews of this unit and company I decided to give them a shot despite the higher price tag... I am absolutely blown away by not only the product but also the support team!

My made my purchase direct due to the return 90 day return policy guaranteed by the company as well as for one of the custom front panels not overed via Amazon.

The filter comes well packaged and easy to understand instructions. Please do make sure you actually remove the filter wrappers before running! Yes the filters are installed in the unit to save space but they are still brand new and wrapped.

After running the purifier initially on turbo for first 2 days while awake and for 2 weeks on full auto the room it is used in has significantly less visible dust on black furniture which cuts down on the number of times I need to clean the room. I've also been waking up with little signs of allergies if any that has been previously plaguing for months (new pet and spring/summer allergens).

title: Serious, workhorse industrial machine. If you want a plastic, pretty piece of junk go to Walmart
text:
I felt compelled to write this review because I am baffled by the negative reviews I'm reading about AllerAir's products. This is a serious workhorse air purifier, not a pretty, plastic piece of junk you'd buy off-the-shelf at Home Depot or Walmart.

This company makes air purifiers for factories and medical facilities. I've bought an industrial one on behalf of a client who manages buildings. Yes, it doesn't have a fancy digital read-out for filter changes (which an engineer friend told me was on a timer anyway and not tied into your filters at all), and is simple in design, but that's fine with me because it works, especially on odors. In fact, in our house it worked a little too well. We discovered that our cat had peed in our son's closet and didn't discover this until the air purifier, which usually runs 24/7, was accidentally shut off. The pee had been there God knows how long, but we didn't smell it because of the air purifier. And that's the AllerAir air purifier we bought in 2005, which still works perfectly after 11 years of constant use. The thing is a tank. We also used it effectively in our very first apartment when our new neighbor had an "alternative" smoking habit. I've also used it in my painting studio with great success. You really can't beat it for odors and chemicals.

I would suggest if you have doubts about this company, call them directly. They were always very helpful and never pushy. They talked me through a filter change and even sent me a free pre-filter one time.

It's really one of the few products I've bought (along with my Dyson vacuum) that I look at everyday and say, "That was worth what I paid for it." Super reliable, long-lasting and very versatile for any chemical/odor. Not fancy, but I actually appreciate that. It just works and doesn't have any garbage features or computer parts to break down. Just turn it on, that's it.

It's good for dust too. We originally bought it to combat my dust allergy and got the upgraded chemical filter as it was on promotion that month and came free. I'm glad we did. I think the thing is great.

title: Great for home wood shops
text:
I bought this to use in my home wood shop (a two-car garage). I saw several brands of these on Amazon and figured they were probably all made by the same company. My suspicion was confirmed when I read the manual and it mentioned Grizzly.

It's a simple design, just a basic squirrel cage fan and a circuit board. The filtration is done through a two-part filter. The main filter is your typical furnace style filter that is attached to the back. Behind the filter (inside the housing) is a large bag filter to capture finer dust. The control panel has membrane style switches, which I could see wearing over time. However, it comes with a remote as well (which is the only way to set the timer). There are three fan speeds and four operation modes (1 hour, 2 hour, 4 hour, and constant ON).

I installed the unit a week ago and have been working on a large product that requires a significant amount of cutting and sanding. On the highest setting it takes the system about 8 minutes to cycle all of the air in my wood shop. I've had the system running during my work and even overnight. There is a noticeable difference in the air quality. I used to be able to see the dust hanging in the air. That is no longer the case since I installed the filtration system.

The main filter shows a good amount of sawdust in it, proving the system is working as intended. The secondary filter is still clear of dust, so I'd say the main filter is of good quality.

Overall, I'm very happy with this filtration system. I would recommend it to anyone who has a home wood shop.

text:
[UPDATE]
After posting my original review, the manufacturer reached out by email to offer a replacement. Not only did they quickly ship me a new unit, they also promised to update future models to allow access to the ozone emitter plate, which in most ozone machines must be removed and cleaned every so often to ensure continued performance. This, in my opinion is excellent customer service, worthy of a better rating and review.

The unit, aside from the flaws listed in my original review (see below) is a solid little performer. It’s hard to find a small ozone machine, let alone one that works as efficiently as this model. I hope the manufacturer stays true to its promise and improves the unit very soon, as access to the emitter plate for cleaning would make this the perfect air purifier.

It’s ideal for small to medium rooms, practically magical in bathrooms, locker rooms, and litter box areas. Flaws aside, this unit is worth the price, as long as you realize you may need to contact the manufacturer for a new unit at some point.

In the interest of honesty and clarity, I feel I should also note that the manufacturer asked me to withdraw my negative review since they offered me a replacement. I do not feel this is ethical, as the unit is inherently defective until they update the model. Reviews on Amazon need to be honest and not swayed by incentives. My original review is below. I only ask any potential purchasers to consider all reviews before making a decision, not just mine.

title: Great in comparison to Blueair 211+
text:
Based on a favorable review in Consumer Reports I purchased a Blueair 211+. I have returned that unit, and replaced it with an Alen Breathesmart 45i, so this review will be a comparison of the two. Both are approved by the state of California as not producing harmful levels of ozone, sometimes a side-effect of ion generation. Both units have ion generation, but on the Alen you can turn it on or off. I found the Blueair caused increasing eye irritation over several days, which I have not experienced with the Alen ion generator turned off.

While the Alen is a bit more expensive (depending on the confusing filter choices on the Blueair), it also has a greater square footage capability. If you like the Alen features, you can get most of them at a lower cost in the Breathesmart Flex.

Here is what I prefer in the Alen 45i. As mentioned, you can turn the ion generator on or off. It has a five color indicator for real time air particulate level, which I have seen change when I clean up a dusty room or empty a document shredder into a waste container. You can set the fan speed to auto, which will change the speed based on the detected air quality. It has a TrueHEPA filter rated at H13. This compares to the HEPAsilent terminology of the Blueair, which you can find criticism of online and which I noticed you can see through when I returned the unit. The Alen has multiple, easy to use lighted controls, and you can turn the light level up, down or off.

If this review sounds like a am an Alen salesman, I am not -- just a retired consumer with no involvement ever in the industry. As to the Consumer Reports ratings, the Blueair is recommended as is the Alen Breathesmart Classic (which is larger and older than the Alen 45i). They did not test the newer Alen 45i. In real world use, I find a slam dunk favorite in the Alen Breathesmart 45i compared to the Blueair 211+, both in results and its' much greater user friendliness and flexibility to control.

title: Health risk!
text: Ozone generators have been marketed for many decades; it is NOT new technology. They have been used extensively in elevators and automobiles. Ozone is an odorless gas and is considered a primary irritant. It is not healthy to breathe in. The smell touted by the manufacturer and noted by consumers is due to the oxidation of the lining of the nostrils. They are smelling the burning of their mucous membranes. It's not great for lungs either. Ozone attacks organic material ranging from living tissue to wood and plastic products. In all cases it breaks down the material. I've seen the entire dashboard in a car crystallize and break from its mounts as the result of having an ionizer plugged into the cigarette lighter for a number of years. If the gas is strong enough, it causes nausea. High-level ozone generators are used to rid the smell of smoke from buildings that have burned. No one is allowed inside the building during the process and access is denied until 48 hours after the equipment is turned off. Not only is 'Thunderstorm' not pet friendly, it is not human friendly and can actually damage the interior of a home, over time. I have built many ozone generators in the past and they are not to be 'toyed with'.

title: Steer Clear of Rabbit Air
text:
I bought this air cleaner as I suffer from terrible allergies and they only seem to get worse as the years go on. To give it credit for the first two months the rabbit air was amazing. It's sleep mode and quality checker worked perfectly and it was very quiet even at full power. I genuinely noticed a difference and was quite pleased with my purchase.

If only I'd listened to some of the other reviews on amazon... soon enough the air cleaner started to get much noisier. While in auto mode the fan speed would always drop down to one even if I told it to go to full power. It would constantly enter sleep mode even if I disabled sleep mode by entering pollen mode. The employees I spoke to were kind but unhelpful. I took photos of the problem and explained my issues but never once was I given any real help. In the end in they were essentially saying "we don't know what's wrong, its a you issue".

Just don't buy this air cleaner. It's far too expensive and it seems clear to me that the quality just isn't up to par. If I spend $600 on an air cleaner I expect a company to jump through hoops to get things fixed not leave me hung out to dry.

title: RabbitAir MinusA2 SPA-700a
text:
I bought 2 of these for my house. I have a dylos small particle counter and my house has had issues with somewhat poor air quality. I also sometimes get dust inside my house from the garage workshop so I wanted to keep all that to a minimum because my wife has Asthma issues.

These purifiers are able to bring down my particle count very nicely. I don't have any exact numbers, but they basically reduced the count by half. I tested one in a closed room for a few hours and it almost made the air 100% clean, pretty amazing.

SOMETHING TO WATCH FOR:
The Activated Charcoal filters DO work! In my case almost too well. I've only had the filters for around 6 months, but for the last few days my house had a slight bad smell like a college dorm room. Well after cleaning the house the smell didn't go away. I did some searching; Turned out all the smell was coming from the AC filters. This means the filters pulled out a ton of smell from my house and eventually saturated, releasing some smell back to the house. If I had known to watch for this I would've caught it right away. So check these right away if you smell something off!

I pulled the AC filters, reassembled the unit with all other filters back inside and the smell stopped right away. Frankly, I see no reason why you really NEED the AC filters. You can buy a complete new filter set for about 75 bucks, or you can buy just the AC filter for 20 bucks ea. That's pretty pricey for just an AC filter. I contacted RabbitAir and they are sending me 2 free AC replacements since they said it's abnormal for it to become full so quick. But the air quality in my house started bad and I have a kid and lots of pets, so I'm not going to ding this review much for it. If it wasn't for the potential smell-release issue, this thing would be 5 stars all the way. Had they not sent me the replacement AC's I would probably just wait until I needed to replace the reset of the filters, which is at least another 6 months from now.

Very silent on silent and low mode, and the airflow is surprisingly good on low. Looks great, great user interface... lots to like!

title: LOW POWER AND NOISY!
text:
[[VIDEOID:2d5a3afd44f4ff143608c58098fd8b0a]] - If you buy it as an Air Purifier with a option as a fan, note that the fan is mostly useless.

Let me put it like this. At the highest setting is powerful as my airmate fan at lowest setting and but with 10x times the noise. They screw this one up big time.

- If you buy it for the fan, is useless, has no power and very very noisy, just don't. They probably tried to use the same motor from the Vacuum or something, I don't know what they tried to do but is definitely wrong.

- If you buy it for the Air purifier and the air quality monitor ...is ok probably because it combines the swing action with the fan which is very helpful, but also in order to do the job probably needs to do be at a higher setting, judging from the amount of air that spits out at a setting lower than 7, it might take a day to actually clean a 20mp2 room, so I highly suspect "night mode" which goes to level 4 max is almost useless. Probably that's why they don't actually say how long it took in their
tests to clean that 80mp2 room they brag about.

- Check if you can download the Dyson Link app in from your region, for some unknown reason you cannot download it from anywhere and if is not available you will have to download the apk manually trough some 3rd party website. Why Dyson... why???

- This product I think is 80% about it's looks rather than functionality but note that the remote control at both end is fully transparent, you can actually see the components inside. I don't know who thought this looks cool but to me looks like an unfished product and is very ugly when you put it on top of the machine.

I'm a big fan of their products, we have the V15 vacuum and the hair dryer but this air cleaner/fan.. I find it very hard to justify it's price, is more like a 300$ at best... .and even at that price I'm not sure I would recommend it. I understand that there were a lot of costs involved, the sensors, the app, the R&D, but the result while it satisfy the nerd in me, unfortunately lacks the most important thing: "the good functionality".
I remember when I first plugged in my first Dyson vacuum, my reaction was "WOW!".
When I first started this air purifier fan... was: "W T F ??"
Although won't look so cool for the same amount of money you can add a fan and a purifier in each room and probably get much better results but not sure you can find someting so convenient ..remote air quality monitoring, controll app etc.

Update after 6 months:
It does the job ok I think.
Stays in the bedroom and I scheduled it to clean the for 1hr at max setting before we go to seleep. (you can't stay innthe same room witht that noise). Then hoes into auto+night mode which caps the power to 4. For me at 4 is still nosy but because I use earplugs I cannot hear it.
In this 6 months I noticed that the formaldehyde value spikes randomly for cooking gases I suspect...so I doubt is so accurate as they claim, maybe better than other within the price range but not great by any means.
So ..would I recommend it?
Depends.
I really like:
- The app, remote monitoring, scheduling etc, very very convenient!
- The fact that it swings, so it projects the air everywhere across the room
What I don't like:
- The noise
- The fact that I had to go trough a 3rd party to download the official app

text: I absolutely am in love with this air purifier. I had bought the little one (Hathaspace HSP001) which you can see in the picture next to the bigger one (Hathaspace HSP002). I thought it would handle the 700 sqft apartment that I live in but I noticed it was struggling a little bit and due to that I bought the bigger one. That area is a little way smaller it does better in there with getting his stinky cigar smell out of that room really well. I also use the medical grade filters for both of the air purifiers. I like those ones better than the regular ones even though you can get them cheaper. They seem to pull more dust and particles out of the air which I need being as though I have asthma and severe environmental allergies.  Normally I would be a sniffley, puffy eyed mess no matter if I was indoors or outdoors but since getting the larger purifier, I now can come in my house and have relief from allergies and not have to drown myself with benadryl. Lol The only disappointment I have about this one is it does not come with a remote like the little one does but after a couple of days of using it you really just set it and forget it, Unless you want to put it on Max or change the speed of the fan or even set the timer if you look in the pictures you can see that it has a touchtop with multiple functions I will say that it is very very sensitive so be warned on that. You will see in the picture that it is red that indicates there is particles in the air that is harmful it's because I had just got done smoking a cigarette (my bed is 11ft from the purifier and after two to three puffs it has sensed the particles already). Typically it takes about 10 to 15 minutes to go back to green after smoking which is safe air. The number that is on the top of the device is the amount of particles that it is sensing in the air, the higher the number the more harmful particles there are. This is worth every penny. Will buy more once I get a house.

text:
I have an Ionic Breeze, and the dust in my house is actually worse since I've used it. The ions attract the dirt to every charged surface in the home where it usally isn't a problem, and it's not just a regular dust, it's a gritty sticky film. My mirrors and windows have a film on them that's hard to remove, my walls are dull, my furniture has a film on it, my wooden floors are dull. The dust is not like regular dust that can just be wiped away.

I didn't suspect that the Ionic Breeze would be the problem, so I checked my furnace filter to see if it needed changed, and it didn't, because I thought it was advertised to do the opposite. I thought I was just thinking there's more dust than usual, and couldn't figure it out, but after I did a web search, it said that the ions charge the surfaces of your home, and the dust in your home is attracted to the nearest surface where it sticks, and it makes complete sense to me.

I found no benefit from this product at all. It did have some kind of "clean smell" that you notice every once in a while, but I never noticed exceedingly fresh air that was any different in quality than before, and I don't breathe easier or whatever they advertise it as.

I would not reccommend this product to anyone. Unless you like to dust more than usual, and you want your house to look like it has a film on everything, go right ahead.

After 6 days, we checked the filter (barely anything on the pre filter, main filter looked clean) and moved the unit downstairs.

The unit runs the same as upstairs though it spends more time in Turbo. One unique thing is anytime we turned on the oven or cooked on the stove, the sensor went to red and the turbo fan kicked on. title: Well built, efficient air purifier - but noisier than its cheaper BioGS cousins
text:
I have owned 3 BioGS and 1 MinusA2 for about a year now.

The MinusA2 has a higher level of quality than the BioGS, which I expect for the increase in price.

The filters are better sealed and easier to remove and install - much less dust gets around them compared to the BioGS.

The electronic controls are superior. It comes with pre-calibrated particle and odor sensors (which can be adjusted on a 1-5 sensitivity level), which is a huge improvement over the manual calibration of the BioGS. In addition, it has a light sensor which allows it to automatically go to Silent mode at night time - which is extremely convenient. This makes the MinusA2 almost complete hands-free.

The MinusA2 suffers from the same charcoal filter problem as the BioGS. With such a small amount of charcoal (compared to several pounds of charcoal in purifiers like IQAir), the filter quickly becomes useless and starts emitting a nasty odor - which, admittedly, some find more noticeable than others. I really wish Rabbit Air would admit the shortcomings and start offering cheaper replacements. A one year expected lifetime is unrealistic for these filters.

The MinusA2 is a bit noisier than the BioGS (which is virtually silent). The MinusA2 has a more restricted vent, which leads to a high pitched whine. Granted, it is barely audible on silent, but it's noticeable. On higher speeds, the whine is much more obvious. I've learned to live with it, but I imagine it could be a deal breaker for some people.

title: and compared IQ Air and others…… So I have a pretty good understanding of what works and what doesn't
text:
First off - I've gone through/use Alen B.smarts, Whirlpool 510, Honeywell 50250, Idylis 280, and compared IQ Air and others…… So I have a pretty good understanding of what works and what doesn't. That being said, I may have received a bad 700A sample, but there is NO WAY these units are hitting the Spec'd noise levels unless you take the readings with the unit elevated on a wall. Poor exhaust design with tight grills adds a resonating static noise when on the floor, or below your ears. Motor also hunted for speed and was annoying on medium and beyond when in manual mode. Pretty quiet from medium and below, but you saccrifice air flow naturally.

Now, I believe the Biogs 2.0 would hit the suggested noise levels as the exhaust design will divert and dissipate that artifact. But, its not goign to pull a ton of air through.

NOTE - the unit was returned and they said it was 'just out of spec'. Well, the recorded noise levels from 1M were NOT "just" out of spec. Again, the unit was on the floor, with SPL taken from unit height at 1M. If you mount it on the wall above your ears, its a different story.

Customer Service was excellent. But, it was returned as the speed hunting and noise was not worth the $$$. Especially when on high and Turbo it was nearly as loud as my Honeywell 50250 on Medium, and then on high vs Turbo of the Rabbit. Not GOOD IMO and completely off the grid compared to Rabbit's Specs.

In conclusion - mount high on wall and it'll be fine, or if in bedroom and you can handle Auto mode changes and/or speed hunting via the motor….well, it may be for you. Beyond that - for not much more i'll gladly keep my Alen Breathesmarts and the new Fit50 on Sale would be the route i'd go as they will pull higher vol of air yet remain very quiet. The Idlyis is dead quiet on low and medium isn't too far behind. The filters/pre filters are more the pain but VERY quiet and what I Expected the Rabbit to be like, thus my added frustration. Final note; I'd rank the Alens, Idylis 280, Whirlpool 510 for sound levels and air flow. They are a lower / deeper river noise than my 700A and nearly any Honeywell i've ever owned, and most other box store units…..very noisey with plenty of restricted air and/or motor whine. Although the AP510 Whirly does have a fair amount of motor whine, just less flow noise.
