title: Upgrade if $ is no object
text:
I originally purchased the BigoGS 580 and found the sensors not reliable in my unit. The sensors went from green to red for no apparent reason if I moved it a foot. Instead of getting a replacement I switched to the MinusA2 Spa 700A (toxin remover) due to the 6 stage filtration. I live below two chain smokers and I want to ensure that I have the extra protection. I had the two units for about 2 days to 3 weeks so I can't comment on longevity.

It does a great job removing pollen and odor like the BioGS. It is pretty quiet. I don't even notice it on unless the room is completely silent. I noticed that the silent & quiet modes are more noticeable than the BioGS. I can hear the motor on the MinusA2 whereas on the BioGS I could not unless I was right next to it.

The only drawback that this unit has is if the room is dark, it automatically switches to sleep mode and turn off the sensor light. If you are living near smokers this does not work! Smoke could be drifting across my face and this unit does not adjust according to room condition. In order for it to do a thorough I have to leave it on low, med, high or turbo at night and this is not efficient use of energy.

Pros: Sleek, quiet, 6 stage filtration, option to turn off mood light, particle sensor, great customer service

Cons: lack of an odor sensor, black background make it tough to read the settings, auto mode not really 'auto' in the dark, cost of filters, bulky remote control

The only feature that this unit has that the BioGS doesn't is 2 extra stages of filtration. Is it worth the extra $60 to $140? The MinusA2 filters also cost more and need to be replaced more often. In my opinion, the BioGS is adequate if you are looking for a good air purifier.

title: Sleek and Efficient Cigar Smoke Eater
text:
I installed the RabbitAir Minus A2 in my 2 car finished 400 sq. ft. garage that I've converted into a cigar lounge. The unit looks great on the wall, is relatively quiet and does a nice job.

The sensor for air purity seems functional as the device kicks into high mode right away upon sensing cigar smoke. It seems to keep up with the level of smoke pretty well but as you can imagine with cigar smell it can take some time to eliminate the odor. After 24 hours of the device running on auto mode it reduced the cigar smell to a very subtle presence. For this test, I only smoked a single Toro sized cigar. My garage has no other venting (and I kept the garage door closed during the entire 24 hour test) its just the RabbitAir doing the job on its own.

Unfortunately, I mistakenly bought the pre installed Germ filter as opposed to the Odor filter, so I had to shell out about $27 more for the right filter unit. It's my own fault for not realizing the different options, so just be aware that there are 4 different base products to buy (Germ, Toxin, Pet, Odor) and each comes with their own particular custom filter.

They did not supply screws and drywall anchors for the wall mounting bracket (which is included), so it required an unexpected quick and last minute drive to the hardware store. It was an inconvenience but hardly anything terribly complicated. For reference though - there are 14 total holes for screws and #8 screws seemed a perfect fit. All in all, the device is light and easy to install and only took a few minutes (after my trip to the hardware store, of course).

Nice product and I'm happy with it so far - I may come back and update once I put it to a real test with a few people smoking multiple cigars.

title: Great COMPACT and EFFECTIVE Unit!
text:
I initially thought it was going to be much larger to a similar style unit I own, but to my surprise, it is much smaller than expected.

MY LIKES:

- This purifier only uses 6 watts, so it is very cost-effective to keep running all day

- I love the night light feature, and the fact that it can be used without the purifier running. It is a very soft white led, around 3000k to 3500k.

- The activated carbon filter did an outstanding job at removing any unwanted or unpleasant smells. Compared to my larger unit, this one actually performed much better.

MY DISLIKES:
- Fan speed settings are not very consistent in relation to one another. LOW would have virtually no effect on air purification, and while MEDIUM is adequate, I feel that the two lower speeds could be more synchronized with the HIGH setting.

With that being said, the high-speed setting is not overly audibly intrusive, and I am still able to sleep just fine while using it in my bedroom.

- When the night light feature is ON, you can see the illumination through the air purifier housing. While not a big deal breaker, I would have preferred that the light reflection be solely focused through the top Air outlet.

The light bleed is due to the fact that the plastic casing is not thick enough, causing a translucent glow through the upper half of the unit. (See attached photo)

Overall, my initial thoughts are very positive, and given the price paid, I would definitely purchase another unit if needed.

title: Visible impact on air quality
text:
We have three long-haired indoor cats. On our main floor our kitchen, dining nook, and living room are open to each other (about 1000 sq. ft. of space total). Our kitchen and dining nook have laminate floors, and before using this product there would be small clumps of cat hair drifting around like tumbleweed as early as a day or two after vacuuming. Additionally, during the winter months, sunbeams enter our kitchen at an angle that reveals every particle of dust or fur on our counters and in the air. It was disconcerting to say the least.

After spending several days comparing air purifiers, I decided on the SPA-700A. There were competing products that were more powerful, cheaper, or more powerful and cheaper, but the determining factor for me was the design. The Rabbit Air MinusA2 was the only one that didn't make me want to hide it in a corner, where it wouldn't be nearly as effective.

With the Rabbit Air standing on the floor against a wall in our dining nook we no longer see any cat fur drifting across the floor and when the sunbeams come through the window the air is empty!

We leave it running constantly on the "Normal" setting (midway between "Silent" and "Turbo"). At this level it is audible, but only barely. When we watch TV we sit no more than 15 feet from it without feeling at all like we need to turn up the volume to hear. "Silent" is nearly silent - you need to stand next to it to hear it. I rarely use this setting because it's not strong enough to pull dust and fur towards it. "High" and "Turbo" are quite a bit louder than "Normal". These levels were clearly designed to move air, and they do it well. I sometimes set it to "High" just before I go to bed to circulate more air, since I can barely hear it from my bedroom. I only use "Turbo" when I'm dusting and vacuuming.

Some tips I've come up with to maximize its effectiveness:
* There's less air circulation near walls, so I move it a few feet into the room when possible.
* When it's standing on the floor dust is more likely to get blown away from it by its exhaust than it is to be sucked into it - especially at higher fan speeds. I put it on a chair or on our dining room table if I know I'm going to be stirring up a lot of dust around it.
* If you can move it away from a wall, use an Air Deflector (like this one http://www.amazon.com/Model-Premium-Unbreakable-Air-Deflector/dp/B00009W3G7) to direct the exhaust behind it instead of blowing straight up.

title: I can finally enjoy my pets inside my home!
text:
The presentation of the packaging was exciting; I felt as if I was opening an Apple product. The instructions manual was simple to understand and straight to the point. The app also has demonstrations on how to activate the tracker. That’s a big plus because I want to send this product to my elderly mother (she suffers from allergies and asthma) for the holidays if it’s a good product. I wanted to test it out for myself first.

I purchased this product because I suffer from allergies. The moment I walk into a room with dust or pets, I get sick. Unfortunately for me, I also love dogs and cats and within this past year, I’ve rescued two huskys and a kitten.

I’m tired of taking antihistamines (pills, nasal sprays, and eye drops) everyday. I live in a 1 bedroom apartment with these pets and the only thing I hadn’t tried was an air purifier.

The past few nights I’ve slept with the Wynd next to my pillow. I tend to blow my nose in the mornings due to my allergies. The last 3 nights I haven’t. I’ve felt the difference. My eyes don’t itch or get watery throughout the day either.

Oh, and a great feature the Wynd has is you can turn off its light at night.

It has a kickstand that helps direct the air. If i could change something, it would be the kickstand. I wish there was a clip as well or some sort of “station” where I could snap it in place in different areas of my home and not just rely on a flat surface. That’s the only reason I haven’t given Wynd a 5 star rating.

In conclusion, seems like I know what I’m getting my mother for Christmas.

text:

I had gone through about 20 models of air purifiers including some of supposedly the best like IQ Air, Rabbit Air etc.

I got this model based on "Active Plasma Cluster technology" which is enhanced by using water in this model over previous year's FPP60CX. The last five months have been amazing. title: Excellent Room Air Purifier
text:
I received this two days after ordering as a Prime customer. The unit comes in a a pretty big box and the packaging is very good - everything looked in pristine condition when unpacking. I ordered the black model shown (available in white as well). The quality build of this is extremely high and this is only confirmed by the first step which is to remove the front cover and then take out (easy to do) the three filters. The first filter is like a typical air conditioner filter - plastic grid with mesh like trap to catch larger piece of dust, etc. The second and third filters are both sealed which was very nice - the 2nd filter is a charcoal filter and you can see and hear if you shake it the bits of charcoal inside. The third and final filter is the HEPA filter. After this first step of opening an reinserting the filters which take under five minutes you are ready to go. You plug the unit in and press the auto button. There are a few settings which change the fan speed, etc. - I left it on auto the whole time. How did it work?

I used it in two rooms - my office and then in the TV/DOG room. It worked great - I noticed after about an hour my allergies were not as bad (in the office). When I set it up in the TV/Dog room my test goal was to see how well it helped to remove that "dog smell" - it definitely helped to reduce it. A few observations as the image of the unit initially threw me a bit:

1. It is relatively light
2. visually it reminds me of a high-end audio speaker except for the "plus sign" cut out in the top right. That is an air quality indicator and is quite intuitive. It changes color based on the air quality. It has 4 colors to it. Green is the best air quality. When it changes, and it occasionally did in the dog room, the fan speed adjusts to help clean "dirtier" air more quickly. That was the only time I actually ever heard much sound from this. It is in no way obtrusive but if you are in a room that is quiet, you will hear the fan kick in for a bit.
3. the color indicator shuts down in a dark room so it won't bother you if you are using it in a bedroom for sleeping.
4. it looks about 3" deep except on the lower back where the fan blows out the clean air - you only see it from the side.

Overall I'm very pleased with the results and the build quality of this. It is my first air purifier so I cannot give a comparison to any other available unit but I will say, it does what it says and I'm going to order a second one.

title: Couldn't be without it
text:
Having just bought this filter to assist with my asthma, I have to say I was amazed by its effectiveness and the fresh clean air it produces and dramatically improved my asthma from the first night.
The fan has 3 speed settings, an auto dust sensor, timer, and ioniser. I typically put on maximum with ioniser, if not used for a while, then switch to auto. In my large bedroom, this works great, and auto switches the fan to low, after 2-3 minutes. This more than maintains the air quality and is very quiet, in fact its quite soothing noise to sleep.
Other reviews have said the auto is just a program setting, I have to disagree, as I've seen it switch back to high, when I moved some furniture in the room, kicking up dust.

I've read other reviews about the back cover not being well fitted. I have to say I've not found this to be the case at all, although there was packing tape on the unit when it arrived, which was quite difficult to remove.

Unlike many other units,this one is very attractive (I have in white with silver grill) with a nice expensive quality, even the switches at close inspection. Some people have bought these for commercial/office environment and I would say the unit performance and quality would be fine in this environment. I feel the unit's price is probably justified.

The quality of air this unit creates makes me really worry about the background air quality of where I live by the Thames in London UK. It feels a little like air conditioning, but fresher with a gentle cooling (and much cheaper to run). My wife also loves it and reminds her of sleeping in one of our favourite beach hotels in south east Asia. You really notice the difference when you enter the room,so we will be buying a second for the living room. I've also recommended this to many friends and family.

I choose this one for the large room capacity and permanent filters as I didn't have confidence on price or availability of replaceable filters on other brands/models especially as the ionizer actually generates more visible dust when the filters need cleaned or replaced. I am probably dependant on this unit for a good nights sleep, so this was critical to me.

The only thing I might change on the product is the brightness of the blue led lights on the top. Although they do act as a night light which is quite attractive, some might find this a little of putting although this is a surprisingly common issues with a lot of these types of units from other brands.
Highly recommended.

title: Bought TWO units and they both broke in less than 7 days.
text:
[[VIDEOID:73c420a7b6f17aade67f6b4bd0933462]] Why I bought the Alen BreatheSmart:

I recently found out I am quite allergic to dust. I live in Hong Kong where pollution can be dangerously high. I started researching air purifiers and ended up choosing the Alen BreatheSmart because 1) They have great reviews. 2) They offer a reasonably priced unit (in the premium range) that could cover a large space (1000 sqft). 3) They offer a Life-Time Guarantee and seem to have good customer support. I ended up buying two units (one for home and one for office) with the upgraded silver filters. I was very excited and eager to try them.

What happened:

When I first turned on the unit (in the office), we were taken back and surprised by the noise it made. It was extremely loud even at the lowest setting. We brushed it off and thought it was putting overtime in and doing its job since it was new. Maybe the noise will improve we thought. After a few days, it did not improve and we decided to turn it off during the day when we were working and turn it on during the night when we leave. I was suspicious about the noise (being a product designer myself), something didn't sound right. Sounded like there was a problem with the fan. One day I came into the office and the unit did not even turn on. It broke in less than 1 week of use.

The EXACT same thing happened to the other unit I was using at home. The video uploaded is the noise it made at the lowest setting. Pretty ridiculous. I could only upload one video per review so I cannot upload the new replacement they sent, which is ALOT quieter and does not make the 'broken' noise. So at least now I know for sure that the two units were 100% faulty.

UPDATE:

So the replacement unit started all good but now it's making another type of noise and it's very annoying again. The unit has only been on for less than 1 hr! What is going on here Alen?

Asking for the replacement units:

It was very straight forward and easy to get the replacement units through Amazon, but they only cover 50 USD for the entire order. That means I have to now send back 3 units from Hong Kong and I will have to pay over 400 USD in delivery. I paid 475USD for two units deliver to Hong Kong. Ridiculous.

TIP: If you have thrown away the packaging, wait until the new one arrive so you can use that packaging to send it back. Otherwise, you'll have to spend and repack everything yourself.

Overall experience / theory / conclusion:

What are the chances that now 3 units are all faulty?!!! I have never in my life experienced this type of faulty products 3 times in a row. I have two theories:

1) The units were damaged during the delivery stage- I see there are dents and marks on the packaging itself, meaning the boxes were probably being thrown around. The build quality is very poor as well.

2) I HIGHLY SUSPECT they reuse the parts and refurbish the faulty units and send them out as new, which leads to a bunch of obvious problems down the product's life cycle.

After 3 faulty units in a row, I have lost all confidence in this brand. Maybe a freak coincidence? I do not believe so.

After spending over $2000 USD on this purchase (with a bunch of upgraded filters), in my own humble experience with this product- I HIGHLY DO NOT recommend this. STAY AWAY AT ALL COST!

title: One of the best products ever made... PERIOD!
text:
Several years ago before Cosumer Reports slandered Sharper Image out of business, I bought an Ionic Breeze Quadra from my neighborhood Shaper Image store. It was expensive at the time but I thought it was well worth it. Well as soon as my wife read the report about ionic air cleaners, she bought it hook, line and sinker... and why not, is Consumers Reports EVER wrong? (BTW the answer to that is yes, more offer than people realize) So she packed it away in the attic and refused to look at it, let alone use it. There is sat for almost 3 years. Today, while cleaning the attic I found my old friend. I dusted off the box, took out the Quadra and hooked it up in my office. Suddenly, my office smells clean. I feel like I can breathe again. It's spring-time in South Jersey... take means everything outside is covered in a thick layer of yellow pollen. well, I'm safe inside with my old friend. It still works perfectly and is completely silent. This product is amazing. Like or not, it works.

For the record, I see nothing that says it will eliminate the need for you to dust ever again. I didn't buy it for that reason and if you did... well, you're either lazy or a fool. And as far as the zapping noise goes, I was instructed when I bought this that you should clean it with a DRY cloth. If you need to use Windex or something, you MUST let it dry before using it. If you get a zapping sound, that means the collection plates are still holding moisture. Think about it... negative and positive ions and a little bit of moisture... that's the same recipe for a lightning storm! Let the plates air dry. Just because you wiped them dry does not mean that they are dry. My Quadra is now and always was COMPLETELY silent. The little bathroom one on the other hand was never silent. It was a free gift for spending $350, what do you expect?

In an objective summary: it remove odors, removes something from the air as the collection plates need to be cleaned twice a week, it is completely silent and costs $10 a year to operate 24/7. The room smells clean and fresh and I don't have allergy problems.

I would love to know from these lemmings (especially from the ones who own a herd of cats) if the best rated Consumer Reports air cleaner eliminated their need to dust?

title: Misleading marketing, not worth the cost
text:
I bought this product when it was $300, and I justified the high cost because it's "medical grade H13" and "cadr 450 m3/h, suitable for "1500+ square foot coverage".
The truth is that H13 is the minimum filter grade that can be considered HEPA--google the BS EN1822 standard to see what I mean. Grades 10-12 are merely "efficient particulate air" filters, or EPA filters. So any filter that is truly HEPA is H13 or even higher H14 grade.
I emailed the company, and the first response I got called the filter "H13-MERV," which I don't even think is a real thing. MERV filters are much less efficient than HEPA filters. I then got a followup from the CEO, Hunter, sharing with me the description of standard HEPA, as defined by the DOE.
So there's nothing special about this filter.

Second, the rating of CADR 450 m3/hr uses a unit of measure that makes the number appear high. Convert it to ft3/m like most other filters report, and you get only CADR 265. Keep in mind that the Honeywell HPA 300 has a CADR of 300 ft3/m, meets exactly the same HEPA specifications (even though they don't market it as "medical grade"), has affordable and easy to purchase replacement filters, and only costs $226 on Amazon. This Hathaspace unit is now selling for $400. Feels gross.

Not to mention, you can't turn the lights off on this Hathaspace unless you put it into bedtime mode, which is the lowest fan setting. If I want to run it on medium or high overnight, I need to cover it with a towel.

title: Awesome air purifier!
text: I have terrible allergies and I got this purifier to help me with my allergies! I love that it has a filter that filters out just about everything! Once my husband was burning leaves  outside and the wind shifted and the smoke blew towards our house and started coming into the house and the purifier cleaned the smoke out of the air fast! So you can really see it work! The only thing I’ve noticed that doesn’t work that good is the air quality monitor. It always bounces back and forth between 7 and 9. Doesn’t seem to react to pollen, pet dander, dust or possibly mold. But it does register VOC’s! If it picks up a any smell, air freshener, smoke, or the VOC’s from using the stove and oven the air quality monitor goes way up! But other than VOC’s it stays at 7 and 9. But I don’t mind that. It works great and I just keep it set on speed 4 instead of using the manual setting because I want to make sure it’s circulating the air constantly to help with my allergies so it does what I need it to. Would be nice to know the air quality for dust, pollen, dogs, and mold just to know what’s in the air throughout the day, but as long as I know it’s cleaning the air, that’s what’s important for me! And it’s amazing how it picks up VOC levels! I never knew ovens created so much VOC’s! I would definitely purchase this again. I love that it cleans large areas instead of just a small room. I did a lot of research before purchasing this unit and it was the best one for the price. If you research the square footage air purifiers cover, the CADR rating, the actual number for the air quality sensor, how many times it circulates air in the room, the warranty, the price, how much the filters cost to replace, how often you have to replace the filters, and what the filters clean out of the air, you can see that this unit is the best overall air purifier for the price. I researched most of the top brands before getting this one! The 5 stage filtration on the filters, and the medical grade hepa filter was a big reason why I got this one. It filters everything from pollen, pet dander, VOC’s, and viruses. I also didn’t trust one that emits ozone because there’s conflicting info on whether ozone is safe or not. And this one doesn’t emit ozone! Other brands I looked at were Germ Guardian, Levoit, Blue Air, Honeywell, Breath Smart, Nuwave, Sharp, Medfy, AirMega, Winix, Austin Air, Oransi, Air Doctor, Ren Pho, and Rabbit Air and Alen and this beat all of them when I compared the square footage, CADR rating, price, air quality sensor, how often air circulates the room, price of filter and how often you change the filter and the warranty. I also researched the Amazon reviews on all the purifiers and chose this one! So if you are looking into air purifiers ignore what companies say about their purifiers. Do the research and compare the above things like I did! Especially pay attention to the square footage and get one that covers the square footage you need for your home! But you can’t go wrong with this one! Its a working machine and does great at keeping your air clean!

title: Sensor is sensitive and motor is whisper quiet.
text:
When my 8-year-old said he wanted his own room, we converted our finished basement into a bedroom for him. It is at ground level and has 4 large windows. It also has a fireplace from 1820 and a bit of dampness at the base of the fireplace. After about a month, he started having a slight cough; almost a tic. To ensure it wasn't a problem with the air quality in his room, I purchased this to see if I could make it any better for him because he desperately wanted to keep this as his room despite our attempts to the contrary.

Assembly was a breeze and the entire unit feels incredibly well built and well designed. The filter assembly is a lovely masterpiece of sequential filters, one of which is supposed to remove mold spores and germs. The air is not noticeably bad in there (my home office is 10' away). However, when I plugged the unit in, the air quality indicate glowed red and it went into full-tilt mode. I was a bit panicked thinking, oh no, this thing is loud. However, after about an hour, that red light had turned to red/blue and then to blue. The unit is now WHISPER quiet and he has already stopped coughing occasionally as he used to. Psychosomatic, maybe. But it worked and I don't think so. This thing seems to actually be doing what it was designed to do.

I am an engineering nerd and designer. This is a fantastic piece of equipment. It is not cheap, but it is great product. I am very pleased with this purchase so far. Will update as time progresses. When I opened my closet door (always a bit dusty in there) the unit jumped to life again and cleared the air after 10m of doing its job. Was very impressed with how sensitive this is. It's kind of awesome.

Only thing I would lose is that weird blue bar across the middle.

title: Great improvement in nightime allergies.
text:
I was trying to decide between Sharp FP-60CX and the Rabbit Air BioGS 421A, which are about the same price. I ultimately went with the Sharp unit because I wanted to operate the unit without a remote (the last thing I want is another remote!), the lights can be turned off, it has a higher CADR rating and is Energy Star compliant. FP-60CX features I like:
- remote is not essential
- the display light can be turned off
- gently kicks into higher gear when dogs leap on the bed!
- adjustable louvers to steer output air
- remote uses AA batteries
- washable pre-filter
- higher CFM/Watt in silent mode: Sharp= 31/4=7.75 versus Rabbit= 39/7=5.57.
- Max CFM rating is 233, which is substantially larger than the Rabbit 421A's 159. Note that the Rabbit is marketed as a 600 sq ft unit, but if you use the same CADR multiplier as the FP-60CX (1.42) it would only yield 225 sq ft. To put it another way... the Sharp unit would yield 879 sq ft (i.e. 600*233/159) if Rabbit marketing numbers are used.

I used to have a Honeywell 50250 in the bedroom, but I still had nighttime allergies and wanted to try something different and quieter. I find the Sharp unit in MAX mode is quieter than the 50250 on "silent" mode. I was also pleasantly surprised to find that my nighttime allergy symptoms improved dramatically with the Sharp unit. Both have equivalent CADR so the improvement may stem from the fact that because this unit is so quiet I can keep it next to my bed and it won't disturb my sleep.

title: Good product, horrible customer service and NO warranty
text:
First off, I want to say that this is a good air purifier. I've had it for years and it's worked wonders to improve air quality in our apartment. However, the customer service is horrible and deceptive.

Long story short, I moved the air purifier a bit too close to the cat tree one day, and my cat, being a Cat, decides to projectile vomit... inside the unit. Of course. It was funny, and horrifying, and just what a Cat would do.
It only opens from the top and can't be deconstructed so despite multiple attempts, it couldn't be cleaned. I didn't want particles of vomit flying through the air, so decided to contact Airthereal to see about getting a replacement, or at the very least some help to get it cleaned.

Well. My partner and I tried contacting them numerous times and were given the run around. We called, emailed, filled out forms and every time they would say "this is an unusual situation... we're looking into it" - then we'd wait a few weeks and they would never get back to us. We'd try again, only to be ghosted again. It's been a year now, we haven't been able to use this air purifier, even though it's literally just like new. Only conclusion I can draw is that they don't want to honor the warranty and are hoping we drop it eventually. They never even said "no, this doesn't qualify for replacement" or offered to help us figure out how to take it apart to clean it! Just a promise to "look into the open ticket" and then silence.

Well now wildfire season is approaching, and we need an air purifier, so we'll be going for a different unit from a different company. It really sucks, because I hate throwing away perfectly good appliances and contributing to landfills. But Airthereal clearly does not care about customer service or replacing broken items.

TLDR - great product, horrible customer service, and there is ever an issue don't count on them helping replace/fix it.
